Heading: Walled city’s two-km stretch too long for Vadodara police - Indian Express
Content:
Heavy rains and breaches in several areas of Rajkot region forced the Western Railway to cancel six trains, divert four and terminate another four on Wednesday.

Those cancelled are train numbers 1463 Veraval-Jabalpur leaving Veraval; 2972 Bhavnagar-Bandra Terminus leaving Bhavnagar; 2971 Bandra Terminus-Bhavnagar leaving Bandra Terminus; 9005 Mumbai Central-Okha Saurashtra Mail leaving Mumbai Central; 9017 and 9018 Saurashtra Janta Express running between Jamnagar and Bandra Terminus. Saurasthra Janta Express has been cancelled in both the directions.

Besides, train numbers 9221 and 9222 running between Ahmedabad and Veraval have also been cancelled.

These apart, as many as 13 trains were cancelled in the country due to heavy rains. Train number 6334 Thiruvananthapuram-Veraval Express was reversed ex Savli, back to Viramgam, and would run up to Veraval via Viramgam-Maliya-Morbi-Vankaner.

Train number 2905 Porbandar-Hawrah Express and 8402 Okha-Puri Express would run via Vankaner-Morbi-Maliya-Viramgam to Howrah. Train number 9006 Okha-Mumbai Express would run via Vankaner-Morbi-Maliya-Viramgam to Mumbai.

Moreover, four trains have been terminated on their routes. Accordingly, train number 7018 Secunderabad-Rajkot Express of September 17 was terminated at Ahmedabad and run as 7017 Rajkot-Secunderabad Express on September 18 ex Ahmedabad to Secunderabad. It will remain cancelled between Ahmedabad and Rajkot.

Train number 9059 Jamnagar-Surat Intercity of September 17 will be terminated at Viramgam and reversed as 9060 on September 18 ex Viramgam to Surat. It will remain cancelled between Viramgam and Jamnagar. Also, train number 5636 Guwahati-Okha Express was terminated at Ahmedabad on Wednesday.

Train number 9215 Mumbai-Probandar Express of September 17 was terminated at Viramgam and reversed as 9216 Porbandar Express on September 18 ex Viramgam to Mumbai. It will remain cancelled between Viramgam and Porbandar.

Heading: Foresters in action mode, chalk out plan to battle langur menace - Indian Express
Content:
Maximum police force deployed around Sursagar Lake, instead of the communally sensitive stretch between Kumbharwada and Champaner Darwaja

Vadodara city witnesses communal clashes almost every year during the Ganesh festival. And it is the 2-km stretch between Kumbharwada to Champaner Darwaja which is the most sensitive area during Ganesh visarjan, communal riots and even cricket matches.

Even local residents of both the communities admitted that the situation remains tense during visarjan every year. It is, however, surprising that Vadodara police installed CCTV cameras and deployed maximum police force around Sursagar Lake rather than plugging the problem areas with additional force.

Interestingly, the Prevention of Crime Branch officials were not even asked to make preventive arrests, despite having information about people who have been involved in past rioting incidents.

PCB police inspector S R Chaudhari told Newsline: "We were not given any instructions to make preventive arrests before visarjan."

Vadodara Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana, however, said that several arrests were made well in advance of Ganesh visarjan. "We have been keeping a close watch on all such elements. Though there were no CCTV cameras installed, we have videographed the processions," he said.

On the other hand, residents belonging to both the communities said that the reason why a small scuffle turned into a full-fledged communal clash on Ganesh visarjan day was the inadequate deployment of police force in the area.

Heading: Old, used up equipment still serves in SSG Hospital - Indian Express
Content:
Vadodara DCF orders survey after Newsline report on the nuisance caused by langurs in RIL complex

The Vadodara Social Forestry Department has ordered a quick survey to manage the menacingly increasing population of Hanuman Langurs (semnopithecus antilus) in the 1,263 acre Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) petrochemical complex in the city.

The order comes after Newsline carried a report on Wednesday describing the possible dangerous consequences of allowing the 200-strong army of langurs to dwell in the RIL complex.

While the primates have already attacked three RIL employees, officials also fear that the langurs might damage the elevated pipelines, which carry highly explosive sensitive petrochemical products such as benzene and Acrylonitrile. This could cause a major mishap.

Nayan Desai, Deputy Conservator of Forest (DCF), Vadodara district, said, "We are trying to arrange for more cages to trap the simians. I have also ordered Assistant Conservator of Forest (ACF) S J Sheikh to look into the matter after learning that three people have been attacked by the langurs."

He added: "We have decided to take suo motto action on the issue mentioned in the report. The Social Forestry Department will also try to conduct a study on the habitat adapted by the langurs." At present, the department has 10 cages. It will have to arrange for 30 more in order to relocate the langurs. "Earlier, RIL officials had relocated around 65 langurs to the outskirts of the city," Desai added.

Heading: Mystery allergy kills woman in Tilakwada village - Indian Express
Content:
After 1970, this is the first time that Sir Sayajirao General (SSG) Hospital, the largest in district, has taken up a proper procedure to dispose of unusable and irreparable articles from the premises.

But even as most of the articles are as ancient as the hospital itself, officials at the helm of affairs are dilly-dallying about the issue. "The process was taken up partially in 2002, but after identifying the irreparable articles, they were dumped, instead of being disposed of. A proper condemnation procedure did not take place after 1970s," said M H Gadhavi, additional collector and executive officer of the hospital. Starting with disposing of decayed and irreparable iron furniture from the wards, the inspection committee will check the wooden articles to assess whether they need repair work or have to be disposed of.

"We are disposing of all the articles that are more than 10 years old and are beyond repair. The contract for iron wares has already started. Wooden furniture will be inspected and the contract given to Khadi Gram Udyog where some of the broken furniture can be fitted back into shape using other broken articles," said Gadhavi.

While most of the doctors are complaining about the sorry state of bio-medical instruments in the various departments and wards, their disposal and replacement still seems a far cry. "Most of the instruments are very old and not in usable condition, but we cannot dispose them of because there is no surety as to when the new ones will come. A department here can be kept in workable condition only if it makes its own efforts," said a doctor requesting anonymity.

Gadhavi however, said: "We will look into that aspect as well. There can be two possibilities — either the instrument is inspected by the engineer of the company it belongs to and is repaired or replaced, or we assign a bio-medical engineer who certifies the condemnation. We will also put up an advertisement for the infrastructure needed in the open market," said Gadhavi.

Heading: Probe against five cops for demanding Rs 60,000 as bribe - Indian Express
Content:
In an unusual incident, a 30-year-old woman from Koyari village of Tilakwada taluka in Narmada district reportedly died of an allergy after a bottle of medicine fell on her on Wednesday afternoon.

According to the Tilakwada police, Sumitra Baria, a mother of two, was cleaning her house on Wednesday afternoon when the bottle of medicine fell on her.

Dr Radhika Devi from the Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL) Narmada Yojana Hospital said the victim was already in a critical condition when she was taken there and couldn't be saved. She said a private practitioner had referred her to the hospital.

Dr Devi who later informed to the police about the incident, said: "According to the statement given to the medical experts and other police officials, Baria died due to allergy. The post-mortem will confirm the facts."

Heading: VIBGYOR High students to take part in NASA Space Camp - Indian Express
Content:
Five cops of Tilakwada police station have been accused of demanding bribe of Rs 60,000 from one Bharat Pathak, a wireman with the Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL).

Pathak filed an FIR against them late on Tuesday evening.

Superintendent of Police, Narmada, Khurshid Ahmed said: "A month ago, Pathak was arrested under IPC 324 for injuring a woman vegetable vendor of the Muslim community. The police officials allegedly demanded Rs 60,000 from him to settle the case. Following this, Pathak filed a complaint against five people. The investigation was then handed over to Rajpipla DSP N A Munia".

The cops named in the FIR are Circle Police Inspector Y A Shaikh, Sub Inspector B M Makwana and three head constables Naginbhai, Danjibhai and Jitendra Bhai. A case has been registered against the five under IPC Sections 323, 405 and 506 for criminal intimidation, corruption and breaching peace.

Heading: Forensic Science University to be set up in Gandhinagar - Indian Express
Content:
As many as 23 students of VIBGYOR High International School have been selected to take part in an eight-week space camp organised at the US Space and Rocket Centre, the official visitor centre of Marshall Space Flight Centre of National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). It is the only school in the city that has been selected for the camp, which will be held in December.

The official ambassador to the NASA Space Camp and the US Space and Rocket Centre, Brij Mohan Sood visited the school on Wednesday to orient the students as well as their parents about the camp.

"Some 100 students have been selected from Gujarat. They will further be interviewed by Mr Sood," said Shirin Wadia, principal of VIBGYOR High International School.

During the camp, the students will be exposed to the practical and life-like applications of the theories they have studied. "They will be exposed to the practical demonstration of zero gravity zone, aviation and areas of science and technology which they have only read about in school," said Seema Panj Nermeti, hostel rector of the school.

After the camp, the students will visit the NASA museum. In addition, there will be a competition between the selected students from all over the world at the end of the camp. "We certainly want our students to fare well when they compete with international students. They have already started their preparation," said Nermeti.

Meanwhile, Sood informed that he has been an ambassador of 17 states in India, which includes Gujarat. "Till now, 64 students from different batches have already been sent to the NASA Space Camp," said Sood.

Heading: Bull’s ‘murder’ stirs up a hornet’s nest - Indian Express
Content:
The Gujarat government has decided to establish a state-run Forensic Science University in Gandhinagar. The government will present a Bill in this regard during the three-day monsoon session of the Assembly beginning September 25. The new university will start functioning from the next academic year.

A senior official in the state Home Department said on Wednesday that a state-of-the art building will be constructed on the 20,000 sq mt land adjacent to the present Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) premises in Sector 9 in Gandhinagar. The government has sanctioned the land for the construction of the university building free of cost.

"An amount of Rs 2 crore has already been earmarked under the budgetary head of FSL for the university. Work on the educational institute will start soon after the Bill is passed in the Assembly. By the time a new building for the university comes up, it will start functioning from the existing premises of the FSL Directorate," the official said.

The university will offer a three-year B.Sc course and a two-year M.Sc course in Forensic Science. The forensic science-related subjects to be taught at the university include cyber crimes, ballistic science, besides physics and chemistry.

Initially, the first batch comprising 25-30 students will be admitted to the university. The teaching faculty will be recruited from the State Directorate, FSL and also other institutes in the country.

FSL Director J M Vyas told Newsline that the main objective behind setting up the university is to meet the increasing demand for forensic science experts in Gujarat and elsewhere in the country.

In addition, the university will create employment opportunities for youths, especially in the police department and judiciary, he said. He added that even serving police officers will get a chance to study forensic science at the university.

Meanwhile, sources said there is a staff shortage of about 30 per cent staff in the state FSL Directorate and its four regional labs in Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara and Junagadh. The government is in the process of setting up a regional laboratory in Rajkot, too, they added.

"When the Forensic Science University becomes fully operational, it will help solve the present staff crunch," sources said.

Heading: I’m an innocent Muslim, says man whose name was in e-mail - Indian Express
Content:
Titled Picturing the Century, some 100-odd photographs that adorn the walls at St Andrews College in Bandra showcase the country's historical experiences from the past century.

The photo-exhibition is a part of a three-day event, Experience America, that highlights the country's cultural, political and educational aspects, taken from the early 1900s onwards. The frames have been taken from the National Archives and Record Administration (NARA) division of the US Government that has over nine million pictures in its still photographs section, that too in the Washington DC area alone.

One of the frames shows Orville Wright's photograph of the aeroplane built by him and his brother, which is dated December 17, 1903. Then there is one taken by one H W Chadwick dates back to 1906, and depicts the destruction caused by the San Francisco earthquake. Another one, Women Rivet Heaters and Passers On, shows a group of both African-American and Caucasian women working together in the Navy Yard, when discrimination was rampant.

The exhibition also have images from America at war like one that shows soldiers landing on the coast of France.

"The exhibition displays hope, and it's fantastic," said Paul Folmsbee, US Consul-General. "There are moments of historical importance in the last 100 years, like that of Lyndon Johnson with Jacquline Kennedy. The photograph must have been taken soon after her husband was killed," he added. As part of the three-day event, the American Centre is also organising a Democracy Video Challenge that invites filmmakers and common people to create online videos that complete the phrase — "Democracy is....".

"Both countries — the US and India have a lot in common. We are both the world's largest democracies," said Folmsbee, adding that the winner of the contest will get to visit New York and Hollywood.

Heading: BJP demands 70% BMC jobs, contracts for Marathis - Indian Express
Content:
The e-mail sent to the media by the Indian Mujhadeen minutes before last Saturday's Delhi serial explosions contained the name of Maulana Mahmood-ul-Hassan Qasmi, 49, and referred to "incidents of atrocities" against him during combing operations by Anti Terrorist Squad (ATS) officials at Mograpada, Andheri.

Maulana Qasmi, a father of four, rents a bakery (name of bakery withheld on request) at Andheri (East) along with four others. He is also the Mumbai unit President of the Anjuman Minaze Rasool, a religious committee which deals with education for Muslim children. He had met Sonia Gandhi in New Delhi as part a of delegation which wanted to highlight to her the general condition of Muslims in the country in 2006.

Expressing astonishment at his name appearing in the terror e-mail, he told Newsline, "I am not in any way attached to any terrorist organisation. Please leave me alone. The police and other investigating agencies should not link me to anyone just because my name has been dropped in some e-mail sent by the alleged blast perpetrators."

A native of Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, Qasmi came down to Mumbai with his family in 1990 to earn a living. Since he knew folks from Bijnor who used to stay in the Mograpada area close to Andheri railway station, he started living there.

Initially, he used to work in the bakery but in 2002 — when its owner wanted to shut it down — Qasmi decided to rent it out from the owner. He borrowed money and started running the bakery on rent. Qasmi, who has two daughters and two sons, was one of the persons assaulted and manhandled by plainclothes ATS officials.

Recollecting the September 1 incident, he said, "I was sleeping in my house with my other family members when the police suddenly entered and started questioning me about the whereabouts of one Tauqeer. They kept on asking me where the person with whom I had snacks in the evening was. I could not figure out what they were looking for but they posted a revolver on my forehead and kept on repeating, 'where is Tauqeer.' They even went to the loft and asked my children why they were studying if they were 'going to take to untoward activities'," he said.

"I showed them the pictures which have been put up in my house and pleaded that I am a respectable person who would not indulge in heinous activities like abetting a terrorist. But they turned down my pleas and kept on hunting my house for Tauqeer," he said.

Commenting on the search, Joint Commissioner of Police (ATS) Hemant Karkare said, "At the time, we had specific information that Tauqir was hiding at the concerned address, and that is why we raided it. We did not even know who the occupant of the building was."

Qasmi, however, said, "I am an innocent Muslim and I don't want harassment from any authority. Please try to understand me and my reasons for being reluctant to divulge my personal information to you."

Heading: Wall collapse in Ghatkopar injures three - Indian Express
Content:
Party corporator moves notice of motion in municipal body's GB, says he wants to put an end to Sena-MNS tug-of-war for Marathi manoos

For the last eight months, as the Raj Thackeray-led Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) and cousin Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena battled it out on the streets "for the cause of Marathi manoos", their ally the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) chose to remain a quiet spectator. But now it has ended its silence and jumped onto the bandwagon — and is claiming that it will put an end to the "tug of war between the two Senas".

In the latest development, the BJP has demanded priority for the Marathi population for jobs in the country's richest civic body, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), as well as for BMC contracts and projects. Party corporator Vishwanath Maske has moved a notice of motion in the BMC General Body (GB), demanding that the civic body make a compulsory "priority" of 70 per cent for Marathi manoos for all jobs with the BMC, its contractors and its various outsourced projects.

"Hoards of migrants are coming into the city every day, due to which locals are being deprived of job opportunities," he said. Maske's notice is expected to be discussed in the coming days. If it is approved by all 247 members, then Municipal Commissioner Jairaj Phatak will have to submit a report on its implementation in a month.

Maske has asked the BMC to give priority to the Marathi population while recruiting staff for the commercial capital's civic administration as well as for other bodies like BEST, distribution of stalls in civic markets and even contractors who are appointed for various projects.

The civic body, with a budget of Rs 16,000 crore, awards numerous infrastructure projects on contract basis. Many of the current contractors as well as labourers are "outsiders".

Maske told Newsline that he wants to put an end to the Shiv Sena-MNS tug-of-war for Marathi manoos. "Both the parties are screaming and running riot in the name of Marathi manoos. Who benefits from all this? No one. It only results in losses," he said. "The main problem will not get solved by displaying signboards in Marathi. The locals need jobs and better financial conditions. Job priority and reservation is the final and only solution," he asserted.

Maske's party colleagues in the BMC are backing him. BJP leader Bhalchandra Shirsat said it is the party's duty to demand that jobs be reserved for locals.

"We support the issue of sons of the soil and there is nothing wrong with it," he said, adding that along with contractors, priority and reservation should also be applicable to contract labourers. "If the project and money are from Mumbai, Maharashtra, then why shouldn't the labourers too be from here? Why bring outsiders?" he asked.

The Shiv Sena, which is the ruling party in the BMC along with its ally the BJP, pointed out that it has been demanding job reservations from the very beginning. "Apart from reservation for staff recruitment, priority should also be given to Maharashtrian contractors if they fit the eligibility criteria," opined Standing Committee Chairman Ravindra Waikar.

While the MNS leader in the BMC was not reachable, the party's general secretary Shirish Parkar said that the demand is an indication of how all parties are slowly uniting on the issue of "sons of the soil". "It is a victory of solidarity and unity for the Marathi manoos. We do not mind if the BJP too supports the cause. If they want to take credit, then let that be. The important aspect is that all this is for the sons of soil," he said.

Heading: Armed miscreants rob shop in Goregaon - Indian Express
Content:
A wall collapsed in Ghatkopar on Wednesday afternoon, injuring three persons of a family. The incident occurred at 2 pm when a wall of the house close to a retaining wall of a nullah crashed.

The structure was located in Bhatt Rajaram bhaiyya chawl near Navyuvak krida mandal in Sanjay Kokate. Injured Shakuntala Mhatre (55), Nilesh Mhatre (56) and Sandesh Mhatre (18) were taken to Rajawadi hospital and were discharged immediately. Civic officials said that the house was touching the retaining wall of the nullah and part of the wall was weakened due to the incessant rainfall in the last three days. The house is an old structure and its walls were weakened.

The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has ordered a probe into the collapse.

Heading: Two women held for stripping a third - Indian Express
Content:
The Goregaon east police are conducting enquires to trace the identities and whereabouts of four men in their mid-twenties who robbed a wholesale shop in Goregaon on Tuesday night at 11:10.

According to the police, the shop-Tombco Wholesaler based at Shivneri Road is owned by one Mukesh Chaubey (26) who was in the shop with his brother when the four men entered the shop.They were armed with a revolver and a knife and threatened the brothers.

"The men made away with a gold chain they pulled off Mukesh's neck and Rs 40,000 cash. The brothers later filed a case of robbery against the unidentified men," said DCP, (Zone 12), Ajit Patil. Patil further informed that the police are trying to make sketches of the accused through descriptions given by the victims.

"From what we have gathered, so far, the motive seems to be plain robbery and not because of any business rivalry, though we are a bit surprised at this incident because crimes are not committed so frequently in that area," he added.

Heading: Naidu in city to discuss petitions on mobile phones, leprosy - Indian Express
Content:
A 33-year-old woman was allegedly stripped off in broad daylight in Ghatkopar's Parsiwadi area. The incident took place on Tuesday afternoon when two money lenders Prema Kunj Nadar and Surekha Pawar accosted the victim Megha Chauhan on the road. She was allegedly stripped because her sister-in-law had taken a loan and was yet to repay it to them.

According to Megha's complaint filed at the Ghatkopar police station, on Tuesday, when she was on her way to fetch her child from school at around 12.30 pm, Nadar and Pawar stopped her at Vitthal Mandir Chowk and starting hurling abuses at her. After the verbal duel, both the women threw her on the ground and tore off her kameez. After the incident, she filed a complaint with the Ghatkopar police and the same evening both the accused were arrested.

The police have booked the two women for assault and criminal force on woman with the intent to outrage her modesty, wrongful restraint and criminal intimidation. Megha alleged that the women were angry at her because she had confronted them when they had barged inside her house a few days back and threatened her sister-in-law, Shashikala Pingle, for failing to repay the loan.

Police Inspector (Community), FS Pawar, said, "Both Nadar and Pawar are known for their small time money lending activities. They borrow small sums of money on low rate of interest and lend it to others." Pawar also said that other borrowers had also made oral complaints against them.

The Ghatkopar police officials added that they had received several complaints against the duo, but most of them were petty in nature. So far, only non-cognizable offences had been registered against them.

Pawar added, "Humiliating a woman by tearing off her clothes in public is a serious offence. The women have been given several warnings in the past and prohibitory orders have also been slapped against them. However, this time they took things too far by striking a woman's dignity in public and we couldn't let it off as a mere non-cognizable offence."

Heading: NABH launches book on standards for healthcare and wellness industry - Indian Express
Content:
Chairman of the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions, Venkaiah Naidu, on Wednesday said that the committee had begun discussions on the two petitions it had received, one on the betterment of lives of leprosy patients, and the other on the use of mobile phones in public places.

The ten-member committee was in Mumbai as part of a series of visits to discuss and understand the various aspects of the results of the petitions filed, one by former petroleum minister Ram Naik representing the leprosy patients in India, and the other by Gurjit Singh, an advocate from Patiala, concerning the use of mobile phones in public places

"The committee interacts and understands problems and then presents them in front of the Parliament, which then decides on the course of action to be followed," said Venkaiah Naidu.

The petition regarding the medico-socio-economic empowerment of leprosy patients demands certain amendments in various acts, which include the Indian Railways Act, 1989, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, and Hindu Special Marriage Act, 1954. "For example, the Hindu Marriage Act allows any person who has a spouse with leprosy to file for divorce on those grounds. This is unfair to the person in question, especially since it has been proven that leprosy is a curable and non-communicable disease," said Naidu.

Among the other demands in the petition was a sustenance allowance for leprosy patients, free medical aid, free bus passes, and the demand that they should get a disability certificate.

The second petition concerns reasonable restrictions for the use of mobile phones in public places.

"There are some demands like the use of phones in educational institutions, hospitals, crematoriums, and places of worship should not be allowed," said Naidu. The petition also demands that use of mobile phones while driving be disallowed and that cameras in phones not be used for professional use," he added.

The committee met with teachers, students, parents, officers from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation and religious leaders in Mumbai to discuss the demands of the petition.

"Overall, the views are that the use of mobile phones shouldn't be banned, but must be restricted to certain areas," said Naidu.

The committee also met with cellphone operators like Tata, Idea, Vodafone and Bharti to discuss how newer technologies could be used and how to deal with connection problems.

"Once we are in Delhi, we will submit our findings to the Parliament and the ministries concerned will then decide on the course of action," Naidu added.

Heading: TRS untimely and impractical: Transport Commissioner - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Clinical Establishments Act (the legislation that will mandate all private hospitals, nursing homes, and diagnostic centers in India to be registered with the government) is still debated in the Parliament, National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare (NABH) on Tuesday launched a book on standards for healthcare and wellness industry with Dr R K Srivastava, director general of health services Delhi.

Wellness has been a booming industry in India since the past year. However, currently it has no standards or guidelines. The industry includes cosmetology clinics, clinics dealing with nutrition, chest disease centers like allergies clinics, psychiatry clinics, orthopedic clinics, neurology centres, gastroenterology clinics, dental clinics, ergonomics and rehabilitation clinics, ophthalmology clinics, ENT clinics, cardiology clinics, infertility clinics, sexual health clinic, nephrology, alternative medicine, substance abuse clinic, toxicity clinic, sleep therapy clinic, weight management clinics, medical termination of pregnancy clinics, gynecology clinics, immunization and travel prophylaxis, exercise, investigation facilities (medical facilities which give diagnostic facilities should be brought under this category).

Prepared by NABH, a constituent board of Quality Council of India (QCI), the standard for health and wellness are applicable for accredited healthcare and wellness companies offering services to consumers in India . Girdhar Gyani, secretary general QCI said, "Indian wellness standards are first of its kind. They cover all aspects of healthcare and wellness." He added, "These would cover aspects like technology, trained manpower, infrastructure, customer safety, processes and controls among many others, statutory and regulatory compliance. The standards would lay down stringent regulations for service providers to obtain mandatory full accreditation of the total services offered."

There is often a thin line between beauty and wellness and customers often fall pray to the marketing tactics of the mushrooming clinics. "We don't have regulatory framework in India for cosmetic trials. Unlike Food and Drug Administration in US, Indian FDA does not crack down on trials for beauty products." added Gyani.

Bombay High Court recently passed a judgment that hospitals should charge the same rates as advertised. "According to the guidelines, it is mandatory for all the clinics both health as well as wellness, to display rates at the counter," said Gyani. When asked about monitoring of the clinics, Gyani said, "The whole idea is self accreditation and monitoring. Also customers should be well aware of the standards, these clinics have to maintain and their rights as clients and patients."

Heading: Bandra-Worli Sea Link set for beautification  to attract tourists - Indian Express
Content:
The State Transport Commissioner on Wednesday told the Bombay High Court that the implementation of the Traffic Restraint Scheme (TRS), proposed for decongestion of vehicular traffic flowing into the island city, is untimely and impractical. A division bench of Justice J N Patel and Justice K K Tated was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Bombay Environmental Action Group (BEAG) seeking the implementation of the TRS in 2003.The court has now adjourned the hearing till September 24.

Transport Commissioner, Shyamsunder Shinde, in his affidavit stated, "the implementation of the TRS, at this point of time, looking at the public transportation effort, the constraints earlier stated in the scheme's implementation and the focus on provision first rather than restrictive regulation renders the TRS untimely and impractical." The affidavit further states, " the state government along with the railways and other agencies of the government are alive to the transportation challenges facing the city. Massive effort has been launched to improve Mumbai's public transport. Some of such projects as cited have been completed, others are ongoing and their impact should be positive in easing congestion."

The affidavit carries a list of projects and schemes which are at various stages of implementation by agencies of the government. These according to Shinde would have a "considerable decongesting effect on road traffic." The court had earlier expressed dissatisfaction over the fact that the government did not deal with the traffic problem seriously. The court had directed the government to file an affidavit stating the measures it proposes to take to avoid clogging up of the city. Government pleader told the court that expert consultants have been appointed to study the situation following which the court sought the report along with the affidavit.

Counsel for BEAG Shiraz Rustomji earlier submitted that none of the things mentioned by the government like the Mumbai Urban Infrastructure Project (MUIP), Mumbai Urban Transport Project (MUTP) and Mumbai Metro Project, had anything to do with private vehicles. Rustomji had earlier argued that cities around the world have seen a marked difference in road traffic and pollution levels after implementing TRS. The court had earlier asked the state government whether it could ensure the voluntary compliance of the TRS. The state, however, said that they can regulate the flow of traffic under the four walls of the statute but the voluntary compliance can be ensured by an NGO. The state submitted that the MUIP, the MUTP and the Mumbai Metro Project were in the pipeline and would go a long way in easing the traffic woes of the city. The government also pointed out projects like widening of the eastern express highway, elevated corridor from the airport and sea-links that will help reduce the congestion. BEAG in its PIL pressed for the implementation of the scheme first proposed by a committee headed by former transport commissioner V M Lal. The committee had come up with 100 ways to reduce Mumbai's vehicular pollution, one of which was the TRS.

Heading: IIT-B alumnus presents alma mater $5 million grant to fuel research work - Indian Express
Content:
The city's much-touted engineering marvel, the Bandra-Worli Sea Link, is all set for a few green stretches in a bid to become a "tourist destination". The link is expected to be opened to traffic in January 2009.

The Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC), which is the nodal agency for the cable-stayed Bandra-Worli Sea Link, has received a good response to its promenade beautification plans as four entities have submitted their proposals. M/s Unitech, M/s D B Realty, M/s Amma Lines and Daily Sagar have submitted the proposals to build the promenade on a built-operate-transfer (BOT) basis. Anil Deshmukh, Minister of Public Works Department said, "The agencies will be given the job of beautifying the promenade and maintaining the same for the stipulated concession periods for which the bids were called in."

The MSRDC had called in proposals for thematic beatification on the 1.6 km approach road to the sea bridge. According to Deshmukh, the beautification proposals put forth before MSRDC include landscaping, plantation of trees in the median, amphitheatre, clock towers at two locations, aesthetic sit outs, joggers promenade, a spot for meditation, water bodies with mural depiction of seven islands of Mumbai along with a glass tower representation, a modern interpretation of traditional light house and public convenience facilities. "With this beautification, this place would develop into one of the magnificent spots in the city of Mumbai," Deshmukh said.

Heading: A US century, frame by frame - Indian Express
Content:
Forty years ago when Romesh Wadhwani, an electronics engineering student at the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay (IIT-B) set up a canteen along with his batch mates at the IIT-B campus, little did he know that the entrepreneurship skills he exhibited then would help him establish himself as an IT entrepreneur, founder, chairman and CEO of Symphony Technology Group at the Silicon Valley. On Wednesday, as a tribute to his alma mater, Dr Wadhwani presented a $5 million grant to IIT-B to establish the Wadhwani Research centre for Biosciences and Bioengineering.

IIT-B signed a memorandum of understanding with the Wadhwani foundation, a non-profit organisation, to set up the centre that is attached to the School of Biosciences and Bioengineering. The centre will help establish 'new standards for world class research with high global impact.' The centre would enable the faculty of Biosciences and Bioengineering to develop partnership with other leading research institutes across the world.

"There is hardly any world class research in India. The Wadhwani Foundation could be a catalyst for establishing world class research in India. Our universities focus only on teaching. We need to achieve global standards in research," said Dr Wadhwani. The centre will aim at making breakthrough research in the field of genetics, malaria, cancer, anti bacterial treatments etc. Wadhwani explained that the reason for choosing this field was that it was an inter-disciplinary field involving engineering, medicine, science, nano-technology etc. The funds would be used directly towards research work and the center would be housed in a new building. Wadhwani said that now that the endowment had been created, the centre would aim at generating funds for the centre from other sources.

Recalling his journey as an entrepreneur, Wadhwani said, "As entrepreneurs you should be incredible optimists at heart. There will be humiliation and failure to turn you down." He added, "The key to good entrepreneurship is that you should be able to motivate your people in good times and bad, take other people with you and have immense passion about your work. Addressing the students, Wadhwani added, "I think it is lack of faculty commitment, technological innovation and investments into research that are obstructing India's growth."

Attributing his success to hard work and luck he said that it was "good to be smart but better to be lucky."

Heading: Hang him if guilty: Mother asks Tauqeer to surrender - Indian Express
Content:
The e-mail sent to the media by the Indian Mujhadeen minutes before last Saturday's Delhi serial explosions contained the name of Maulana Mahmood-ul-Hassan Qasmi, 49, and referred to "incidents of atrocities" against him during combing operations by Anti Terrorist Squad (ATS) officials at Mograpada, Andheri.

Maulana Qasmi, a father of four, rents a bakery (name of bakery withheld on request) at Andheri (East) along with four others. He is also the Mumbai unit President of the Anjuman Minaze Rasool, a religious committee which deals with education for Muslim children. He had met Sonia Gandhi in New Delhi as part a of delegation which wanted to highlight to her the general condition of Muslims in the country in 2006.

Expressing astonishment at his name appearing in the terror e-mail, he told Newsline, "I am not in any way attached to any terrorist organisation. Please leave me alone. The police and other investigating agencies should not link me to anyone just because my name has been dropped in some e-mail sent by the alleged blast perpetrators."

A native of Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, Qasmi came down to Mumbai with his family in 1990 to earn a living. Since he knew folks from Bijnor who used to stay in the Mograpada area close to Andheri railway station, he started living there.

Initially, he used to work in the bakery but in 2002 — when its owner wanted to shut it down — Qasmi decided to rent it out from the owner. He borrowed money and started running the bakery on rent. Qasmi, who has two daughters and two sons, was one of the persons assaulted and manhandled by plainclothes ATS officials.

Recollecting the September 1 incident, he said, "I was sleeping in my house with my other family members when the police suddenly entered and started questioning me about the whereabouts of one Tauqeer. They kept on asking me where the person with whom I had snacks in the evening was. I could not figure out what they were looking for but they posted a revolver on my forehead and kept on repeating, 'where is Tauqeer.' They even went to the loft and asked my children why they were studying if they were 'going to take to untoward activities'," he said.

"I showed them the pictures which have been put up in my house and pleaded that I am a respectable person who would not indulge in heinous activities like abetting a terrorist. But they turned down my pleas and kept on hunting my house for Tauqeer," he said.

Commenting on the search, Joint Commissioner of Police (ATS) Hemant Karkare said, "At the time, we had specific information that Tauqir was hiding at the concerned address, and that is why we raided it. We did not even know who the occupant of the building was."

Qasmi, however, said, "I am an innocent Muslim and I don't want harassment from any authority. Please try to understand me and my reasons for being reluctant to divulge my personal information to you."

Heading: Whistleblower alleges victimisation - Indian Express
Content:
Breaking her silence for the first time since Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer was named as one of the masterminds of the Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Delhi blasts, his mother Zubeida today said her son should be hanged if found guilty and asked him to surrender irrespective of whether he is guilty or not.

"If my son is involved then he should be punished in front of us. We will not stop him being hanged also if he is found guilty," Zubeida said at a press conference. Family advocate Mubin Solkar said while the entire family had decided to address the media, the others kept away fearing that they would be hounded. It was left to Zubeida to field the press, hungry for any information on the man who has emerged as the technological face of SIMI and who continues to elude the authorities.

"My family has suffered a lot," said Zubeida, breaking down. "Like all mothers I too am craving to see my son. But if he is guilty, he should be punished."

"All my children have had an excellent upbringing," Zubeida said, adding that it's a shock to hear her son being blamed for such heinous crimes.

A written statement signed by her and Tauqeer's father Usman Qureshi said that following the blasts in Ahmedabad and Delhi, they found "to their horror" that their son was being named as an accused. "We wish to state that given the values and principles with which we have brought up our children, it is impossible to believe that Abdus Subhan would ever indulge in such acts of violence and terrorism," they said.

Pleading with him to surrender, they said that by concealing himself Abdus would only make himself more prone to further accusations and would become a "soft target" in the event of any other terrorist act in future.

"It is very painful that the media has already passed a guilty verdict against our son even before he has been tried by a court of law," they said.

Zubeida added that Subhan had moved out of the family's residence after his marriage in 1998 and they had lost touch. He stayed with his wife and child before he went missing in 2006.

"The family is not even sure if he is alive or dead and has made no attempt to contact him fearing action from authorities," said Solkar. He added that Tauqeer, who was educated in a convent school in Mumbai and then acquired a diploma in engineering, was also a Microsoft-certified software engineer. "The family is unaware if he ever turned towards fanatic ideology and was not a religious fundamentalist."

His parents said Abdus had studied and worked with people from different communities and therefore it was unlikely that he had hatred for them.

Solkar said that the family had decided not to get in touch with Abdus after his interrogation in the Mumbai train blasts as they felt that they could get in trouble for doing so. He added that Abdus had not been shown as a wanted in the case. Sometimes, even an innocent person might run away fearing police action, Solkar said.

Asked why the family did not file a missing persons complaint after Abdus went missing in 2006, Solkar said that after interrogation by various agencies they decided not to do so.

"We have no idea if he had any contact with SIMI functionaries like Safdar Nagori or Ahmedabad blasts accused Abu Bashar," Solkar said.

Heading: Hands-on training for agri-engineering students held - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has issued notices to the Union Sports Ministry, Central Vigilance Commission, New Delhi and the Sports Authority of India (SAI) on a petition filed by Raj Kumar, a stenographer working with SAI at its Northern Regional Centre, Sonepat. Raj Kumar is a resident of Sector 44-A, Chandigarh.

The whistleblower has alleged that he is being victimised for raising his voice against the alleged rampant corruption, running in hundreds of crores of rupees at SAI.

The contentions of the petitioner before the High Court are that the Union Sports Ministry is shielding the corrupt officers of SAI for the last more than two decades as no action has been taken against them under the CVC Act and the rules framed thereunder.

Raj Kumar has sought protection from the Court and demanded that directions be issued to the Central Vigilance Commission for taking stern action against the officials of SAI.

Raj Kumar has alleged that he was threatened that he will be eliminated or implicated in some false criminal cases including the cases under the NDPS Act in order to pressurise him to withdraw his petition. Disciplinary proceedings were initiated against Raj Kumar by the SAI for raising his voice against the alleged corruption. It has been further submitted by Raj Kumar that the disciplinary proceedings were concluded and finding nothing adverse against the petitioner, the inquiring authority directed the petitioner to join his duties immediately on April 24, 2008. Subsequently the Inquiring Authority submitted his inquiry report whereby the petitioner was exonerated from all the charges framed against him. Despite vigorous efforts made by the petitioner, a copy of the inquiry report has not been supplied to him, the petition alleges.

Heading: Rain plays spoilsport; 39 runs deficit for Chd - Indian Express
Content:
The Department of Farm Power and Machinery, Punjab Agricultural University, organised a four-day training programme on "Overhauling of TAFE (MF1035DI) tractor engine."

Twenty eight B.Tech students of the College of Agricultural Engineering (COAE) participated in the hands-on training wherein they dismantled an engine of a TAFE - MF 1035 DI tractor, learnt about overhauling and re-assembling the engine part-by-part.

A team of experts including Er. Sandeep Singh, Senior Area Manager (Service), TAFE, Varinder Brar, Service Engineer from Simpsons Co., Kishore Kumar, Executive-Training from Product Training Center of TAFE at Alwar and Jujhar Singh, Senior Area Manager (Marketing), TAFE, provided useful tips and guidance to students.

Dr. Rohinish Khurana of the department, who coordinated the programme, informed that during the training, the students were exposed to the intricacies of engine, functioning systems, management and repair, together with various aspects of overhaul, and precautions to be taken while handling the repair and assembly of engines.

Dr P.K. Gupta, Dean, COAE, while giving away the certificates to the successful student trainees, exhorted them to come forward with their queries and doubts. He explained how such hands-on trainings were important to supplement the classroom teaching to improve the learning of the students.

In the concluding function, Dr. I.S. Dhaliwal, Head of Department of Farm Power and Machinery, said that organisation of practical trainings proved helpful to students to know about the realistic functioning of machinery, thus providing them an advantage during their professional careers. Dr Anoop Dixit presented a report on the activities performed by the students during the training.

Heading: ONGC wins on D/L basis - Indian Express
Content:
On a rain marred day, Chandigarh could add just 47 runs to the overnight score of 103 runs against Ludhiana, losing two more wickets on the second day of the Punjab inter-district tournament played for the Katoch Shield at the PCA Stadium in Mohali on Wednesday.

Resuming from the overnight score of 56 for 4 to 103 for 6 in 49 overs, Chandigarh received an early blow as Gurkirat Singh was sent packing on 28 runs on Gagandeep's out swinging delivery. Falling prey to another Gagandeep's out swinging delivery, Anil Sihag without scoring. Chandigarh was 103 for 6 in 49 overs. Gaurav Gambhir stayed on his ground and played responsible innings of 34 not out off 81 balls. The match is in interesting stage, Chandigarh still needs 39 runs to over haul Ludhiana's first innings total of 141 with four wickets in hand.

Brief Scores:
Chandigarh: 103 for 6 in 49 overs (Gaurav Gambhir 34 not out, Gurkirat 28, Gagandeep 2 for 30, Sunny Kumar 3 for 32)

Heading: Chandigarh, Amritsar declared joint - Indian Express
Content:
ONGC edged out State Bank of Mysore (SBM) in a rain-marred match by eight runs on the basis of Duckworth-Lewis method in the inaugural match of the 15th All India J P Atray Tournament for the PEARL Trophy being played at Sector 16 Cricket Stadium on Wednesday.

Batting first, ONGC were cruising at 101 for 3 in 26 overs when the rain played the spoilsport. ONGC posted a total of 184 runs for the loss of eight wickets after the overs were reduced to 44. After losing the first wicket of Tilak Nayudu cheaply, Sandeep Sharma and skipper Gagan Khoda came together and bore a fruitful partnership of 45 runs for the second wicket. Then Ajay Ratra and Mohammad Saif also put on a partnership of 45 runs to take the score to 146 runs. The ONGC innings finally folded at 184 for 8. Ajay Ratra top scored with 45 runs while Sandeep Sharma chiped in with a useful knock of 43 runs. For SBM, Chetan Williams bowled a brilliant spell and returned back with a match winning haul of four wickets while Anand Katti bagged two wickets.

Chasing the revised target of 191 runs on the basis of D/L method, SBM started off well as the openers put on 50 runs for the first wicket. Thereafter, SBM lost three quick wickets which cost them dear as the match was stopped due to bad light and rain and ONGC won the match by eight runs on the D/L basis. M K Manjunath scored 31 runs for his team while Shoib Manager contributed 25 runs. Parvinder, Vikramjit and Sauresh claimed one wicket each for ONGC. Chetan Williams was adjudged the man of the match for his fine spell that fetched him four wickets.

Brief scores:
ONGC: 184 for 8 in 44 overs (Ajay Ratra 45, Sandeep Sharma 43, Mohammad Saif 31,
C Williams 4 for 42, Anand Katti 2 for 28, B Akhil 1 for 35); State Bank of Mysore: 74 for 3 in 21 overs ( MK Manjunath 31, Shoib Manager 25, KN Ramesh 13, Parvinder Amana 1 for 24, Vikramjit Malik 1 for 24, Sauresh Kumar 1 for 6).

Heading: Regional workshop on national food security organisedExpress News Service - Indian Express
Content:
In a nail-biting finish, Chandigarh and Amritsar women were declared joint-winners when the match finished in a tie during the final of the Punjab U-19 inter-district tournament that concluded at the Guru Nanak Public School-36 in Chandigarh on Wednesday.

Winning the toss, Chandigarh skipper Shivani Nayyar chose to bat first. Taking the charge, Shivani along with the in-form Aakriti opened the innings for Chandigarh. Batting confidently, right-handed batswoman Shivani Nayyar unleashed flurry of shots and put the Amritsar bowlers on the back foot. Aakriti could not continue with her fine-form and was removed early by medium-pacer Monika Mehra. Right-handed batswoman Lalita joined skipper Shivani and provided some stability to the innings. Soon, Lalita perished. Shivani continued making runs for her team but did not get enough support from the other end as wickets kept on falling regularly. Finally, Shivani also got out leaving Chandigarh reeling under pressure. The hosts could muster 116 runs in the allotted 50 overs. Medium-pacer Monika Mehra and left-arm spinner Renu Verma wrecked the opposition with their accurate bowling. Monika scalped 3 for 28, while Renu took 2 for 17, respectively.

It looked like as if the run-chase would be a cakewalk for the defending champions, but Amritsar women made a mess as their batting order crumbled. Six-run outs and casual approach affected Amritsar's chances. It was Renu Verma (33) and Navdeep (26) shone with the bat for the visitors. Later in the match, Amritsar were tottering at 116 for 7 in 42 nd over, and could not surpass 116 losing 3 wickets successively. They just needed one run to clinch the tournament, but Chandigarh medium-pacer Aarshiya bowled a stunner to trap last Amritsar batswoman leg before the wicket. The match got tied.

With this brilliant performance, Chandigarh has stamped their authority at the U-19 circuit, considering the fact they have been declared joint winners with the defending champions Amritsar. Based on their performances in this tournament, players will be selected for the U-19 State tournament to be held in October.

Brief Scores:

Chandigarh: 116 for 9 in 50 overs (Shivani Nayyar 42, Lalita 18, Monika Mehra 3 for 28, Renu Verma 2 for 17)

Amritsar: 116 all out in 43.3 overs (Renu Verma 33, Navdeep 26, Anjali 14, Radhika Bhutani 2 for 24, Hema 2 for 24)

Heading: ‘Dancing Lines’ opens in the city - Indian Express
Content:
A workshop on "National food security" under the aegis of National Food Security Mission for Northern States was held at the wheat auditorium of Punjab Agricultural University today.

Inaugurating the workshop, Dr Manjit Singh Kang, Vice-Chancellor, PAU, said that to sustain national food security, 10 million tonnes of rice, eight million tonnes of wheat and two million tonnes of pulses are needed by the end of 11th five-year plan. National Food Security Mission is gearing up to achieve these targets by not only creating new infrastructure but also by improving the existing facilities.

Mukesh Kular, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture, and Director, National Food Security Mission, said that production levels of different crops varied from area to area and that the mission aimed to increase the production levels in areas where it was low. We will sustain food security by bridging the gap between high and low production areas, he said.

Speaking on the occasion, the PAU Director of Extension Education, Dr N.S. Malhi said that global warming was one major factor for limiting the production of wheat and rice. Citing research data, he informed the delegates that a rise in temperature by 10 C will lower the yield levels of wheat and rice by 5-10 %. Every effort must be made to check the climatic change.

Dr P.S. Minhas, Director of Research, PAU, projected the research efforts with a focus on national food and nutritional security.

Heading: PAU scientists discuss tips on pest management of maize, other crops - Indian Express
Content:
The lights seemed to be dancing and singing in more than 42 photographs put up by Swaranjit Savi. Titled "The dancing lines" a photo exhibition put by poet painter and photographer, Swarnjit Savi, opened at the art gallery, 'Artmosphere' here today. The exhibition was inaugurated by eminent photographer A.P. Singh.

Hemant Sathe, an eminent painter, curator and art critic had described Savi's work as "Exploring the journey of light in a very poetic manner." Savi has juxtaposed a variety of visual ideas. Talking about his works, Savi says, "Camera is my constant companion. This is a collection of pictures that I have taken over a period of time. These lights adorn the gurdwaras and the temples and are even the projection of busy city life, the manner in which these lights seem to criss-cross on the roads."

Savi, who has seven books on poetry to his credit, and is also a well-known painter, adds, "And when I saw the pictures, it was the lights that stood out. The forms were gone, left behind were these lines and spots created by lights. Lights seemed to dance in front of me creating images that at times belied the original pictures. The lights simply enraptured me and hence I created this series."

But then the artist who wants to share his "work with the city" is pained at the fact that, "Ludhiana has such a great art gallery in form of Atmosphere. It is one thing that this cash-rich city lacked so grossly. I have put up my works here and now leave it to Ludhianvis to appreciate it."

Savi adds, "It is not that city lacks art sense, it is just that people find it very hard to take out some time from their busy life to roam through a gallery. I really want to make an appeal that it is literally thereupatic to walk through the works of art. Our self becomes well when one sees colours and beauty around and we should visit such places."

Dr A.P. Singh, who teaches photography at PAU, said from the five basic elements of design, Savi has taken the two-colour and line and created poetry out of it. Savi says this was just one of those ideas which he sees as a point in his evolution as an artiste, that produced this series of photographs of light in its various hues.

Heading: Kapri holds workshop - Indian Express
Content:
According to the Head of PAU Department of Entomology, Dr N.S. Butter, a field day-cum-training programme on Integrated Pest Management (IPM) of maize was organised at Sahungra village in Nawanshahar district on September 12 under the Sir Ratan Tata Trust-funded project "Validation and dissemination of IPM technology for quality production in basmati rice, vegetable crops and maize" in collaboration with KVK, Nawanshahar.

About 150 regional farmers attended the field day-cum-training programme. Dr A.K. Dhawan, Principal Investigator, urged farmers to follow the IPM approach to reduce cost of cultivation even as he stressed on the importance of integration of bio-control agents with other pest-control options in the management of maize borer.

On this occasion, Dr S.P.S. Brar, spoke on the importance of maize crop for diversification in agriculture. Dr Nirmal Singh, Dr Vijay Kumar and Dr H.S. Bhullar shared details of the IPM modules for different crops including maize, paddy and vegetables, respectively. Dr. B.S. Kang, Associate Director, KVK, Nawanshahar thanked the farmers for their participation.

Heading: Vet mela to be a must-watch for people from all walks of life - Indian Express
Content:
British Council in collaboration with Kapri Institute of English Speaking, organised an IELTS orientation at Hotel Le Baron today.

Dhiraj Gurung (Marketing Manager), Examination services, British Council, gave a special training for the IELTS students of Kapri Institute. More than 200 students of Kapri Institute got benefit from this session. Dhiraj guided the candidates about all the steps and modules of IELTS.

Speaking on the occasion, Anjali Chawla (HOD) said Kapri was a form registration centre for British Council. It has already trained more than 10,000 students. Nitin Chalwla (Director) thanked Dhiraj and Harjot for sparing time precious time.

Heading: Rs 7 crore seized during income tax raids - Indian Express
Content:
The Pashu Palan Mela of Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal University here will be a must-watch show for people of all the walks of life.

Dr V.K.Taneja, Vice-Chancellor, GADVASU, expressed these views on the eve of Pashu Palan Mela which is going to be held on 18 and 19 September. He said that it will be a centre of attraction for children, youth, senior citizens as well as women because different items will be on display for different age groups, sections and nature. Dr Taneja revealed that whereas cattle, buffalo, goat, rabbit, different species of fish, etc. will be the main attraction for children, country-side scene of university will be special attraction for urban children.

He further said that Pashu Palan Mela would be more useful to vocational courses students studying animal husbandry and rural culture as they will get more valuables information about the latest interventions in the field of animal husbandry, dairying, fisheries, etc.

The experts of the university will provide on-the-spot know-how regarding upkeep, vaccination and other timely care of the small pets like dogs, cats, etc. The pet owners will also get information about the latest products which are now available in the market.

Beside this, the university has done a commendable work on ornamental fish. The people interested in keeping ornamental fish in their houses/workplace can also get latest information about the feeding and management practices. He added that the different species of coloured fish kept the mind fresh and helped in relieving the mental stress. Moreover, fish is a pet of calm nature who does not produce any kind of filth and noise pollution.

The housewives who have either independently taken up the livestock profession or are helping in it can also interact with the experts of the university to get the latest information about the livestock products and their usages. It is also a good privilege to taste and know about the different mouth-watering vegetarian and non-vegetarian delicacies like sweetened and salted lassi, sweet milk, meat patties, different types of meat pickles and good quality buffalo cheese prepared by the Department of Livestock Products Technology.

Now a days, a large quantity of synthetic milk is out in the market. The facility will be at display in the mela to check the quality and adulteration of milk. Awareness about good quality milk will be useful for the health of the human-beings.

The exhibition depicting latest interventions in the field of animal husbandry will also be very helpful for the unemployed youth of the state who are especially interested in setting up their own business in livestock sector with minimum finances.The financial institutes like banks, insurance agencies etc. and experts from the university would provide them the up-to-date knowledge. The food processing machinery will also be on display in the mela to educate the masses about the latest interventions involved in the preparation of hygienic, fast and good quality food products. It will be beneficial for a common man as well as an entrepreneur.

University publications containing information relating to livestock diseases, their remedial measures and informative literature regarding training courses to set up new livestock units would also be available.

Heading: Thieves strike at house in Moti Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
The income tax sleuths raided five steel mills in Khanna and seized unaccounted amount of Rs 7 crore. The raids which started on Tuesday afternoon, continued till 7 a.m. on Wednesday.

A total 75 officials from Khanna, Ludhiana and Malerkotla in three groups swooped down on the premises of steel mills. About 15 policemen accompanied the raiding parties.

The additional commissioner of Income Tax of Khanna range, D.S. Brar, who was leading the operation told Newsline, "The search was conducted at five mills of three groups."

"A total Rs 7 crore were recovered which included Rs 3.50 crore from Chopra group firms including Chopra Strips, Chopra Steels and Chopra Alloys (Furnace Mill), Rs 1.50 crore from Pepsu Steels and Rs 2 crore from Gopal Steelsm," said Brar.

While claiming that it was the biggest surrender of unaccounted amount in the area, Brar said, "Income tax of Rs 2 crore was slapped while Rs 1 crore has been deposited."

Brar said, "The accounts of Pepsu Steels has been surveyed for the first time as it has been working in Mandi Gobindgarh and at the head office in Khanna while Chopra Group had surrendered 15 lakh four years ago."

"An unaccounted amount of Rs 13 crore has been unearthed in the past two weeks and Rs 4.5 crore income tax has been slapped. Six firms were raided two weeks ago and Rs 6 crore were seized," said Brar.

Heading: GLADA auction fetches Rs 11 cr - Indian Express
Content:
This is nothing short of a fairy tail. Subhash Goel, a textile manufacturer by profession and a resident of Moti Nagar, complained of a major theft on Wednesday morning.

As per Goel, thieves stuck at his home at about four in the morning and fled with 1.5 kg of gold and some cash, totalling about Rs 17 lakh. A police party from focal point police station led by SHO Gurdev Singh rushed to the spot and all necessary finger printing was done. The story however turned on its head later in the evening when the family told the police that they had found a part of the stolen booty.

Sumit Goel, the elder son of the family says, "My wife who was admitted in a local hospital with dengue had just come back and we all were sleeping in one room. This entire material was stolen from our lockers that were in the adjoining room."

Sumit adds, "Basically, my mother knows just about her jewellery while my wife who is still under heavy medication and shock over the theft could not tell about how much of her jewellery was stolen. We gave one estimate to the police in the morning and after we opened the second locker, we found some of material lying there. So while we have not found the total stolen booty a part of it has been recovered."

SHO Gurdev Singh meanwhile added, "The family is yet to give us the exact details. They have told us that a part of material which they claimed was stolen has been found and they are yet to check what all is left. We have registered an FIR and investigations are on."

Heading: Councillors want mohalla sanitation panels to stay - Indian Express
Content: Six shops-cum-flats(SCF) measuring 158 square yards  and two booths measuring 33.33 square yards each situated in the commercial market in Phase-II Urban Estate Dugri Road were auctioned  by the Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority( GLADA) at a total price of Rs 11.50  crore against the reserve price of Rs 9.55 crore. S R Kaler, ACA, GLADA, presided over the auction. Kaler said that the SCFs are in the area ranging between 1,09000 per square yard and Rs 1,20000  per square yards against the reserve price of Rs 94,000 per square yards  and booths at Rs 1,14,000 against the  reserve price of Rs 1.05 lakh per square yard. He said 20 bidders participated in the auction.

Heading: Health dept confirms 2 more dengue cases, number reaches 19 - Indian Express
Content:
Itseems that a war has begun between the councillors and union leaders of safai workers. The councillors are adamant that the Mohalla Sanitation Committees should stay. However, the union leaders of safai workers have warned the government to withdraw their support in the coming Lok Sabha elections, if their demand is not met.

At present, 3,200 workers are employed on contract basis in various mohalla sanitation committees. If MC takes over the recruitment of the safaisewaks, only 800 employees will be regularised in the corporation while the rest will go jobless. Moreover, the work of 3,200 employees cannot be done by 800 employees.

An all party meeting was also held today afternoon at mayor's camp office to decide on the issue but they could not reach any conclusion.

Meanwhile, acting on the demand of workers, on August 28, the chief minister had announced to dissolve the mohalla sanitation committees.

Senior Deputy Mayor Parveen Bansal said, "We want mohalla committees to stay. At the moment, the employees are being given Rs 3,500 per month but we can make some better provisions for them within the existing system."

Meanwhile, councillors have maintained that 1,700 regular employees are working in the corporation. They opined that sanitation of the city will be badly affected once the committees are formally dissolved after three months.

Heading: ‘Greedy docs bring bad name to fraternity’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Health department today confirmed two more cases of dengue thereby taking the number of confirmed cases to 19. On the other hand, many patients of the suspected disease are undergoing treatment at differehospitals across the city.

Dayanand Medical College and Hospital has registered over 100 suspected patients of dengue in the monsoons with half of them being the residents of the city. The hospital reported about six more cases of suspected dengue today.

Meanwhile, Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCH) did not report any fresh case today. CMCH has already registered 48 suspected patients of dengue from the district on the basis of positive IGM report.

In a statement issued here by the Indian Medical Association (IMA) today, it said that the about 235 cases that have been reported in the different city hospitals so far is alarming and therefore asked the civic authorities to take up the mosquitocidal spray actively. "Such sprays are essential to prevent the rise in the number of cases of dengue and malaria," the statement said. The association also asked the residents and specially the children, to wear full length sleeves and socks and cover all the exposed parts of the body to keep mosquito at bay.

Heading: Govt doctor caught running private practice - Indian Express
Content:
On earlier occasions too, few doctors of the Punjab Civil Medical Services (PCMS) have been found to be involved in private practice.

Various senior doctors in the city feel that there are only a small percentage of such doctors, who in an attempt to make more money, are bringing a bad name to the profession.

The point has been highlighted earlier too, and recently, a doctor in the district, who is also posted at a dispensary, was also reportedly found to be involved in private practice.

Reacting to the issue of private practice by government doctors, PCMS Association President Dr Hardeep Singh said most of the PCMS doctors are doing their duty well but there may be some who are violating the rules of the department. The association has has nearly 2,200 members.

"This should not happen at any level and therefore I urge all the PCMS doctors to shun any such activity that brings bad name to the profession. Some doctors may have their own style of working but as far as the rules of the profession are concerned, they should be adhered to strictly," he remarked.

Speaking about the issue, Dr Arun Mitra, district president, Indian Medical Association (IMA), said the rules of the profession should always be respected and hence followed. "Therefore, the authorities should take care of such people who go against the ethics of the profession," he added.

However, defending Dr Mandeep Kaur, Mansura Block Samiti member Paramjit Kaur said Mandeep is a honest doctor and was only doing what had been accepted by various members of the Panchayat.

"She was not doing this job in the clinic for herself but she has been asked by us to attend to the patients as she is competent and deals with about 250 patients daily in the village. I do not think she should be blamed for it," she said.

Heading: Sexual abuse charges against PAU dean: Kang marks inquiry - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on a complaint against a Punjab Civil Medical Services (PCMS) doctor, who is alleged to have been involved in private practice, the Health department conducted a raid at a clinic in Mansura and caught him red-handed.

The Health department team that included Dr Rina Sandhu, district family welfare officer and Dr Puneet Sidhu visited the said clinic today where Dr Mandeep Kaur was said to be practising privately.

Giving details about the raid, Civil Surgeon Dr SP Sharma said, "We had received a complaint against Dr Mandeep Kaur, who had been posted to Raikot recently but had taken leave after joining there. The doctor was practising privately and therefore we had sent a team to check this and found the doctor indulging in private practice." He added that the case would be forwarded to the higher authorities.

He further stated that the doctor was earlier posted at the dispensary at Mansura and had recently been transferred to Raikot. "Instead of resuming her duties, the doctor started practising at a private nursing home in Mansura."

Earlier too, the doctor has been charged with causing blindness to four patients while she was working at a dispensary in Mansura village. Complainant Mandeep Singh, a resident of Mansura village, had alleged that the doctor rendered four patients, including his father, blind after they were operated upon for cataract by her. He alleged that in that case too he had told the enquiry team of senior officials of the department that she had opened her private OPD in the government dispensary and used to charge heavily."

However, when asked, Dr Mandeep Kaur said, "A doctor whose business is suffering from my popularity here has been giving me a bad name. As for private practice, I want to know how many PCMS doctors in Ludhiana are not involved in it."

Heading: ‘Delhi blast victim died of medical negligence’ - Indian Express
Content:
By stating that the investigations are on to probe sexual harassment charges made against Director Students' Welfare (DSW) Dr Dulcha Singh Brar, Punjab Agricultural University Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang has clarified that withdrawing the charge of girls' hostel from Brar is not mere an 'administrative order'.

With this, the rumours surrounding the decision of PAU V-C to withdraw the charge of girls' hostels from under the jurisdiction of the DSW have been explained. Dr Kang had taken this unprecedented decision just before leaving for the US.

Before leaving for the US, the Vice-Chancellor had handed over the charge of the girls' hostels to the Dean College of Home Science and had even put Welfare Officer For Girls Lali Brar as the incharge by shifting her services from the DSW office. It is for the second time that the hostel charge has been withdrawn from the DSW. It was earlier done in the 70s. Dr M S Randhawa had taken a similar action against well-known hockey Olympian Prithipal Singh by making him the Director of Sports from DSW.

While both the DSW and Dean College of Home Science Dr Neelam Grewal had earlier explained this as mere administrative change, Dr Kang remarked, "An investigation is going on to probe the matter. We have received a complaint and we will divulge the details only after we are through with the investigations." When asked whether any sexual harassment charges have been made, Dr Kang said, "Whether it is sexual harassment or not, it will be clear only after the inquiry is complete."

Meanwhile, DSW Dr Brar said, "I have no information about the complaint as no one has approached me. I have not been called for any inquiry. My conscience is clear and I have nothing to fear."

A new policy in the offing

The Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) will soon adopt a policy to deal with issues related to sexual harassment, which according to university V-C Dr Manjit Singh Kang `will be gender neutral'.

Dean Postgraduate Studies Dr S K Mann along with Dean College of Home Science Dr Neelam Grewal have been entrusted with the task of designing the policy, the first print of which has already been submitted to the V-C.

It has been learnt that while the university has a separate cell that deals with the complaint related to the cases of sexual harassment, a policy on the same is needed in the wake of a complaint by an athlete to whom some lewd remarks were reportedly made on the field.

Dr Kang said, "ICAR has a policy on this issue and so does the Government of India. Though we can adopt the policy designed by the ICAR as it is, there are a few amends that need to me made in the policy for want of a gender neutral policy. The policy's that we have at present mainly deals with the women-related issues. However, in the changing times, even boys may face such a problem. Hence, I have asked Dr Mann to include this issue also in the new policy."

Dr Kang added, "Similar policies are in place in the US and we will take some reference from them too."

Heading: Statues of Dalit icons make an exit from Smriti Upwan - Indian Express
Content:
Friends of Vikas Anand, a Lucknow resident, who was killed in Saturday's blasts in the New Delhi, have alleged that doctors at the Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital had not done their bit to save his life.

Vikas, who had completed his MBA from Lucknow University a year ago and was recruited as an Assistant Branch Manager of IDBI Bank's Connaught Place branch in New Delhi, was with his friends on the fateful evening when a bomb went off in a dustbin near him.

"We were sitting hardly 10 meters away from the dustbin. At first, we heard a distant bang and we all knew it was a bomb, but within seconds the dustbin near us also exploded," recalled Anand's friend Virendera, who is from Mirzapur district.

He and his friends Arun, and Sudhanshu received minor injuries. "Vikas, despite being injured, was helping in the relief work. It was only after some time he felt the pain in his stomach and was admitted to the RML," said Sudhanshu, who along with others have come down to Lucknow to meet Vikas' family.

Pellets from the bomb pierced Vikas' stomach and entered into his intestine and liver as the X-ray report conducted on him the same evening revealed.

"Had the doctors at RML Hospital been more sensitive and attentive, Vikas would have been saved," said one of his friends.

"During night, his pain increased and when we pointed out to the doctors they simply avoided us saying that they had given appropriate medicines and Vikas would be all right," said Sudhanshu.

"The condition, however, worsened in the night. In the morning, when we insisted, senior doctors ordered an immediate operation," said Sudhanshu.

According to his friends, they were kept waiting by the doctors for the next eight hours. "By then Vikas' condition had become critical. He did not speak after the operation and succumbed to his injuries early on Monday," his friend added.

On Wednesday, there was a gloomy atmosphere at Vikas' house at Rajajipuram, as relatives remained inconsolable. "I have lost my son," were the only words that his father, Chotey Lal, Project Director with the state rural development department, could utter. Vikas' mother Purnima Kureel stood in silence. "She has not spoken since they came to know about Vikas' death," said his brother-in-law Naveen Arya.

Heading: Third Front to be in place by Lok Sabha polls, says Karat - Indian Express
Content:
Three days after Chief Minister Mayawati's visit to the Smriti Upwan, the Lucknow Development Authority started removing the statues of dalit icons there, but nobody was ready to say why this was being done.

"The statues are being removed on the direction of the state administration. There government may have some plan to change the features of Upwan, which I do not know," said LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram.
