He added since the LDA is only executing the project, it is following the directions of the state government. Even engineers involved in project cited ignorance.

After the BSP came to power in 2007, the state government ordered the renovation of the park that was earlier planned as memorial of Kargil War martyrs.

The state government, however, installed statues of 11 Dalit icons, including those of Mayawati, Kanshiram, Bhimrao Ambedkar, Chattrapati Shauji Maharaj, Kabir Das, Sant Ravi Das, Jyotiba Phule, Birsa Munda, Gautam Buddha.

On Sunday night, when Mayawati visited the park, she noticed the use of sub-standard red stones. She was also unhappy with the flooring work of the pavement and immediately asked the LDA vice-chairman to investigate the matter.

The revamping of the Smriti Upwan project has had its fair share of controversies. There was even a move to rename it after Kanshiram and the LDA board had even passed a proposal to this effect. But the move failed after the High Court, acting on a petition, disallowed any change in the name of the park.

Last week, in another case, the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court questioned the LDA about the need to make changes in the Smriti Upwan.

The matter came during the hearing of a petition that objected to Lucknow Municipal Corporation (LMC) using a section of the park to dump garbage.

The LMC had told the court that it was filing up a low-lying area, which, according to the petitioners, was a water body that needed to be preserved.

Meshram had told the court that the government wanted to make some changes in the Smriti Upwan, but he did not know what these changes were. The court had then directed the LDA to submit the details of the proposed changes on September 29.

Heading: IIT-K professor to get first Infosys award on maths - Indian Express
Content:
Communist Party of India (Marxist) General Secretary Prakash Karat said talks are underway with secular non-Bharatiya Janata Party and non-Congress parties, including the Bahujan Samaj Party, for the formation of a Third Front.

The Front will be in place before the next Lok Sabha polls, he claimed.

Karat, who is in the city to chair a two-day meeting of the state committee of the party, took serious note of the recent incidents of communal violence in the state. "We are concerned about such incidents, particularly the one in Azamgarh," he said on Wednesday.

"The state unit of the party will announce agitational programmes in this connection on Thursday," he said. The meeting will also identify potential Lok Sabha seats for the party and discuss names of the probable candidates, he added.

Speaking on the recent changes in the global economy, the CPM leader demanded immediate reduction in the prices of petroleum products following the drop in the prices of crude oil in the international market.

"There is no reason for the Centre to delay in reducing the prices of petroleum products after the prices of crude oil has come down by at least 30 per cent," Karat said.

"A reduction in the prices of petroleum products will help in bringing down inflation and give the much-needed respite to the common people," he added.

Heading: RPF rescues five addicts, sent to Childline - Indian Express
Content:
For his outstanding contribution to Mathematics, Professor Manindra Agarwal of the Indian Institute of Technology-Kanpur (IIT-K) has been chosen as the first recipient of the Infosys Mathematics Prize.

The head of the computer science and engineering department at IIT-K, Agarwal has been selected for the award for his design of algorithms for testing of prime numbers.

In a ceremony likely to be held in December at Bengaluru, he will be handed over the prize and a cash reward of Rs 10 lakh.

"Earlier, the design of algorithms used for testing prime numbers was slow and did not provide the correct reading. This is much faster and can code as many digits as possible," Agarwal told The Indian Express.

Explaining the practical side of the design, he said it is most useful for the online payment system. "For online payment, the prime number is important. A slight error in judging the prime number can lead to the decoding of the credit card," he said. Possibilities of hacking of credit cards increase if even numbers are used for online payment. Agarwal claimed that his design of algorithms is being used by Prime Number Generation Softwares.

Agarwal completed his BTech in computer sciences from IIT-K in 1986, and his PhD in 1991. Over the years, he has been working on Complexity Theory, a branch of mathematics. "Under the Complexity Theory, we design algorithms which has a step by step solution to each problem. Be it railway reservation or a touring map, the design of algorithms helps in carrying out a programme in the easiest way possible," he said.

According to Agarwal, the Infosys Mathematics Prize will go a long way in attracting youngsters towards mathematics.

Heading: Appointment of judge: HC to submit report in sealed envelopes - Indian Express
Content:
The Railway Protection Force (RPF), Lucknow rescued five children on Wednesday addicted to inhaling eraser fluids and solvents like taulene.

The RPF handed over the children to a child help line service — Childline.

The children, all runaway kids from different parts of the state, used to live on the platforms of Charbagh Railway station and earned money by selling water bottles, cleaning train wagons and begging.

They have been identified as Monu (8), Indrajeet (9), Abhishek (12), Akmudin (14) and Suraj (11).

"When diluted and inhaled, these substances give a high," said Monu terming the mixture as Chuna-Paani.

"A bottle costs Rs 22 and I alone could use two to three bottles daily," said Inderjeet, who ran away from his Gorakhpur house, as his parents could not bear his expenses.

According to Inderjeet, there are at least a hundred more such children on the platform who sniff such products. "We have been caught many times but the police used to release us after we paid them some money," said Akmudin from Bareily.

The police, however, denied all allegations. Inspector in-Charge A P Mathur said the RPF have caught hundreds of such children and handed them over to various organisations from time to time. "This time we asked the Childline to rehabilitate these children," Mathur added.

"After proper counselling they would be sent preferably to their families or government protection houses," said Varsha, Centre Coordinator, Childline.

"We will trace their families, contact them and handover their wards to them. In certain cases, when the children or the parents do not want to reunite, we send them to shelter houses," she added.

Heading: Six held for extorting money from traders - Indian Express
Content:
A Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court has directed the High Court to submit the report of the committee that recommended Dr Satish Chandra's name for the appointment of the High Court judge in sealed envelopes.

Hearing a petition challenging the appointment of Chandra on Wednesday, the Division Bench, comprising Justice Shushil Harkauli and Justice Vikram Nath, passed the order after the advocate representing the High Court, S P Gupta, expressed his client's inability to show the records of the three-judge committee that had recommended Chandra's name.

"We are left with no option but to direct the High Court to produce the reports of the committee in a sealed envelope," the Bench observed. The Bench also said that if the High Court had any objection regarding presenting the records, it should state it along with the report of the committee in sealed envelopes by September 25.

The court would first decide on the objection of the High Court and then open the records, the Bench said.

The Bench also observed that the official website of the High Court showed that Chandra's appointment was made on the ground of his legal service, said Ravi Kiran Jain, counsel of the petitioner.

On September 8, the High Court had demanded committee's record on the consultation process in the appointment of Justice Satish Chandra. The record was produced before the court on September 12. On the same day, the court had demanded the recommendation report of the three-judge committee.

Earlier, a writ petition was filed by a practising lawyer M C Gupta, requesting the court to issue a writ of quo warranto directing Justice Satish Chandra to show the authority of his office and to justify the constitutionality of his appointment.

Heading: Order reserved on CBI chargesheet against home secretary - Indian Express
Content:
The district police arrested six people allegedly for extorting money from coarse sand traders and transporters in Sarojini Nagar on Wednesday.

The accused, disguised as Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) representatives, allegedly collected money from the traders as rent for the land they were using.

Responding to the complaints of local traders, LDA officials and Sarojini Nagar police raided the coarse sand market and arrested Ajay Singh, Lallan Tiwari, Pramod Shukla, Jaichand Yadav, Gopal Yadav and Bablu Yadav.

They have been booked on charges of extortion and forgery.

The LDA officials, however, denied granting permission to any person to recover the rent of the land or any other tax on their behalf.

LDA Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram said: "The accused claim that they had been realising the rent and depositing it with the LDA since 2004. But when asked they failed to produce the documents to corroborate their claims."

The LDA checked its own records and found that no permission was granted to any person for realizing any money from the traders, said Meshram.

The accused, however, produced some receipts of payments from LDA dated 2007. 

"I suspect that a tax inspector of LDA and some other officials were involved. An inquiry headed by a joint secretary has been ordered," said Meshram.

"If involvement of these employees is found, strict action will be taken against them," he added.

Earlier, LDA officials had received complaints of extortion in Sarojini Nagar. This is the first time that they have taken any action.

Heading: Anandsen’s wife accused of murder attempt - Indian Express
Content:
A special court has reserved its decision over taking cognizance of the CBI chargesheet against UP Home Secretary Mahesh Kumar Gupta and three others in a recruitment scam case till September 27.

On Wednesday, the court heard the arguments of both the CBI and defence lawyers.

CBI prosecutor K P Singh said: "We have put each and every detail of the case before the court. We have also given the reasons behind filing the chargesheet against the IAS officer without seeking prosecution sanction. We also cited a 1999 decision of the Supreme Court to support our petition."

Nandit Srivastava, the counsel of home secretary, however, said that the CBI's chargesheet defies directives issued by the Allahabad High Court.

"The court had merely ordered the CBI to conduct an inquiry into the 1998 Information Directorate recruitment and file a report within three months. The court did not give any instruction about filing the chargesheet."

During the last hearing on September 12, the court had asked the CBI to produce the references of the prosecution sanction sought from the Uttar Pradesh government.

"But the CBI merely filed a one-and-half page application citing an apex court order and claiming that no sanction was required for the chargesheet," Srivastava added.

He claimed that prosecution sanction against Gupta was initially sought from the Central government, which had referred it to the state.

"Later, both governments refused to grant the sanction. Moreover, the writ petition that led to the inquiry into the recruitment scam was disposed of in 2006," he said.

On September 9, the Central agency had filed chargesheets against Gupta, two other government officials — Prabhat Sinha and Raj Gopal Singh Verma — and Kanpur-based Akhilesh Shukla.

The government had turned down the request for the prosecution sanction against Gupta, but it has yet to take a decision on Sinha.

The government has, however, allowed prosecution sanction against Verma.

Heading: Power regulators recommend Gujarat model for UP - Indian Express
Content:
Indusen, wife of BSP legislator Anandsen, has been accused of attempting to murder the complainant in the Bhawani Pher murder case.

Pher's son Om Prakash, who is both the main witness and the plaintiff in the case, has alleged in his FIR that Indusen tried to mow him down with her Tata Safari on Tuesday evening.

According to the FIR, the incident took place when Prakash was returning to his village in Milkipur tehsil after attending a hearing. He was on his motorcycle and a security guard was on pillion. He claimed that Indusen, a Block Pramukh of Milkipur Development Block, was driving the Safari and six armed guards were sitting in her vehicle.

Failing to hit his motorcycle, she threatened to kill him if he didn't stay away from the case, said the complaint.

He said he had informed the Faizabad SSP, the Inspector General and Principal Secretary (Home) about the incident. SSP R K S Rathore admitted that it was a serious matter and the police was investigating the matter.

Indusen, however, refuted the charges. "Om has lodged a false case against me," she said.

Her husband and father-in-law, BSP parliamentarian Mitrasen Yadav, are the main accused in the case.

The case is being heard in the court of the additional district judge of Faizabad.

Heading: UP govt official accuses two judges of corruption - Indian Express
Content:
Even before the Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Regulatory Commission (UPSERC) could recommend to the state government ways to check its power transmission and distribution losses — which are the highest in the country — the UPSERC chairman himself has voiced doubts over its success.

"A strong political commitment is required to check power transmission and distribution loses," said Chairman Vijoy Kumar.

"At the same time, to meet the undertaking given to the Prime Minister that all the states will bring down their line loses to 15 per cent by 2012, it is necessary that

Gujarat's experiment be replicated across the country," he added.

Gujarat has bifurcated its rural power supply. It provides domestic consumers round-the-clock power on a single-phase transmission line. It also provides uninterrupted eight-hour power supply to private tubewells for irrigational purposes on a three-phase transmission line. Besides bifurcation of the rural supply, the Gujarat government has installed specially designed transformers which trip whenever a single-phase consumer tries to draw electricity from a three-phased line.

Among the states that face enormous power thefts and line loses, Uttar Pradesh — with its astounding 40 to 45 per cent transmission and distribution losses — tops the charts. It is followed by Jammu and Kashmir, Bihar, Jharkhand and Haryana

To discuss the issue of line loses and power theft in states, the Forum of Indian Regulators had held a meeting in Varanasi last weekend. In the meeting, the members had reached a consensus that every state should follow the Gujarat model for bringing down transmission and distribution loses.

In Uttar Pradesh, UPSCERC is working on a draft of suggestions, which will be submitted to the state government in the next 15 days.

Stating that time was running out, the UPSERC chairman said: "Gujarat has already brought down its losses to 15 per cent. By the end of the 11th Five-Year Plan, it will probably bring it down further to 10 per cent. If the rest of the states do not take any action soon, they will be way behind the scheduled time period."

Uttar Pradesh State Power Consumers Council chief Awdhesh Kumar Verma, however, shared his apprehensions on the state government's willingness to implement the Gujarat model.

"When state authorities have not been able to execute their own model properly, how will they ensure the implementation of the Gujarat Model?" he asked.

Heading: In Kanpur, Ramdev all set to protect Ganga - Indian Express
Content:
An additional district government counsel (ADGC) accused two judges of the Lucknow Session court of corruption and misconduct before mediaperons on Wednesday, inviting the ire of the state government and the bar association.

ADGC Aslam Javed Siddiqui was the prosecutor in the case against Varanasi blast accused Waliullah, from whom explosives and arms were allegedly recovered in Lucknow. On Wednesday, Siddiqui alleged that the two judges had forced him not to file an appeal for acquittal.

District Government Counsel (DGC) R S Dwivedi termed Siddiqui's act as illegal and against the norms laid down for a government counsel. He added: "Siddiqui has also been held responsible for lapses in the court proceedings related in an inquiry conducted by the SP of Rae Bareli."

"On September 4, one of the judges against whom Siddiqui has levelled allegations, had complained against him to me and the principal secretary of the Law department," said Dwivedi. The complaint held Siddiqui responsible for lapses in legal proceedings against a rape accused, following which, the latter was acquitted, the DGC said.

"The government has taken cognizance of the irregularities and he will soon be removed," he added.

The president of the Lucknow Bar Association, C L Dixit, said: "The ADGC had opted for an illegitimate way to show his discontent, as both the judges named by him are of good repute. He could have gone to the district judge or the administrative judge at the High Court. We will hold a meeting at the bar association tomorrow to discuss the issue."

Heading: Micah, Aandrita enter finals, Saurav enthralls - Indian Express
Content:
Yoga guru Swami Ramdev will now play a key role in the campaign to save the Ganga.

In presence of thousands of followers, schoolchildren and prominent politicians, Ramdev started the Aviral Ganga-Nirmal Ganga campaign of Ganga Raksha Manch from Sarsaiyya Ghat on Wednesday evening.

On the occasion, Ramdev demanded that the river be accorded the heritage status and declare polluting of the river a heinous crime.

According to the Yoga Guru, "If the Taj Mahal can be declared as a national heritage, then why not River Ganga?" The holy river has a special meaning for every Indian; therefore it should be ensured that it is not polluted, said Ramdev.

As the maximum pollution of the river is being carried out from Kanpur, the city has been chosen as the starting point of the campaign.

"The large scale pollution of the river is a collective failure, and no single political party should be held responsible," said Ramdev.

The Yoga Guru also took the opportunity to laud former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi for initiating the Ganga Action Plan.

Ramdev claimed that political parties across the board are united in their efforts to keep the river clean. "We have already met several senior politicians, who have been quick to extend their support to our campaign," he said.

Appreciating the efforts of the spiritual guru, Union Minister of State for Home, Shriprakash Jaiswal extended his support to the campaign. "I will make all the efforts required to keep the river clean and free of pollution."

In the flow, Mayor Ravindra Patni also announced a package of Rs 60 lakh for the cleanliness drive of the river in Kanpur. Patni said, "At the same time, we expect some co-operation from the people's end, as the fate of the project lies in their hands."

Heading: Dressing it Up - Indian Express
Content:
Micah Muhury and Aandrita Deb stormed into the finals of the Ladies' Open Singles at the Calcutta Hard Court Tennis Championship 2008 organised by Calcutta South Club. Micah Muhury defeated Ishani Mukherjee 6-2,6-0 while Aandrita got the better of Andrea Das 6-1,6-1.

In the Men's Open Singles Wild Card Saurav Panja ousted the fourth seed Robin Das 6-1,6-3. Manoj Kumar Sewa, Vinod Kumar Sewa and Harshvardhan Thirani are the other players to make it to the semi finals of this event.

Today's results: Men's Open Singles Quarter Finals: Manoj Kumar Sewa (1) beat Prem Singh (Q) 6-3,6-4; Harshvardhan Singh Thirani (3) beat Ajay Singh 4-6,6-1,6-2; Saurav Panja (WC) beat Robin Das (4) 6-1,6-3;Vinod Kumar Sewa (2) beat Baibhav Das 6-0,6-3.

Men's Open Doubles Quarter Finals: Robin Das & Ram Kumar beat Debashish Hait & Asho Kumar Prasad 6-3,6-2; Manoj Kumar Sewa & Saurav Panja beat Bhagirath Kumar & Prem Singh 6-1,6-2.

Ladies' Open Singles Semi Finals: Micah Muhury (Jha) beat Ishani Mukherjee 6-2,6-0; Aandrita Deb beat Andrea Das (2) 6-1,6-1.

Boys' Singles Under 14 Pre Quarter Finals (Best of 13 Games): Rahul Agarwal beat Rohan Deb 7-4;

Girls' Singles Under 12 Quarter Finals (Best of 13 Games): Priyam Periwal beat Priya Ghosh 7-3; Shreya Das beat Shweta Sen 7-1; Shiuli Dasgupta (3) beat Aishwarya Kundu 7-3; Neha Prasad beat Marium Javed 7-1.

Girls' Singles Under 14 Pre Quarter Finals (Best of 13 Games): Shuvangi Sen Chowdhury beat Aparajita Mullick 7-5.

Men's Handicap Singles Semi Finals ; Farid Alam beat Ashray Bhasin 6-2,6-2.

Heading: Streetwise - Indian Express
Content:
Chiffons and velvet sarees, digital printed kurtis, skirts that double up as sarees — city's designer brigade is lining up an unusual collection this Pujo

As old as the tradition of pujos may be, there is one thing that keeps changing every year— fashion trends. Some things like the traditional Bengali tant may be the eternal fashion symbol, but for the fashion-conscious youth of today, it's not enough. Most want something that can be traditional enough to be worn to a pandal but also funky enough to be worn to the pub. Agrees Kolkata-based designer Vivek Kumar, "Youngsters today want something that can serve a dual purpose and to meet such demands the spaghetti dresses are perfect." For the uninitiated, he explains the concept behind the spaghetti dresses— something that is a combination of the western sensibilities as well as the eastern, a dress that can double up as a kurta and can be worn over a churidar or patiala. Perfect for the demure look that woman prefer for pandal hopping and the western look that they favour for nights out.

Nets, claims Kumar will be big this year but it will not be the sheer variety, rather, he emphasises, that foil printing and bold prints on them are what will turn heads. Kumar is not the only one swearing by prints on dresses, even Abhishekh Dutta feels that nothing is more fashionable than digital prints on t-shirts, men's shirts and even kurtis. "And if you want to be different I suggest embellishing the prints with some embroidery. I am still partial towards the tunics this season that can be worn with leggings or without it. Team it up with a colourful stole. One thing that is so last season are the kalidaar kurtis that have been done to death," feels Dutta. But most surprising this pujos is the gowns that are making a come back in fashionable wardrobes.

Agnimitra Paul's pujo collection has been partial towards the gowns that she calls 'murmur ke na dekh'. Her black velvet gowns will have Indian motifs in front and colourful layered texture at the back. "Velvet is really big this year and even my sarees will have a touch of them along with chiffons and net. The sarees will have velvet in the upper portion, chiffon in the lower portion with chiffon sarees," says Paul.

But for those who like to keep it simple, georgette sarees in muted tones are still in vogue, feels Pali Sachdev of the Monapali duo. "More than the pujos, what we have kept in mind while designing the collection is the autumn season that is neither too hot nor cold. So warm tones are what will rule as far as colours go," says Sachdev. Their collection also has a lot of salwars and patialas that can be worn with short kurtis. Certainly no spaghettis, their collection is for those who like to keep it simple yet elegant.

The best news however, is for those who dreads draping the nine-yard cloth, designers have invented the readymade sarees that can be worn as skirts with the pallu and pleats pinned on top to make them look like traditional sarees. "People like to wear traditional attires during the festive season but today's generation are not very comfortable in sarees, this is the perfect alternative, intended to keep everybody happy," says Dutta.

Heading: Karim focuses on youth-senior blend for I-League - Indian Express
Content:
Skinny ties, sheer shirts, fish cut lehengas and zardozi belts. When it comes to street fashion this pujo, it's bling all the way

HIS
The influence of Bollywood on pujo fashion has been there since the time of Shammi Kapoor and Jeetendra, when the Panchus and Tutuns of the para queued up at the local darzi's to get their drainpipe trousers (which considerably reduced the ease with which they boarded buses), until Amitabh Bachchan decided to give them a break with bell-bottoms.

The modern-day Panchus and Tutuns however, will sacrifice their freedom of movement to keep abreast with the latest fashion trends this pujo. "Skinny jeans are in. Most young men are opting for these tight fitting jeans. They look very much like the drainpipe trousers that Jeetendra sported in his early films ," says Bilal of Icon (Shreeram Arcade). When you go pandal hopping this pujo, you will be well advised to expect an explosion of Shahid Kapoor wannabes at every possible hotspot of the city. The Kismat Konnection star's waistcoat and skinny tie look in the film seems to be a great hit with young men of the city. "The waistcoats come in different materials-silk, lycra, satin and leather. They are priced in the Rs 600-Rs 1500 bracket," informs Bilal. The skinny ties which come in funky prints and colours, will set you back by Rs 150, or lesser, if you have a talent for bargaining.

One is also likely to spot a riot of shiny colours on the backs of many youngsters this pujo- fitted, lycra shirt with blazing stripes of different colours are "in this season". Shipped from the Mecca of low-end fashion, Bangkok, these shirts are sure to make you look hot, literally. "Since they are imported from Bangkok, the prices are a bit steep. The range starts from Rs 695," says a representative of Bhagwati Fashions, Shreeram Arcade.

The other fashion idol this pujo is Akshay Kumar with his Latin-trash look in the popular reality show, Khatron Ke Khiladi. Distress jeans teamed with fitted t-shirts and a gamcha like scarf casually warped around the neck. If you are an Akshay Kumar fan you are most like to don this look. Never mind the muggy Kolkata heat. One can pick up such scarves from the Firangi Bazaar in New Market for Rs 100 or less.

Accessorizing for men this season will mean faking it with faux tattoo bands. "These are innovations if you don't want a permanent tattoo. They are skin-coloured with various motifs drawn on them. They shouldn't cost you more than Rs 100, " says Kabir Khan, who mans a stall which specializes in men's accessories near the Indian Museum. Mismatched flip-flops with graphic prints and metal waistbands , will complete the trashy look.

HERS
The day Ekta Kapoor decided to walk off our living rooms for a very invigorating walk past brusque and not-very-kind aunties loaded with shopping bags and committed to using the elbow on the living and non-living alike, she would be a happy woman. Because she would probably be at some shopping hub that had dressed up generations of Pujo revellers in bling, Bollywood, and the crazy brand of Guccis goofed up in the tail. In fact, she would have the wardrobe for some 10 serials to come. While we would know what to expect off pandal-hoppers this year.

To start with you have zardosi belts. At the several belt-and-watches shop that line Dharmatala, select shops have stocked up on these bling belts that seem straight out of the goddess' couture. For ninety rupees and some haggling, there's divinity in several colours (read gold, silver, blue and lilac) literally under your belt.

And bling is the word too for the girls it seems this year. At Dulhan at Shreeram Arcade, a shop that specialises in Indian wear, fish cut lehengas seem to be the flavour of the season. Richly embroidered with a generous use to zardosi, sequins, stones, beads and multiple colour panels, these heavy mirror work lehengas can come to you for less than a thousand rupees even. "Though the prices can go up to Rs 10,000 the costlier ones are usually bridal stuff. But these are not meant for pandal hoppers. Rather, people who have pujos at home, prefer to deck up and stay back," says Kishar Makhwana of Dulhan.

Now with all that glitter off the pandals then, one has to turn to the Armanis, the Kolkata way, of course that are jazzing up shops now, and are most likely to leave a trail of broken hearts, blinded gazes on its way. If the purple scooped neck, sequined lycra gown at Ishtyle (Shreeram Arcade) would leave hearts aflutter with the long side slit, the white and lavender net gown at another corner would well make for a Goa-meets-80's Bollywood wedding in the middle of Maddox Square. For the less adventurous, there are K-serial staples — like a black crochet gown black or a flesh coloured-sequined off-shoulder number at Spice Girls.

So, how does the Bengali bhadralok take in the culture shock of audacious, irreverent shoulders, sleeves, necklines and slits? "The price range is such that it caters to the middle class. Most families can afford to shell out Rs 800-Rs 1000 for a fancy gown," says Sarfaraz of Spice Girls. And spending they are and how. "Why do you think we have stocked these. The last stock has already sold out," adds Sarfaraz. And so for the not-very-adventurous Dad, there's an antidote at hand —feather stoles. From the small thicker ones in blacks and blues to the slimmer, longer varieties in a riot of colours, the backstreets of fashion have the safety bands for anything between Rs 100-150. And if you have been cribbing that all that has not travelled over the seas to be haute enough, think again. It's Bangkok and China that seems to have Kolkata in their bling bags this year.

However, the clincher should be the Sania Salwar suit. Inspired from her shorts, the suit takes the way around her fatwas, to create a low-waist suit, with a flaring layered skirt bottom. "It's like combining her long tees and cute skirts and shorts on court for a salwar suit," says N K Bansal of Her Choice.

Heading: Man strangulates wife to death - Indian Express
Content:
Buoyed by success of young guns in the Premier Division, Mohun Bagan coach looking to try out similar focus in national meet

He is one of the few coaches in the Indian football scenario over the past couple of years to have religiously focused on working away at his club's youth development programme, what if it put added pressure on him for his role as the club's senior team coach. For Karim Bencherifa, it's become a trademark these days to work simultaneously on the young-driven feeder line as well as Mohun Bagan club's senior players.

Bencherifa tasted his first success with his the dual-focus technique with Churchill Brothers. And he then tried it out with Bagan in the just concluded Premier Division. The team's blend of youth and seniors stood out as Bencherifa's outfit took the title ahead of stalwarts East Bengal and Mohammedan Sporting.

After the successful city league campaign, Bagan are now eagerly waiting for the all-important I-League, which begins in 10 days' time. Says Bencherifa: "All the youngsters who participated in at least one match in the Premier Division have technically qualified for the I-League also, which is a big thing. But as things stand, opportunities will be hard to come by for these youngsters. But I promise, the junior players who were consistent in the Premier Division here can be seen in action in the I-League. There was criticism over the recruitment of several young players before the star of the season. Some of the critics doubted if the youngsters would click in the city league. Today, I am happy with the boys' tremendous response."

Elaborating on the youth development programme, the Moroccan coach told The Indian Express that he was particularly excited over the return of popular junior India international Branco Cordozo for the I-League. Branco, after playing a couple of matches in the begining of the Kolkata league, was forced out of action by a hamstring injury. "He was unfortunate that he couldn't prove his mettle in the city league due to the injury. He is expected to be back for the I-League, and obviously has increased his fitness level. I think he will be totally ready from the second week of the I-League onwards."

The Mohun Bagan seniors are resuming their five-day residential training programme at a five-star Kolkata hotel starting Friday. Under the watchful eyes of Bencherifa, the team will train at the its home ground and also at the Barasat Stadium, which is one of the venues of the I-league.

On the issue of foreign players, Bencherifa wants to go slow. After the two foreigners failed impress last week, he now wants to start the I-League with the duo of Jose Barreto and Peter Odafa. Two more foreign players will appear for trials here next week.

Heading: CU in a fix over environment science paper - Indian Express
Content:
A 30-year-old man, Soumen Sarkar, strangulated his wife to death in the presence of their two children late on Tuesday night. After committing the crime, he went to the Tiljala police station and made a voluntary confession.

The children, aged between seven to nine years, will be making an in-camera confession before the magistrate in Alipore court.

Sarkar lived with his wife and two children at a rented house in Nonapukuri. He was originally from North 24 Parganas.

According to the police, Sarkar suspected his wife of having an illicit relationship, which caused regular fights between the couple. On Tuesday night, he strangulated his wife Astami (22), in the same room where the children were sleeping.

Dispute between the couple could have also arose due to financial problems, as Sarkar worked as a plumber and got a meagre salary of Rs 5,000, said a police officer.

Locals admitted that there were regular quarrels between the couple. "We never knew that the quarrels could lead to such an end," said a neighbour.

Sarkar was produced in Alipur court and was remanded to police custody. The two children have confessed that they saw their mother being murdered by their father, said sources.

Heading: Buddha blows Ramadoss request away with smoke - Indian Express
Content:
The Calcutta University (CU) is yet to decide who will conduct the examination of Environmental Science (EVS), even as months have passed since the academic session began this year. The university has also not figured out the number of unit tests that it would conduct in an academic year.

So, the university authorities have now asked various colleges across the state to give their suggestions on these two issues by September 30.

Earlier, the university had received a letter from the University Grants Commission (UGC) in which the latter had directed the CU to follow the six-month module of Environmental Science and increase the weightage of the paper from 50 to 100 marks. The commission had also warned the university that if it fails to do so then it will forward the matter to the ministry and stop the payment of the grant earmarked for the university.

Speaking at a workshop organised by the undergraduate council of the university, CU vice-chancellor Suranjan Das described UGC's order as a "fatwa" and added that it will have to follow it.

Reeling under pressure of conducting examinations of over 1 lakh students, CU is trying to put the burden on the respective colleges for conducting the Environmental Science examination. Sceptics, however, say that it will dilute the academic standards if the colleges hold the tests.

"If there is no urgency, the university can wait for some time before raising the marks for EVS to 100," said Biplab Chatterjee, secretary of the West Bengal Principals' Association. "There are instances when teachers of Bengali subject are teaching Environmental Science. Since the student-teacher ratio is very high, it will put a burden on the college infrastructure to hold the EVS examination," said Tarun Patra, general secretary of West Bengal College University Teachers Association.

In this situation the university can have a multiple choice question (MCQ) pattern which can be answered on an optical mark reader and can be checked electronically by the respective colleges, said Patra. Officials of the university are also considering this as an option, as it would lessen the burden on colleges as well as the universities.

On the issue of a number of unit tests, the university is also in a dilemma. With the decision of having four class tests in a session, the students are losing out about 40 teaching days. However, CU has a system of continuous comprehensive evaluation for teachers.

"The number of teaching days has been reduced in certain colleges instead of getting increased in the (1+1+1) system. The university is required to have a minimum of 180 days in an academic year," said Srutinath Prohraj, a syndicate member of the university.

Heading: Buddha now appeals to Mamata’s ‘conscience’ - Indian Express
Content:
Shah Rukh Khan might be embarrassed about his smoking habit and meekly admit so in face of the regular onslaught from Union Health Minister Anbumani Ramadoss.

But not so Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee.

A day after Ramadoss admitted to sending a letter to the chief minister asking him to kick the butt, Bhattacharjee kept his perfect nonchalance in the face of amused media queries. And his officials flatly denied that the incident ever took place.

On Wednesday, Bhattacharjee refused to comment when reporters, at the fag end of a media conference, asked him about Ramadoss's letter.

"No comments," was all he said and got up, ending the press meet on Singur issue abruptly. And as he was about to leave, he turned back and quipped: "I am now concerned with cars."

Officials in the Writers' Buildings denied that the chief minister got any mail from Ramadoss.

"The CM has not received any such letter. Moreover, smoking is not a big issue either," an official told The Indian Express.

Environmentalists, though, rallied behind Ramadoss, alleging that the chief minister has a habit of flouting environment laws.

"The chief minister is spoiling his health. And he smokes at the Writers' Buildings, which has been declared a no-smoking zone by his government," said environmentalist Subhas Dutta.

Heading: Cong froths over Subrata visit to rally - Indian Express
Content:
With Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee renewing her threat of a fresh agitation after she meets the Governor on his return to Kolkata after September 19, Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee on Wednesday appealed to her once again to help restore the atmosphere for resumption of work at the Tata Motors plant in Singur.

"The Tatas are anxiously waiting to come back. The situation has improved, but it needs to be better before they resume operations. The commerce department officers and I are in touch with the Tatas," said Bhattacharjee. "I will appeal to her conscience. I will request her to be realistic in finding a solution. It's not a question of the Tatas or the Birlas, nor of the Rs 1 lakh car or Rs 5 lakh car. I am concerned because the project involves huge employment potential; it will benefit our state," he added.

Asked if he had spoken to Ratan Tata, the CM said: "Of course, even yesterday we had a talk. They are anxious to be back, but a congenial atmosphere is yet to be restored. We have lost nearly one month of work."

On her part, talking to the media on Wednesday evening, Mamata said the government has broken its promise. She even sought Central intervention.

"If the state government does not give credence to the agreement made in the presence of the constitutional head, it is a case of violation of the Constitution and it is time that the Centre steps in," she said. "We will continue our peaceful agitation."

Replying to Mamata's charge, Bhattacharjee said: "The government and the protestors' representatives could not agree. The government has gone to the maximum limit to offer 70 acres. It cannot go further. Going beyond this would imply that the factory would not come up."

Heading: Gorkha League slams GJM for unleashing terror - Indian Express
Content:
Congress leader and former mayor Subrata Mukherjee's visit to Mamata Banerjee's rally has the state Congress in a turmoil.

Mukherjee had gone to the rally as a mark of protest against the growing importance of Deepa Dasmunsi, wife of WBPCC president Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi, said a party source.

"When I came to know that he (Mukherjee) was going to attend the rally, I immediately informed Dasmunsi. He did not approve of this act," said Deepa Dasmunsi. The partymen, too, she said, had not approved of Mukherjee's act.

Mukherjee, on the other hand, maintained that he has done nothing wrong. "I thought that everyone should support this issue. I do not think I have done anything wrong by going there," he said.

Sources in the Congress said this is not the first time party leaders have been undermined by Deepa Dasmunsi.

"One of the major reasons for Somen Mitra leaving the Congress was her growing importance as the state party chief's wife," said one of the leaders. Many have started speculating when Subrata Mukherjee, too, will leave the Congress.

Mukherjee, a former Trinamool leader, had left just before the KMC elections in 2005.

He is known to be close to Dasmunsi, which is why many wonder if any punitive action will be taken against him.

Heading: Govt to distribute computers at 200 madrasas - Indian Express
Content:
The All India Gorkha League — the oldest Gorkha party that was formed in 1943 — has accused the Gorkha Janamukti Morcha of employing strong-arm tactics. Considered to be the most outspoken voice of Darjeeling, the League's president Madan Tamang said the GJM's bullying tactics have pushed his party into political oblivion.

"We wanted to hold a rally two months ago, but couldn't because the GJM activists had threatened our members," he said.

He further added, "The Morcha cadres are coercing and intimidating the masses. It's almost like the era of the Gorkha National Liberation Front, when my house was set on fire." After being pushed out of the Gorkhaland politics in 1980s by the Subhas Ghising-led GNLF, the League had hoped to regain its base after Ghising's downfall. But the GJM recent violent protest had taken the centre stage, pushing the League again to the periphery.

After participating in the tripartite talks involving the Centre and the West Bengal government in New Delhi, the GJM leaders are now organising several public meetings in the Hills to garner support for its movement.

Tamang, however, dismissed the tripartite talks by terming it nonsense. He claimed that the government had given undue importance to both the GNLF and the GJM. "Earlier, the government allowed Ghising to indulge in corruption while running the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council. Now, Gurung has come to the fore," he said.

The demand for a separate Gorkhaland, claimed Tamang, was first raised in 1980s under the auspices of the League by the Prantha Parishad, of which he was a founding member. "Our League became the victim of politics and we were marginalised by the Bengali community," he said.

He accused the state of ignoring the aspirations of the local residents. "The Municipal elections haven't been held here in the last 14 years and the DGHC elections in eight years."

While he admitted that the demand for a separate state was legitimate, he rejected the methods adopted for it by the Morcha. "The GJM's ongoing non-cooperation movement is extremely selective. While the GJM has rejected several initiatives of the government, the Morcha continue to follow the Bengal Municipal Act, the DGHC Act and the Panchayat Act."

He claimed that the administration is losing nearly Rs 10 crore of revenue per month due to the Morcha's tactics,. "Yet, the government does not involve other parties in the talks and concentrates only on the GJM," said Tamang.

Heading: Civic bodies unaffected as Jadavpur continues to grapple with enteric - Indian Express
Content:
The state minority affairs and madrasa education department (MAMED) has decided to introduce computer education for madrasa students, in collaboration with the state information technology department.

Initially, 200 madrasa schools will be given computers for educational purposes, with the facility being extended later.

A notification to this effect was issued by the MAMED recently. The main aim of the policy is to bring these students at par with other convent-educated students.

At present, only a handful of the madrasa schools in the state have computer facilities. The notification also mentioned sorting out all issues relating to computer education in madrasas. A six-member expert committee has also been constituted, which will submit its proposal to the government very soon.

The team of experts comprises professors from Jadavpur University, Calcutta University, Bengal Engineering and Science University's (BESU) information and technology school, besides one representative each from the state IT department and the madrasa education board.

"The government approached us to work on issues like what methodology needs to be used, what should be the syllabus for computer studies, who will be the teachers and how they should be trained. We have already had our first meeting and by next week we should be able to give a proposal to the board," said Professor Nandini Mukherjee, computer science department, Jadavpur University, who is also one of the committee members.

The main objective of the committee is to decide on the technical specifications (both hardware and software), instructor's qualifications, teaching methodologies, curricula, monitoring and supervision system that needs to be implemented.

"There has been a need to integrate the students of these madrasas into the mainstream. In today's age, computer education is a must, without which one may lag behind in the race for good jobs," said another committee member, Professor Hafizur Rahaman, School of IT, BESU.

As per the notification issued, the committee's work will also consist of selecting an agency, which will supply hardware and software, provide qualified instructors and related services for the 200 madrasas. The committee will have to follow the usual government procedure for selection of the agency through an open two-bid process.

With a lot of madrasas having Bengali as the medium of instruction, some of the committee members propose that the computers might have the option of both English and Bengali language software.

"We might be using the new Linux software which enables Bengali to be used in computers," said Rahaman.

According to Professor Sankar Sen, former vice-chancellor of Jadavpur University, who is also the chairman of the committee, the software used in the computers might be open software, which — unlike Microsoft Windows — does not require license money.

"We are thinking about making computer education compulsory for students from Class V to VIII, while making it optional for Class IX to XII," said Sen.

Every student needs to have an idea of computers no matter in which field they will work at the end.

"The government has asked us to come up with the framework and the entire process is at a preliminary stage. We hope to complete the mission by May 2009, before the new session begins," he added.

Heading: Inmate dies, security lapses exposed - Indian Express
Content:
The water contamination followed by an acute enteric outbreak in Jadavpur — which affected hundreds of people — has failed to rouse the Kolkata Environment Improvement Project (KEIP) into taking preventive measures to check further contamination in the area.

At present, KEIP — the nodal agency of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) — is laying a drainage pipe beside a nullah that carries the liquid waste of the enteric-affected area. The entreric outbreak had originated after a breach in water pipe — which occurred as the KEIP was at work laying water pipes.

Surprisingly, the agency seems not to have learnt from its mistake, and is not taking any precautions to protect the existing supply line from contamination. The work is being executed by contract labours, who are unaware of the risks of water contamination, and there is no supervision by any KEIP official or contractor.

"We are scared of using tapwater and are forced to buy mineral water for drinking purposes," said Sanjeev Mondal, a resident of Ward number 101, one of the affected areas.

The civic authorities, too, seem to be taking the situation lightly.

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya said: "In reality, no precautions can be taken while carrying out the underground project work. We have discussed the issue with our engineers but no solution has emerged. Moreover, it is not always possible for the KMC or the KEIP officials to supervise the work of the contractors. At the most, we can only prepare our departments to act promptly, if any contamination is reported again."

Although the KMC records say not more than 600 people have been affected by enteric diseases, the NGOs working in the area have claimed that the count has exceeded 800. Most of the patients have been sent to Beliaghata ID Hospital and Baghajatin State General Hospital, where some of them are still undergoing treatment.

"We received many patients from the area. Some of them have been referred to the hospital by the KMC health camp and some came to us directly. Some patients, suffering from blood dysentery, were in typically bad condition, but they are recovering gradually," said M Ghosh, principal, Beliaghata ID Hospital.

Adding to the woes of the people, the KMC also withdrew the health camp on Wednesday, even though the enteric-affected locals are still dependent on the camp.

"The condition has improved. So we have decided to remove the health camp," said Chandana Ghosh Dastidar, the local councillor, by way of explanation. According to KMC records, no enteric-affected patient was registered on Tuesday.

A health official at the camp, however, confirmed that at least 20 patients came on Tuesday.

Heading: Rains, tidal waves hit coastal Bengal: one dead, hundreds affected - Indian Express
Content:
On Wednesday, Mohammed Azharuddin, an inmate of the Presidency Central Jail in Kolkata, succumbed to his injuries that he had suffered in a clash between jail inmates and prison guards on Tuesday. Jail sources said nearly 40 inmates and 30 guards were injured in the clash.

Inspector General of Police B D Sharma visited the jail after his death. Deputy Inspector General of Police (Prison) S R Hussain said: "Azharuddin died in the jail hospital. The clash had taken place, when a group of jailbirds resisted the transfer of notorious gangster Zafar Siddiqui alias Gudda from the jail to the Dum Dum Central Jail."

Jail sources said Azharuddin, an associate of Gudda, was among the 40 inmates, who had attacked the guards with razors and blades. The guards, in turn, attacked the prisoners with batons that hit Azharuddin on the head.

Jail sources said Gudda had slashed his stomach and hand with a blade to prevent his transfer from the jail. He is now undergoing treatment in the jail hospital and his transfer has been postponed till he is discharged from the hospital.

Asked as to how the inmates got hold of razors and blades, Hussain said, "The IG prison himself is probing the matter."

Jail Minister Biswanath Choudhury said: "We have ordered an inquiry into the incident and action will be taken against the guilty. I have discussed with the chief minister the need to constitute a special combat force to check untoward incidents in jails."

He also admitted that the Presidency jail guards had applied force to control the inmates on Tuesday.

Hussain said, "We are investigating if any foul play had led to Azharuddin's death. His body has been sent for postmortem."

The incident has also exposed the growing irregularities in the jail management. A few days ago, a SIM card was recovered from Gudda's ward.

An officer of the jail said: "Besides razors and blades, the gang members had also sneaked in a firearm in the jail and were extorting money from other inmates. Search is on for the firearm."

Jail authorities also informed that in March, a gang war had broken out in the jail, in which Gudda was involved and thereafter a decision was taken to shift him to the Dum Dum Central Jail. But Gudda had refused to leave the Presidency jail.

The incident also highlighted the lack of preparedness of the state jail administration to control the rowdy inmates. The jail guards are not adequately trained and have no modern equipment to control the crowd.

Heading: HC says remove hawkers, municipal corporation blinks - Indian Express
Content:
One fisherman was swept away and around 250 others went missing as high tidal waves hit the coastal belt of Digha, Shankarpur and Contai on Tuesday night. Heavy rains, caused by a deep depression over Bay of Bengal, also lashed large parts of South Bengal, causing major damage in the area, official sources said.

Government officials said the worst hit areas are North and South 24 Parganas, East Midnapore, Howrah and Hooghly. An alert has been issued in the coastal areas in view of the situation.

The authorities, meanwhile, are yet to track down 15 trawlers with around 250 fishermen, who went missing in the sea. "The tidal waves have damaged sea walls at Khejuri, Shankarpur, Contai, Ramnagar, Egra, Nandigram 1 and other areas along the coastline. We are taking all possible measure to provide relief to the affected people," Sreekumar Chakraborty, Additional District Magistrate (general) said.

At least 20 villages spread over an area of 64 kilometres along the East Midnapore coastline were flooded when 15-foot high tidal waves hit them on Tuesday night. The waves also washed away 100 make-shift eateries along the coast at Digha, an official said.

More than 20,000 people had to be sheltered in 11 relief camps set up in the worst affected Ramnagar blocks 1 and 2 and Khejuri block 2.

Incessant rains also lashed parts of Sunderbans, breaching embankments at various spots. In North and South 24 Parganas, rains and tidal waves flooded Sandeshkhali 1 and 2 blocks, Minakha, Hasnabad, Bashirhat, Hingalgunj and other areas. Over 500 people in Mousumi Island, Kakdweep and Patharpratima have been affected by the waves.

Heading: Afghan women’s paintings to showcase hope amid despair - Indian Express
Content:
After four days of the High Court's directive to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) to prepare an action plan for evicting hawkers from the city pavements, the civic body denies that it has received any directive.

Mayor Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya said, "We have not got any order from the High Court regarding the issue. Discussions are on with hawkers' unions and the Kolkata Police. But no solution has come out yet."

Hawkers have again come up in the Park Street area, where the KMC and the Kolkata Police had jointly carried out an eviction drive a few days ago. Nisar Ahmed, Officer-in-Charge Park Street Police station, said: "Though there is no permanent structure on the stretch where the eviction drive was carried out, some hawkers are still there."

The civic body had earlier declared that an eviction drive would be carried out on the entire stretch facing the heritage buildings, starting from the Park Street Metro station to the Museum. While the pavements in front of the heritage buildings have been declared as "no-hawking zone" by the civic body, the pavements near the Indian Museum and the Asiatic Society are still being used by the hawkers.

Bhattacharya said, "We are planning to carry out an eviction drive in the area soon."

Heading: Politics scuttles promo plan for Youth Games - Indian Express
Content:
Sara Nabil may just be 13, but the artist in her defies her age and portrays a mature perspective towards political and social issues. A member of the Centre for Contemporary Arts — Afghanistan (CCAA) 2006, Nabil is one of the 19 young Afghan women whose works will be showcased at the Rabindranath Tagore Centre — the Kolkata chapter of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).

"I have lost many things during the era of war and misery... I have portrayed in my paintings Afghanistan's political problems and situations, while being reflective about cross-border politics at the international level," Nabil writes philosophically in the catalogue published by the ICCR.

The exhibition, which will be held in Kolkata from September 19 to September 27, is the first independent art exhibition of Afghan women in the art history of Afghanistan. All the participants are members of CCAA, and are either school students, graduates or students pursuing formal training in Fine Arts. And although the women would not be present during the exhibition, they are happy that their pictorial depictions of Afghanistan will reach an audience beyond the borders of their nation.

The catalogue, which is a curtainraiser to the exhibition, has quoted the Director of CCAA, Rahraw Omarzad, as saying: "Representational art is more under criticism in the Islamic countries. The extremists are looking for an excuse to ban pictorial arts for once and all, since representational art embodies human forms and figures of living creatures. They think this concept contradicts the Islamic beliefs. In this case, the new symbolic and unrealistic paintings have more chance of acceptance in Islamic societies."

The exhibition aims at focusing on women's life in Afghanistan, and the miseries that have befallen them in the trouble-torn land. Twenty-eight-year-old artist Jahan Ara Rafi voices the feelings of an entire generation of women when she says she has only suffered from one thing in her life — the lack of real freedom.

"Unfortunately, this society has never been able to define the meaning of freedom to me. Based on this, most of my works have colours of this deprivation," Rafi writes.

This deprivation is something that manifests itself in the paintings of other women too. While the social and political turmoil of their homeland remains the backdrop of the paintings of these women, there is also a glimmer of hope shining through the dark representations. As 21-year-old artist Fareeha Ghezal says: "Hope is vital for living. So, I love to portray hope and light in my works".

Heading: Bulb of an idea: More subsidy, better storage, cheaper onions - Indian Express
Content:
Sena, NCP join hands with BJP to shelve Rs 20-cr project, Congress fumes

Controversy has rocked the Commonwealth Youth Games (CYG) with only 25 days to go for the October 12 start. A Rs 19.5-crore promotional plan for the event has gone into the freezer, with the ruling NCP-Shiv Sena joining hands with the opposition BJP in the standing committee to scuttle it.

The civic administration had proposed sanctioning of funds for cultural programmes during the youth baton relay and after, promotional hoardings, special mobile vans for publicity and advertisements in the media. The Congress was left fuming as three parties - NCP, Shiv Sena and BJP - opposed the proposal saying that it was a waste of public money.

Congress corporators alleged the opposition to the promo plans had a political motive. Even though Congress found support from the sole member of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), other parties came together and decided to shelve it.

Later, talking to reporters, Congress corporator Ulhas Bagul said, "This decision by the standing committee does not augur well for the image of the city. While the youth baton relay has been receiving a warm welcome in other parts of the country, Pune will not be able to do so, thanks to the politically motivated decision of the ruling alliance with support from the opposition."

Anil Bhosale of the NCP said there was no political motive behind this decision. "The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has spent a lot of money for the development of infrastructure projects in view of the CYG. In fact, the PMC is also constructing roads in Mhalunge village just for CYG, even though it does not fall within PMC limits. Besides, the PMC has already embarked upon the beautification of the city for the CYG," he said.

The PMC had tabled the proposal in response to a request made by the additional director general of the Games requesting the former to jointly promote the CYG event. The BJP, had however, came out in opposition of this proposal saying that it was not the PMC's job to do so.

Standing committee chairman and Shiv Sena leader Shyam Deshpande said, "We are not opposing this proposal just because the Congress had opposed a proposal for a special purpose vehicle (SPV) for various projects."

The ruling alliance has approved the proposal to set up the SPV - to be named Pune Municipal Infrastructure Development Corporation (PMIDC) - to carry out development work worth Rs 24,000 crore. A subsidiary under full control of the PMC, the company, being set up at Rs 125 crore, will implement various infrastructure development projects including Metro rail, monorail, flyovers and so on. It will have a 12-member governing council including five elected representatives.

Heading: Brace for Kosi all over: City study - Indian Express
Content:
It is a bid to stabilise the perpetually fluctuating price line for onions and will benefit at least 5,000 farmers from Pune district, the third largest producer of onions in a state that accounts for 30 per cent of the national production.

The Maharashtra State Agriculture Marketing Board (MSAMB) has proposed an onion storage scheme with a subsidy component of Rs 1,500, up from Rs 500. Farmers are now being encouraged to improve their storage capacity with the help of the designs and scientific method provided by the Pune-based National Research Centre for Onion and Garlic (NRCOG). With a target of 13,000 tonnes for the coming year, the board has sought Rs 1.95 crore as subsidy to increase the storage for Pune district.

"This will prevent the usual trend between June and September, when the price per quintal goes up to Rs 1,000 from Rs 200-Rs 300," said project manager DM Sable of MSAMB.

The new scheme is looking at increasing the storage capacity from 3 lakh tonnes to 8 lakh tonnes in the state. The model looks at a larger aereated space, with subsidy sought under the central government's National Agriculture Development Project (NADP) for storage of one lakh metric tonnes of onion in the state.

The subsidy for construction of the facility has been put at Rs 6,000 per metric tonne capacity, with 25 per cent being given to the farmers at Rs 1,500 for each farmer. The scientific model looks at storage units built with bamboo and wooden sticks — their weight ranging from five to 50 tonnes, height seven feet and width four feet — wherein onion can be stored up to a height of five feet. With the NRCOG model, the farmers stand to face only losses of 5-10 per cent as against the usual 25-30 per cent, said Sable.

Heading: Ration card in CM name: Official, clerk suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Kosi may not be the end of the story; in fact, it may be just the beginning. According to research by a team at the University of Pune (UoP) and at the College of Military Engineering (CME), there has been an increase in the number of 'high altitude flood events' in the four Himalayan rivers of Sutlej, Chenab, Beas and Ravi in the last 40 years.

A high-altitude flood event happens when river flow at a particular point exceeds its average. This could portend more floods in the areas in the vicinity of these rivers.

Dr MR Bhutiyani, scientist at the DRDO now on deputation to CME, Dr NJ Pawar and Professor Vishwas Kale of UoP studied changing river patterns in the northwestern Himalayas and published their findings in the September issue of Current Science.

Glaciers have receded over the past four decades in both the Ravi and the Beas, reducing the contribution of snow and glacier and making the rivers largely monsoon-fed. Given the vagaries of the monsoon, there is a further change in flow patterns.

"The main reason is global warming, to which glaciers react immediately. Glaciers act as natural regulators of floods and that is not happening because of their near absence.

"The discharge in the rivers is now based totally on the monsoon, but its pattern has changed owing to which high precipitation events have increased.

The Kosi phenomenon occurred mainly because of very high precipitation in the upstream areas," said Bhutiyani.According to him, the only way to avert such tragedies is to prevent the unnatural routing of the glaciers in the Himalayas.

"The ecology of that region is being destroyed due to commercial interests and this needs to be curtailed," Bhutiyani said.

Kale, head of the department of geography at UoP, however, feels that nature has its own mechanisms to absorb the changes and the effects of the global warming may take a few years to be visible.

Even then, one cannot accurately predict the outcome of the all the variables that one is observing right now.

Heading: Two nights of worry during Ganesh festival - Indian Express
Content:
A day after it emerged that Dehu Road resident Sanjay Jayram Dhutadmal had procured a ration card in the name of Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh and his family members, assistant zonal officer A N More and clerk Vidya Gangale at the zonal rationing office "A" division at Nigdi were suspended. Sunil Tatkare, state Minister for Food and Civil Supplies confirmed the action that followed preliminary investigations conducted by divisional commissioner Nitin Kareer.

"Deputy Commissioner (supplies) Arun Unhale will carry out a detailed inquiry and give a report in three days," said Tatkare.

Dhutadmal had filed a complaint against the ration office authorities of Nigdi on Tuesday. Dhutadmal had attached a photocopy of the ration card. He said he procured the ration card after paying Rs 2,000 to officers in the ration office.

While speaking to The Indian Express on Tuesday, More had said the allegations were false. "I never issued the ration card to Dhutadmal. He might have prepared a bogus ration card in the name of the Chief Minister by some other means. He is now blackmailing me," More had said. More and zonal rationing officer Vaishali Waghmare too filed a complaint against Dhutadmal at the Nigdi police station.

Dhutadmal said, "I procured the card to expose corruption in the rationing office. There was no other motive."

Heading: Tickets for Youth Games go on sale - Indian Express
Content:
Ike strike: After struggling to make contact with Texas, NRI parents get help from forum

Last weekend, while most Puneites were celebrating the last leg of the Ganapati festival, about a dozen parents of NRIs were desperately trying to contact their relatives staying in the hurricane-struck Houston.

Hurricane Ike struck the coast of Texas on Saturday, affecting Houston and nearby areas. "We tried to contact my daughter Vaishali, our son-in-law and grandchildren on the phone. They had shifted to Houston from Oklahoma barely a week ago and were yet to settle in the city. But with no electricity in the hurricane-affected areas, their telephone was not working," said Neeta Sao, a senior citizen.

She and her husband spent all of Saturday tying to call them. On Sunday they contacted Kumar Kiwalkar, president of the NRI Parents' Organisation (NRIPO).

"Finally at midnight on Sunday we received a call from my daughter who confirmed that the family was safe. We spoke to her for barely two minutes and have been unable to contact her since," Sao said.

N V Swadi and his wife, who live in Parvati, also struggled to get in touch with their son Shantanu and his family in Houston.

"We spoke to him two days after the hurricane. They were all safe but their house was damaged when a huge oak fell on the compound. Both my son and daughter-in-law are working from home since their offices are damaged and the children's schools will reopen only after a fortnight," he said.

S B Nimishe of Kothrud had to go through a similar experience. "My son Sujit had moved to his friend's place for two days following the hurricane warning. Although we were in touch with him before the hurricane, we could speak to him only two days later," said Suchitra Nimishe, mother of Sujit who is working with Infosys in Houston. Kiwalkar said he had been flooded with calls on Sunday from people struggling to get in touch with their relatives.

"I made at least 20 calls that night trying to help them. We got help from Abhijit Bhide, who earlier stayed in Houston but is now in Bangalore, and Shrikant Kulkarni in Houston, whose landline was working that day," he said.

Kiwalkar called for a centralised information centre so that NRIs can contact NRIPO in such emergencies.

Heading: Action against 20 Ganesh mandals - Indian Express
Content:
Tickets for the Commonwealth Youth Games went on sale from on Wednesday. Suresh Kalmadi, MP and chairman of the organising committee for the Games, unveiled the ticket sales programme.

Former India women's cricketer Shubhangi Kulkarni bought the first ticket for the Games while Paromita Das made the first bulk booking of tickets, for HSBC.

For further details, one can log on to www.kyazoonga.com or call the KyaZoonga-CYG ticketing call centre at 2563-KYAZ (5929). Tickets cover eight disciplines - athletics, badminton, boxing, swimming, table tennis, tennis, weightlifting and wrestling - and will be sold for individual days of the Games. Opening and closing ceremony tickets will cost Rs 100, Rs 500, Rs 1,000 and Rs 5,000, On game days, tickets will cost Rs 50, Rs 100 and Rs 500 Suresh Kalmadi said, "We are bringing cutting edge technology and access to the people. The majority of the tickets for the Games will be reserved for the two lowest-priced categories."

Heading: Foreign officers visit NDA - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune police have initiated action against 20 Ganesh mandals for using loudspeakers after the 12 am deadline on the main immersion procession routes, deputy commissioner of police (Zone I) Raghunath Khaire said on Wednesday. Cases had been filed at Vishrambaug police station against these mandals, Khaire said.

"Police have noted down the names of Ganesh mandals playing loudspeakers and music systems after the deadline on Laxmi Road and Tilak Road during the immersion procession. We have a list of at least 20 Ganesh mandals. Action has been initiated against the respective presidents and loudspeaker providers," he said.

"We have not seized the loud speakers of any mandals because it might have resulted in a quarrel, causing a delay in completing the immersion procession," Khaire added. "There might be cases against Ganesh mandals on other immersion routes in the city. But the information has not been complied yet," he said.

Heading: Equipment worth Rs 56 cr for maintenance of canals - Indian Express
Content: A team comprising five foreign officers from the armed forces of friendly countries recently visited the National Defence Academy (NDA) in Khadakwasla.  They were briefed about the training activities at the academy and taken to various training areas. The officers showed a keen interest in the training activities at Equitation Line and flying training at Air Force Gliderdome. The officers were also shown the Naval training at Peacock Bay and given a firsthand experience of the facilities available. Heading: Army bikes South to rope in recruits - Indian Express
Content:
The Irrigation Department is getting fresh equipment worth Rs 56 crore for maintenance of canal network across the state by the year-end, water resources department officers said. The Department is receiving new equipment in such numbers after a gap of 23 years.

While Vidharbha is getting the maximum number of new machines, the Pune region is second in line and is set to get 44 of them.

"After 1985, we are again in the process of procuring machines — in all 217 — like excavators, loaders, dozers for maintenance and de-silting purposes. These should be available by December this year," J D Parmar, superintendent engineer with the Mechanical section of the Water Resources Department, told reporters at a press conference in the city today to announce the 50th anniversary eventsof the establishment of the department.

Over the years, the department has moved from the construction of dams and canals to maintenance work. "We are involved in earth work, gate manufacturing of dams, their maintenance, repair and inspections, boring, lift irrigation, canal repairs and river silting," Parmar said.

Out of the 217 pieces of equipment, 138 will be focused on the Vidharbha region. "Unlike western Maharashtra which is fairly well irrigated, Vidharbha and Marathwada are lagging in the setting up of irrigation networks. We are, therefore, focusing on the Vidharbha region. There are many old canals that need to be de-silted. Besides Vidharbha, the Pune region will get 44, Konkan is getting 12 and Tapi 23," informed Parmar.

The department also announced that a fresh crop of 170 junior engineers joined the Mechanical Section recently. On September 20, the Mechanical Section will celebrate 50 years and an event to commemorate this has been organised. State home minister R R Patil and Water Resources Minister Ajit Pawar are scheduled to attend.

Heading: Security guard foils theft bid at BSNL office - Indian Express
Content:
For the last 20 days, eight defence personnel from the Southern Command have been undergoing special training in bikes in anticipation of an expedition that will be flagged off on Monday morning. Called the Golden Katar Motorcycle Expedition, it is an attempt to kindle interest in the forces in the South, where people have traditionally not taken to the Army as a career option.

"We will spend over 20 days on the road, visiting schools, villages, interacting with people, introducing them to the army's way of life, and giving information on how best they can serve the Force," said Captain Sagar Pushp, team leader of the contingent. With the Indian Army still facing a shortage of officers, Pushp hopes that their efforts would pay off.

"In the last couple of years, the Army has not been attracting the best talent. Most youngsters are opting for other fields like engineering, medicine or management. We want to target this cream for the Army. We are carrying over 1,000 posters and pamphlets to distribute and hope to encourage students to opt for the Army as a profession," he added.

Three reserve personnel will travel along with this team of three officers and seven jawans. Including the reserve personnel, the team will have one person from each of the Southern states. This will aid communication with locals, he explained.

The team will complete the 4,400-km route through Panaji, Kannur, Kanniyakumari, Rameshwaram, Pondicherry, Chennai, Ongole, Vishakhapatnam, Vijaywada, Hyderabad, Nanded and Aurangabad, and finally terminate at Pune. In preparation for this winding route on bikes, all members of the contingent have been training by riding to various locations of the city for a few hours in the morning every day.

"We have been riding to the NDA in the morning to get a feel of the bikes. Some days we have interspersed this with rides to Kothurd or Sinhagad Fort because on the road, the route is different every day. One needs to be prepared for uncharted terrain," said Captain Anand Tandon, a member of the team.

The early morning rides have been followed up with yoga and workout sessions. "In the evening, we ride around barrels to get a hang of the maneuverability. There are a lot of team building sessions. Its different to ride on the roads of a city. On long trips, if eight bikes are going together, we have to operate as a team," Pushp said

He has participated in a similar expeditions in the past from Siachen to Chandigarh — in an effort to increase awareness about Siachen.

Heading: No bookstore? Call mobile library for home delivery - Indian Express
Content:
A security guard foiled a theft bid at the BSNL office in MIDC, Bhosari, in the wee hours of Tuesday. A complaint has been lodged at Bhosari police station.

Police said Bhaskar Ashruba Mhaske (45), an ex-serviceman, was on night duty at the BSNL office. Around 1.10 am, three persons came on a motorcycle and one of them entered the premises of BSNL office. Mhaske noticed the intrusion and fired a bullet from his 12-bore gun. The burglars fled from the spot leaving their motorcycle behind. Mhakse then informed the police and BSNL authorities about the incident. The police have seized the motorcycle.

"The motorcycle was stolen from Landewadi area a few days back," said sub-inspector S H Sali. "We have not identified the burglars yet. We are trying to confirm what the burglars wanted to steal from the BSNL office," he said.

Heading: A flood of emotions - Indian Express
Content:
People living on the periphery of a booming city can now have any book they want delivered at their doorstep.

An engineer has brought to Pune an ingenious mobile library concept, which helped address the problem of lack of bookstores in Mumbai's suburbs. Pankaj Kurulkar's project, Books on Wheel or Granthayan, is aimed at making reading more accessible.

Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh had inaugurated the project on August 18; it came formally to Pune on September 17. Specially designed Tata trucks have been purchased for the project and stationed in parts of the city that do not have proper bookstores. The vehicles are well equipped with the latest machines, security equipment and intranet facility. People can visit the vehicles and buy books, or place orders through a toll-free number.

With his 10 vans catering to the needs of readers in 35 districts of Maharashtra, Kurulkar now wants to expand the business in terms of not only area but also language.

"We aim to cover more districts of Maharashtra. And in future we also plan to publish books in 22 Indian languages. We will translate award-winning books into Marathi and Marathi works into English to give them a wider reach," says Kurulkar.

He says Granthayan will encourage young people to take up writing. "We will give a royalty of 30 per cent to our solicited writers and 50 per cent to our unsolicited writers. This is done so that writers feel financially secure and thus devote more time to writing. Usually it's seen that authors are not full-time writers given the fact that prospects are not so lucrative," says Kurulkar.

Heading: Researcher finds reference to Shivaji Maharaj in foreign newspaper - Indian Express
Content:
Swatantra theatre comes up with the play Aaj ki taaza khabar that gives a poignant picture of the condition of flood victims in Bihar

They aim to paint the plight of flood victims. In a succession of fast-moving and highly stylized scenes, 25 actors re-enact critical moments in the lives of flood victims who strive for their survival.
