Train no. 1464 Jabalpur-Veraval Express was terminated at Ahmedabad and will run as 1463 Veraval-Jabalpur Express from Ahmedabad to Jabalpur on Friday. The train stands cancelled between Ahmedabad-Veraval-Ahmedabad. Train no. 9059 Surat-Jamnagar Intercity has been terminated at Viramgam and would be reversed as 9060 from Viramgam to Surat on Friday. It will remain cancelled between Viramgam-Jamnagar-Viramgam.

Train no. 9215 Mumbai-Porbandar Express has been terminated at Viramgam and will be reversed as 9216 Porbandar Express from Viramgam to Mumbai on Friday. It would remain cancelled between Viramgam-Porbandar-Viramgam.

Train no. 248 Okha-Ahmedabad Passenger, which leaves Okha and reaches Surendranagar on Thursday has been terminated at Surendranagar and will be reversed as 203 Viramgam-Okha Express from Surendranagar on Friday. This means that 248 Ahmedabad- Okha Passenger would be partially cancelled between Surendranagar-Ahmedabad and 203 Okha-Virmgam Passenger would be partially cancelled between Viramgam-Surendranagar.

Train No. 204 Okha-Viramgam Passenger leaving Okha on Thursday will be terminated at Surendranagar and reversed as 247 Okha- Ahmedabad Passenger from Surendranagar on Thursday.

Heading: Boats go off sea, fishermen suffer huge losses - Indian Express
Content:
Vulnerable minors may also be used for anti-India activities, believes Coast Guard

Every fifth fishing boat in Jakhau harbour has one or two children as its crew members, said the Indian Coast Guard stationed at Jakhau.

Recently, the Coast Guard also received a message from the Pakistan Marine Security Agency (PMSA) expressing apprehension that the Indian fishing boats have under-age crew members. The PMSA suspected this when it apprehended Indian fishing boats in the Pakistani waters opposite Jakhau coast.

Sources in the Coast Guard stated that many crew members' ID cards had other people's photographs on them. The ID cards are issued by the state fisheries department for Indian boats during the fishing season — between mid-August and March. However, the main fishing activity is witnessed at the fish-rich Jakhau waters, apart from the adjoining Pakistani waters in the Arabian Sea.

The fact that many fishing crew members are children can be dangerous for India, said sources in the Coast Guard. "This is very dangerous, as the ISI-controlled Pakistani regime may use it in their own interest. They can easily prepare young, impressionable minds for anti-India activities, or even sneak in trained agents on the basis of such documents by simply replacing the photographs".

While the fisheries department and other concerned security and civil agencies have been informed about this lapse, the Coast Guard has urged the department to ensure that the photograph on the ID card is the latest, and there is a proper department stamp on it. The department officials should physically ensure that the photograph on the ID Card is that of the person going to the sea, the Coast Guard stated, adding that if lapses were found during on-board checking of Indian trawlers at high sea, the fishermen, along with the boat, would be sent back shore to face legal action.

A coast guard high official stated that they had written several letters to the fisheries department, but no action was taken. The official said that no one in the department as much as attended the meeting convened by the coast guard.

District magistrate and collector R R Varsani said he had visited Jakhau and planned to visit it again. He said he had contacted senior officials in the state fisheries department for a permanent solution to the security related problems.

Fisheries commissioner Arun Solanki was not available for comments, while fisheries secretary Arun Sutharia declined to speak saying he did not have details about the issue.

Heading: Will UGC’s generosity bless GU this year? - Indian Express
Content:
The rough sea and the high waves have forced Saurashtra fishermen to drop anchor for the past five days. With nearly 6,000 boats off sea at Veraval, Mangarol, Porbandar and Vanakbara, fishermen have suffered huge financial losses.

Members of the Veraval Fishing Boat Association said since the last five days some 2,500 fishing boats have been returned from the Arabian Sea and are now anchored at Veraval port. Another 1,500 boats are anchored at Mangarol and some 2,000 at Porbandar.

Bachubhai Kasta, an office-bearer of the Veraval Fishing Boat Association, said: "The sky-high waves and wind velocity has left fishermen with no option but to return from the sea. As almost all the fishing boats operating from the Saurashtra coast are equipped with the GPS system and wireless sets, we have flashed them messages asking them to return. Our timely action has saved the lives of fishermen and their boats. However, most fishermen have been forced to abandon their catch in the sea. In case some of them manage to bring it ashore, they will be forced to dispose them at very low prices," said Kasta.

"We hope for an improvement in the weather so that stranded fishermen are able to return. As of now, the fishing community leaders have placed a ban on fishing till there is an improvement in the weather conditions. Any violation will invite strict action from us," said Kasta.

Heading: IAF comes to the rescue - Indian Express
Content:
Varsity to put forward a demand of Rs 120.3 cr; last year it had got Rs 4.3 cr

The University Grants Commission's (UGC) XI Plan Expert Committee will start assessing the Eleventh Plan requirement (2007-2012) & Tenth Plan Review Performance (2002-2007) of the Gujarat University (GU) on Friday at 11 am.

The GU will ask for Rs 120.31 crore for its upgradation in the next five years. Parimal Trivedi, the Vice-Chancellor (V-C) of GU told Newsline: "In the UGC X Plan, we received only Rs 4.29 crore, but for the development of the varsity, we will need Rs 120.31 crore. In the Eleventh Plan requirement report, we have tried our best to explain in detail the requirement of such a huge budget."

He added: "There is nothing wrong about starting new courses for students, as that would benefit them. None of the V-Cs before me built 15 new building complexes and got a NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council) accreditation of B++, which is the best in western India."

As per Sudhir Nanavati, member of the GU Executive Council (EC), the academic system is on track; but when it comes to administrative work, it is very weak. He said: "The administrative work is very much weak and there is an urgent need to improvise it." Narhari Amin, another EC member said, "The GU-level problems that we had in the last five years have been solved almost. But those pertaining to the state government level are yet to be solved, as we need approval from the state government."

According to Pradeep Prajapati of the Academic Council (AC) of GU, the V-C and the varsity authorities are ignoring the suggestions made by the NAAC for the development of GU, at the time accreditation last year.

He said, "The V-C announces new courses without consulting the EC, AC or the HOD of the respective departments." He added: "In half of the courses announced in the last two years, the process of syllabus making and recruiting the faculties has not started. There is no point announcing new courses without the required force needed to begin basic work."

Manish Doshi, member of EC told Newsline, "There is no transparency in the GU financial matters. Two years ago, applications were invited for vacancies and Rs 750 was charged from each candidate. No follow-up has been done till date." It needs to be seen how far the GU demands will be met.

Heading: Winds of change must sweep the power sector - Indian Express
Content:
An MI-8 helicopter of the Indian Air Force (IAF) has been pressed into service for rescue operations in the flood-hit Lakhatar taluka of Surendranagar district, after a request by the state government.

"The state government made a request to rescue the marooned villagers, and the Air Force station, Jamnagar, began operation at 10.30 this morning at Nani Katechi, Nani Majethi, Khara Ghoga and Bhaskarpur villages of Lakhatar taluka," Joint Defence PRO, Wing Commander Satish Menon told Newsline over phone on Thursday. He said some 30 villagers are stranded in these villages.

Meanwhile, Surendranagar District Superintendent of Police, Ashok Yadav, said rain water has started receding in the area.

"The situation is fast improving with the district administration, police and the state reserve police helping the affected people. We have deployed one company of the SRP specially trained in the disaster management in the area," Yadav said, adding that Education Minister Ramanlal Vora and Forest Minister Kiritsinh Rana visited the area.

Heading: Male cops keep two women in custody for whole night - Indian Express
Content:
State should tap wind power potential in coastal areas to achieve CDM goal

About 20 per cent of all the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) projects in India pertain to wind energy. This is probably due to the attractive prospects offered by the provisions under the Kyoto Protocol that there is a rush to earn carbon credits.

Cases of false depreciation claims by wind farm owners have also come to light. Even allegations of forcible acquisition of land for wind farms keep surfacing from time to time.

Also, due to the absence of reliable data on the manufacturing cost of Wind Turbine Generators and a monopoly of a few players, the wind farm developers are earning huge profits.

The wind energy business is for any entity which is cash-rich. Any financially sound entity can invest in the lucrative wind energy sector by approaching the wind farm developers who commission, operate and maintain the plant, at their desired price.

As per the data supplied by the Centre for Wind Energy Technology, Tamil Nadu, an autonomous institution under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), the major wind farm developers in India are Enercon (India) Ltd, Suzlon Energy Ltd, Vestas Wind Technology India Private Ltd, Powerica Ltd and Eliokem India Pvt Ltd.

The biggest player in Gujarat is Suzlon Energy Ltd. It has recently commissioned a 50 MW Wind Power plant for ONGC at a turnkey cost of Rs 307.78 crore, making the cost at Rs 6 crore per megawatt approximately. The operation and maintenance contract has also been given to Suzlon for Rs 5.5-6 crore per year for a period of 10 years. Suzlon had also commissioned a 150 MW Wind Farm for DLF in Kutch in October last year.

To sum up, it is a win-win situation for both the developers and the investors. Developers earn big by setting up a Wind Farm and by operating and maintaining it; the investors enjoy huge tax benefits (with 80 per cent accelerated depreciation and 20 per cent subsidies) and also earn profits by selling wind power to the grid along with the sale of carbon credits.

Anoop Kayarat, Corporate Communications Officer of Suzlon differed. When contacted by Newsline, he said, "Although it's for the government to frame policies, the allegations of false depreciation claims and forcible acquisition of land are completely untrue. Gujarat is one of our focal areas as far as developing wind farms is concerned."

V H Buch, Director, Gujarat Energy Development Agency, the nodal authority for renewable energy in Gujarat was not available for comment. With fossil fuels depleting fast, the need for venturing into the clean and green sources of energy cannot be denied. The west coast of Gujarat has the highest wind power potential in the country. The state stands third after Tamil Nadu (around 3,800 MW) and Maharastra (1,750 MW) in terms of production. Its gross wind power potential is estimated to be nearly 10,000 MW, representing over a fifth of the national total.

Probably, the need of the hour is for the government to come out with a comprehensive 'National Policy for Wind Energy' to encourage serious independent power producers into the wind power sector, who are there not for profit but for change.

Concluded

Heading: MSU gets Rs 1.60 lakh for youth fest - Indian Express
Content:
Arrested for minor offence, they were kept in a police station which did not have a woman officer

In a case of alleged human rights violation by the Ahmedabad city police, two women — one of them a tribal — were allegedly arrested for a minor offence by Sabarmati police station officials earlier this month and kept in custody for the entire night in the absence of any woman police officer.

The two women — Gilloben Khristi alias Dilluben (40) and Santokben Bhil (50), both residents of Ambedkar Nagar, Sahibpura na Chhapra in Sabarmati area — have now submitted a written complaint of human rights violation to the Ahmedabad Commissioner of Police, a copy of which is with Newsline. The Sabarmati police officials have, however, termed the allegations as baseless.

Speaking to Newsline, Khristi said: "A builder wants to illegally construct a building on our chawl (a type of tenement) and we are opposing it. On the morning of September 5, power officials came to cut off our electricity connection at the behest of the builder. Since we opposed it, we were arrested by police officials, none of whom were women. The whole night, we were made to sit on a bench behind the police station on the pretext of some senior officer coming to meet us."

"Not only did the police officials use abusive language, there was not a single woman police officer present with us either," said Bhil.

The next morning, Khristi complained of pain in the chest and reportedly also vomited. She was taken to a hospital run by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation and then produced in the court of the Executive Magistrate. All along, there was no woman police officer present with them.

When contacted, Sabarmati police inspector K B Jhala said: "They were arrested in the presence of two women police constables, who were present in the police station all along," he said. Commissioner of Police O P Mathur, however, could not be contacted.

Valjibhai Patel, secretary of Council for Social Justice, who has also approached various authorities in this regard including the State Human Rights Commission said: "Keeping two women in police custody for the whole night, and that too for a minor offence under Section 107 and 151 of the Criminal Procedure Code, shows the high-handedness of the Sabarmati police. It seems that the police station officials have manipulated official records to show the presence of the women constables at the police station," he added.

Heading: Incessant rains throw life out of gear in central Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time, the Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) has been allotted a budget of Rs 1.60 lakh for its youth festival, expected to take place in January, 2009.

On Thursday, MSU union general secretary Hari Kiran Rao called a budget meeting in which it was announced that Rs 3.70 lakh had been allotted for the youth festival and other university functions and activities.

"Ratri Before Navratri will be the first event to be organised from the sanctioned fund, on September 27," Rao said.

Speaking to Newsline, MSU union president Sharad Bansal said: "The treasurer presented Rs 1.60 lakh budget for youth festival, Rs 60,000 for various functions, and Rs 45,000 for other activities such as organising film shows and events such as Ratri Before Navaratri, campus beautification and entertainment."

Heading: Barricades, scaffolding and midnight tea breaks - Indian Express
Content:
Life in many parts of central Gujarat was thrown out of gear as incessant rains lashed the region.

While many areas of Kheda district remained marooned, long distance trains going towards Rajkot had to halt in Ahmedabad for over 12 hours, due to sifting of earth under the railway tracks.

In Kheda district, over 500 people from the low-lying areas of Nadiad were evacuated to safety on Thursday after it received over 531 mm of rainfall. "A large number of people, especially from Indira Nagar and Kanjari, have been shifted to safe areas. Evacuation had been done in the same areas during last month's rain as well," said Kheda district collector Mohammad Shahid. He added that most local transport services remained disrupted in Nadiad with 224 mm rainfall. Matar and Kheda recorded 154 mm and 96 mm rainfall respectively.

Most trains originating from Okha were also stranded because of sifting of earth under the railway tracks between Virangam and Surendranagar. "Trains from Vadodara could not go beyond Ahmedabad, while the trains from Okha, Veraval and Surendranagar have been stopped. The filling up work is in progress, and if monsoon permits the trains will resume service by Thursday midnight," said K Chachondia, senior divisional commercial manager, Vadodara division.

Though daily train services in Vadodara were not affected much, some trains beyond Ahmedabad did face problems.

Meanwhile, the level of Ajwa Dam has reached 211.74 feet, almost touching the 212-feet danger mark. The area recorded 33.2 mm rainfall in the past 24 hours.

In Vadodara, open storm water drainage system proved dangerous, as a few cattle fell into it at Subhanpura and Dabhoi road.

VMC Commissioner M K Das said: "No serious incident has occurred, but care has been taken to barricade the susceptible areas. We cannot opt to close storm water drains, as it decreases the life span of the construction. We have post-monsoon plans to clear storm water drains and install netting of the drains."

In Bharuch district, Waghwa received maximum rainfall of 125 mm on Thursday followed by Jhagadia (94 mm) and Bharuch (80 mm). The level of Narmada dam is close to the danger mark at 121.02 feet.

Surat received 3 inch of moderate rainfall. The water level at Ukai dam has crossed 328 feet with an inflow of 41,000 cusecs. The outflow has been stopped to maintain the rule level.

Heavy to very heavy rainfall has been predicted over the next 24 hours in all the districts of south Gujarat.

Heading: Teens murdered in Greater Noida - Indian Express
Content:
The Kalkaji Metro station has to open before the 2010 Games and Kali joins 65 others to ensure that it is ready in time

Every evening, when the streetlights come on and most of us head home, 22-year-old Kali straps on his iron-soldered boots, dons a fluorescent orange jacket, grabs his yellow helmet and takes position. A construction worker at a Delhi Metro construction site near the crowded Kalkaji Temple, Kali's day begins every evening at 7, as a "helper" on the graveyard shift.

Amid the roar of galvanised machines warming up for a long night ahead, the yellow barricades are shifted or removed by him — only to be restored to their original position before dawn to accommodate morning traffic. Lights mounted in every nook and corner of the site are switched on and Kali joins 65 other workers building the Kalkaji Metro Station, as part of the Central Secretariat-Badarpur line, scheduled to open before the Commonwealth Games in 2010.

The action, of course, takes place 11 meters above the ground. And it offers a beautiful view of the Lotus Temple and the heavy night traffic whizzing by.

But it's the clink of the hammers used to fix the scaffolding to build the structure of the Metro station, and the orders of his supervisor that matter to him most.

"I have never seen the Lotus Temple because I live in Harkesh Nagar and come here only at night, with the contractor who arranges the labour," Kali, who came to the Capital barely six months ago from Madinapur district in Bihar, says.

"My work usually involves assisting people in lifting things, and climbing the scaffolding and handing over material and tools. The shift ends at 2 am and then I head home to sleep," he says.

While the rest of the world works during the day, Kali says he prefers the night shift, particularly during the hot and sultry months of August and September. "As it is, construction sites are hot and humid, and during the day it can be worse. The nights are cooler and less noisy," he says, while joining the rest of his gang, who in their yellow hats, resemble bees working on the scaffolding that is their beehive.

The night also means less traffic and less hindrance for transporting boulder-like concrete structures and construction materials on trailers that are not allowed to ply during the day, site engineers say. "We usually set the stage by doing preparatory jobs during the day," one of them says.

As a trailer from the Delhi Metro's shed at Sarai Kale Khan arrives at the spot, the workers take position according to the colour of their hard hats. Workers with the yellow hats are supposed to carry out civil work and operate machines; those with the blue and red ones supervise work for the contractor. Workers wearing green helmets ensure that safety norms are maintained at every stage. The boss — the DMRC engineer — gets to wear a white hard hat.

While posters about a quiz contest and a painting competition on this side of the yellow barriers do give a hint of recreation and fun in this space driven by targets and discipline, a board outside a tin structure lined with benches says "resting room". This is where all the workers take a break for their midnight chai.

"We usually get a break of about half an hour, when we just gather to rest. We eat at home and come, so snacks are out. But there is a light midnight breeze in this area because it's slightly off the main road, which is very refreshing," Kali says.

Heading: Blasts a wake-up call, market associations seek tighter security - Indian Express
Content:
Grandfather of the girl maintains she had to die to save family honour, say Noida cops

They had met in the maize fields of the village several times, but this time, 18-year-old Rekha and 17-year-old Sonu were caught.

Her family allegedly strangulated her and beat the youth to death. The bodies were later set on fire in an apparent attempt to destroy evidence.

The alleged honour killing took place in the Wair village near Kakod in Greater Noida on Thursday. The girl belonged to Jatav community, the boy to the Khatik community. Her family owns a ration shop, his father Raju is a farmer.

According to the police, the two were neighbours and fell in love. "Around 11.30 am, they had slipped away to meet in the fields. But a villager saw them and informed Rekha's family. Her father and grandfather reached the spot to find them in a compromising position. They smothered the girl with her dupatta and beat the youth to death," said R K Chaturvedi, Senior Superintendent of Police, Noida.

After the couple died, some members of the girl's family riddled Sonu's body with bullets, using a countrymade gun. The bodies were then drenched in kerosene, put on haystacks and set afire.

A local watchman, who found out about the incident, informed a constable. The bodies were already half consumed by fire when the police reached the spot.

An FIR has been lodged against Puran Jatav, the girl's grandfather and Gulab Jatav, her father. Two other relatives — Samay Pal and Kailash — have been booked too.

"The family is absconding, though we have managed to detain the grandfather," said Chaturvedi. "Puran is unrepentant and maintains that the girl had to die. He says he saved his family's honour," the SSP said.

Sonu was studying at Anand Raj Surana Bhati Wair Inter College in Class XI and the girl was a student of Class X, the police said.

But Mahipal Singh, village pradhan and former principal of the college, denied this. "Rekha had been our student but had failed twice in Class X. The UP education board does not allow a third shot at the exam. Sonu had quit studies a long time ago," Singh said.

With the postmortem pending, the boy's family is yet to receive the body.

"Sonu had never missed my aloo parathas," said Saroj, his aunt. "He was the simplest boy in the village and an introvert. Rekha's family could have sorted this out through discussions. His mother is bedridden and father is almost inconsolable," she added.

"By tomorrow, we hope to arrest the rest of the accused," said Chaturvedi.

Heading: Govt increases compensation rate for North Delhi farmers - Indian Express
Content:
In the wake of last week's serial blasts in crowded markets across the Capital, market welfare associations have decided to re-check security arrangements in their areas. Some market associations already have a security system but they are "not satisfied with it" now.

Palika Bazaar

Palika Bazaar in Connaught Place is not satisfied with its security arrangements.

Bazaar association General Secretary Vinay Kumar said: "Our market comes under the NDMC and security guards for the market are also provided by the civic body on contracts of two to three months. We had requested the NDMC for more CCTV cameras and security guards in the market. We have been given assurances time and again but that's it."

The association had bought nine cameras, one each for every entrance.

Karol Bagh

The Karol Bagh market suffered the biggest loss in business after last Saturday's blasts. The market association is divided in seven parts, with each part having its own president. Darshan Lal, president of the Ajmal Khan Market Shopkeepers' Association, said: "This market comes under the MCD and the security system comes under the Delhi Police. We have demanded that more CCTV cameras be installed in our market. People are still scared to visit the market; after the blasts we are all alert."

Some shopkeepers have personally installed CCTV cameras in their shops.

Shankar Market

Shankar Market, close to the spot on Barakhamba Road where one of Saturday's blasts took place, has a lax security system, shopkeepers said.

The market welfare association secretary, Kulvinder Singh, said: "Our market is divided in seven blocks and all the blocks have two gates for entry and exit; it is hard for us to appoint security guards at every gate. We need the support of the NDMC for ensuring security."

The association is in talks with the NDMC and has placed a request for security guards and CCTV cameras.

Sarojini Nagar

The Sarojini Nagar Market Welfare Association is satisfied with its security plans. Mohan Kukreja, chairman of the welfare association, said: "We have managed to arrange security guards along with those posted by the police; mistakes from the past will not be repeated."

The market has Door Frame Metal Detectors that were put up by the Delhi Police. CCTV cameras, bought by the market association, with monetary help from the Delhi Police, have also been put up. "There are 27 cameras in and around the market," Kukreja said.

The shop owners have also appointed security guards for night duty. The Delhi police has also increased the presence of security personnel during peak hours.

Heading: KV murder: postmortem report says 7-yr-old sodomised - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Cabinet decided to offer compensation to farmers of six villages in Northwest Delhi, including Kanjhawala, at a new rate of Rs 75 lakh per acre, in a meeting held this evening.

Land was acquired by the Delhi government in six villages a few years ago and the farmers were not happy with the old compensation rate, as market rates have risen considerably in the past few years. Also, a large number of farmers did not get the compensation in the first place.

The farmers, under the banner of the Bhartiya Kisan Union, had held protests outside the Delhi Assembly on the first day of session last week and scuffled with the police.

Farmers from several villages, including Kanjhawala, Karala, Sultanpur Dabas, Put Khurd, Tikri Khurd and Tikri Kalan, have been staging a sit-in outside the local deputy commissioner's office from the last six months. They alleged that nearly 60,000 people were affected by the government's decision of giving less compensation for land.

The Delhi government had acquired 1,450 acre of agricultural land in North Delhi on Aug 25, 2005, through a notification. The government revised the compensation rate from Rs 15.7 lakh to Rs 17.5 lakh per acre within four days of the notification. The farmers claimed that the market price of land was nearly Rs 3 crore per acre and the government offer was very low.

Heading: Building brand connect vital: marketing gurus - Indian Express
Content:
Almost a week after a 7-year-old boy was found dead in a water tank of his school in Uttam Nagar of West Delhi, a postmortem report received on Thursday suggests the boy was smothered to death before being thrown into the tank. Police sources also said the boy was repeatedly sodomised before being killed.

The victim was reportedly missing since September 12 and his parents had registered a missing complaint. The boy was Class II student of Kendriya Vidyalaya in Hastsal Vihar and was a resident of flat number 16, Pocket 7, DDA Janta flats in Naseerpur in Dwarka. The police had asked the school authorities to conduct a search in the school premises.

"On September 13, his decomposed body was found in the water tank situated near the toilet of the school," a senior officer said.

Police has not recovered the murder weapon. Police said the staff and senior students of the school are being questioned.

Meanwhile, the boy's father demanded a CBI probe into the matter.

Heading: New central placement cell for students at DU - Indian Express
Content:
Bringing together a divergent India residing in urban and rural pockets remains a challenge for the corporate sector, which can be addressed only if their brands understand and speak the language of its target audience.

Speaking at the Brand Managers' Conclave, organised by Delhi-based B-school, Faculty of Management Studies, on the "Evolution of Consumerism and the Future Brand Paradigms", marketing gurus got together to focus on the issues faced by marketers globally. Distinctly, the psychosocial aspect of customer behaviour is increasingly responsible for the recent onslaught of consumerism.

MART partner and senior consultant Benjamin Mathew said the Indian rural segment should not be ignored. Pointing at the massive potential of the rural markets, he said that it is feasible to create brands to cater to thinly populated villages by evolving a market midway between urban and rural areas, like towns; and having sustained efforts at these points.

Stressing on the duality that exists in present day India, JWT Vice President and Client Services Director Hari Krishnan warned of the pitfalls in not recognising this facet.

The importance of maintaining brand consistency, building brand connect and brand love still gets top priority, felt Coca Cola India Director (marketing) Avinash Pant, even though consumer expectations have changed.

Citing the reasons for such a consumer drive, Spice Communications Global President (marketing and branding) Vivek Bali said: "The substantial population below the age of 28 years (approximately 57 per cent of India's total population) is fuelling the massive consumerism widely seen today."

Connecting with this age group is not the only challenge faced by marketers. Perfetti Van Melle CEO Sameer Suneja, while emphasising the unique offerings of his company, said that in case of the confectionery and candy industry, the retailer is "king" and should be appropriately engaged.

Heading: City’s second dengue death in Burari - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi University Vice Chancellor Deepak Pental launched a Central Placement Cell at the New Council Hall in the university on Thursday. Representatives of ASSOCHAM, CII, FICCI and other industrial corporations were also present at the occasion.

Pental said the main objective of this cell is to provide a unique platform to Delhi University students, wherein industry will get a wider choice to select from, with students with varied backgrounds and competencies representing different disciplines.

Joint Dean of Student Welfare Suman Verma said off-campus students would benefit from the new initiative as much as students living on campus. "We will only disclose the qualification of a student and not the names of colleges. That ways, companies will not end up taking students from only campus colleges," he said. Verma said students applying to the cell should have at least 60 per cent marks in higher secondary results.

The cell will start registering students as well as industries immediately after its launch. Students interested in placements will be required to fill in the prescribed Student Registration Form, obtainable from their respective colleges or online at the Delhi University website.

Interested corporate houses may contact the cell and register themselves through the prescribed performa. The response sheet and soft copy of the brochure for industries will also be available on the university website www.du.ac.in and http://placement.du.ac.in.

This year, placement facilities will be available only for undergraduate students. In the coming years, however, this may be extended to cover postgraduate students as well.

Heading: Motorcyclist mowed down in Central Delhi - Indian Express
Content:
Another dengue death was reported from Burari, where a man succumbed to the deadly viral fever on Thursday. The number of cases reported from the city crossed the 300 mark this week, with over 100 cases being reported last week itself.

The National Institute of Communicable Diseases (NICD) has confirmed the death. The patient was undergoing treatment at St Stephen's Hospital.

"We were notified by the hospital today. Lack of participation and sporadic rainfall together are to be blamed for high indices of mosquito breeding across the city," Dr N K Yadav, Municipal Health Officer, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), said.

This comes at a time when 2,500 inspectors responsible for checking the breeding of mosquitoes are on strike. The workers, employed with the MCD on contract basis, are demanding the regularisation of their jobs. "It is still not an epidemic situation, as cases are expected to peak during this time of the year. There is no need to panic but people must ensure their premises are free of mosquito breeding," Dr V K Monga, Chairman of the MCD's Health Committee, said.

Heading: Less is more - Indian Express
Content: A 29-year-old motorcyclist was reportedly mowed down by a Blueline bus in Gole Market area of New Delhi district at 10 pm on Wednesday night. The police, however, said that an unknown vehicle was involved in the incident and has not confirmed the involvement of a Blueline bus. Sources said Robert Mathew died on the spot. The driver and conductor of the bus fled the scene after the incident. Robert was a resident of Shakti Nagar extension and is survived by his wife. "We got to know of his identity from the driving license found in his possession," the police said. A case of rash and negligent driving has been registered against the unknown driver and efforts are on to nab him. "We are trying to establish what vehicle caused the accident and who was driving it," the police said.

Heading: Lucky at 13 - Indian Express
Content:
Three low-budget films release today, each one out to prove that unconventional storylines can rule the box office

The script of filmmaking has changed for some years now. It's the small- and medium-budget films with unconventional storylines that have been setting the box-office ringing. This Friday, their audience-drawing power will be put to test once again when Welcome to Sajjanpur, Saas Bahu Aur Sensex and Hulla release.

In fact, these movies are the only ones on offer this week. The preceding weeks have not been very different with Mumbai Meri Jaan, A Wednesday and Rock on!! not exactly contending for the big-budget tag.

"Making smaller films has always been a safer bet. After all, you won't lose Rs 50 crore if such a film flops. With the amount spent on a big-budget project, one can make three small or medium budget films," says Vikas Bahl, COO of UTV Spotboy, which has produced Welcome to Sajjanpur.

Small-budget films are not an option for many. They're mostly driven by the urge to tell a story and the biggest constraint faced is finding a sound financial backing. A case in point is Jaideep Verma, writer-director of Hulla. "I had this script with me since 2001. It's in 2006 that Sunil Doshi agreed to finance it," he says. The director, however, is firm that he would not like to make another movie with a shoe-string budget. A film like Hulla made with Rs 1 crore budget means less remuneration for the cast and crew. "If I can't manage more money for my next film, I would at least make sure that those involved with it have some share in the film."

Call it coincidence, many conventional stories on the celluloid in the recent times have been small-budget films. Shona Urvashi promises this in her second directorial venture Saas Bahu Aur Sensex. Both men and women will like this film, she says. Urvashi, however, feels that small-budget films are under the magnifying glass for public scrutiny more often than those with huge financial backings. Welcome to Sajjanpur, a medium-budget film, too will see Shyam Benegal tackle an unusual subject for rural comedy though "it has all the elements of Indian cinema".

Sushant Singh, who plays the lead in Hulla along with Rajat Kapoor, says, "It's the originality of the story that made me take up the project." The actor, however, feels that for a good story to click it should also be high on entertainment.

According to Benegal, the budget goes up when stars are roped in. "But their presence assures one thing—the initial draw. This reduces the financial risks involved in a big-budget venture." For him, it's the script requirement that often decides the budget. For example, UTV Spotboy's Aamir was a small budget film, Welcome to Sajjanpur is medium with the production cost at Rs 6 crore and upcoming Main aur Mrs Khanna, with Salman Khan and Kareena Kapoor in the lead, has a bigger budget.

Chetan Motiwala, executive producer of Sajjanpur, says, "Rs 30 crore can be called a decent amount for a big-budget film while those with Rs 5 crore should come under the small budget category." Less money for the projects demands discipline, sticking to the schedule and limited time to complete the project. Benegal, Urvashi and Verma vouch for that.

More money in the market has made the making of a slew of smaller budgets possible, says Urvashi. And this has made new talents come to the fore.

Heading: FACE TO FACE with Muzammil Ibrahim - Indian Express
Content:
Rock On!! makes history as the first Indian album to make it at Number 13 in the iTunes' World Music charts

* How does it feel to hit the iTune World Music charts?

Shankar Mahadevan: The enthusiasm is upped, so we want to come back after a weekend or even every day with that extra spring in our step.

* How rocking was the Rock On!! experience?

Loy Mendonca: Film music here has a definition. But why should it do so? Rock On!! proves that receptivity is high to anything good, even if it is not within regular parameters.

* How did Farhan Akhtar come to sing on it?

Ehsaan Noorani: It was Abhishek Kapoor's idea. He did a test shoot with Farhan singing a U2 song. Farhan would always strum a guitar while jamming with us. When we were making Dil Chahta Hai, Farhan never even touched a guitar. And by the time we were making Don, he was playing songs on the guitar. The first song we recorded was Na na na. It was when we made him hear what we had recorded that his confidence zoomed. By the time we came to the ballad Tum ho to, his confidence had shot up from 40 per cent to something like 95 per cent.

* How did Javed Akhtar tune with the music?

Shankar: We completed the score within 15 days.

* And did you deliberately put in less effort for the rival's song in the competition because he was to lose?

Ehsaan: Well, we wanted a hard-rock song there because of its dark quality; as hard rock is more intense and louder and we needed a heavy metal feel. After that song Na na na was obviously softer and more meaningful.

* You have been introducing several new singers like Suraj.

Ehsaan: We introduced Nikita Nigam in Marigold and are giving her a song again in Shortcut. Shekhar of Vishal-Shekhar has sung for us in Zoya Akhtar's film Luck By Chance and we are also introducing Kirti and Arijit.

* Shankar, you are now a judge on Zee's Sa Re Ga Ma Pa. How do you find the talents in the current season?

Shankar: It's terrific to know what kind of talent is out there.

* Is it that you are particular about whom you work with?

Loy: Yes, we do like to work with people with whom we are comfortable with. It's very important to know where a filmmaker is coming from in terms of the work-ethic.

* What else is coming up from you?

Ehsaan: We have Karan Johar's My Name Is Khan and Wake-Up Sid, Farhan Akhtar's next, a film with Bharatbala Productions, Walt Disney Productions' next with Satyajit Bhatkal as director, Arshad Warsi's home production and Vipul Amrutlal Shah's London Dreams. There is also a Tamil and a Telugu film and Amol Palekar's film Dumkata.

Heading: Joining Forces - Indian Express
Content:
Not just the life, but the works of Jnanpith awardee Gurdial Singh form the spine of a docu-drama

His life is not separate from his writing and art. Precisely why, the docu-drama 'Gurdial Singh Ji', is not solely a biographical sketch of the Jnanpith awardee, but gives a deep insight into the works of the renowned and contemporary Punjabi writer. Commissioned by the Sahitya Akademi, Delhi, the docu-drama, according to GS Chani, its producer and director is the latest in the series of docu-dramas on the lives of prominent Indian writers, which will form part of a library and will be sold individually as well. The script has been written with inputs from the writer himself, who didn't want it to be just a commentary on his life's events, how he grew up et al, but focus on the integral part of his being, his literary work.

Born into a family of artisans in Malwa, as a boy, Gurdial moulded iron sheets for long hours and encouraged by his school teacher, resumed his studies and went on to be a professor at Punjabi University. His first major work, 'Marhi Da Deeva' was translated into English as 'The Last Flicker' and is considered a modern classic. 'Anhoe', 'Anhe Ghore Da Daan', 'Parsa'...and then notable collection of short stories and also plays followed. Gurdial has won the Punjab Sahitya Akademi Award, the Soviet Land Nehru Award, the Bhai Veer Singh Fiction Award and of course, the Jnanpith. "We've taken up five major novels and enacted scenes from them as part of the movie. The main characters of the novels talk about Gurdialji, the structure of the novels and themselves. We chose not use commentary, but included interviews of Gurdialji's contemporaries for a terrific flow,'' adds Chani.

'Gurdial Singh Ji' will be screened at Punjab Kala Bhavan on September 20 at 5:30 pm.

Heading: Sizzling Hot - Indian Express
Content:
Australian filmmaker Megan Doneman on her documentary on Kiran Bedi

There was enough of India in Toronto last week — from the slums of Mumbai and the sets of Kaun Banega Crorepati? flickering on Danny Boyle's Slumdog Millionaire to the razzmatazz of Punjab in Singh is Kinng. And then there was Kiran Bedi — in Australian filmmaker Megan Doneman's compelling feature-length documentary, tongue-in-cheekily titled Yes Madam, Sir. The story of the first woman IPS officer, narrated by Academy Award-winning Helen Mirren, was screened as part of the Toronto International Film Festival's Real to Reel section that showcased 20 of the finest non-fiction films of 2008.

Doneman first read about Bedi when she was just 13 in a newspaper article her mother brought home from India. "The story was headlined 'Kiran Bedi: India's First Woman Police Officer Doing it her Way!' Even as a young girl, I knew how significant and bold that was," says Doneman, who next spotted her on television. She watched in disbelief the programme on Bedi introducing Vipassana meditation in Tihar Jail. "About 1,000 prisoners practised Vipassana in complete silence for 10 days and emerged from the experience weeping in the arms of the stoic prison guards, repenting their criminal behaviour. It was unbelievable," reminisces Doneman.

Nine years ago, Doneman began e-mailing Bedi, hoping that she might agree to let her do a film. "Bedi is one of these fascinating people. What motivates her to live her life the way she does? What drives her to continually oppose the status quo in the face of huge adversity and personal consequence? I had to know," says Doneman. Even as she pursued Bedi over the years, Doneman, a graduate of business communications and film at the University of Technology, Sydney, worked as assistant editor in Mission: Impossible 2 and The Lord of the Rings trilogy's The Two Towers and The Return of the King. But Yes Madam, Sir was to be her directorial debut. Doneman is not surprised by that. What she wondered, instead, was why did Bedi decide to go with an "unknown girl from Australia after turning down offers from esteemed filmmakers for 15 years". Finally, when Bedi invited her to fly to India, Doneman put the question to the top cop. "She replied, 'Because I am going to enjoy watching you struggle and fight to somehow pull this off.' I guess she had done that all her life," smiles Doneman, who watched Bedi at home and at work for months and pored through archives. And she found the clue to her character. "The true drama lies not in Bedi's extraordinary courage, but in the inherent contradictions in her character," says Doneman. "The very qualities that allow her to triumph could ultimately lead to her undoing." Bedi wouldn't disagree.

Heading: Neighbourhood Watch - Indian Express
Content:
A stylish new Indian diner serves kebabs on sizzler trays and offers popular Lucknawi curries with a twist

It's raining restaurants in Gurgaon. After popular diners like Sahib Sindh Sultan from Bangalore and Fresc Co from Spain set up branches in Gurgaon, now Graviss Hospitality that operates the Intercontinental hotel in Mumbai has taken a shine to the suburb. The hospitality group has set up a standalone restaurant, Coal: Indian Grill and Kitchen, at Cybercity that houses plush office spaces. "Gurgaon has become an important address and we need to tap the potential of this growing market. We intend to expand Coal as a chain," says Romil Ratra, vice-president, Graviss Hospitality. The 130-cover diner is worth a drive if sumptuous kebabs are your thing. Interestingly, most of the kebabs are served on sizzler trays so that your starters remain warm for as long as you want. We drive to the restaurant for a weekday dinner, elbowing the office traffic, and are greeted by a stylish diner done up in black translucent tapestry and earthy brown seating with charcoal blocks as the centre piece.

Must-Try

The kitchen rolls out exceptionally well-done kebabs, and Gilawati Kebab (Rs 425 for mutton, Rs 325 for rajma) is the crowning jewel. Six palm-size portions of soft and juicy mutton kebabs are delicately perched on white moons of chapatti. The vegetarian version is equally competitive with its delicious and well-spiced portions. Achari Tawa Chops (Rs 425) is another surefire starter. Six spicy sticks with a dominant tangy flavour make the dish a must-have. We also sample portions of Lahsooni Murg Tikka (Rs 425), flavoured with garlic, and Pomfret Tikka (Rs 575) with char-grilled fillets, both equally well-done and generously spiced. For the main course, we try Nalli Tariwalla (Rs 475) that is described as a spicy Lucknawi curry. A copper bowl fetches us two lamb shanks anchored in creamy, yoghurt-based gravy. In most eateries in old Lucknow, this dish is a dark- brown curry laden with hot spices, but at Coal, the version is toned down and subtly spiced. Pair it with Ajwain Parantha (Rs 70) for a perfect combo. Lahsooni Palak (Rs 350) takes the humble leaf to a completely new level, with a sprinkling of roasted garlic.

Give a Miss

Kumbh Nawabi (Rs 325) is averagely done. The large chunks of mushrooms completely lose their flavour to the cheese and mint filling. Also, Pomfret Masala Tikka

(Rs 525) with fillets blanketed in tangy onion-tomato gravy fails to bring out any memorable flavours, which the kitchen effortlessly rustles up in other entrées.

Contact: 95124-4645555

Meal for Two: Rs 1,500

Location: Building 6, DLF Cybercity, Gurgaon

Heading: On Razor’s Edge - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistani singer Shafqat Amanat Ali releases his first solo album in the country with a concert

Even the heavy rains on Thursday evening could not deter many from driving to the Siri Fort Auditorium to be a part of Pakistani singer Shafqat Amanat Ali's launch of his first solo album in India. The nine-track contemporary Sufi album Tabeer — which means fulfilment of dreams — was unveiled at the event, with Ali belting out a concert as well. "With this, I have realised my dream of composing the kind of songs that inspire me," smiled Ali. There's one more reason to cheer: even before its launch, the album has soared the charts.

The performance, which lasted for over two hours, had him croon tracks such as Naina, Khairhenya de naal and Dum Ali that feature in the latest compilation. But that wasn't all. He belted out his Bollywood hits Mitwa from Kabhi Alvida Na Kehna and Ye haunsla from Dor, apart from Aankhon ke saagar, Tere bina and Mora saiyan from his earlier album with the Pakistani band Fuzon, which he left in 2004 to pursue a Bollywood career. As the audience screamed encore, Ali got several people on stage to sing along with him. And as the concert drew to an end, the mood mellowed with Allah tero naam, Ishwar tero naam. "If it were up to me I would have had this song on the album too," said a wistful Ali. As part of an initiative by Music Today and The Indian Express, Ali will next be touring Mumbai (September 20) and Kolkata (September 22).

Heading: Abu Bashar in Delhi, being questioned by cops - Indian Express
Content: The charmingly dishevelled Kunal Kapoor is ditching his sexy stubble, persuaded, possibly, by a lucrative deal to go clean shaven. At the launch of a new Gillette razor blade at the Shangri-La Hotel in Delhi, Kapoor and Milind Soman slathered on foam and sexed-up shaving. "I've been considering the clean-shaven look since someone told me it's the fastest way to get girls. Let's see if I get lucky," Kapoor said cheekily. He had stuck to long, curly hair and stubble since his first film, MF Husain's Meenaxi: Tale of Three Cities. Fans needn't be disheartened. In four weeks, Kapoor will return to sporting a stubble and moustache for Rahul Dholakia's Lamhe opposite Sanjay Dutt.

Heading: To secure Delhi, Centre OKs 7,612 posts, 11 more police stations - Indian Express
Content:
Named Qayyamudin and Abdul Rafique, say police, who were entrusted with the job of planting the bombs

The investigation into the Delhi serial blasts got a boost today after the Ahmedabad police brought Mufti Abu Bashar to Delhi for questioning.

Bashar, a suspect in the Ahmedabad blasts, was reportedly involved in the conspiracy of the Delhi blasts. He is also wanted in the Jaipur blasts case.

Bashar reportedly told the Ahmedabad police that he had stayed in Delhi between July 24 and 27. To probe his whereabouts on those days, the Ahmedabad police have brought him to Delhi during his 15-day custody. But he is also being questioned about his involvement in the Delhi blasts and his links with Abu Subhan, who allegedly sent the e-mails containing the terror warnings.

This afternoon, he was questioned by the Gujarat Police at the New Delhi Range office of the Special Cell. Thereafter he was taken to a few other places including Rohini and Okhla.

During questioning, he reportedly named one Qayyamudin and Abdul Rafique, who were entrusted with the job of planting bombs in Delhi on Saturday, said a police officer. The Delhi Police has begun a search for them and several places have been raided already. "We are trying to get to know more about their hideouts in Delhi and how the other suspects in the Delhi blasts," the officer said.

"We need to corroborate his interrogation report and his physical presence will help us to establish a few other facts — like his contacting a non-government organisation and a publishing house in Delhi for financial assistance. These leads will help the investigation into Saturday's serial blasts," said a senior police officer.

Also, he reportedly said his brother Abu Zar, one Danish and Aftab, who are on run, were behind Ahmedabad blasts. Police suspect that they may be involved in the Delhi blasts too.

After Bashar's interrogation, the police might seek the remand of Safdar Nagori — who is in Indore — to question him. Nagori, the general secretary of SIMI, is also wanted in connection with a case of unlawful activities registered against SIMI in 2001.

The Delhi Police had applied for Nagori's remand earlier too and then again after his arrest in Indore, but were turned down by the court both times.

The next chain in the investigation is Shahbaz Husain, a Lucknow-based businessman, arrested for his alleged involvement in the Jaipur blasts. He is being questioned by the Jaipur police about the Delhi blasts.

After his interrogation today, Delhi police also picked up four persons and are questioning them. Yesterday, the police had detained three persons — whose appearance matched the sketches released on Tuesday — from the Janakpuri district centre. All three belong to Sangrur in Punjab.

Heading: Schoolgirl shot dead at South Delhi bus stop - Indian Express
Content:
CCTVs to monitor 58 busy markets, public places, 27 border posts

Finally waking up to the problem of huge vacancies in police forces — one of the main handicaps in fighting terror — the Central government on Thursday announced that it had sanctioned 7,612 new posts in Delhi Police and decided to set up 11 new police stations.

The government also cleared a proposal to procure 130 additional police vehicles for Delhi Police, some of which can act as mobile police stations, Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta told reporters here.

As of now, more than 4,000 posts in Delhi Police, at various levels, are lying vacant. The government had earlier sanctioned 5,000 new posts and 170 new vehicles for Delhi Police to meet their increasing demand in view of the 2010 Commonwealth Games, Gupta said.

Gupta said the decisions regarding Delhi Police were among a number of suggestions made by Home Minister Shivraj Patil at the emergency cabinet meeting on Wednesday to deal with the internal security situation.

He said Patil had also informed the Cabinet meeting about the proposal to bring all major public places in the Capital under video surveillance. The Delhi government had already identified 58 busy markets and other public places, and 27 border posts, which will be brought under extensive CCTV coverage. As of now, only nine markets in Delhi have CCTV surveillance.

"All these projects will be implemented in a time-bound and turnkey manner," Gupta said.

The government will also ask all malls, office complexes, stadia and other buildings to install "basic minimum benchmark" of security, including CCTVs, scanning, Door Frame Metal Detectors (DFMDs) and the like.

"These security systems will be integrated with the central security mechanism of the state and Central government," he said.

Under the Home Ministry's mega-city policing scheme, such measures will be implemented in all major metro cities, Gupta said.

The Cabinet also approved a major strengthening of the intelligence apparatus of the country, including the setting up of a dedicated centre for research and technology under the Intelligence Bureau to facilitate better technological preparedness to meet the increasing sophisticated terror attacks in the country.

The blueprint

Ruling out a new law on the lines of POTA repealed in 2004, the Government on Thursday announced a slew of anti-terror measures in the wake of the Delhi blasts:

* Major public places in Delhi to be under video surveillance. CCTVs to monitor 58 busy points, 27 border posts

* Malls, office complexes, stadia, other buildings to have CCTVs, scanning, Door Frame Metal Detectors

* Govt also cleared a proposal to procure 130 additional police vehicles for Delhi Police, some of which can act as mobile police stations,

* Home Ministry says such measures will be implemented in all major metros

* Dedicated centre for research and technology under the Intelligence Bureau for counter-terror preparedness

Heading: The youngest victim of blasts, 2-yr-old Kishan, was scared of crackers - Indian Express
Content:
Man surrenders in Bahadurgarh, says he shot her because she had spurned his advances

A schoolgirl was shot dead at a crowded south Delhi bus stop on Thursday afternoon.

Neha Gupta, 16, was waiting for a bus back home when two assailants on a motorcycle fired at her and fled.

Neha, the only daughter of Anita and Ashok Gupta, an Aya Nagar tailor, was a Class IX student of Rajkiya Sarvodaya Kanya Vidyalaya in Mehrauli.

Later in the evening, a man, identified as Manish, who allegedly shot her surrendered before the Bahadurgarh police.

Police officers said that Manish said he shot Neha because she turned down his proposal.

DCP South H G S Dhaliwal said that Delhi police are contacting their Haryana counterparts to bring him here for interrogation.

According to police, the incident was reported at 2.50 p.m when a bystander called the PCR. Police rushed her to the AIIMS Trauma Centre where she was declared dead on arrival.

Anita said her daughter was a simple girl, who did not have any enemies.

"I got a call from police at about 3 pm and they informed me that my daughter was very sick. I rushed here (AIIMS) and doctors told me she was shot dead. I could not believe my ears. She was a very silent girl and I don't know about anybody who might have any enmity with her," Anita said.

Heading: Man mistaken for thief, lynched - Indian Express
Content:
Two-year-old Kishan was frightened of fireworks.

The youngest victim of Saturday's serial blasts used to hide behind his mother during weddings and Diwali. The thought of his dying in an explosion was far beyond the wildest nightmares of his parents.

It was a stunning blow when doctors declared him "dead on arrival", when he was taken to the hospital with fatal head injuries. Grandmother Basanti requested the doctor to try to revive him just once more — but in vain.

Kishan's wish to watch the bustle of the Karol Bagh market with his grandparents turned out to be his last.

"I was carrying him when tragedy struck. I was looking the other way when the bomb went off. Something hit Kishan on the back of his head. I failed to register what happened until I saw injured people lying around," says Basanti.

Kishan's grandfather Banwari Lal was also injured, suffering lacerations on his face and head.

Kishan's mother Meera is still suffering fainting spells. His father Ashok is yet to get over the shock.

"I did not tell Meera about Kishan's death on Saturday," said Ashok. "I knew she will not be able to bear it. I told her that he was with his grandparents. Later, when she was talking about him, other family members broke down."

Meera, in fact, had to be taken to a hospital for medical aid.

The only person oblivious to the tragedy is Kishan's sister —four-year-old Arti.

"I have told her that Kishan has gone to America to study and will come back to play with her again when he completes his education," sobbed Ashok, who is yet to receive the Rs 5 lakh compensation announced by the government.

Heading: Cyber goons go ‘phishing’, airport employee poorer by Rs 1.5 lakh - Indian Express
Content:
A 26-year-old man was allegedly beaten to death by a group of people, including a security guard working at a flyover under construction in Nand Nagri area of Northeast district.

According to the police, the incident occurred on Wednesday night when the victim Rajinder went to buy liquor along with one of his co-workers, Dashrath.

"Rajinder, a resident of Baghpat in Uttar Pradesh, worked in an iron shop in Nand Nagri area. He had missed his night train to Baghpat and then returned to the shop," the police said. The police added that when Rajinder came back, he and Dashrath decided to have drinks. "Late in the night, they went out to buy liquor," a senior police officer said.

They reached the liquor shop at 1 am and found it closed. As they were on their way back to their shop, a security guard of a nearby an under-construction flyover, mistook them to be thieves and nabbed them with the help of other labourers working at the site and beat them up.

"Though Dashrath managed to escape, Rajinder was severely beaten up and was then taken into a room by the group of around five men," the police added.

In the morning Dashrath came looking for Rajinder and found him dead in the room.

Police added that the accused security guard is absconding after the incident and they have detained the labourers working at the site on Wednesday night for interrogation.

"We are questioning them about what happened last night and are trying to trace the guard," a senior police officer said.

A case under Section 304 has been registered at the Nand Nagri police station and further investigations are on. The body of the deceased has been sent for postmortem and Dashrath is being questioned about the incident.

The Deputy Commissioner of Police, Northeast district, Surender Singh Yadav said, "We have zeroed in on two or three suspects and the case should be solved soon. Investigations are on and teams have been dispatched to nab the accused."

Heading: Curtain Call - Indian Express
Content:
On August 22, airport employee Parveen Puri received six messages on his mobile from the ICICI bank informing him that Pradeep, Sonali and Neha had accessed his account on the Internet and withdrawn Rs 50,000 each.

Puri froze. That money was his salary and bonus and he did not know any Pradeep, Sonali or Neha.

Since then, Puri has been sprinting between the bank's branch and several police stations trying to get back his money, or even trace where it might have landed. The bank maintains it is a case of 'phishing' which would mean the password to Puri's account fell in wrong hands during one of his electronic transactions. The police — at the Inder Puri station, and even at Connaught Place — have only asked him one question: What is Internet banking? They are yet to register a case. Puri, who works at the IGI Airport, said: "I had left my cell phone with my daughter that day. She told me about the messages."

The first message read: "You have registered Pradeep as a payee. Please enter your unique registration number 441225..." — to complete transaction. There were two other similar messages, registering 'Sonali' and 'Neha' as payees. Then there were three more in the next few seconds saying Rs 50,000 had been debited each to Pradeep, Sonali and Neha's accounts.

"I panicked and immediately called the bank. All other transactions were immediately put on hold," Puri told Newsline. He said: "Next morning I rushed to the police station near my house in Inder Puri. They would not register my complaint and asked me how transactions were made on the Net. The officer also directed me to the station in Connaught Place, which is where the bank's branch is."

Here too, officers refused to register a case, saying it would only be done after proper investigation. The ICICI Bank on the other hand directed Puri to its Mumbai office, which handles the net banking division. There has been no reply from there either. However, the bank offered to compensate Rs 50,000 by September 1, but still no money in his account.

Puri said: "The message asked for the unique registration number each time to confirm payment. This number is crucial for any transaction. The culprit knew this number too. He typed it thrice to take out money."

A spokesperson for the bank told Newsline: "The case is being investigated. We shall take action based on what we find." But Puri has given up hope. "When things went wrong, the bank became faceless. There were no answers," he said.

Heading: Fashion weak - Indian Express
Content:
Feluda takes on the stage as a 50-year-old armchair journalist. Topshe is settled in holy matrimony

A 50-year-old Feluda, is now more of an armchair journalist. Topshe, 37, is about to get married. Mukul, from Sonar Kella is a student of History at Presidency College, while Riku, from Joi Baba Felunath is pursuing a degree in English from Jawaharlal Nehru University. They all unite to match wits with Maganlal Meghraj, arguably Feluda's most dangerous adversary. Sounds like a plot of a hitherto unpublished Feluda story? Think again. This reunion of iconic Satyajit Ray characters, happened a few months ago in Bangalore. Young theatre enthusiast, Srijit Mukherji's play, Feluda Ferot, which was staged at Bangalore this July, is an attempt to make the Feluda series "timeless".

"Like most Bengali youngsters, I grew up reading Feluda. Eventually, I grew out of it. However, I rediscovered the stories recently, and realised that Feluda stories were solely targeted at children. Which is why Ray, refrained from making it complex," says Mukherji who gave up a flourishing career in the IT industry to pursue a career in the arts.

The play was inspired from the famous Kabir Suman song dedicated to Feluda. "The song has haunted me for a long time. All Feluda fans like me must have wondered how Feluda ages? Whether Topshe ever gets married? What happens to Mukul? Feluda Ferot is an attempt to explore these possibilities," adds Mukherji.

For those who have some questions about Feluda's love life, the play has some answers. "We allude to an Irene Adler kind of figure in his life. Like Sherlock Holmes, Feluda too seems to be a one woman man," says Mukherji.

The play is much more than a detective story, Mukherji layers it with different elements like folk traditions of Jatra and Pala Gaan projected through video clippings on the stage. The play also incorporates a short film made by Mukherji. "We wanted the play to be a complex study of the characters. It takes a philosophical look at different ethical issues," adds Mukherji.

The cast includes names that have been associated with Ray or Feluda in some way or the other. Barun Chanda, who plays the elderly Feluda, was the main lead in Ray's Seemabaddha. While Parambrata Chatterjee, who played Topshe in the last two Feluda films, reprises his role in the play. "This is a very different Topshe. He looks different and of course older. But the character is also layered. He is much more than a sidekick in the play," says Chatterjee. Playing the character in a different medium was a "bit difficult" adds, Chattrejee. "Film is my medium, am not very comfortable with theatre. However, it was a learning experience to interpret the character in a different way," he says.

Mukherji, who is in the city to work on another play, had invested all his savings into it. "I was sure it will work," he grins. And it did. With the full support of sizable Bengali population in Bangalore, there is no way Feluda Ferot could have failed. "We plan to stage it in Kolkata early next year. I will try and take it to other cities as well," says Mukherji.

Heading: Top seed Shukrit in last-four - Indian Express
Content:
It was a tepid opening for the HDIL India Couture Week

When the red carpet turns into a wet carpet, part of the venue's tent collapses, and it takes about an hour to get your car to hop across to the adjacent hotel for the after-party—the first day of India Couture Week wasn't exactly the lap de luxe.

If the elements can be forgiven, so be it. But a very senior designer's poorly put out collection was the real dampener. Ritu Kumar, the mistress of ready-to-wear and queen of prints, the designer every burgeoning fashionista dreams of getting married in, showcased a retrospective of all that Indian fashion used to be.

With a Rajasthan fort as backdrop (originality anyone?), Kumar presented a line of lehngas with churi sleeved cholis, chogas, long tunics, kutchi gathered coats worn over divided loose pants, ghararas, khara dupattas with intricate embellishments, interspersed with a line of antique textiles like kalamkari and jaamdaani. What were lovely embroideries and techniques, the treatment left us with a feeling of déjà vu.

The showstopper for the evening was Priyanka Chopra, delicious in a burgundy lehenga and an emerald choli, earned the hoots of Karan Johar and Varun Bahl on the front row, while Shabana Azmi and Javed Akhtar saved their nods for Neha Dhupia and Raima and Riya Sen. The Comeback Clique of Anna Bredmeyer, Sonalika Oberoi and Shyamoli Verma (she really needed a drink to calm her nerves) were still delightful to watch.

Among other guests, Madhu Sapre looked like a tropical tease in all black, Suchitra Pillai dressed like an astronaut and Rozza Catalano beamed in red.Kumar got a standing ovation, but as one Delhi designer told us later: "Out of respect for her age." The after-party was where the young and hip headed. Shah Rukh and Gauri Khan came with Raveena and Anil Thadani, Anil Kapoor, Fardeen Khan, Laila Khan Rajpal, Sohail Khan, Malaika Arora and Ritesh Deshmukh proved there's no shine like the afterglow of Bollywood.
