Heading: EB try to rope in Brazilian Jobson to replace Musah - Indian Express
Content:
'Failed' coach Anup Das in running for junior selection panel!

After weeks of suspense, legendary Bengal skipper of yesteryears Sambaran Banerjee is all set to return to mainstream cricket as the state's chief selector.

If CAB's plans don't turn upside down overnight, the former stumper-skipper is likely to replace Arup Bhattacharjee as the chairman of the senior selection committee. Banerjee, who has served as national selector in the past, is also in the running for the same east zone high-profile job this time round.

Banerjee could be pooled with Saradindu Mukherjee, Kalyan Choudhury and Raju Mukherjee to form the new-look CAB selection panel for the senior circuit. And as for the junior selection panel, Barun Burman — who is currently on the senior committee — is likely to given charge of the junior panel.

Interestingly, the CAB has more or less decided to make former cricketer Anup Das a junior selector, despite protests after Das failed miserably at a recent coaching exam conducted by the BCCI.

Heading: Now, buildings will get green ratings - Indian Express
Content:
East Bengal players satisfied with new coach Stanley Rozario's 'Houghton model' of training

In a bid to strengthen its defence, East Bengal Club is trying to rope in a Brazilian defender. The red-and-golds are targeting 36-year-old defender Jobson Banto Dos Anjos, a seasoned campaigner who has represented sides like Olaria FC, Sao Cristo Vao FC and the more popular Brazilian club Fluminese FC.

East Bengal officials are already comparing Jobson to their former defender Douglas da Silva, who had a couple of succesful seasons with the red-and-gold brigade. The defender is expected to arrive in the city this month-end.

The East Bengal management is desperate to sign in the new foreigner because the club officials are not too sure if Ghanaian defender Suley Musah will be able to perform consistently in the gruelling I-League, starting September 26.

Meanwhile, the East Bengal players are quite excited over new coach Stanley Rozario's initiative to implement national coach Bob Houghton's style of training in the upcoming three-day residential programme at SAI Centre. The team's Brazilian striker Edmilson Marques, who has been struggling to regain form, is looking quite focused ahead of the training stint.

A senior East Bengal player, supporting Rozario's style of training, told The Indian Express: "He has got great communication skills, which is perfect for us. He talks to all the 31 players during every session of training. Nobody feels awkward even if he fails to perform well during training. And following the Houghton style, particularly the shadow-practice tactics, has been of great help for all the players, and has helped us regain our confidence ahead of the I-League."

Coach Rozario's deputy Mridul Banerjee, too, is quite charmed by the new coach's method of treatment of the players and his way of interacting with the entire team.

East Bengal's assistant coach Banerjee said: "First of all, Stanley discusses with me and the goalkeeping coach Debasish Mukherjee on the team's training, strategy, fitness level, etc every single day before the training session gets underway. Secondly, he has already gained acceptability among the players, which in turn has pushed up the team spirit. I am optimistic about the team's performance in the I-League."

Heading: SER fears inability to meet revenue target - Indian Express
Content:
An Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the West Bengal Energy Development Corporation, and The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) is likely to be signed next week, introducing voluntary building rating systems in West Bengal.

The Rs 9 crore-project has been taken up by the corporation in partnership with the Bengal DCL Housing Development Company.

The initiative is called Teri-Griha where ratings will be provided for green buildings with TERI assisting in the technical evaluation.

The rating system will evaluate the environmental performance of a building, based on accepted energy and environmental principles. The guidelines may be revised every three years to accommodate latest scientific developments.

The Science and Technology building that is being developed by the corporation has become the first building to voluntaryly apply for the ratings. It will house various wings of the state science and technology department.

Calcutta's first green building with a manoeuverable, shell-like exterior designed to let in sunshine in winter and deflect heat in summer will come up in Salt Lake's DD block by 2010.

"Work will start in December this year and we hope to complete the project in 18 months," said S.P. Gon Chowdhury, the managing director of the West Bengal Green Energy Development Corporation Ltd.

The building will have vertical and horizontal steel fins that can be controlled from a computerised control room, depending on whether the structure needs to be cooled or heated.

The common green-building practices include taking advantage of renewable energy sources such as sunlight through passive solar, active solar and photovoltaic techniques. Green roofs and rain gardens are popular, too.

Eco friendly building materials like bamboo and straw, lumber, recycled stone, recycled metal and non-toxic, reusable products like linoleum, panels made from paper flakes, baked earth, clay, vermiculite and wood fibre will be used for these buildings.

"We hope to spread eco awareness this way. Recently we have been approached to rate a commercial building that will be developed by Siddha group in Rajarhat," said Gon Chowdhury.

Heading: CBI seeks permission to reopen Nobel theft case - Indian Express
Content:
The South Eastern Railways fears that they might not be able to meet their revenue targets for this financial year, as their freight revenues have gone down.

"There is a total collapse in the loading of iron ore as the industry and export demand has dipped considerably," said Ashok Kumar Jain, General Manager, SER.

The railway authorities believe that the falling iron ore prices in the international market, which have gone down from 140 $ per tonne to 100 $, have caused the decrease in the demand of the ore. They also claim that Australian and Brazilian mines have increased their capacity to mine the metal that has created an adverse affect on Indian markets.

Heading: Defence wants death penalty for Banka murder accused - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Thursday filed an application before the additional chief judicial magistrate (ACJM) of Bolpur seeking permission to reopen the investigation into the theft of Rabindranath Tagore's Nobel medallion after the agency got new leads in the case.

The application was filed by CBI DSP P S Bose before ACJM Hridaya Tulya Bhutia. The court will hear the plea on September 26.

Sources in the CBI said that the agency got a few clues in the case recently. Following which, the agency decided to reopen the investigation, which was discontinued a year ago.

The Nobel medallion and 47 other memorabilia were stolen from Santiniketan on March 25, 2004.

Initially the CID started an investigation. Later, the state government handed over the probe to the CBI. But the CBI discontinued the probe after failing to make a major breakthrough.

Jiban Bagdi (34), who was a prime accused in the case, was stabbed to death on September 11, at Kirnahar village in Birbhum district. The CBI got some new leads while investigating Bagdi's murder.

Heading: No upper age limit for JEE - Indian Express
Content:
The defence lawyer of the Banka couple murder case will plead death penalty for the accused, Kebol Roy. The court was to announce the quantum of punishment on Thursday. Due to the death of a lawyer, the case has been deferred till Saturday.

Public prosecutor Ganesh Maity said the case was among 'rarest of rare' ones. "Roy was the domestic help of the elderly couple, who had placed immense trust on him. Yet, he brutally murdered them. We will demand death penalty for the accused," he added.

The Supreme Court had also used the term 'rarest of rare' case, when Dhananjoy Chatterjee was sentenced to death in the Hetal Parekh rape and murder case.

If the court awards death sentence in the Banka murder case, this will be the second incident in less than thirty days, when a domestic help has been awarded death sentence for murder of the employer.

On August 29, Nikku Yadav ( 24) was sentenced to death by the Alipore sessions court for the murder of Ravinder Kaur Luthra (51), in whose Ballygunge Circular Road apartment he had worked for seven years. Roy also worked as a domestic help for Tarachand Banka and wife Sarda. Both were found brutally murdered in their Camac Street apartment three years ago.

Heading: 3 districts flooded, red alert sounded after tides hit coast - Indian Express
Content:
The West Bengal Joint Entrance Examination Board (WBJEEB) decided on Thursday that there will be no age limit for appearing in the Joint Entrance Examination for admission to engineering and medical colleges of West Bengal.

From now onwards, any student above the age of 17 years can appear in the JEE examination.

Last year the board had fixed the upper age limit to 24 years for both medical and engineering entrance examination in the state, a decision which did not find favour with the students.

"There is no upper age limit prescribed by the Medical Council of India (MCI) or the All India Engineering Entrance Examination, (AIEEE) so the board has decided to do away with any upper age limit," said Siddharth Datta, Chairman, WBJEEB.

According to sources in the board, a section of the members were keen on changing the pattern by introducing a more subjective question pattern. However, the other members opposed this decision. "Since it is September, the board does not want to confuse the students with any change in the examination pattern," said Datta.

The board has formed separate committees to look into the infrastructure of the examination centres, publication of prospectus and admit cards.

After the recommendations of the committee the board will decide on date of issue of forms by the end of the year, said the representatives of the board.

Heading: RPF tears down shops, hawkers cry foul play - Indian Express
Content:
Tidal waves of over 20 feet continued to lash the West Bengal coast, even as the government issued a warning to tourists urging them to stay away from the sea.

State Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta said: "More than 30 villages and 15 towns in the districts of East Midnapore, South and North 24 Parganas have been flooded. Over 60,000 people have been affected and over 10,000 houses have been washed away in the last 24 hours in these districts."

East Midnapore district administration said 40 seaside stalls and 300 fishing boats have been washed away so far. "We have sounded a red alert and asked fishermen to stay away from coasts," said an official.

The worst-hit areas include popular seaside resorts of Digha, Mandarmoni, Shankarpur in East Midnapore, Kakdweep and the Sundarbans in South 24 Parganas.

Dasgupta, who held a meeting with state Relief Minister Murtaza Hussain, said 30 relief camps have been set up in the districts. The state government has also allocated Rs 2 crore towards flood relief and Rs 10 crore for the reparation of affected dams, said the minister, adding that additional funds would also be provided, if needed.

The incessant rains and surging tidal waves were caused by a depression over the Bay of Bengal. The tides have damaged walls at Khejuri, Shankarpur, Contai, Ramnagar, Egra and adjoining coastal areas.

Heavy rainfall also wreaked havoc in parts of the Sunderbans, causing breaches in embankments.

Heading: Govt to crack the whip on unruly employees - Indian Express
Content:
Hawkers near the Howrah Railway Station have claimed that RPF officials pulled down six shops, besides confiscating the goods on Thursday.

Soon after the incident, members of the Hawkers' Union blocked the road leading to the station for more than 30 minutes disrupting train services and causing inconvenience to commuters.

An FIR has been filed against the RPF in Gholabari station.

Sixty armed RPF personnel, accompanied by labourers, allegedly took away the goods in a lorry after destroying the shops.

Howrah Business Committee Secretary Kuntal Basu said: "We had no inkling that the RPF would come and destroy our shops. We have a trade licence from Kolkata Port Trust to use this land. When we asked a RPF personnel why our shops were being pulled down, he said he had been given an order to evict us."

Basu added that if such an incident happens again, the hawkers, who had incurred a loss of over four lakhs, will launch an agitation.

A shopkeeper, Avinash Bhagat, whose shop was damaged, claimed that the RPF took away all his belongings including Rs 30,000 and goods worth Rs 60,000.

He added that the shopkeepers requested the RPF personnel to give them some time to vacate, but they did not pay any heed.

After the roads were blocked for an hour, the Government Railway Police (GRP) arrived on the spot and requested the shopkeepers to withdraw their blockade.

"The hawkers have a trade licence and can use this land. This land doesn't belong to the railway authorities, so the RPF cannot come here and damage the shops. Law and order should be maintained at any cost," said GRP DSP Abdul Aziz.

Senior Divisional Security Commissioner of RPF Raja Ram, however, said: "The hawkers have been given a portion of land by the Kolkata Port Trust, but they have gone beyond the demarcated area. That land belongs to the Railways and therefore the RPF can take action to evict them."

Heading: Some good news at last: World Bank office in city - Indian Express
Content:
State Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta said action will be taken against the employees, who had assaulted an assistant secretary during office hours in the Writers' Buildings earlier this month.

The employees are members of the newly-floated Mahakaran Sangram Committee (MSC), which has been involved in several cases of vandalism in the Writers' Buildings in the last three weeks.

On September 9, the accused employees had allegedly thrashed Swapan Moitra, Assistant Secretary (Finance), in his office. Immediately after the incident, Dasgupta had announced a departmental enquiry against the guilty. Sources said the state coordination committee, the pro-government employees union, had asked the administration to take action against the employees, who were the members of its rival group.

On Thursday, Dasgupta said the committee has submitted its report, which held the seven employees guilty of assaulting Moitra. "Departmental action will be taken against them," he added.

If the Left Front government punishes its employees, it will be a rare instance in the annals of its governance. Dasgupta's comments evoked sharp reaction of the employees. An MSC leader accused the state coordination committee of following a vendetta against its members.

"The committee leaders are annoyed with us because a large number of their members have left their organisation and joined the MSC," he added.

The CPM-backed coordination committee leader Manoj Guha, however, criticised the Sangram committee saying that it has violated the decorum of the Writers' Buildings.

"Effigies of the chief minister are being burnt in the administrative headquarters of the state," he said.

Heading: Subrata removed from Cong post - Indian Express
Content:
Amid the gloom at the Writers' Buildings with Karnataka offering land to relocate Tata Motors' small car manufacturing plant, came one good news: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) — a part of the World Bank — will set up its office in Kolkata.

The Kolkata office will cater to the entrepreneurs of the entire eastern region. This will be the fourth office of IFC in India — the other three are in Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai.

The international organisation, which finances and provides advice for private sector ventures and projects in developing countries, is not concerned with the developments in Singur. "This is an issue between the state government and the Tata Motors. We have nothing to do with it. We believe there are a lot of business opportunities in the state, which is developing steadily," said Paolo M. Martelli, Director, South Asia, IFC.

Martelli led a four-member delegation, which met Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee. The delegation later met Finance Minister Asim Dasgupta.

According to government officials, the chief minister sought IFC's help in sectors like silk, jute, agro-business, apparel park, health, technical education, self-help group and leather. Martelli, on his part, offered assistance in cluster development of industries.

The official also said the IFC was doing a study called 'Sub-national business' in which Kolkata had been identified as one of the places which has prospects of doing excellent business.

Heading: Delhi NGO petitions HC to keep Nano project in Bengal - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee (WBPCC) leader Subrata Mukherjee was removed from his post of official spokesperson for the party on Thursday.

This came after Mukherjee had participated in a Trinamool Congress rally in Singur last Tuesday, where he had joined party chief Mamata Banerjee on the dais. Mukherjee had joined the anti-land acquisition rally, saying he supported the movement for return of land to unwilling farmers.

According to sources in the Congress, WBPCC president Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi was miffed with Mukherjee's action. On the day he attended the rally, Dasmunsi had said Mukherjee had participated in the rally on his own. "The state Congress has nothing to do with it," Dasmunsi had stated.

Mukherjee may be replaced by Pradip Bhattacharya, who has close relations with senior party leader Pranab Mukherjee, said a source.

Mukherjee's removal could prompt him to join Trinamool again. Although he had started out as a Congressman, he had defected to the Trinamool and had served as the mayor of Kolkata. Later, he had returned to the Congress.

Heading: Singur phones ignore Mamata, don a Tata name - Indian Express
Content:
The Coalition for Rural Empowerment Group, a Delhi-based NGO, filed a public interest litigation (PIL) in the Calcutta High Court on Thursday seeking a directive to the state government to ensure that Tata Motors does not leave Singur.

On September 2, the Tata Motors had announced the suspension of work on the small car project for an indefinite period, after Trinamool activists blocked the entrance gate to the Nano factory on September 1.

As a result, a bus carrying the engineers and employees of the factory had to leave the project area.

The petitioner demanded that Tata Motors resume production at the earliest and expressed hope that the state government will remove all obstructions hampering the progress of the project.

The petition said it was the duty of the state government to create a favourable atmosphere at Singur so that production proceeds smoothly, as the Trinamool Congress activists had created disturbance at the factory site from the last week of August.

Describing the Tata Motors as one of the biggest automobile companies in the world, the petitioner pointed out that the development of a society as well as the state was not possible without industrialisation.

The small car project at Singur is a part of the industrialisation drive of the state. So the state government should ensure that production at the factory proceeds normally as this project will change the social and economic scenario at Singur.

The PIL is likely to come up for hearing before a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court on Friday.

Heading: Metro Rail progresses, 3 contracts awarded - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Metro One Private Limited (MMOPL), a special purpose vehicle formed to construct and operate the Versova- Andheri- Ghatkopar (VAG) Metro Rail project, has awarded three major contracts — for track work, the communication system and for an automatic fare collection system.

The MMOPL, which comprises the Mumbai Metropolitan Regional Development Authority (MMRDA), Reliance Energy Limited and French transport firm Veolia, awarded the contracts for laying of tracks to VNC Rail One of Germany, for the Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) to Indra of Spain and for the communication system for the corridor to Thales of France.

Indra is known to have worked with Metro projects in Madrid, Lisbon and Shanghai, Barcelona and Athens. Thales is a giant in defence and communication systems, which has also worked on the communication system of the Delhi Metro.

"The proposed communication systems would entail the use of closed circuit camera system at all stations, within the trains and in the depot," said an MMOPL spokesperson.

However, the Mumbai Metropolitan Regional Development Authority (MMRDA) is still to hand over Right of Way for construction to the MMOPL on a 3.5-km strech. Also, MMOPL is still to receive clearances from the Western Railway for construction of a bridge across the suburban railway tracks at Andheri station.
