Heading: Blood donation drive as part of IIT-B’s cultural festival - Indian Express
Content:
The police recovered the body of a twenty-year-old woman behind bushes near Dharavli village in Malwani on Thursday morning.

According to the Malwani police, they received a call from the police control room at 10 am informing them of a body of a woman who was wearing a saree and a blouse, which was discovered in the bushes at the Dharavli village near the Aksa Beach. "From what could be seen, the woman had been strangled with a rope and there were marks on her throat. We also found a rope nearby, which might have been used to strangulate her, said senior police inspector Jaywant Hargude from the Malwani police station. The body has been sent to Bhagwati Hospital for post-mortem. "We asked the people in the village from where the body was found, but no one in the area could indentify the body. We have registered a case of murder and are conducting further enquiries into the matter," added Hargude.

Heading: Bandra Kurla Complex: Bidders get offers, finally - Indian Express
Content:
Mood Indigo team will also stage motivational street plays

If you thought Mood Indigo (Mood I), the annual cultural festival of the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay (IIT-B) was just about fun, games and grandeur, then you might be mistaken.

For the first time in the history of Mood I, IIT-B is organising a blood donation drive as part of Mood I celebrations.

The students of IIT kick started the blood donation drive at the IIT-B campus on Thursday. Touted as the largest college cultural festival in Asia with a budget that is expected to touch 1 crore this year, Mood I will be held from December 20-23.

The drive called Khoon Chala (a song from the popular Bollywood film Rang De Basanti) will encourage not just the 25,000 strong IIT-B community on the campus to donate blood but will also reach out to more than 60, 000 students from 500 colleges who are expected at the IIT campus during the four day Mood I festival in December.

The campaign will also be taken to 18 colleges in the city.

The drive will be conducted in three phases. In the first phase, the campaign will target around 5000 IITians across all the 13 hostels on campus. In the second phase, it will be conducted in 18 colleges and shopping malls. The third phase will comprise a blood donation and thalassemia detection camp during Mood I. The Mood I team will also stage motivational street plays to sensitize people towards blood donation.

The Mood I team has also produced a short film on the blood donation drive.  

Ishank Gupta, core group member, media and PR, Mood I says, "When the need arises you have to run from pillar-to-post because there are more blood seekers than donors. For this reason, we at Mood Indigo aim at inviting eligible people to come forward for this noble cause. If we can motivate such a large number of students to participate in Mood I, we can influence them to participate in this drive too."

Organising such a large-scale campaign is an onerous task in itself. As Ishank puts it, "We (students) had to take permissions from several authorities. We had to manage everything on our own.  But inthe end we were able to rope in several blood banks and colleges from across the city."

Apart from the usual host of events including dance, dramatics, speaking, literary arts, fine arts, music, workshops, exhibitions,interactive sessions and prom nights, Mood I will feature performances by Limca book of records holders, a Poland based band that uses a dining table embedded with musical instruments to create music, an art street, on the lines of the Kala Ghoda Festival, a vintage car exhibition, fencing and archery games, ice wall climbing, wind tunnel among others.

Heading: Alleged Shakeel aide Bacchi Singh shot at, injured - Indian Express
Content:
After a prolonged deadlock over the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) plots that were put on the block in March this year, the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) has finally handed over the allotment letter to the winning bidders. Two of the plots on auction had no takers, while one commercial plot had received a sole bid of Rs 826 crore from Jet Airways. In case of the two residential plots Starlight Systems (a collaboration of Piramal Group and Suntech Realty) had quoted the highest bid of Rs 248 crore for each. As the realty market plunged further, both the bidders had developed a cold feet and expressed their inability to pay up as per the MMRDA's payment schedule of three months from the time offer letter was placed. Both firms had asked for time until November-December to pay up. The MMRDA was in a sticky situation as it had to choose between setting a precedent of bending rules or cancelling the deal. However, the MMRDA was bailed out of taking a call as the offer letter could not be placed until approved by the authority headed by the Chief Minister. While MMRDA Additional Commissioner Milind Mhaiskar confirmed that the offer letter has been handed over recently, a senior MMRDA official said, "The delay occurred as the authority meeting was adjourned a couple of times due to various reasons. It was finally held last week where the proposal was sanctioned." The bidders will now be required to make the complete payment by December, fifty percent payment within a month and the rest over the next two months.

Kamal Khetan, managing director of Sunteck Realty said, "We have received the offer letter just four days back and will decide whether to go ahead with the deal. Considering the current market scenario, we had asked for at least one year's time from the date of allotment to make the payment. Anyway we still have a month to decide."

Officials from Jet Airways, who had earlier announed plans to set up the company's global headquarters at the site, refused to comment.

Heading: Hong Kong ship hijack: Wait becomes unbearable for hostage’s family - Indian Express
Content:
Some unidentified persons opened fire at alleged Chota Shakeel aide Dharamraj Ramnarayan alias Bacchi Singh on Thursday afternoon near Amboli. Bacchi Singh, who is suspected to have links with Chhota Shakeel, is also an accused in a land grabbing case in which dismissed encounter specialist Pradeep Sharma was also allegedly involved.

According to the DN Nagar Police, the incident occurred at 4.40 pm. Four persons who are suspected to be shooters of the Chhota Rajan gang started firing indiscriminately on the Honda City car (MH-04-2233), in which Singh was traveling at Amboli, said the police.

"Singh was out to buy some fruits. As soon as he parked his vehicle near Amboli Naka, four persons came from the opposite direction and fired at him. They then fled from the place," said ACP (DN Nagar division) Dilip Suryavanshi.

According to Suryavanshi, a police team soon reached the spot and rushed Singh to nearby Sanghvi Hospital situated at Lokhandwala in Andheri. "Singh sustained two bullet injuries. While one bullet hit on his left hand palm, the other bullet brushed his back. According to the doctors, he is out of danger," he said.

When asked about the possible reason that could have led to the firing, he said, "We're not sure about the exact reason. But, since he has SRA projects in Amboli, we're investigating whether he had any rivals in the projects. A case of attempt to murder has been registered at the DN Nagar police station and we would be soon preparing sketches of the shooters," Suryavanshi said. Another police official said on condition of anonymity that the shooters could be the men of Chhota Rajan, since Singh was allegedly close to his rival Chhota Shakeel, a trusted lieutenant of underworld don Dawood Ibrahim.

Heading: Parliamentary panel to assess airport modernisation - Indian Express
Content:
The Somalian Pirates hijacked MT Stolt Valor off the Gulf of Aden on September 15, after its last port call at Suez Canal. The Directorate General of Shipping was intimated by the managers of the vessel on September 16 that the vessel with a cargo of over 23,000 tonnes of oil products was hijacked and 22 crew members were taken into custody.

Ever since Rosary Fernando received the news of the hijack of the vessel, on which his brother-in-law Pani Rayan Lobo was an employee, he has been trying to soothe and provide comfort to his troubled family.

The vessel was supposed to reach Mumbai and the last reports have confirmed that the crew is safe. "I have to take care of my wife who is worried about her brother's safety and on the other hand I have to keep my in-laws family continuously updated over the phone," said Fernando, a hospital employee.

Lobo, who started working aboard ships five years ago, hails from Tuticorin in Tamil Nadu. He is married and has a four-year-old son. He had boarded the ship in February and would call his family every month. The family received his last call in July and according to Fernando the vessel was expected to reach Mumbai this month. However, his father received a call from one of the company's officials on September 15 about the hijack and he immediately informed Fernando asking him to make further enquiries. Since then Fernando has been making frantic visits to the offices of the Ebony Ship Management in Nerul and Andheri and the National Union of Seafarers of India hoping to get some news about the hijack.

"The hijackers have not put forth any demands, so far, and this waiting period is unbearable. Till now I have managed to make the family members stay in Tuticorin.They are greatly concerned about Lobo's safety and sit next to the phone hoping to get a positive news," said Fernando. Meanwhile, the Somali pirates have released two hostages after two weeks of holding them captive. The hostages, both French national were in a sailing boat which was hijacked in the Gulf of Aden on September 2. The entire rescue operation was conducted by the French military. The operation left one pirate dead and six were captured.

Heading: Robbers who broke into comedian Raju Shrivastav’s house convicted - Indian Express
Content:
The Parliamentary committee on transport, tourism & culture headed by Rajya Sabha and Communist Party of India (CPI-M) politburo member Sitaram Yechury arrived in Mumbai on Thursday to assess and get a feedback on various issues that have been generated by Mumbai airport's privatisation programme.

The committee will meet staff members of the state owned Airport Authority of India (AAI) and hear their grievances as the AAI Union is opposed to the entire privatisation process.

Incidentally, it was only last month that the committee had lambasted private airport developers of the Mumbai and Delhi airports where, according to its report, "passenger space —on the airport premises— had shrunk considerably to make way for commercial activities for private developers."

Heading: Mumbai not to host beer fest this year due to shortage of hotel rooms - Indian Express
Content:
A Sessions court on Thursday convicted two of the three robbers who broke into comedian Raju Shrivastav's house in May last year.

After the incident, Shrivastav's 11-year-old daughter Antara was bestowed with National award for foiling the robbery.

Of the two accused convicted on Thursday, Zulfiqar Choudhary was sentenced to seven years imprisonment on the serious charge of "attempt to commit robbery when armed with a deadly weapon" under section 398 read with 34 of the Indian Penal code as he was found in possession of a gun.

Another accused Gohar alias Raja Jamil Sayyed got a year in jail for "attempt to commit robbery." However, mastermind Sagir Ahmed Shafrulla alias Rizwan, who managed to flee, is still at large.

On May 30, 2007, three people under the pretext of them being dress designers entered Marigold building in Oshiwara where Raju Shrivastav was living with his family.

They even showed samples of some embroidery works, after which the watchman let them in. At Shrivastav's fifth floor residence they repeated the same story to Raju's wife, Shikha.

According to the confession given by Choudhary and Sayyed, the attack was pre-planned and they knew Shrivastav was out of India on an assignment at that time.

Shrivastav's wife in her deposition told the court that when they identified themselves as dress designers she believed them and allowed them in and went to the kitchen to fetch water.

As soon as she came back, two of them — armed with knife and a country made gun tried to gag her. The third robber stood guard at the door. On hearing Shikha's cries, Shrivastav's daughter Antara, who was in the bedroom, bolted herself from inside and screamed for help.

After hearing Antara's cries other residents, two beat marshals and constables patrolling the area along with the watchman jumped to action and managed to nab two of the three accused.

The prosecution examined 18 witnesses in all, The seizures and confession of the accused aided the prosecution process.

Heading: Six youths arrested for raping minor - Indian Express
Content:
OKTOBERFEST , the German beer fest that was supposed to be held this October in Mumbai and Goa for the first time, has been cancelled - thanks to non-availability of hotel rooms in Mumbai and other issues that played spoilsport.

Earlier,as reported by Newsline in August, Mumbai and Goa were all set to witness the German extravaganza — better known as the world's greatest party— wherein over six million tourists from across the world visit Germany to lay their hands on freshly brewed German beer.

The beer is manufactured by the top six breweries in Germany, colloquially called 'the big six'.

According to director of the Bangalore-based GVCM Trading Company Chris Pohl, who is the representative of over 17 German brands in India and the brain behind the entire project of bringing this festival to the country, the event has been postponed to October 2009 due to an array ofreasons.

"The hotel which was going to hold the fest has no vacancy to hold the activities during the suggested time and we are planning to hold it in October, 2009," said Pohl. Instead of the beer-fest, a small scale Bavarian film festival, which anyhow will have beer flowing, will be taking place, he said.

But, the postponement of the event does bring into picture the limited hotel infrastructure in the city, and that too during the peak season— from September to March — because of which the extravaganza could not be accommodated.

This is despite the fact that demand has not been so buoyant compared to the previous years.

"Comparing the industry trend in Mumbai, this year has been remarkably different in terms of room rates and occupancy because of the general downturn in the global economy," said Manish Tolani, director of sales at the J W Marriott Hotel, Mumbai. "Still everyone is quite positive," Tolani added.

Tolani does agree on the shortage of hotel rooms in Mumbai and said that with each passing year starting next year and new properties coming up, more hotel rooms will be added to Mumbai to cater to the rising demand. "Even as demand is on the decline and with most corporate clients in a cost control mode, Mumbai will get another 1100 five star hotel rooms next year," he said.

Despite this, the event could not be accommodated. But, Chris Pohl claimed other reasons for the cancellation of the fest. "There are various other issues. Lack of hotel rooms is just one of them," Tolan said.

Heading: After cave-in tragedy, corporators slam civic administration for using paver blocks - Indian Express
Content:
Six youths were arrested by the Dadar police on Thursday morning for raping a 15-year-old girl in a house at Prabhadevi. According to the Dadar police, the incident took place on September 13 when Seema (name changed), a resident of Virar, came to Dadar after visiting the Lalbaugcha Raja. "After offering prayers to the Lalbaugcha Raja, Seema went to the Siddhivinayak Temple in Dadar where she met the two accused— Kishore and Pradeep — who sell flowers outside the temple. She was friendly with them as she knew them already," said Senior Police Inspector Madhukar Sankhe of the Dadar police station. According to Sankhe, the two youths lured her to their house in Prabhadevi and raped her.

In her complaint, Seema said that she was then taken to a house in Worli, where the other four persons— Abhishek Joshi, Papu alias Sandep Shukla, Lovely alias Siddhesh Chauhan and Prasad Gawale— also raped her. "All of them sell flowers near the Siddhivinayak Temple. Seema was imprisoned in the house in Worli till September 17 and repeatedly raped. She was also threatened with dire consequences, if she tried to escape or seek help," the police said.

The incident came to light when one of the six accused reportedly took Seema for a ride on his motorbike in the wee hours of September 17.

Some policemen, who were patrolling the area stopped the couple on suspicion and took them to the Dadar police station for enquiry. "When quizzed, she told the officers what had happened over the past few days. Following her statement, we arrested all the other five accused from Worli. All the six youths with ages ranging from 19 to 22 have been booked for rape and remanded to police custody till September 25," said the police.

"However, we suspect that the girl had gone willingly with them and was not forcibly imprisoned as she had claimed. However, as she is a minor, the youths were arrested on rape charge," said an official on conditions of anonymity.

Heading: Bank employee among five arrested for cheating, forgery - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after a paver block side-strip at the Saat Rasta near Mahalaxmi caved in claiming three lives, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) headquarters was abuzz with 'politics on paver blocks'. While elected representatives slammed the use of paver blocks and demanded two-minute condolence for the victims, the civic administration countered it by saying that the same corporators had demanded the conversion of cement concrete roads into paver blocks.

The discussion on the paver blocks and its poor quality dominated the general body meeting of the civic body on Thursday. "The paver blocks are just like quick fix cosmetic surgery and do not have long life. They have become death gallows. The officials who favoured the use of low-quality paver blocks should be identified soon," said BJP leader Bhalchandra Shirsat.

However, replying to the queries and protest of the corporators, Additional Municipal Commissioner, R A Rajeev said the civic administration had received a number of letters from the corporators demanding the conversion of CC roads into paver blocks. "As many as 165 letters are with my department," he said.

While, many corporators said the paver blocks should not be laid on the complete length of main roads and internal roads, the BMC said the delay in getting permission from the traffic department to carry out the work of CC road forced them to use paver blocks. Rajeev said the work of the CC roads was to be carried out at 240 sites. "However, at two roads in Vile Parle and Borivali, we had to go ahead with the use of paver blocks as there was a delay in traffic department's approval."

Corporators, however, expressed their dissatisfaction with the low-quality and ill-maintained paver blocks. "The paver blocks at the Scion Circle is already sunk below the ground level and the junction can cave in at any moment. Despite informing the ward officer and civic officials, no action has been initiated," said Upendra Doshi.

The BMC has now assured the corporators that paver block will be laid only where it's necessary. "As per the STAC committee guidelines framed in July 2008, paver blocks will be used at side strips — where utility cables are laid — and on the road junction," Rajeev said.

Heading: Crime Branch busts call girl racket; two youths, one girl arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The Oshiwara police recently arrested five people, three from Dharwad, Karnataka, including a former branch manager of ICICI Bank in Lokhandwala, in connection with cheating and forgery, involving false transfer of money from two joint accounts in the ICICI branch at Lokhandwala.

The arrested accused are Salim Sirhaddi, Suresh Kulkarni, Bharat Mudgal, who transferred money to an account in Dharwad in Salim's name, Chetan Anand a former clerk at ICICI Lokhandwala, and Panchanan Bhushan a former branch manager of the bank. A sixth person is also suspected to be involved in the case who has been identified as Rashid.

The investigation was started by the Oshiwara police after a complaint was filed by Jahir Sheikh (21) a manager of ICICI Bank. They discovered that cash worth Rs 16, 80,000 was missing from the joint account of their clients Nikhil Shah and Sonal Shah and cash worth Rs 41, 22,000 was also missing from another joint account of Darshana and Umesh Parekh. The accused have been charged with cheating and forgery. Salim, Kulkarni and Mudgal had opened two accounts one in Salim's name and another in the name of Messrs Inform Technologies in Co-operative Bank, College Road, Dharwad and and State Bank of India College Road ,Dharwad respectively. After this they took a RTGS form (used for transfer of funds) from ICICI Bank and transferred the funds from the respective account to their accounts. This is where Bhushan and Anand came in. They furnished the details of the victims' accounts and provided the other three with documents so they could forge their signatures, thus making the procedure seem legal. Anand and Bhushan also received Rs 3 lakh as commission from them.

"After investigations we came to know of Anand's and Bhushan's role first. We arrested them on September 5," said senior police inspector Kiran Sonone from Oshiwara police station. "They then gave Salim's and his accomplices account numbers and confessed to their crimes. We then obtained Salim's address from the banks and arrested him from Dharwad on September 9. After interrogating him we picked up Kulkarni and finally Mudgal on September 13. All of them have confessed to the crime and, so far, we have recovered Rs 50,000," added Sonone. About the accused who is still at large, he said.

"We are still searching for him and confirming if he exists since they say he has all the money with him."

Heading: Couture Week or marketing gig? - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP-led MCD is in open conflict with the Delhi government with the Mayor, Arti Mehra, protesting today against the transgression of her powers by Chief Minister Sheila Dixit.

Mehra has written to the Lieutenant Governor seeking his intervention in the matter. "We have requested him to take up the issue and direct the CM not to encroach upon the domain of the Mayor and jurisdiction of the Mayor's office," said Mehra. In the letter, the Mayor alleged that Dikshit as CM joined an organisation named Asia Network of Mega Cities-21 which is primarily an organisation of the heads of major cities of Asia. Dikshit has signed an MOU with various other cities including Tokyo, which, as alleged by the Mayor, is not correct. Since the organisation is of Asian cities, the Mayor of Delhi should have been involved in the signing of any MOU. The CM did not even inform the Mayor at the time of signing of these agreements, she mention in her letter.

Mehra also protested against the fact that the CM entered into an agreement with the Mayor of Yerevan, Armenia, to name a street in Anand Niketan as Armenia Street, as the naming of streets falls under the jurisdiction of the Mayor.

"We will write to the International Mayors' Forum explaining to them Delhi's administrative structure and informing them that all MoUs should be signed with the Mayor alone," said Mehra.

Heading: Blare your horn, pay Rs 2000: Rs 100 fine set to turn history - Indian Express
Content:
HDIL lets its slip show; designers are paid to participate instead being charged

India's first couture week is tripping on its baby steps. Not only is the show earning the brickbats of designers and media alike for its shoddy show area and poor-quality organisation, a few designers have revealed that they were actually paid to present fashion shows here.

At fashion weeks around the world, whether ready-to-wear or menswear, designers have to pay a participation fee. Many are rejected on other grounds as well such as not enough experience, not enough selling points and the like. But to actually offer money for participation takes away from the credibility of the event and makes it an expensive but brilliant marketing gig for the sponsor company.

In this case, it is HDIL, a real estate development house better known for its page-three proprietor, Sunny Dewan Wadhawan and his wife Anu. The designers from Mumbai have been paid Rs 20 lakh to put up a show while designers from Delhi have been paid Rs 24 lakh each.

"I was paid Rs 24 lakh," says Varun Bahl, one of fashion's newest faces. "We were paid because they only gave us a structure for a stage and we had to take care of the models, choreographers, sets, hair and makeup personnel." Bahl adds that they didn't pay a participation fee at all and "for the first three years, this seems to be the structure".

The HDIL sponsored India Couture Week is taking place in Mumbai from September 16 to September 21. It has some of India's biggest designers showing their excessive and elaborate designs and the cost of an average outfit is Rs 3 lakh. Some of the designers invited are Tarun Tahiliani, JJ Valaya, Pallavi Jaikishen, Manish Malhotra, Rohit Bal, Suneet Varma and Ritu Kumar.

Even though the India Couture Week is a tie-up with the Fashion Design Council of India (FDCI), the country's official governing fashion body, the designers are hand-picked by HDIL which has a three-year contract with FDCI. Some names, like Jaikishen and Malhotra, are not registered with the FDCI either. "They have just registered themselves as FDCI members," corrects Sunil Sethi, the new FDCI president, "But HDIL did have an independent, anonymous jury to choose designers. Ninety per cent of these designers would have made our list anyway."

"We haven't been paid a single penny," says Suneet Varma, who's replicated the sets of his Midsummer's Night Dream collection he was to present in Delhi last Saturday, and cancelled on account of the bombings. "The remuneration is for the production costs. Anywhere in the world, you need to be invited to take part in a couture week and you cannot just pay to get in," he said, adding that he has previously participated in couture weeks in Rome, Hong Kong, Shanghai and even Paris.

But Sumeet Nair, whose brainchild the India Couture Week was while he was still executive director of the FDCI until three months ago, had said that the participation fee for designers would be Rs 12 lakh each.

"Because this is the first couture week, we wanted to make it larger than life where production is concerned," justifies Sethi. "Let's say, instead of taking Rs 4 crore from the sponsor ourselves, we asked them to pay the designers. Going forward, we are also going to put up a set of rules of who can be called a couture designer."

Heading: Hoax e-mail leads to  bomb scare at railway stations - Indian Express
Content:
The penalty for excessive honking is set to be increased to Rs 2,000 for every offence. According to an affidavit filed by the State government before the Bombay High Court in response to a PIL filed by city-based NGO Awaaz Foundation on the issue of noise pollution, the State Transport Department is planning to increase the fine for honking in silence zones from the current Rs 100 to Rs 2000.

The proposal to increase the fine was discussed at a meeting held by Chief Secretary Johny Joseph to review the measures taken by various civic authorities and the police for reducing noise pollution. According to the minutes of the meeting, the fine for a first-time offender would be Rs 1,000 while for others it would be Rs 2000. The decision would require an amendment to the Motor Vehicles Act and a proposal has been sent to the Central government, the affidavit said.

According to the affidavit, the State government will allocate responsibilities to different government departments regarding the various aspects of noise pollution.

The affidavit states that various agencies like MMRDA and MSRDC would be given the responsibility of curbing noise from numerous infrastructure projects and traffic is to be regulated by the traffic police and the RTO. There are also plans to carry out noise mapping, which is to be done by various agencies.

The affidavit further states that since 2004, the traffic police have collected fines of Rs 26,80,700 for honking and registered 37,259 cases. Joseph directed during the meeting that the Home Department provide adequate number of decibel metres to the police.

As for fire crackers and loud-speakers, the police department has been directed to take action suo-motu, the affidavit says. The government will soon come out with the Bombay Prohibition and Regulation of Fireworks Rules, 2008, which has provisions for dealing with noise pollution due to firecrackers.

A Division bench of Chief Justice Swatanter Kumar and Justice A P Deshpande has now adjourned the hearing till November 28.

Heading: City tackles threats, perceived and fake - Indian Express
Content:
Hoax calls are proving to be a tedious affair for the Railway security agencies, especially the state managed Government Railway police (GRP) and the Railway Protection Force (RPF). The Railways today got yet another threat message of bombs at Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus (CST), Churchgate and Borivali stations.

"A television channel received the threat. We got the information from the city police and the state Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) is looking into this," said Mumbai Railway Commissioner of Police A K Sharma. "The mail, sent by a group which has identified itself as 'All Mujahiddin', sent the message saying that the three stations on the suburban rail network would be bombed," said a senior RFP official.

"We are investigating the matter and are probing the source of the e-mail. However, it doesn't seem this e-mail was sent by those who sent the Ahemdabad terror e-mail," said Parambir Singh, Additional Commissioner of Police, ATS. As soon as the Railway police were alerted, both the GRP and RPF geared into action with the bomb detection squads and dog squad.

Security was beefed up at the three stations to avoid any untoward incident and spots like dust bins were thoroughly checked. "We are checking the Churchgate and Borivali stations after the alert. But apart from it, we are also keeping a vigil on other important stations like Dadar, Andehri, Bandra and Mumbai Central," said M K Bhosale, DCP (Western Railway).

"We are conducting the regular check-up as we normally do after we receive an alert message. We are also taking the GRP's help for the check-ups," said S D Padhi, senior divisional security commissioner with Central Railway. Central Railway alone got six threat calls and messages in the month of August, all of which turned out to be hoaxes. today's threat is the third hoax call received by Central Railway this month.

To curb the menace of hoax calls, B S Sidhu, the chief security commissioner with Central Railway, had prepared a proposal which asked hoax calls to be declared 'terror activity' and demanded more stringent action against such callers. The proposal is currently with the Union Railway Ministry for discussion.

Heading: Linking up, by road & rail - Indian Express
Content:
Surprise checks proposed at city hospitals

The Mumbai Metro One Private Limited (MMOPL), a special purpose vehicle formed to construct and operate the Versova- Andheri- Ghatkopar (VAG) Metro Rail project, has awarded three major contracts — for track work, the communication system and for an automatic fare collection system.

The MMOPL, which comprises the Mumbai Metropolitan Regional Development Authority (MMRDA), Reliance Energy Limited and French transport firm Veolia, awarded the contracts for laying of tracks to VNC Rail One of Germany, for the Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) to Indra of Spain and for the communication system for the corridor to Thales of France.

Indra is known to have worked with Metro projects in Madrid, Lisbon and Shanghai, Barcelona and Athens. Thales is a giant in defence and communication systems, which has also worked on the communication system of the Delhi Metro.

"The proposed communication systems would entail the use of closed circuit camera system at all stations, within the trains and in the depot," said an MMOPL spokesperson.

However, the Mumbai Metropolitan Regional Development Authority (MMRDA) is still to hand over Right of Way for construction to the MMOPL on a 3.5-km strech. Also, MMOPL is still to receive clearances from the Western Railway for construction of a bridge across the suburban railway tracks at Andheri station.

Heading: Ravinder’s anticipatory bail plea dismissed - Indian Express
Content:
Plan to connect trans-harbour bridge, freeway

The State government is planning to provide an approach to the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link (MTHL), which will link Sewri in mainland Mumbai to the Nhava across the creek, with the Eastern Freeway project, which will run from the Chatrapati Shivaji museum to Ghatkopar. Senior State government officials said funding for work on the eight-lane bridge, which is estimated to cost around Rs 8,000 crore, would be met in phases through sources like a hike in the FSI in areas which will benefit from the 22-km bridge, the kitty of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), financial institutions and auction of toll rights.

They added that the approach road to MTHL from the Eastern Freeway would ensure better connectivity to Navi Mumbai and surrounding areas without vehicle owners coming on to city roads and said the company working on the design of the MTHL had been asked to incorporate it in the plan.

The bridge will be the fourth largest in the world and connect Sewri in mainland Mumbai to Nhava across the creek and provide access to growth centres like the southern part of Navi Mumbai, the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT), the proposed SEZs in the region and the international airport near Kharghar.

The Rs 336 crore work on the nine-km Eastern Freeway, which will initially connect the museum to the Anik Panjarpole link road has started, and will be subsequently extended to Ghatkopar at a total cost of around Rs 550 crore in the next phase. The 22-km project, which is being funded under the Centre's Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) aims to provide better access between the city and eastern suburbs, and linking it to the MTHL will provide faster connectivity with Navi Mumbai and surrounding regions.

"A hike (in the FSI) will be given depending on the potential of the area on the Navi Mumbai side," said the official, adding that areas like Panvel, Karjat and even places beyond that would come under the zone of influence of the bridge and would benefit.

"We are working out the quantum of FSI hike," said the official, adding that it would be extended to all the areas affected by the bridge. Expressions of interest (EoIs) have already been invited for the project and the bids are to be submitted in the last week of November, with the letter of acceptance for the selected party being awarded in the last week of January. The state government plans to start work by January 26.

The government is in the process of procuring land for the approach roads and casting yards, and officials said the bulk of land on the Nhava side was with the City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) while the rest would be acquired. The Mumbai Port Trust (MbPT) has also approved the grant of land for casting yards at the Sewri end. The proposed approach road will pass through the MbPT area.

In June, the State Cabinet Sub-Committee on Infrastructure had decided that the work on the sea link would be undertaken by the government itself without the public private partnership (PPP) route, after the bids submitted by the two Ambani brothers in the fray were found "unrealistic".

The cable-stayed MTHL bridge will also save 15 km and two hours of commuting time. The 4,400 sq km MMR, which had a 16 million population in 2001, is expected to see the numbers rise to 24 million in 2021. By 2015, the Vashi bridge that connects Mumbai and Navi Mumbai is expected to see traffic of 1.9 lakh passenger car units daily without the MTHL.

Heading: 5 fatal accidents in less than 12 hours - Indian Express
Content:
CASH AT JUDGE'S DOOR: HC holds custodial interrogation of hotelier essential, says Bansal and Ravinder treat money like toys

The Punjab and Haryana High Court turned down the anticipatory bail application of Ravinder Singh, co-accused in the cash-at-judge's-door case, on Thursday. In a strongly-worded judgment, the court justified the need for his custodial interrogation.

The judgment by Justice A N Jindal highlighted the ill effects of corruption in the society and expressed deep concern over the integrity of the legal system that was at stake. The judge made some scathing observations over the conduct of Sanjeev Bansal, former Additional Advocate General, Haryana, and Ravinder Singh, a Delhi hotelier. The judgment also highlighted the divergent statements made by Sanjeev Bansal.

"Both the members of the legal profession and the higher judiciary being directly involved in the case and the very integrity of legal judicial system being at stake, to save the prestige of both the systems and also to prevent any subversion or suppression of truth or any miscarriage of justice in the investigation, custodial interrogation has become essential," read the judgment.

Commenting on Bansal and Ravinder, the court held: "So far, it transpires that Bansal and Ravinder are influential people and affluent with money. They were dealing with money like kids do with toys. There is definite admission made by Bansal that he sent the money but he has changed his statement thrice... One thing has come to the surface from his divergent statements that the money was handed over by Ravinder for onward transmission... such statements raises hundreds of questions to be answered by Ravinder Singh."

The High Court also paid no heed to the arguments of Ravinder's counsel who feared use of third degree against him in custody. "The argument needs not be countenanced, for such an argument can be advanced by all accused of all categories of crime," held the court.

Justice A N Jindal said: "Keeping in view the fact that Ravinder has thrown dust over judicial sodality, it could be expected from him to surrender before the investigating agency and unfold the truth."

The High Court observed that Ravinder's plea, that the money was meant for purchase of land in Himachal Pradesh, stood contradicted from the sale transaction, where his address was not shown to be that of Delhi, where he was said to be residing. The contradictions in the statements of Sanjeev Bansal were also pointed out by the court.

Hotelier lists conditions for surrender

In a twist to the cash-for-judge case, Ravinder Singh's counsel, in an application submitted on his behalf in the court of Special Judge, CBI, at the District Courts on Thursday, said the investigating agencies had not revealed any other fact with regard to the delivery of Rs 15 lakh by Ravinder to Bansal. "Obviously, the statement of Bansal cannot be of any evidentiary value against the applicant when he has taken a definite stand that no such incident or transaction took place," it said. "The applicant wants to get himself identified by such a witness in a test-identification parade and that can only happen if the applicant is permitted to surrender in a muffled condition to be sent to judicial custody," adds the application. "Since the accused is seeking identification parade, it will be in the fitness of things if he is permitted to surrender before the Special CBI Magistrate, Delhi," says the application. The application will be taken up for hearing on Friday.

Bar Association to meet CJI

The Punjab and Haryana High Court Bar Association will meet Chief Justice of India K G Balakrishnan regarding the ongoing investigations in the case. "We will apprise the CJI on the issue, since it requires the intervention of the High Court Bar," said association president Rupinder S Khosla.

High Court on corruption

* Corruption is one of the most talked-about subject today in the country. The tentacles of corruption are spreading fast, corroding the moral fibre and consequently, in most cases, the economic structure of the country. It has assumed alarming proportions in recent times. Eyebrows are raised over people working at the helm of affairs by the general public and though they are themselves responsible for it. The position of the bribe giver is worse than its receiver...

* All types of people have a place in every walk of life in this humanitarian society. Corruption in any shape has become just customary or a common phenomenon but still high expectations are made from judicial wheel of the government, so as to maintain integrity and uplift the dignity of the nation. Despite unhealthy criticism, the rich or poor, howsoever high or low they may be, their eyes remain fixed to get justice at the hands of custodians of justice. Barring a few exceptions, it would not be reasonable to say the Indian Judicial system is proving to the expectations of the public...

Heading: Centre asks UT to explain its position on encroachment - Indian Express
Content:
Road accidents claimed five lives in Chandigarh and Panchkula since the early hours of Thursday. While three people died in Chandigarh, two lost their lives in Panchkula.

In the first incident, a speeding Tata Spacio rammed into a bike, killing a 24-year-old man at the Aroma light point around 2 am on Thursday. In the morning, an unidentified man was run over by an unknown vehicle on the Sector 9/17 dividing road, while a school bus ran over a man in Sector 21 around noon.

In Panchkula, Yadavinder and Subreen Chaudhary lost their lives in two separate accidents early on Thursday.

Victim #1

Jagtar Singh

Triple riding on a motorcycle without helmet claimed the life of Jagtar Singh in Chandigarh, police said on Thursday. Along with Pradeep and Gurbej, he was going towards Sector 22 to drop the latter at his brother's house.

Crossing the Aroma light point at a breakneck speed, their Splendor was hit by a speeding Tata Spacio. All three occupants of the bike sustained serious injuries and were taken to the PGI where Jagtar (24) was declared dead on arrival. He died of head injuries. A resident of Faridkot, Punjab, Jagtar had been staying in the city for the last one year. He was an architect.

Pradeep works as a customer executive with an IT firm while Gurbej had come to stay with them from Australia. Police said the car driver (CH02 T 1801) fled after the accident.

The accused was yet to be identified and arrested till the filing of this report.

The victim's friend Surjeet, who was following the three on another bike, was a witness to the accident and was in a state of shock at the at the Sector 16 hospital where Jagtar's postmortem was conducted.

"Pradeep got free from work at 11 pm after which we planned to hang out for sometime. The accident happened so suddenly. After hitting the bike, the car turned 360 degrees several times before speeding away," Surjeet told Newsline.

Sub-Inspector Jaspal Singh, in charge of the Sector 22 police post, said a case had been registered against the car driver and efforts were on to arrest him.

Victim #2

Ram Tej

Working as a domestic help in Sector 21, Ram Tej (20) was on his bicycle when he was hit by a school bus in Sector 21. He came under the front wheels of the bus, which belonged to St. Kabir's School. The bus was on its way to drop children home around noon when the mishap occurred. The driver, Surjeet Singh, was arrested and the bus impounded. A case was registered in the Sector 19 police station.

Victim #3

Unidentified

An unidentified pedestrian died when an unknown vehicle hit him around 3.30 am. The mutilated body of the deceased was found on the Sector 9/17 dividing road. The police said the man's clothes were torn, which indicated he was dragged for a distance with the vehicle after it hit him. "He might have been crossing the road when the accident occurred," he added.

Victim #4

Yadavinder

A resident of Manakya village near Ramgarh, Yadavinder lost his life when his car collided with a canter near Suncity in Ramgarh. The victim, along with his friends Sandip and Jaswant, was returning to the village when accident occurred. The canter was driven by Ram Kumar, a resident of Khet Purali village. While Yadavinder died on the spot, Sandip, Jaswant and Ram Kumar are undergoing treatment at PGI.

Victim #5

Subreen Chaudhary

A resident of Rajasthan, Subreen Chaudhary died when an unidentified vehicle ran over him on Wednesday night. Subreen had come to Panchkula to meet his nephew in Golpura village near Raipur Rani. He was hit minutes after he had got down from a bus and died on the spot, the police said.

Heading: Network plays matchmaker for Positive people - Indian Express
Content:
Unauthorised religious structures have become a national issue, with the Centre asking state governments and union territories to furnish details on their policies to deal with such encroachment.

In its letter to the Administration, the Centre said: "A balance must be struck between the need to preserve and protect religious structures and that to protect public property from encroachment."

The development follows an order of the Gujarat High Court on religious encroachment that was challenged in the Supreme Court. The Centre has told the apex court that it will convene a meeting of all secretaries concerned of the various states and reach a consensus on the manner in which such encroachment should be dealt with.

The Gujarat High Court had invoked a suo motu writ jurisdiction and directed various municipal corporations and other authorities concerned to take immediate steps for removal of religious structures encroaching upon public places, without any discrimination. The Supreme Court issued a notice on the petition and stayed the operation of the impugned order of the Gujarat HC.

The communiqué sent to the Administration mentioned that the removal of encroachment required a strict approach, but it was also desirable that efforts should not hurt the religious sentiments of people, or disrupt communal harmony.

In Chandigarh, there are around 307 unauthorised religious structures, which encroach upon nearly 650 acres of prime government land. While there is a provision of only 57 temples, 27 gurdwaras, 10 churches and seven mosques in city, according to the statistics maintained by the Chandigarh Administration, there are 240 unauthorised temples, 56 gurdwaras, six churches and five mosques.

In December 2005, the UT Administration had recommended relocation of unauthorised religious structures. A sub-group on "encroachment and unauthorised religious structures" was constituted and it was proposed that the managements of such religious organisations be offered alternative land at concessional rates near the sites, where labour colonies were proposed to be shifted under a rehabilitation scheme.

UT Home-cum-Finance Secretary Sanjay Kumar said: "Our policy is quite consistent on this issue. We don't want any encroachment to come up on government land. We have a rehabilitation and allotment policy for such religious institutions. Those covered under the scheme will be allotted alternate land for religious institutions. Illegal construction will not be tolerated at any cost."

Heading: Realtors threaten, booked - Indian Express
Content:
It is a rather unusual task that is pre-occupying the Network of Positive People Living with HIV in Chandigarh these days. Members of the NGO are busy finding suitable matches for Positive young men and women who are ready to give life a second chance.

Network president Pooja Thakur was scanning the latest biodata of a 30-year-old HIV Positive man from Indore when Newsline visited her. "This is the latest profile I have with me. The groom is a Punjabi and wants to marry a Punjabi Positive girl. His first marriage ended some time ago after his status was known and he is now ready to make a fresh start by disclosing his status."

"Positive marriage" is a still a new concept in the region, where the society still sees HIV as a taboo subject and most of the affected people prefer to hide their status.

According to Network officials, however, the scenario is changing gradually for the better. They said around 15 Positive people — both men and women — had approached them to hunt for prospective brides and grooms. The Network acts as an interface between the two parties, letting the families take their decision.

"Two successful marriages have taken place in the last one year while there have been several cases where we acted as a channel for these young men and women to find partners. With the launching of specific matrimonial websites for such people, like www.positivesaathi.com, there are now choices for the affected people," says a counsellor.

Many of the Positive people walk into the NGO's office themselves, sometimes accompanied by their parents (especially in the case of women), to drop their biodata.

The Network "matchmakers" scored their first success a few months ago when they helped a 32-year-old man from Mumbai meet a girl from Lucknow in Chandigarh. They were soon a couple.

"Positive networks in other states sometimes get requests to hunt for a match from their home states. We got similar requests from the networks in Mumbai and Lucknow and facilitated the meeting of the two families. The marriage was fixed within days," adds Thakur.

Story of a Positive couple

"It is the second marriage for both of us," says 35-year-old Baljinder Kaur, now settled in Kaithal, Haryana, with her husband Krishan Lal. Both Lal and Kaur had lost their spouses to AIDS. "We did not know each other before and our match was arranged. After giving myself a second chance, I feel I have done the right thing. Rather than becoming a burden on my parents, I have got a partner who understands my ups and downs. We can take good care of each other," says Kaur. Advocating a "positive marriage", she says: "The marriage has lent me tremendous emotional support." Besides his wife, Lal had lost his three children from his first marriage to AIDS. Kaur, on the other hand, has a daughter from the first marriage who has tested positive.

Heading: Mohali: Alcometers, speed radars put brakes on rash driving - Indian Express
Content:
The Zirakpur police have registered a case against two realtors on charges of threatening to kill a business rival in the city.

The complainant, Ram Kumar, a property dealer based in Zirakpur, said the accused had demanded Rs 2 lakh from him. When he refused, they allegedly threatened him with dire consequences.

Kumar alleged that the Zirakpur police refused to lodge his complaint after which he approached Mohali SSP Jatinder Singh Aulakh, who finally ordered that a case be registered. On August 29, Kumar said, property dealers Sukhwinder Singh and Harnam Singh came to his office in Silver City and demanded Rs 2 lakh at gunpoint.

His friend Om Parkash Hooda, who was present there, averted any untoward incident.

They said while they went to the police on the same day, though a case under Sections 386, 452 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) was registered at Zirakpur police station on Wednesday evening.

Property dealers cheat industrialist, nabbed with Rs 19 lakh

Dera Bassi: Two property dealers have been nabbed by the CIA staff of Kharar and Rs 19 lakh been recovered from their possession on Wednesday night. The dealers had reportedly cheated an industrialist of Rs 20 lakh. The police have registered a case under Section 420 and 34 of the IPC against them. As per reports, Manav Kumar, a resident of Pathankot and Kulwinder Singh of Mohali, came to the office of Dera Bassi Industries Association chairman Kewal Garg at Mubarikpur on Wednesday. They offered him a land deal but Garg turned down their offer, saying he would inspect the land and its documents before finalising any agreement. They left the office, while Garg left for Dera Bassi. The dealers visited Garg's office again and demanded Rs 20 lakh as advance from his manager, claiming that the deal had been finalised. The manager Jagdish tried to contact Garg for his consent but could not as his cell phone was switched off. Meanwhile, they managed to get away with Rs 20 lakh. Garg immediately filed a complaint with the Kharar CIA staff, who nabbed the duo and recovered the money.

— ENS

Heading: MC employees threaten to cut power, water supply in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
The next time you drive on Mohali roads, beware of the traffic cops. With added force and gadgets, the Mohali Traffic Police have tightened the noose around violators.

"The checking drive is on the lines of Chandigarh. We want to change the prevailing notion that there is no one to check you once you enter Mohali," Deputy Superintendent of Police (Traffic) Raka Ghirra told Newsline.

The use of alcoholmeters and speed radars has put the brakes on drunken and rash driving, continuing unnoticed in Mohali till recently. The number of challans and amount of fine recovered from violators has doubled in the last year.

According to official figures, 1,862 traffic challans were issued in August 2008 as compared to just 715 challans in June 2007. This year, the fine touched Rs 6.4 lakh, which amounted to only Rs 3.06 lakh in 2007.

From June 2007 till August 2008, 24,401 traffic violators have been issued challans and Rs 89.76 lakh has been recovered as fine.

For traffic violators, the cloud has a silver lining — now they do not have to visit judicial courts to pay the fine. Mohali's District Transport Officer (DTO) has been empowered to deal with traffic challans. The DTO holds hearing at his office in Phase I every Tuesday and Friday between 10 am and 12 noon and 3 and 5 pm.

In case the defaulter fails to appear before the DTO within 90 days of the challan being issued, the SP (Traffic) summons them for punitive action.

With a total of 155 personnel, the Mohali Traffic Police have created special traffic wings in Mohali, Kharar, Dera Bassi, Zirakpur, Lalru, Kurali and Mullanpur Garibdass. Each wing includes an Inspector, three Sub-Inspectors and Assistant Sub-Inspectors.

Heading: Unfinished widening work gives way to choked roads, potholes - Indian Express
Content:
BULL'S 'MURDER': Work at MC office suspended as staff on indefinite strike

Power and water supply to Mohali will be cut from Saturday, if an FIR registered against the Municipal Council (MC) employees for "causing the death of a stray bull" is not cancelled. This was the ultimatum served by the MC Employees' Union to Mohali Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari and Senior Superintendent of Police Jatinder Singh Aulakh.

Already, work at the MC office has been suspended as almost 400 MC employees went on an indefinite strike on Thursday.

The union also sought the immediate arrest of the protestors who "assaulted the MC employees and obstructed them from perform their duty".

This comes a day after a stray bull was reportedly strangled to death while MC staff were trapping it near the bus stand in Phase VIII.

Municipal councillor Harman Preet Singh Prince sought the resignation of MC president Rajinder Singh Rana and Kharar MLA Balbir Sidhu holding them "responsible for the assault on MC employees".

"Instead of pacifying the residents, who were protesting the bull's death, these public representatives incited the mob. Later, they assured the protesters that action will be taken against the employees," said Prince.

Rana and Sidhu, however, categorically denied the charges.

On the other hand, the Chandigarh Chapter of People for Animals (PFA) founder trustee Payal Sodhi sought the intervention of Punjab Chief Secretary Ramesh Inder Singh on the issue.

"The Mohali MC officials are unwilling to take responsibility of the regular incidents of cruelty to animals. It seems they are not ready to find a permanent solution to the problem of stray cattle in Mohali," she said.

She added that the bull's "murder" was in violation of Section 11 of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, Prevention of Cruelty (capture of animals) Rules, 1972, and Section 429 of Indian Penal Code.

Condemning the attitude of MC officials towards animals, People for Animals appealed to Mohali residents to come forward and assist the organisation in bringing such offenders to book.

Heading: SC stays arrest of BIS Chahal till Sept 29 - Indian Express
Content:
The widening work on the internal roads of various sectors is proving to be a nuisance for the residents. The incomplete work has given way to deep potholes and choked roads after rains.

Work had started a few weeks ago in Sector 27 and 22. Pits were dug and were left open after the heavy rainfall started. In the intermittent dry spells, the work restarted but the recent rains proved fatal for the project.

R K Garg, a resident of Sector 27, said: "The work is stopped for days and water fills the open pits. There is mud scattered all over the roads. We cannot park our vehicles inside our houses due to all the digging. They have to be parked outside the lanes, raising concerns about security. The senior citizens are facing a harrowing time as they cannot venture out."

One half of the road is completely paved with mud. Experts say this can prove lethal for those driving on these roads as the chances of skidding amplify.

Shalini, a resident of Sector 22, said the MC must make efforts to finsh the work soon. "The situation is especially dangerous at night, when the half-finished work cannot be spotted due to inadequate light. Widening of roads is certainly required but it should have been started after the rains," she said.

While the widening of roads in Sector 22 was started a few weeks ago, the work on one in Sector 27 has been going on for more than two months. Earlier, an electric cable had to be shifted from the spot which delayed the process further.

An official of the Municipal Corporation said the work is getting delayed due to the prolonged spell of rain. "The work cannot continue while it rains. The widening of roads will be completed in a month's time once the monsoon is over," the official added.

Heading: Come Oct, Estate Office to go hi-tech - Indian Express
Content:
Providing a reprieve to former media adviser of Captain Amarinder Singh, B I S Chahal, the Supreme Court stayed his arrest in any fresh case till September 29. The orders have been passed on the special leave petition (SLP) filed by Chahal.

In the SLP, Chahal had challenged the orders of the Punjab and Haryana High Court wherein the three-day prior notice, which was issued to Chahal earlier, was recalled by the High Court.

Chahal had raised the same demand from the Supreme Court apprehending false implication at the hands of Punjab Police.

Earlier, the High Court had directed the Punjab government to issue three-day prior notice to Chahal before arresting him in any fresh case.

The directions had been issued to all wings of the Punjab Police and Punjab Vigilance. This relief was granted to Chahal, after he had moved the High Court seeking directions to the Punjab Vigilance and Punjab Police to issue a ten-day prior notice.

Chahal had alleged that he may be made a victim of political vendetta yet again for his close association with former Punjab CM Captain Amarinder Singh.

Chahal had also alleged that since Amarinder Singh is now the president of the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC), the Punjab Vigilance or Punjab Police may register a false case against him in order to tarnish the former CM's image.

The Punjab government had then filed an application in the High Court demanding that the order be recalled.

Allowing the application of Punjab government, the High Court had withdrawn its relief awarded to Chahal.

The case will come up for hearing in the Supreme Court on September 29.

Heading: Blast aftermath: MC committee to raid ‘illegal’ guesthouses, hotels - Indian Express
Content:
Mid-October is the expected time of the launch of the UT Estate Office's website, which will enable online filing of Value-Added Tax (VAT) returns. Testing of the website is already underway. A separate module for the Excise Wing is also being developed to facilitate the department in the issuance of transport and liquor licences.

The UT Estate Office took the first step towards launching this project in July, when it started receiving VAT returns through Sampark centres. "Online accessibility will definitely result in increased transparency and efficiency in routine working," said UT Deputy Commissioner R K Rao.

The new software will allow online viewing of tax collections and help in better treasury operations resulting from faster encashment of cheques and drafts. "It would also minimise the interface between administration officials and dealers, which earlier resulted in several 'under-the-table' dealings," said a senior official of the Administration.

Till date, the process of receipt of returns is handled manually, which delays the encashment of cheques. Also, UT Estate Office officials have to compile the tax collections for each ward separately, which makes it difficult to ascertain the increase/decrease in revenue.

Moreover, repeated defaulters go scot-free as there is no 'handy' record available to monitor dealers.

Office to be revamped

Modernisation of the UT Estate Office is also on the cards, which includes the establishment of a Taxpayers Service Office on the lines of the Sampark Centres and workstations in air-conditioned environments. — ENS

Heading: Ravinder’s anticipatory bail plea dismissed bail plea dismissed - Indian Express
Content:
In THE wake of serial blasts in Delhi recently, a committee of the Municipal Corporation (MC) will check the 'illegal' guesthouses and hotels in the city. The committee, to be headed by the Town Planner, will also review the status of the guesthouses.

After a series of stories by Newsline, the MC had conducted a survey of the guesthouses and directed the owners to submit their building plans. Only 40 plans, however, have been received by the Planning Office till date. The MC had asked for the plans to study the violations and conformation of norms by such guesthouses.

Joint Commissioner T P S Phoolka convened a meeting on Thursday and directed the committee members to visit every site and verify the particulars with regards to the width of roads, exit and entrance of guesthouses, light and ventilation, covered area, height permitted in the building bylaws, fire safety norms, parking norms and the structure stability of the building.

The officers have also been directed to seal those guesthouses which are unauthorised and have not submitted their building plan.

The committee will submit its reports to the commissioner within three weeks.

Interestingly, guesthouses in localities of Kajheri, Burail and Attawa among others run without paying the conversion fee. Many such structures violate all building bylaws, are constructed haphazardly and do not pay any heed to the fire safety norms. Experts believe that the MC would be able to generate substantial revenue through the exercise.
