Heading: Requiem for a dream - Indian Express
Content:
Lok sabha Speaker Somnath Chatterjee will be inaugurating an exhibition titled 'Indian Parliamentary Democracy: A Journey Forward' in the Haryana Vidhan Sabha premises on September 21.

The Parliamentary Museum and Archives Division of the Lok Sabha Secretariat and Haryana Vidhan Sabha Secretariat in collaboration with the Directorate of Advertising and Visual Publicity, Chandigarh, under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting is organising the show.

As part of the Conference of presiding officers and Secretaries of Legislative Bodies, the exhibition is spread over 13 sections and traces the growth and development of democratic traditions in the country, beginning from the ancient times to the modern parliamentary institutions.

The exhibition will also showcase the country's federal system and the legislative set up in different states.

Besides this, the exhibition will include audio-visual inputs on computer multimedia and LCDs.

Visitors would be able to hear audio narrations of shlokas from the Rig Veda. Original voices of Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, Dr B R Ambedkar and Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose would also be aired in the exhibition hall.

The other attractions at the exhibition will include a scanned copy of the Constitution and various programmes on ancient democratic heritage, legislative reforms, Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and state legislatures, besides films related to important events during the freedom struggle and on the election process in the country.

Heading: Consumer forum declares orders of namesake NGO illegal - Indian Express
Content:
For N'wolley Ebapole Samuel, a 20-year-old African lad from the Ivory Coast, India was a dream.

Enrolled in Massif International College, Sector 20, Panchkula, for the Business Information System course, Samuel was shocked to discover that he was the only student in the class.

To further add to his woes, he found that the Association of Business Executive (ABE), UK, had withdrawn its affiliation long ago. But the damage had been done — Samuel had already deposited Rs 64,500 as tuition fee, examination fee and hostel accommodation for a month.

"It all seems like a horrific nightmare now. But thanks to the media, I got justice in the end. I remember the day when I saw photographs of the college on the internet, it looked beautiful and a perfect destination for academics. Even my friends told me that I was lucky to have such a wonderful campus," he said.

Samuel reached India on March 20 and the rosy façade painted by the authorities crumbled.

"The infrastructure was abysmal. As I was the only student, the period of study was reduced to two months instead of the prescribed six and had to arrange for all the study material on my own. Contrary to all assurances, the college did not help me acquire a residential permit from the Ministry of Home Affairs, owing to which I was slapped a fine of Rs 1,478 later," he explained.

It was then Samuel decided to submit a written complaint to Superintendent of Police, Panchkula, Sandeep Khirwar (later withdrawn).

He moved the consumer court as well. This decision paid dividends as the college director, Sandeep Chauhan, quickly chose to refund the amount.

Now, Samuel plans to complete a three-year Bachelors in Science course from the Punjab Technical University.

Heading: Beggars back on streets, as UT plan fails - Indian Express
Content:
The UT District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum has declared orders passed by an NGO, Consumers Forum Chandigarh, as illegal. The NGO's name could mislead the consumers as it sounds similar to that of the official consumer court, the Forum said on Thursday.

Commenting on the organisations working for consumer awareness, the court said even if a parallel organisation was working under a similar name, it was duty-bound to only educate the people about consumer rights and not pass any orders.

In the particular case that led to the remarks, a resident of Sector 15, Damyanti Chopra, had alleged medical negligence on the part of the PGI. She had accused the hospital of causing harassment, saying she was not rendered proper treatment despite being charged Rs 2 lakh.

In its reply, the PGI said the complainant was irresponsible in her behaviour towards the surgeon and denied charging Rs 2 lakh.

Damyanti had gone to the Sector 11 NGO, which directed the PGI to pay Rs 1 lakh as harassment. After it was not paid, the complainant came to the official consumer court in Sector 19, which declared the order illegal and unjustified. It also dismissed the application of the complainant.

"There is no deficiency on part of the medical institute and the complaint is dismissed," the Forum said.

Heading: Lobbying begins for last phase of PU Senate polls - Indian Express
Content:
Another well intended plan of the Education department seems to have failed to reap the desired results. The department's proposal to trace beggars from different areas in the city and educate them seems to have gone down the drain. Even months after starting the campaign to trace beggars and child labourers and educate them, the officials say that the programme is still being 'chalked out'.

The Education department had started a campaign in February with much fanfare to find beggars and children working as labourers in different parts of the city. After locating such children, the department was to provide them with uniforms, books and hygiene kits among other things. According to the plan, it was also decided that apart from giving them admission in a residential school, they will also be given a monthly stipend of Rs 250 if their attendance was 75 percent or above.

The 'inspectors' deputed by the department could be seen surveying various parts of the city for a few days to find such children. In a press statement issued during the same time, S K Setia, Director Public Instructions (Schools) had also claimed the plan to be a 'great success' in view of the sudden disappearance of beggars from the city.

Though the department also planned to put these children in the mainstream education after sometime, they could be seen back to begging on the streets of the city. Commenting on the way the programme has shaped up, Setia said that the department is still 'working' on it. "We are trying to find more beggars. It is a tedious process to educate these children as most of them are the bread winners for their families. But we are still hopeful that we will be able to accomplish our goal," said Setia.

Heading: Punjabi University gets ‘A’ grade by NAAC - Indian Express
Content:
The PU Senate election fever for the fourth and last phase for the largest graduates' constituency has gripped the five contenders from the city who are vying for place among the 15 seats of the constituency.

One of them, who claimed to be the only one to have come up with a manifesto, held a press conference on Thursday and disclosed his agenda.

The five candidates who are in the fray from the city among the overall 42 contenders in the constituency have been trying to make their presence felt to the over 4 lakh graduate voters who will decide the fate of these candidates on September 21.

They are Dr Madanjit Kaur Sahota, principal of Master Tara Singh College for Women, Jagpal Singh, Head of Political Science department at SCD Government College, Lakhvinder Singh Bedi, Head of PG department of English at GGN Khalsa College and Rajeev Bhasin and Praveen Sharma from Arya College.

Lakhvinder Singh Bedi, who held the press conference today, said: "If I am elected as the member of the senate, I would like to sensitise the youth in the emerging education scenario, orient them towards rural education, redrawing the education and administrative dimensions of Panjab University Regional Centre in the city." Bedi, who fights from ballot number 20, added that he would also work towards setting up vocational and guidance bureaus in the colleges.

Some other candidates, meanwhile, are employing the traditional methods to reach out to the voters. "I have been working day in and day out to visit every corner of the society and meeting the voters," said Dr Madanjit Kaur Sahota, a sitting senator who had contested from the principal's constituency last time. As she feels that women empowerment needs to be given more importance, she would stress to make women education better, besides working to bridge the gap for opportunities for rural students, especially boys.

Praveen Sharma, who has started canvassing heavily with the help of banners and posters, said, "I am a known person in the senate and therefore I do not think there is much need to introduce myself to them. I have anyhow started campaigning with letters as well as posters."

He said he would like to emphasise the importance of modern professional courses and the need to implement them in an effective way by providing all facilities. Jagpal Singh, another old member of the Senate, said that the issues related to the students like fees hike or problems in re-evaluation or late results would be his top priority.

Heading: Sanchayika Day celebrated to promote saving habits among students - Indian Express
Content:
Punjabi University has yet again been awarded the highest 'A' grade on a three-point scale among over 350 universities in the country. The status has been awarded for a period of five years by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), which is an autonomous institution of the University Grants Commission.

The status is given by NAAC on the basis of the overall performance of a University during a period of five years. Punjabi University was earlier given the 'five star level' by NAAC for the period covering 2002-2007.

The NAAC has recently reformatted the grading system from 'one star to five star level' to 'A to C' grade, equating 'five stars' with 'A' grade.

A 10-member NAAC team had visited the University from August 26 to 28 this year, and scanned the activities and achievements of its various departments to review it's accomplishments at micro and macro levels.

Vice-Chancellor, Dr Jaspal Singh said that the NAAC team had made a special mention about the fact that the University has not deviated from its statutory and fundamental responsibility of promoting the cause of Punjabi language, art and culture.

The continuing qualitative research and use of innovative techniques by various departments were the other major factors which contributed towards retaining the status, he said.

The grading, he added, was important in more ways than one as it helped in getting enhanced grants from various funding agencies for the promotion of academic and research activities and establishing tie-ups with prestigious institutions and organisations of national and international standing.

Heading: Scene Stealers - Indian Express
Content:
The Directorate of Small Savings, UT Chandigarh organised a Sanchayika Day at the Government College for Girls, Sector-11, on Thursday. The function was held in collaboration with the National Savings Institute, Chandigarh Centre. Special Secretary, UT Finance, Raji P Shrivastava was the chief guest.

Shrivastava appealed to the principals of various schools to persuade students and their parents to invest in the scheme and promote saving habits. She said that 42 government schools are already participating in the scheme and 25 more are going to be added soon. Efforts would also be made to include private and other aided schools to adopt the scheme. She also awarded various schools and students for their contribution to the Sanchayika Scheme.

Rajiv Sagar, regional director, National Savings Institute, Chandigarh Centre explained the significance of the scheme and said that the scheme will help in inculcating a habit of saving money in students and further facilitate the management of money. More than 29,000 students have adopted the scheme.

Government Model Senior Secondary School (GMSSS), Sector 46 attained the first position with a total contribution of Rs 36.62 lakh, Government Senior Secondary School (GSSS), Sector 37 was best among government schools whereas GSSS, Sector 38 (W) was best among rural schools. An amount of Rs 2.12 crore was collected under the scheme during 2007-08.

Heading: Story in a Strip - Indian Express
Content:
PU's Youth and Heritage Fest is incomplete

without these talented regulars

It's not everyday that you see girls dressed in dhotis and 'twirling' their fake moustache. So when you do, you know it's time for Panjab University's Youth and Heritage Festival. And you'd also know that there are regulars who put up a dazzling show, year after year. It's time when energies levels shoot up, volumes pump up and classrooms wear an empty look. We catch up with those who are readying themselves for yet another action-packed performance at the Zone B Fest to be held from September 23 to 26.

Having participated in the fest thrice and won twice, Priyanka Singh, an MA (English) first year student, tells us, "It's like old wine, it just gets better each year!" Craving for more, this girls on a high doesn't mind painfully long practice hours. Preparing for the light vocals event, this is a platform that helps her gauge the improvement over last year, chips in friend Harpreet Kaur Shergill, a final year student, who won the first prize in Vaar singing last year.

With a maximum number of five chances given to each student, once a student participates in the fest, she keeps coming back every year, observes Sunita Dhawan, the organizing secretary of the girls event. "Though the first time is really tough, it gets easier with time," chorus twins Sonika and Monika Gahlawat of MCM College, who won the first prize in group bhajan and group folk respectively. "Of course your legs shake and vocal chords get jammed, but it's an addiction." Ramandeep Kaur, a BA final year student, looks up from her notepad and nods in agreement. "Last time was bad, I could hardly write anything," she says this time her essay will surely win an award.

While some participate to hone their talent, others follow the bandwagon. But one thing is for sure, it's the quickest way to become the campus idol. Ridhima Puri, a BA final year student, for instance is more remembered by the character she played last year than anything else, Shushi Sharma of GCG-11 is addressed as the Dance Queen and Vandana, a BA final year student, the Perfect Actress. Now that they've bagged awards over the years, it's the next level they want to get to. "We want to get into full-time theatre," assert Jaspreet Kaur and Malvika Bhanushree of Guru Gobind Singh College, who won prizes for skit and play last year and have now been putting in 12 hours a day for the last one month. With many like Gurdas Mann and Divya Datta having born out of this, Dr S M Kant, Director Youth Welfare, sums the fest aptly — winning or losing, the fest is about putting up a great show and the show must go on.

Heading: The Queen quotes - Indian Express
Content:
Enter the graphic, visual world of colour, fantasy and intellect

The strip's not only about humour, fantasies, super-heroes, macho men or superlative women. The comic strip is unfolding a brand-new saga, one that appeals to both the eyes and intellect. The genre of comics or graphic novels as they describe it, is getting more creative, absorbing and stimulating. One look at Buddha, amazingly illustrated and written by Ozamu Tezuka, a series which tells the story of Buddha in comic strip form, will change your perception about comics. It's a brand-new world, waiting to be devoured, cover to cover. "Yes, the graphic format has undergone a metamorphosis and people are rediscovering the beauty of comics,'' Pankaj P Singh of Browser talks about the popular section, which has a large set devoted to children as well. In the humour section, the absolutely brilliant Gary Larson can never fail to bring a smile on your face, while the humour section has some writings by women in comic format. A concept that never fails to attract people of all ages is the Beginner's series in graphic format on famous personalities. "It's done with both the head and heart and is high on looks and content,'' Singh also talks about introduction to various concepts in comics strip forms and also the Agatha Christie series in graphic format.

At the Book fair in Sector 17, you can lay your hands on MAD, Batman, Superman, Tarzan, Asterixs, Tin Tin...at throwaway prices and according to the section in charge here, comics are hot-sellers, being lapped up by both children and adults. Here you scout for rare and old editions of these comics.

An interesting way to introduce children to the myths, legends and folk stories of India is through the new collection by Vaibhav Comics. Beautifully illustrated, the comics have legends, tales of love, bravery, mystery, humour from different parts of the country, from Madhya Pradesh, Kerala...There are stories of The Santhals, one of the largest tribal communities of India, the Sunderbans et al. "These are more colourful, attractive and so easy and fun to to read,'' Vaibhav and Shaurva pore over Prithvi Raj Chauhan in comic format. Also, get ready to laugh your heads off, with the new and converted comic format of the popular Great Indian Laughter Challenge and the serial Office Office and also movie story books like Stuart Little 2 and Charolette's Web. Get booked.

Heading: God of all things - Indian Express
Content:
"Now that I have a Yashraj, it feels like heaven"

No matter what, we all simply louve her. Be it her loud antics, bare dare acts, latka jhatkas, the occasional spats and run-ins, Rakhi Sawant rules, and rocks. In town for the shoot of Yashraj's next film, Victory, we connect with the motormouth, who is right now on top of the world. When you've got a Yashraj on your resume, top of the world is an understatement. "I've never seen such luxury...Yashraj knows how to pamper its actors," Rakhi lazes around at The Taj, soaking in the five-star treatment. "No other production house gives you this much luxury, I've literally gone mad," she says, dazed with disbelief.

Drama queen, dancing queen, reality queen, the bindass item girl..."queen of controversy, I love it when you call me a queen, feels like heaven," Sawant's getting used to the crowned queen effect. Now that she's stepped onto the acting platform, she, as dramatic as ever, corrects us, "please don't call me an item girl anymore." This is one tag she wants to snip off. "There was a time when I wanted to be this, and it still is my rozi-roti. But now, I want to be known as an actress." High on the brandwagon, she's already shot high on the TRPs with her Rakhi Sawant Show. "Get ready for the next season, and I promise all the Khans will come," she sure is spicing up Season two. In the meantime, it's another show that's got doing the balancing act. "I'm a judge on a children's reality show on Zee, Tata Indicom Ek Se Badhkar Ek Chhota Packet, Bada Dhamaka," she tells us. It's easy being rude to adults and telling them off, but how do you tell kids? "Well, that's a tough one, but I tell you, we all think that children are being pressured into doing all this and it's hard on them.

It's not. Most of them are earning money for further education, and all of them are having fun on it!" With Rakhi Sawant around, fun is not far off.

Heading: The couture myth - Indian Express
Content:
After various entertainment media swore by God, there's now a mobile phone to encash on myth-o-mania

Just when we thought that we had exhausted all scope of mythotainment, out came the Ramayana mobile phone to re-stir our collective cultural consciousness. With the entire epic squeezed into one compact gadget, the phone seems to have gone furlongs ahead of other applications of myth and legend. It also points to the renaissance of mythology in popular Indian culture.

Although the economics of it are irresistible, the tradition bandwagon is also attractive because of its mammoth appeal. The 'holy' mobile phone—with a tilak, and mantras and shlokas for ringtones—is in keeping with that appeal. Prem Sagar of Sagar Arts, the production house synonymous with mythological shows, has personally edited the 45-hour original Ramayana into a compact one-hour-and-nine-minute one for the phone. He says, "It was a quite a formidable task to condense the Ramayana without tampering with the content and the sensibility of the epic. Short-cuts are unacceptable to us as we wanted 'bhakti' in it. Apart from devotional songs, one can listen to the entire Ramayana."

The gods and the goddesses of the Vedic age have been quite a catalyst for boosting TRPs on television. Many rush home to catch the Mahabharata, Ramayana or Mahima Shani Dev Ki on the idiot box. However, there's more to mythology than meets the eye. "Although some new people try to make up by using SFX and gloss over lack of perfection, they miss out authenticity. The stories of Rama and Krishna cannot be packaged so fancily that the audiences are unable to connect to it," says Sagar.

Meanwhile, mythology-inspired theatre is always in want of funds. Bijon Dasgupta, the protagonist of Karna, the Generous Prince says that it takes a huge effort to produce a mythological for stage. "As actors, we have to put in many months of exhaustive rehearsals. For instance, we trained in two types of martial arts for our show. To make it look grand, we always need loads of cash pouring in." Scherazade Kaikobad, director of Retellings, did away with the need for grandeur in her play. She brought out Shakuntala, Sita and Surpanakha from the confines of legend in a simple manner.

Artist Rajat Kanthi Dharr gave a new look to Lord Shiva in his paintings. He says that in Shiva, Ready For The Ramp, "I have interpreted mythology my way. It's up to people to accept it or not. I just feel that new and improved takes on mythology are a great way for young people to catch up on what they missed out. For artists, these gods with incredible powers are definitely a fantastic inspiration."

However, it's a subject that needs careful handling if one doesn't want to come under fire for presenting a pejorative perspective. "It's a job that demands responsibility. People take what we say in our shows as the absolute truth so even a small error is unpardonable. At the same time, we have to go by popular belief. Mythological characters were pretty unorthodox but we can't show it too explicitly. An orthodox approach is better," Sagar cautions.

Heading: Quiz Master - Indian Express
Content:

Heading: Firth coming - Indian Express
Content:
Vikas Swarup on Slumdog Millionaire, the adaptation of his debut novel Q & A, winning the People's Choice Award

Slumdog Millionaire, British filmmaker Danny Boyle's movie based on Indian diplomat Vikas Swarup's debut novel Q & A, has won the People's Choice Award at the just concluded Toronto International Film Festival. And in Pretoria, Swarup has a million-dollar smile — his picaresque through urban India has not only wowed the audience in Canada but is also set to close the forthcoming London Film Festival. "I guess everybody loves a good fable. In fact, Simon Beaufoy (who adapted the novel) told me that it was the element of Dickensian drama that drew him to the book in the first place," says Swarup, now India's deputy high commissioner to South Africa, over the telephone.

The film, which revolves around the tale of a poor Dharavi waiter who wins the Indian version of Who Wants to be a Millionaire and who has to explain how he knew the answer to each question, is set to make its debut in India in November. It has a largely Indian cast — NRI Dev Patel playing the protagonist Jamal, Anil Kapoor as the quizmaster, and model Frieda Pinto and actor Irrfan Khan in other important roles. Even though Swarup has yet to see Boyle's adaptation of his novel, he is convinced that the director of Trainspotting and 28 Days Later would have done justice to it. "I have watched all his movies and I was certain that his own unique style will bring a completion to the craft. It was him and Simon's mastery over the script that made me sign the contract in the first place. I am sure it deserves every bit of the adulation it is getting," he says.

In fact, it was the involvement of Boyle and Beaufoy, who had earlier written The Full Monty, that made it easy for Swarup to accept the creative changes. "In any such adaptation, you can either accept the change or reject it. I knew they had retained the framework of the novel and I saw both the first and second drafts of the script since I had the creative rights. It would have been cinematically boring to have retained all the 12 questions and answers. I trusted their creative vision and now, I am waiting to see the DVD which Danny has promised he will send," he says.

Heading: Happy Surfing - Indian Express
Content:
Colin Firth chats about his latest movie, Mamma Mia

* Mamma Mia! was a massive stage success. Were you concerned that it might not translate well to the screen?

Yes, I was. With the stage production, the house lights come up and everybody participates. It's as if the barrier between the cast and the audience has broken down. How do you recapture that on celluloid? The only way we could do that was to find a sense of exuberance between ourselves that would communicate across the screen.

* Were you immediately captivated by the script?

I might have been if I'd understood it. It was a total leap into the unknown.

* Do you think Mamma Mia! has any serious points to make?

On the face of it, Mamma Mia! is a piece of pure uplifting escapism. Then you look closer and there's a very subtle subversive quality. It's about what it's like to get older and how that changes your perspective on sex and relationships.

* Did you have any qualms about taking on the role of Harry Bright?

I knew the movie could be a good one. The only doubts I had were about whether I would be up to the demands of the role. I don't have any history of singing or dancing. But I think they really wanted some ropey old amateurs. It makes other people comfortable when you dance and sing as badly as we all do.

* Were you able to improvise on this movie?

It's quite difficult to improvise on a musical. I might have tweaked a few lines here and there to fit it in with my sense of humour. But you can't take too many liberties with a piece like this. The margin of error is tiny. If you miss by a millimetre you've missed everything.

* Are you a big ABBA fan?

Not when I was growing up. But I think I've secretly liked their tunes all along.

Heading: Baddi master plan proposes relaxations for rural areas - Indian Express
Content:
The Himachal Pradesh government today decided to relax norms for allotment of vehicle route permits to Shimla citizens for the town's 'sealed' and 'restricted' roads. The processing fee for the issuance of vehicle permits has been slashed from Rs 500 to Rs 100. Some routes for plying vehicles have been rationalised too.

The decisions were taken at a meeting of the Cabinet held here today. Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal presided over it.

The Cabinet approved the proposal to simplify the Shimla Road Users and Pedestrians (Public Safety and Convenience) Act, 2008, to enable the public to ply vehicles on the sealed and restricted roads within Shimla. The rules will now be made more liberal and peoplefriendly.

The Cabinet has also permitted rationalization of the routes. The road from Chhota Shimla Chowk to Shimla Club has been made one 'sealed road', instead of the existing two routes. Chalet Day School to Jodha Niwas parking has been declared as one 'restricted route'.

The 'restricted route' from Cart Road to AG Office has been amended as Cart Road to State Bank of India Chowk, to facilitate the residents of Fingask Estate area. Kennedy House Chowk to Boileauganj has been clubbed as one 'restricted route' against the two routes at present. Cart Road to Subzi Mandi and Tara Hall to Shimla Typewriter via Kalibari have been deleted from the 'Restricted and Sealed Roads' category.

The route fee currently stands at Rs 2,500 for 'sealed roads' and Rs 2,000 for 'restricted routes'. It has been reduced to Rs 1,000 for both categories. Secretary Home will be authorised to issue permits in respect of 'sealed roads' and the Deputy Commissioner, Shimla, for 'restricted roads'.

The Cabinet has proposed an ordinance to replace the Himachal Pradesh Private Universities (Establishment and Regulation) Act, 2006, to open Chitkara University in the state. It has approved another ordinance for the establishment of Eternal University. The Cabinet has sanctioned 1,190 posts of different categories. Of these, the Education Department will get 1,135 posts of lecturers in the school cadre.

In addition, the Cabinet has decided to raise the PDS quota for ration card holders in the tribal belt and hard areas like Dodra-Kawar and Bara Bhangal. A spokesman said people living in these areas will get 8 kgs of rice and wheat each per head, instead of the maximum limit of 35 kgs of wheat flour and rice to every ration card holder. This will be applicable from July 1, 2008 to June 1, 2009.

The Cabinet has decided to provide subsidized essential commodities to Antodaya Anna Yojna, BPL and APL categories of 15.42 lakh ration card holders. For this, the government has sanctioned additional subsidy of Rs 51 crore.

Heading: E-mail threat: Security to be stepped up - Indian Express
Content:
Faced with mounting public pressure over the issue of excluding a large number of villages in the proposed Baddi Master Plan, the government is considering giving special relaxations for rural areas for day-to-day activities.

In the proposed master plan, the central Business district between Baddi and Nalagarh has been proposed for commercial and related activities. More than 65 percent area of Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh (BBN), earlier under the Town and Country Planning (TCP) Act, will be given relaxations for construction of houses, shops, small commercial units and agricultural operations, without any formal permission or fee.

Officials say the government has no plan to take over the management of Baddi and Nalagarh civic bodies including gram panchayats. Instead, the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh Industrial Development Authority (BBNIDA) will work in complete coordination with these institutions to address the various problems of the region.

"Since BBN is a fast-growing region, it has become essential to check haphazard growth here, and fully explore the potential of the area," said Deputy Commissioner Dr Amandeep Garg.

The DC added that in the proposed master plan, 124 villages beyond Nalagarh, which had been notified in May last year under the TCP Act, have now been exempted from any formal permission or procedure for change of land use in their routine activities.

The villagers residing in 'Abadi Deh' areas within the villages, which earlier were under the control of the TCP Act, have been exempted from map approval and fee for the construction of houses and commercial buildings.

BBNIDA will control only industries, commercial complexes, apartments, resorts and institutions. The DC said that the land use plan is highly flexible. It provides for 'mixed land use' concept.

The government had earlier attempted to segregate industrial activities from residential use of land. The DC said that the exemptions will not cover 100 meters on either side of the national highways and state highways, and 50 meters on either side of other major roads.

A provision has also been made to re-define the 'Abadi Deh' areas. Under the plan, only one industrial zone has been proposed between Baddi and Nalagarh at village Daawani. Other such zones have been proposed on the Nalagarh-Swarghat and Ropar roads, and around Bagheri Panchayat. In order to provide the regional rural mobility, an efficient public transport system has been proposed to minimize the crowding of the employment generation centres.

Heading: ‘Make efforts to find solution to Tibet issue’ - Indian Express
Content:
Taking seriously the recent e-mail threat of Indian Mujahideen about their plans to target the hill state, the government today decided to step up security all over the state, and keep a strict vigil on suspicious foreign nationals and migrants staying here as tourists and labourers.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, who returned here this morning from a two-day tour of Hamirpur, held a meeting with top police, intelligence, security and Home Department officials. The chief minister issued specific orders to strengthen security at all entry points, prominent religious shrines, venues of important fairs and festivals, and important installations like hydro-electric projects.

Other places where security will be stepped up include busy markets, crowded public places and important tourists destinations.

The security agencies have been advised to keep a track of the movements of the foreign nationals overstaying in the state, and also unregistered migrant labourers coming to Himachal for work. Senior government officials present at the meeting said the CM was very particular about security at the fairs, organised during the 'Navratra' festival and the Kullu Dussehra.

The vehicles entering the state will be searched thoroughly. The CM said there was a need to maintain strict vigil on guesthouses, hotels, resorts, sarais, parking places and other establishments, besides increasing the night patrolling.

Heading: New wheat variety attracts thousands - Indian Express
Content:
The Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile has resolved that all the Tibetans living in exile will make efforts in a peaceful manner to find out a solution to Tibet issue.

This was decided following deliberations during the eight-day long sixth session of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, which concluded on Tuesday.

Speaker TT Karma Chophel spoke of the efforts initiated by the Tibetan Parliament in gathering support of the international community to resolve the urgent situation inside Tibet after March 10 this year.

The Speaker said that in order to call for the much-needed support, efforts were made to attend important international forums, including the European Parliament in Brussels and the United Nations' Human Rights Council in Geneva.

The Speaker underlined the significance of the special general meeting on Tibet in November. He said the representatives attending the meeting, including settlement and welfare officers, members from local assemblies and Bod Rawang Denpai Legul Tsokchung, must take the opinion of a large number of Tibetans. PM Prof Samdhong Rinpoche spoke on the need to focus on legislations concerning the welfare of Central Tibetan Administration (CAT) officials.

Heading: Laser show to replace fireworks at Golden Temple - Indian Express
Content:
Farmers queue up at 3 am to get seeds of PBW-550 at PAU counters

The sale of a new wheat variety seed, PBW 550, today brought thousands of farmers to Punjab Agricultural University. Be it Patiala, Abohar, Mansa, Muktsar or as near as Jagraon, farmers from all over queued up at university seed sale counters as early as 3 am. Kuljit Singh a farmer from Dilwan, Mansa district, was in the queue since three in the morning and managed to get two bags of seed at noon.

Unlike him, Tehal Singh, a farmer from Patiala, was not so lucky. Waiting since 6 am, he could get only after 5 pm.

Another farmer, Amarjeet Singh from Moga, showed a pack of soiled notes from his pocket, saying, "I had brought this money to buy the seed. But the notes got soiled with sweat after standing in the heat for so long. Now the people at the sale window are refusing to accept these notes."

Unbearable humidity, long queues, torn clothes, soiled currency notes and heated arguments — none of these could deter the farmers who braved all odds to get the seed. On day one of the kisan mela, PAU had put up 10,000 bags of seed for sale, each bag weighing 40 kg, and by the end of the day, as per Dr Guriqbal Singh, Director, Farms, PAU, "Our sales have touched the 9,000 mark and the queue outside our sale windows is just as long as it was today morning."

The university is bringing in more seed tonight from its Laddowal farm and Dr Guriqbal Singh assures, "The sale of this variety will continue at our seed counters even after this mela ends."

B.S. Sidhu, Director, Agriculture, says, "Last year we had very less quantity of this seed, which is why we did not distribute it among the farmers. The department this year will distribute 10 kg seed kits to farmers all over the state for seed multiplication. Our target is that in the coming four years, PBW 550, along with PBW 502, will be able to phase out the current favourite wheat variety, PBW 343, which is now quite old and giving indications of varietal fatigue."

Dr N.S. Malhi, Director, Extension, PAU, adds, "This new variety is significantly superior to the popular varieties PBW 343 and PBW 502 as it possesses high degree of resistance to yellow and brown rust diseases." He says that this variety possesses resistance to the new virulent race (78S84) of yellow rust, to which all other varieties are susceptible. PBW 550 also has high degree of tolerance to terminal heat stress, which is usually seen during April when the temperatures shoot up. The grain and chapatti quality characteristics of the variety are also good.

PBW 550 was officially released last year, but was made available to the farmers this season. The state so far has only 20,000 quintals of seed of this variety. The seed of another new variety, PBW 502, was sold last year and currently covers 17 per cent of the total 35 lakh hectares of the crop area in the state.

Heading: Villagers start work on cleaning Sutlej river bed - Indian Express
Content:
In an effort to check pollution around the Golden Temple, the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee plans to replace the temple's legendary aatishbazi (fireworks) with a laser light-and-sound show.

On Diwali and Gurpurabs, lakhs of people throng the temple to enjoy the fireworks. A Punjabi adage eulogises the Diwali celebrations of Amritsar: Dal roti ghar di, Diwali Amritsar di (home cooked food and Amritsar's Diwali have no parallels). Gigantic firecrackers are burst by specialists designated as aatishbaz, who are hired by the SGPC just for this job. Each show lasts four-five hours and fireworks worth lakhs of rupees are burst on a single evening.

This show may be a visual delight for onlookers, but it does irreparable damage to the architectural marvel that the Golden Temple is. "Firecrackers emit toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen, which are extremely corrosive in nature. This show takes away a bit of the gold every time. Laser is a form of energy, which gets dissipated and is not dangerous. Trouble is, we are so attached to fireworks that nothing less than hawais and anaars will do for us. So, the laser show will have to be simulated well with sound effects to make it appear close to the real thing," says Prof A.K. Thukral from the Department of Environmental and Botanical Sciences at Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar.

"By now, aatishbazi has become an inalienable part of the Golden Temple's festivities. Being a long-time observer of the damage pollution has done to the temple, I strongly advocate making positive changes in keeping with our tradition. So a light and sound show is the most plausible option. We will begin our feasibility study in a few days," says SGPC president Avtar Singh Makkar.

"The gold isn't solid, but electroplated, and thus, delicate. The frescoes inside the sanctum sanctorum are done with vegetable dyes, thereby making them extremely vulnerable to fading away with corrosive gases. The white marble is getting yellowed. These features add to the beauty of the shrine but also make it prone to irreparable wear and tear," says Dr P.S. Mahoora, head of department of architecture at the university.

Early this year, a team from the Central Pollution Control Board visited the Golden Temple to compare its case with Agra's Taj Mahal. The team found that the levels of toxic gases and suspended particulate matter (SPM) around the temple were far less than that of the Taj Mahal. Interestingly, the Golden Temple receives more visitors on any given day than the Taj Mahal. The team suggested that after further investigation, vehicular traffic might have to be restricted in a radius of 500 metres from the Golden Temple, as is the case with the Taj Mahal.

Heading: BJP’s ‘silence’ on Capt’s expulsion does all the talking - Indian Express
Content:
Fed up of official apathy, residents of about six villages in Gidderpindi area, where floods played havoc recently, today started work on cleaning of the Sutlej river bed. They were led by environmentalist Baba Balbir Singh Seechewal.

Due to hundreds of sand mounds on the river bed created due to the flood, even a small release of water brings floods to the areas on the bank.

After an ardas today morning, Baba Seechewal and the villagers entered the river bed close to Giddarpindi railway bridge and started clearing the sand mounds. A ditch machine was brought by the Baba, while villagers were asked to bring tractor-trolleys to lift the sand. The surplus sand would be used to strengthen the "dhussi bandh", which developed a breach recently. Shankar Singh, sarpanch of Darewal village, said Baba Seechewal had conducted various meetings in all the flood-hit villages and they had decided to take action themselves. Baba Seechewal said after the cleaning, the flow of the river water will be in the right direction.

Heading: Strike at Pepsi’s Channo plant ends - Indian Express
Content:
Denials apart, the ruling Akali Dal's alliance partner BJP has been conspicuous by its silence all through the episode on Amarinder Singh's expulsion from the state Assembly. The BJP has preferred to "distance" itself from any offensive posturing against the former chief minister, leaving much of the onslaught to the Akalis. That the two alliance partners have had long bouts of confrontation during this tenure will not find many rebuttals, while observers say the Punjab BJP has made its intentions vocal by way of its silence.

Unlike dozens of Akali leaders, not one BJP leader from Punjab, or even the party high command in New Delhi, has chosen to come out with a statement against Amarinder Singh. A top BJP leader in New Delhi, requesting anonymity, quipped, "The BJP has its own agendas to pursue. The party has a lot to deliver instead of getting into such issues. The BJP needs to make the most of its overwhelming victory in the Assembly polls".

Leaders, both from the BJP and the Akali Dal, say the two alliance partners have agreed to disagree on certain issues on which neither side is willing to compromise. Sources in the party said the BJP's reluctance to join the debate on the issue has its roots in the "cash-for-query" scam that rocked the Parliament. Sources say senior BJP leader Arun Jaitely had then officially expressed concern over the danger of expelling opposition leaders by the House by way of majority.

There have been several indications that both the alliance partners in Punjab have agreed to pursue agendas independent of each other. This is the first time that the SAD (Badal) has decided to fight the ensuing Delhi Assembly elections without the BJP by its side as a partner. Its recent rally in New Delhi was also organised independent of the support of the BJP. Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, whose party is a significant constituent of the BJP-led NDA, has more than once expressed his willingness to prospects of having a tie-up with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) for the elections — the NDA's resistance to the move, if at all it fructifies, notwithstanding. Leaders in the Punjab BJP maintain that the matter is no longer about the contentious issues between the alliance, but about both the parties growing independent of each other even while remaining in the broad fold of the alliance.

The Dera Sacha Sauda is another issue. SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal has categorically ruled out seeking support of the Dera for his party in the elections. Its alliance partner, however, holds a completely different view. BJP state in charge Balbir Punj said his party will seek the support of all, including the Dera Sacha Sauda. In fact, the state BJP has been making inroads to garner the Dera's support. Interestingly, all through during the tenure of Amarinder Singh as chief minister, there were not many BJP leaders seen as "victims" of the alleged vendetta politics. State BJP president Rajinder Bhandari could not be contacted for his comments.

Heading: Badal makes more promises, pats own back - Indian Express
Content:
The month-long workers' strike and lockout at FritoLay India, a unit of PepsiCo India Holdings Limited, ended today, with an amicable settlement reached at with the intervention of the local authorities.

While the unit was opened today by the company management, regular production at the unit would only start tomorrow, after an intensive cleaning and washing operation was launched at the plant today.

The plant has been shut since August 20 after a dispute between the workers' union and the management arose and workers struck work and sat in a dharna outside the plant. The plant workers were joined by other employee unions, including the BKU, which lent support to them. A big rally was also organised outside the plant on September 9, whereby traffic was also held up on the busy Sangrur-Patiala state highway.

Incidentally, the company management had shifted its production base from here to West Bengal and Pune following the strike. Speculation was also rife about the company moving out the plant from Punjab in case the strike did not end. The plant was set up in 1989 and was producing "Kurkure" and "Lays" potato chips and utilising over 120 tonnes of potato everyday from nearly 1,500 farmers in the area. The company management today said in a statement: "PepsiCo is glad to announce that we have reached an amicable solution with the workers which benefits all. The plant will resume its operations from September 18". The management also thanked the administration, community and workers for their support.

Sources say an agreement was signed between the workers' union and the management last night, with the district authorities and local panchayats and the truck union also signatories to it. The meeting last night was held under the supervision of the district authorities, where the Sangrur Deputy Commissioner and SSP were also present.

The settlement was reached following the intervention of Sangrur MP Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa, who had helped convince the management for taking back all the suspended employees. He also took upon himself the responsibility of getting the terminated union president back into his job within two months. As per the agreement, the management would start operations at the plant from September 18 and the workers would end their strike. While the management would revoke the suspension of six of the 12 suspended workers and take them back on duty on the first day of the plant operations, the remaining six workers would be taken back within 15 days, after the district authorities complete an inquiry into the allegations against them.

Regarding revoking of the termination of union president Sanjeev Kumar, his case would be dealt with separately and Sangrur MP Dhindsa would press upon the management for his reinduction soon. Sources add that all future disputes would be handled by a committee comprising the management, workers and the local authorities, including the assistant labour commissioner. Meanwhile, workers sitting in a dharna outside the plant on the Sangrur-Patiala highway continued to remain there and will do so till tomorrow, when they will hold a "sadbhavna rally" outside the plant. The earlier proposal of the workers to hold traffic on the Sangrur-Patiala highway again tomorrow has been withdrawn, said striking workers' committee convener Krishan Singh.

Heading: Tourism in for an overhaul in state - Indian Express
Content:
With Lok Sabha elections in mind, Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today wooed voters, especially youth, with promises of development, adequate power supply and employment, besides berating the Congress-led government at the Centre and former chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh for "duping the public and committing several financial irregularities".

Meanwhile, the Congress rally remained a damp squib with the top brass of the party failing to show up.

Addressing a gathering at Khadoor Sahib on the occasion of 'Gurgaddi Divas' of Guru Angad Dev, Badal, while chiding the Congress with being "anti-Punjab", gave credit to his own party for planning out the development of the state. He outlined a number of power projects to be inaugurated at various places in the near future. "The foundation stone of a 2,000-MW thermal plant has already been laid at Talwandi Sabo, while the foundation stone of a 600-MW power generation plant would be laid on October 18 at Goindwal Sahib," he said.

He said foundation stones would be laid for a 1,500-MW thermal plant at Rajpura in December and 2,600-MW thermal plant in Malout in January. On this occasion, Badal also tried to woo the educated but unemployed youth by urging them to develop hi-tech dairy farms and produce and sell milk.

He added that the dairy development board would provide subsidies amounting to Rs 1.5 lakh to hi-tech farms, besides bearing the complete cost for animal insurance and construction of model sheds. Later, addressing mediapersons, Badal said according to a survey conducted by a leading magazine, Punjab had been ranked as the number three state in terms of revenue generation during the SAD-BJP tenure, while it was at 24th position during Capt Amarinder Singh's regime.

SAD (B) president Sukhbir Singh Badal, in his address, lambasted the Central government for not giving farmers the due prices for their crops. He added that the MSP for paddy was very less and amounted to fooling the farmers.

He said the first Indian Institution of Technology (IIT) in Punjab was being set up in Ropar, besides which the Dhirubhai Ambani Institute of Information Technology was also in the pipeline.

Avtar Singh Brar, Congress MLA from Faridkot, while speaking from the Congress stage, said the party would "avenge the wrongs done to former CM Captain Amarinder Singh" on returning to power.

Heading: Former minister Punia launches own party - Indian Express
Content:
In a move that could provide a major boost to tourism in the state, the Haryana government has decided to develop Gurgaon, Pinjore and Karnal as Meeting Incentive Conference Event (MICE) destinations. The decision to this effect was taken in the first meeting of the Haryana Tourism Development Council, held under the chairmanship of Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda.

It was decided in principle that the Tourism Department would develop pilgrim destinations at Kurukshetra-Pehowa-Haridwar and Hodal routes as part of Brij circuit. It was also decided to develop Narnaul as heritage city on the route to Shekhavati. Strengthening of air, road and rail connectivity to various tourists places is also on the cards, with special focus on Kurukshetra.

A decision was also taken to develop an integrated tourism resort at Kalesar, on the public private partnership (PPP) model, spread on nine acres. Kalesar is situated in the foothills of the Shivalik range of Himalayas in the Yamuna Nagar district, sharing its boundary with three states — Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh.

The area is a treat for nature lovers with a lot of bio-diversity, with dense sal and khair forests and grass-lands, which support an amazing variety of plants and animal species. A mere two-hour drive from Chandigarh and four-hour drive from New Delhi, Kalesar seems a natural choice for the resort.

The council also recommended an integrated tourism resort and spa at Mallah. With the construction of the bypass from Pinjore to Parwanoo, Mallah is set to become strategically important. Another such resort would be built at at Madhogarh, which lies on Mahendragarh-Loharu state highway, about 150 kilometres away from Delhi.

Principal Secretary to Chief Minister of Haryana, M L Tayal, said the government aimed to provide a thrust to tourism promotion activities so that it becomes a major engine of economic growth and of employment generation.

Heading: Slump expected in cotton yield even as per hectare production set to rise - Indian Express
Content:
Former industries minister of Haryana, Dr K R Punia, today launched a new political party - the Rashtriya Janhit Party. Announcing this at a press conference here today, Dr Punia claimed it would be the "first real pro-poor" political entity in the country. He said he had decided to form a party after fighting for the cause of the poor and the downtrodden under the banner Janhit Seva Sangathan for the last 15 years.

Dr Punia has been in and out of several parties in the past and has also served as industries minister in the Lok Dal-government led by the late Devi Lal.

He said his plan was to make it a national party, but his focus would be Haryana. He announced that the new party would contest the coming Lok Sabha elections and also the Haryana Assembly polls.

A number of BSP leaders, who have quit their party today to join him, were present at the press conference. Among them were Rajender Sharma, Rajiv Ahuja and Sanjay Jindal, all general secretaries of the BSP, and Sunil Kodala. Many more political leaders from different parties would join the new party in the days to come, he said.

He named Rajender Sharma as the working president of the party and Gyasi Ram as vice-president. Rajiv Ahuja was named the head of the youth wing of the party.

Dr Punia said that if he came to power in the state, jobs worth a minimum of Rs 10,000 a month would be provided to the educated unemployed and unemployment would be eradicated "within five years". He also promised long-term employment opportunities, 18-hour power supply to farmers and equal rights and opportunities to people of all castes and religions.

Heading: Hafed data now a mouse-click away - Indian Express
Content:
Cotton production in the state, in all likelihood, is set to go down this year. The yield is expected to be about 4.5 per cent less than that of last year, according to sources. However, as far as productivity is concerned, the cotton crop production per hectare in Haryana has improved this year.

In Haryana the cotton production this year is likely to be around 18 lakh bales against 18.85 lakh bales last year. But the productivity this year would be around 700 kg per hectare compared to 663 kg per hectare of last year. This was a very encouraging sign, according to sources in the Haryana Agriculture Department.

Dr B S Duggal, Additional Director, Agriculture, Haryana said that the reason for the expected decline in production this year was due to the reduction in the total land under cotton cultivation. While last year, cotton was grown on 4.83 hectares of land in the state, this year it was sown on just 4.17 hectare, he said.

Haryana and Punjab together contribute about 12 per cent of the country's total cotton production and even in Punjab, the output is expected to fall this year.

The major reason for the shrinking of area under cotton cultivation was unexpected rains, threat of mealy bug pest and anticipation of higher MSP of paddy, according to sources. Interestingly, both Punjab and Haryana had targetted

to bring 6.5 lakh hectare and six lakh hectare, respectively, under cotton crop during the start of kharif season this year.

Mealy bug did attack the cotton crop in Haryana, but timely action limited the damage, said Duggal.

The BT cotton production, though limited, was encouraging. "It is BT cotton that has saved the farmers. The cotton production per hectare too has increased as a result. The seed is costly, but the yield is much more, resulting in more profit for the farmers," said Duggal.

Heading: Dark temptations - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana State Co-operative Supply and Marketing Federation Limited (HAFED) has integrated its wide-spread network through computerisation of its core business activities. The federation has incorporated the data of its core applications, including food grain procurement, financial accounting and management and warehousing management, and has made it available online. The Enterprise Warehousing Management System, as it is called, was inaugurated by Dharam Vir, Chief Secretary, Haryana at HAFED's corporate office here today.

Sudhir Rajpal, Managing Director, HAFED, said, "We were working on this project for the past one and a half year and have been able to procure the data of more than 130 mandis and about 6,000 arhtiyas spread over 200 locations in the state." The project was implemented on pilot-basis at the corporation's district offices at Sirsa and Fatehabad.

The work for the food grain and warehousing management system was outsourced to WE EXCEL softwares and for the accounting and financial management it was given to Tele softwares. "The cost of the project is about Rs 15 lakh and we are looking forward to further extend it to fields like photo identity, geographical information system and to finally bring it down to the farmers' level," he said.

"Last year we collected data about wheat procurement from 131 centers in Haryana but it was offline. Then, customisation of all accounts was done and now, with the integration of data, daily reports about expenses, revenue and movement of goods in and out of warehouse can be maintained," added Rajpal.

As for financial accounting and management, the accounts of the corporate office and about 40 other independent accounting centres have been computerised and integrated. The application is also being rolled out in 62 Warehousing locations, however, linkages have been finalised to capture the data of all the 200 storage locations of HAFED.

Heading: Word power - Indian Express
Content:
Nikita Malhotra is all set to make Puneites an irresistable offer with her array of designer chocolates

A three feet fountain springs out the irresistibly dark melted chocolate swirling about itself, bouquets with chocolate bars in place of flowers and fire crackers wrappers that conceal these sinful enticements rather than crackers--all of these greet you as you walk into Nikita Malhotra's recently opened Chocolate Story, a store that serves chocolates in hundreds of inimitable forms, flavors and shapes. "I am a chocoholic and started making chocolates at home a year ago. People appreciated the effort and the designs and in due course I started taking orders for occasions, which eventually inspired me to open the Chocolate Story," adds Malhotra.

The seventeen year old is a twelfth commerce student and has also taken up various courses on chocolate making in Mumbai, Delhi as well as in the city. Speaking about the display Malhotra says, "The assortment has chocolate bouquets, chocolate champagne and much more in exotic flavours such as Dutch truffle, rum and raisin, dark chocolate, white chocolate, liquor chocolates and so on. The arrangement is one of the keys to the display. I have used a lot of presentation material such as glass cases, trays and pouches to give each design a matchless look."

Malhotra aims to go on experimenting with patterns and designs. "A lot of effort has gone into designing the bouquets that may vary from rupees 200 to 5000. However, a three feet chocolate fountain in which you can dunk everything from paan to marshmallows wil be a major attraction. I am also planning to come up with occasional designs such as chocolate crackers and rockets for Diwali. A section also includes chocolate walnut fudge, the well known Lonavla chocolate fudge, mousses, pastries, cakes and ice creams," adds Malhotra who also plans to get a degree in culinary arts in future and shift her focus towards desserts to come up with a concept of 80 desserts around the world.

"I can make at least 50 to 60 different chocolates. Dark chocolates have minimal calories and I will soon introduce a sugar free variety. The shelf life of my chocolates is up to six months but I bet they would not practically stay for more than a few hours once you get your hands on them," smiles Malhotra. The girl has that right for sure!

Heading: Sole mates - Indian Express
Content:
Sage and Diamond Publications have entered into a joint venture for the Marathi adaptation of serious non-fiction books

Scanning through the shelves in bookstores, to get hold of the Marathi adaptations of books reflecting the socio-political culture in India, will no more be that tedious an affair. Replenishing the Marathi section in the bookstores and libraries in Pune, will be the Marathi adaptation of a set of 12 books. As professor Narendra Jadhav, vice chancellor, Pune University releases the set of 12 books, today; the avid readers of serious non-fiction will be spoilt for choice.

In an effort to reach out to a larger group of readers by getting into vernacular medium, Sage Publications, in association with Diamond Publications, has come up with a set of books that apart from academic and reference books also include professional books reflecting practical approaches to new perspectives.

"Our main aim is to target those who are into serious non fiction reads. We also wanted to add content to Marathi. The reason we chose these books was to cover a wide area of subjects in social studies that are of concern to the current scenario of the country. We have women studies, socio political studies and the likes in the first set," elaborates Vivek Mehra, managing director, Sage Publications. The soon to be released set of 10 books also includes the Marathi adaptation of books that provide their readers with an insight into the issues that concern various walks of life.

Whether it be Sadiq Ahmed's review of the critical debate in the context of India's long term growth experience, opportunities and challenges or a collection of narrative on motherhood of women from all walks of life in the book Janani, the books encompass an array of topics, which provide a captivating read to those who look for serious non fiction.

"The vernacular medium often is the best medium to reach to the readers. As a publisher it also gives us immense satisfaction to provide people with what they want to read in their own mother tongue. Especially when it comes to reference and academic books it's always better to flip through the version, which is in one's own mother tongue," shares Mehra.

Apart from the books, which are academic in nature, the first set also has books reflecting practical approaches to new perspectives and challenges in life. For instance, the book Stress – burnout and balance guides its readers through managing stress and tackling with it in a relaxed way.

"The college goers have a lot to look for reference this semester. We are also hoping that the university will pick some of the books as secondary readings," says Mehra.

Heading: Marathi writer Gadgil dead - Indian Express
Content:
Two nineteen-year-olds move beyond books to set up a customised shoe store with a difference

Wonder years

At an age when most young boys are busy with friends, having fun or tapping technology on networking websites, 19-year old Samrit Shah and Himay Kumbhani have used their talent for setting up their firm, Toe 2 Head, a shoe customising outlet. It all started in December 2007 when Shah was sitting idle at home and to kill time he decided to paint his white sports shoes. "At the New Year's party, my friends saw my shoes, they loved the design and they wanted me to work on their shoes as well. This made me think that I can make a career out of it," says Shah.

Foot work

Soon Shah's friend Himay Kumbhani also joined him and the duo started operating in Pune and Mumbai. Currently, the two of them are studying liberal arts at the Foundation for Liberal and Management Education in Pune.

Boosting factor

Elaborating on the response and the outputs from the venture, Kumbhani says, "Although we did not expect that what we started as a time-pass activity could turn into a profit-making venture. But the response that we got was more than we expected and it encouraged us to give our 100 per cent. We work on 5-10 pairs a month and charge Rs 2000-3000 per pair, depending as per the design."

In-order

The orders that they get are mainly from college students or parents who want to gift unique shoes to their children. Besides, they have already finished an order from Muscat and are in finalising terms on an export order for Canada. They use special waterproof paint, which they get from Spain. However, bulk orders are not what they are looking for. Explains Kumbhani, "We want to work with different colours and experiment with various designs. With bulk orders, you have to stick to one design and there is no scope for creativity. Also, such orders consume a lot of time and being students, we cannot give so much time, as we cannot ignore our studies."

Challenges

One challenge, which they faced when they started, was their high charges. Kumbhani says, "We are very different from other shoe customising companies. We are specialised and give personalised designs. Art has got its value and if people really like our work they will pay for it, immaterial of whether it costs 2,000 or 20,000."

Fun time

Apart from work and studies, both of them have keen interest for sports. While Shah loves football, music and adventure, Kumbhani loves to catch up with friends during weekends and is also very fond of football and poker.

Balancing act

Both Shah and Kumbhani make sure that they maintain a right balance between studies and business. Says Shah, "We usually work during the nights, and attend classes in the afternoon."

Future ahead

"Once we are finished with our course, we will start taking bulk orders also. Till now, we have been operating from Pune and Mumbai, but now we also plan to expand our designing horizons to shirts, bags, caps and so on as well. So we are thinking of opening a studio. Also we are working on various ideas to promote our firm, which include setting up a website of the company as well," says Shah.

Words of wisdom

They feel that there is no age-limit on thinking big. "If you are young and have a dream, go for it. Since age is on you side, you have nothing to lose. One should always give his dream its due chance of pursuance, no matter whether he or she succeeds or fails in the end," smile they.

Heading: Zensar launches infrastructure management unit - Indian Express
Content:
Well-known Marathi writer and economist Gangadhar Gadgil (86) passed away in Mumbai on September 15 following a heart attack. Gadgil was an economist by profession but contributed to Marathi literature in a big way and wrote short stories, stories for children and novels.

Gadgil started writing short stories in 1941 and did not lay down his pen till June 2008, when he wrote five fairy tales for children. He was translating these stories in English and working on it till September 13. He was recipient of Sahitya Akademi award for his creation Eka Mungiche Mahabharat in 1996. He received many prestigious awards from state government and other organisations.

As an economist, Gadgil worked as a consultant for different companies and also stood for consumer rights. He was president of Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Sahitya Sammelan (Marathi Literary Meet) in 1981.

Heading: Meet of political parties, Dalit leaders to mark 75 years of Poona Pact - Indian Express
Content:
Zensar Technologies, a provider of software and business process outsourcing services, on Wednesday, announced the launch of its infrastructure management business unit. Ankit Ghosh, global head of Zensar's infrastructure business, said, "Zensar has invested in a robust IM practice, launching new services lines called ZenRIMS (Zensar Remote Infrastructure Management Services) and ZenGDC (Zensar Green Data Centre). Eastern Europe is an important market for these services while South Africa, Australia and Singapore too have shown growth potential. Zensar could be looking at an acquisition in the networking and security space to enhance capability and scale for expansion into these territories. IM Shared Services has been showing significant traction with its pay-per-use model and the fixed services packs."

Since its pilot launch earlier this year, Zensar has signed several deals with existing clients and new customers in the US, Europe and South Africa, totalling to over $ 10 million of business booked in the current fiscal. Ganesh Natarajan, deputy chairman and managing director, Zensar, and chairman-NASSCOM, said, "The global infrastructure management business is growing steadily and older assertions are being amended to reflect the growth. Zensar's IM practice is aiming at being a $ 50 million entity by 2010-11, with a workforce of over 1,000. The company is also looking for an acquisition worth $ 5-6 million in the 2010 fiscal for market penetration in Europe or South Africa in this area."

Krishna Ramaswami, vice president and head of the newly formed strategic services and supply units at Zensar, said, "The worldwide infrastructure management services market today is $ 524 billion. The industry growth has been at 60 per cent year-on-year in the IM space."

Heading: Bank vice chairman held for rape - Indian Express
Content:
As the Poona Pact — between the Hindu caste leaders and the oppressed classes led by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar — will complete 75 years on September 24, a unique convention has been organised to mark the event where the Dalit and OBC leaders from various parties will share the dais at the BJ medical college ground.

A large number of Dalit, OBC leaders will participate in the meet, announced former MP and Bharipa Bahujan Mahasangh (BBM) leader Prakash Ambedkar.

Ambedkar said that he has spoken to several leaders and was keen on forming an alternate political front and that the BJP and Shiv Sena are expected to be part of the Front. "I will not divulge details now as talks are still on,'' he said at a press meet.

The leaders expected to attend the meet include BJP leader Gopinath Munde, Jamaat-e-Islami leader Mustaffa Faruki, Peasants and Workers Party leader and MLA Ganpatrao Deshmukh, Jansurajya leader and minister in the state cabinet Vinay Kore, Adivasi leaders Divakar Pedam, Laxman Mane, Dhangar community leader Haribhau Bhade and Annarao Patil.

Ambedkar came down heavily on the present political system calling it "insensitive" and said that next elections will answer this discontent. He said that a five year plan in terms of power, agriculture, employment and urban development has been readied.

Heading: ‘PCB’s development work in full swing’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune police have arrested Prabhu Jadhwani, vice chairman of Seva Vikas Bank, for allegedly raping a 32-year-old woman, who approached the bank for a loan on August 17.

The victim, in the police complaint, alleged that Jadhwani offered her a cold drink laced with sedatives. Jadhwani then allegedly took her to a hotel in his car and raped her.

Jadhwani told the lady that he had recorded obscene videos of her on his mobile phone and that he will circulate the clip if she told anyone about the incident. Jadhwani was produced before the court on Thursday and was remanded to police custody till Saturday.

Heading: Three years RI for gangster Marne, nine accomplices - Indian Express
Content:
Development work in several wards under the jurisdiction of the Pune Cantonment Board was on in full swing, with several projects and initiatives proposed by the recently elected board members already underway, Santosh Kavade of the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and elected member from ward seven said on Thursday.

PCB vice president, Prasad Kedari of the Congress said, "The members are concentrating on their respective wards and going all-out to meet the requirements of residents across the cantonment zone. Development is our top priority and collective agenda," Kedari said during an interaction with media persons.

Elaborating on the various initiatives taken in the Ghorpadi region, Kavade said, "The focus is on education and providing jobs to unemployed youth. The PCB has recruited a few persons from ward seven. I have also asked industries in the area to give preference to those who are unemployed," Kavade said. Kavade stressed on the need to improve standards of education and infrastructure in the schools. "There is a proposal to convert the Swami Vivekanand School, which currently functions in Marathi medium, into an English medium school. A junior college also will be started in the Ghorpadi Village High School," he said.

Development projects worth Rs 1.5 crore have been planned for Ghorpadi region, he said.

When asked if he would aim at bagging the post of PCB vice president next year, Kavade said, "It is too early to comment. However, I am willing to contest provided my fellow members extend their full support."

Heading: Promotional projects in freezer: Mayor backs decision - Indian Express
Content:
The Shivajinagar court on Thursday sentenced the ten accused in gangster Sandeep Mohol murder case to three years rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1,000 each for illegal possession of sharp weapons.

Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) S J Ansari passed the order in this regard.

The convicts include gangster Ganesh Marne and his nine accomplices identified as Rahul Ramchandra Taru, Nilesh Kisan Mazire, Anil Balu Khilare, Deepak Mokashi, Sharad Tukaram Vithkar, Vijay Mahipat Kangude, Jameer Mehboob Sheikh and Indrajeet Mishra.

Gangster Sandeep Mohol was shot dead near Kothrud police station in broad day-light in October 2006. Soon after the incident, the members of Marne gang fled to Ambejogai in Beed.

But the team of Anti Extortion Cell of Pune police Crime Branch arrested them at Ambejogai .

The police recovered a jeep, a car, three swords, three choppers and two daggers from the gangsters. In addition to charges of murder, they were also booked under the Arms Act.

The defence lawyers had argued that the case of murder was registered with the Kothrud police station but the Crime Branch officers arrested the accused.

Assistant public prosecutor Shilpa Mahatekar argued that the crime branch was holding a parallel investigation into the matter.

Heading: ATS probes blast accused’s links with SIMI’s Pune module - Indian Express
Content:
Mayor Rajlaxmi Bhosale on Thursday justified the decision of ruling alliance NCP-Shiv Sena and opposition BJP to put the Rs 19.5-crore promotional plan for the Commonwealth Youth Games starting on October 12 in freezer even as the Congress critised the move.

"The standing committee members are responsible leaders and they must have thought well before taking the decision. They are capable of taking decisions in the interest of the city," Bhosale told reporters.

The PMC has invested a lot of money gearing up for the international event, Bhosale said. "The decision to not to allow any additional funds for 'luxury' must be taken considering the financial status of the civic body." She maintained silence when pointed out that the plan was proposed only after in-principle approval of all political parties in a meeting called by her.

City Congress chief Abhay Chhajed said that the NCP, Shiv Sena and BJP are unnecessary politicising the games by putting the proposal in freezer. It was meant for creating a better image of the city.

"The ruling alliance is following the agenda of opposition BJP and has put the pride of city at stake," he said adding the Congress will ensure that the proposed work will be carried out at any cost.

The civic administration had proposed sanctioning of the funds for cultural programmes during the youth baton relay and promotional hoardings, special mobile vans for publicity and advertisement in the media.

Heading: Sutali bombs banned - Indian Express
Content:
The state anti-terrorism squad (ATS) is investigating whether Abdul Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer, the suspected mastermind behind the recent serial blasts, was in touch with the members of the SIMI module in Pune.

"We have some inputs that Tauqeer was in Pune. But there is no concrete evidence as of now. It is matter of investigation," said state ATS chief Hemant Karkare.

Meanwhile, the ATS has taken custody of Bilal Ghulam Rasool Kagzi, a law graduate from Pune who was arrested in August by the Mumbai crime branch in an extortion case. According to the ATS, Kagzi was supplying jihadi literature to the SIMI sleeper cell members in Pune. He had given 'jihadi' literature to SIMI suspects Feroz Mehboob Pathan of Makka towers in Ghorpade Peth and Imtiyaz Baba Miya Sheikh of Thane, who have been arrested by the Pune ATS unit.

Sources from ATS said 40 books of 'jihadi' literature were seized from Pathan, while a book of jihadi literature and some CDs were seized from Sheikh. The ATS is now investigating if Kagzi was in any contact with Tauqeer. Both were reported to have good communication skills and technical knowledge. Police suspect that they conducted several secret meetings of SIMI module members in Pune, aimed at developing the logical support for the front-liners.

Kagzi, a native of Kosamba village in Surat, was present in Gujarat during the serial blasts at Ahmedabad. Investigations have revealed his links with the Chhota Shakeel gang and it is suspected that he was gathering funds for jihadi movement.

ATS sources said the sleeper cell in Pune was well connected to the state and nationwide network of SIMI. Kagzi, who completed his law studies from A A Khan Law College and Dr Mohammed Salim Honali, a former professor of dentistry at M A Rangoonwala College of Dental Sciences and Research Centre at Azam Campus, who was arrested from his native place in Karnataka in connection with the Ahmedabad blasts were indoctrinating the Pune youths into jihadi culture. Honali was reported to be proficient in liquid bomb technology and apparently trained SIMI cadres at a camp in Dharwad, Karnataka.

Investigations by the Mumbai crime branch had revealed that a key SIMI leader, Yusuf Khan, also a law graduate from Pune, had indoctrinated Kagzi to the jihadi ideology. Khan's name came up during the interrogation of Kagzi by Mumbai crime branch sleuths.

"Kagzi has told us that Yusuf Khan, who was his senior at the A A Khan law college, indoctrinated him to SIMI's ideology. Kagzi then introduced him to Ayaz Khan and Nadeem Sheikh, who were arrested in fake currency case by the Pune ATS," said joint commissioner (Mumbai crime branch)Rakesh Maria.

"Yusuf is a native of Dhule. Our teams have conducted searches there, but he could not be traced," Maria said.

Heading: How deafening was the festival? Scientists study effect on your health - Indian Express
Content:
The Pune police have banned the sale, possession and bursting of big crackers usually called sutali bomb, said Commissioner of Police Satyapal Singh in a relese issued here on Thursday.

It also said that the last date for issuing the temporary licenses of selling crackers is November 10 and that no license would be issued after this date.
