Bursting crackers is banned around the police commissionerate as per the Mumbai police Act 1951. Anyone violating the law will be punished. Besides, blowing of crackers making loud noise is banned from 10 pm to 6 am.

Police have appealed to the citizens to avoid bursting crackers that make noise more than 125 decibel. As a precautionary measure, citizens should avoid bursting any crackers around cracker stalls.

Citizens should abide by the laws and action would be taken against those who are found bursting crackers that create loud noise and air pollution, especially around hospitals, educational institutions, courts and on roads, the release said.

Cracker stall owners have been asked to provide adequate parking space for their customers. The cracker stall owners should alos make sure that their stalls are not causing traffic jams or accidents.

Heading: Acquisition for airport: Farmers not happy with  rehab package - Indian Express
Content:
Did you face symptoms like nausea, giddiness and vomiting after being exposed to more than two hours of noise on the concluding 'immersion' day function of the Ganesh festival? Could you hear your mobile ring during the cacophony and did you raise your voice while talking to a friend standing at arm's length?

These and other questions were asked during a random but scientific survey conducted by doctors from the Indian Medical Association (IMA), environmental science students from Fergusson College and University of Pune. While the initial findings show that noise levels had touched nearly 119 decibels (dB) at Mandai - the annual survey of the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) also shows a rise in the noise levels at certain places in the city.

While the decibel recordings were taken every 10 minutes at three spots in the city and presently are being analysed, the initial trends show that the noise levels were the highest at Mandai at 119 dB,. According to Indian medical standards the maximum permissible limit of noise in the residential areas during daytime is 55dB and at night is 45dB.

Simultaneously, the annual survey conducted by MPCB during the last five days of the Ganesh festival too showed that there was an increase in the noise levels this year. Results of the survey conducted at 20 places in the city are being analysed, P K Mirashe Regional officer, MPCB said but trends show an increase in the deafening noise levels at various places.

According to Dr Avinash Bhondwe, President of the city unit of the IMA, health effects of noise pollution can range from irritation to even hearing loss. While noise may not seem as harmful as the contamination of air or water, it is a pollution problem that affects human health and can contribute to a general deterioration of environmental quality, he said.

Below a sound level of 80 dB hearing loss does not occur at all. However temporary effects are noticed at sound levels between 80 and 130 dB. A sound level of 150 dB or more can physically rupture the human eardrum. The degree of hearing loss depends on the duration as well as the intensity of the noise. Prof Sarika Singh and other team members Rupali Bhosale, Priti Kulkarni, Dr Pallavi Shinde assisted Dr G R Pathade, chief coordinator of the Environmental Science Department at Fergusson College, in the survey.

According to Singh, as many as 150 people were given questionnaires pertaining to the deafening levels during the Ganesh festival that saw the participation of nearly 3,000 mandals. Students positioned themselves on September 14- the day of the immersion of Lord Ganesh at three busy points in the city-Laxmi road, Tilak road and Mandai.

Heading: Anti-Dow lobby gets Shiv Sena support - Indian Express
Content:
Farmers whose land is being acquired for the proposed Rajguru International Airport have demanded reconsideration of the government's proposal. In the first round of talks with Pune district Collector Chandrakant Dalvi, the farmers demanded that nearly 15 per cent of irrigated land be left out of the project, coming up on 2,565 hectares.

Among the demands put forth by the farmers are a Special Economic Zone-kind of rehabilitation policy with guaranteed employment as well as a buyback scheme of developed land. The regional committee led by Dalvi is set to discuss these demands with the technical committee for airport evaluation from Delhi.

"We have started with the discussions with the farmers and all their demands will be placed before the technical committee for evaluation," he said. Deputy Collector and coordinator of land acquisition Dnyandev Thube said this was the first of such meetings with the representatives of the affected villagers. The plan is to gradually meet all the affected farmers, he said. With the Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh asking the revenue officers to speed up the process of acquisition, talks with the farmers have begun at five of the seven villages that have been listed for acquisition. The villages include Chandoos, Shiroli, Waki Budruk, Koregaon Budruk, Kiwle, Pimpri Thakur and Wadgaon. Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) Pune region officers said the notification for acquisition of land was issued in September last year and the measurement for the land would start in a month's time. The objections and suggestions will be under Section 32 (2) of the land acquisition act.

While MIDC will be carrying out the land acquisition, issues relating to airport construction is to be tackled by Maharashtra Airport Development Corporation (MADC). The site is located three km from Rajgurunagar and is slated to have two airstrips.

Heading: Extra test to select lecturers hits time warp - Indian Express
Content:
The agitation against a research centre being set up by Dow Chemicals at Shinde village in Pune district has taken a political turn with the Shiv Sena coming out in open support of the campaign to scrap the project.

Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly Ramdas Kadam on Thursday vowed full support to the villagers of Shinde village who have been putting up stiff opposition against the company officers. The villagers have been stalling work at the construction site since January this year. On Wednesday, a furious mob burnt down a vehicle used by Dow India for its Pune project.

"We will not allow the company to come to the state and our party will take up the issue strongly," Kadam said, extending full support to the villagers. Kadam visited the proposed R&D site of Dow Chemical. "I am planning to take up issue in the upcoming Assembly session as well," said the leader of Opposition.

Recent violent outbursts saw a mob of 100 people setting fire to a tin sheet and damaging machinery and other materials of the company in July. Kadam has assured the villagers all support and said they would be provided all support to prevent the company from laying base here.

Lokshasan Andolan and Bhamchandra Dongar Bachao Warkari Shetkari Sangharsh Samiti with support of former high court judge BG Kolse Patil, social activist Vilas Sonawane have been putting up stiff opposition against the centre since January 16.

The company has plans of setting up a research and development centre with an initial investment of Rs 400 crore. It plans to put in place by 2010, as many as 500 scientists looking into energy conservation, water purification and pharmaceuticals.

Heading: After 25 yrs of high risk, a free house as a gift - Indian Express
Content:
Twice-a-year proposal: UGC clearance comes too late for exam in October, university cannot hold one till January

A delayed decision by the University Grants Commission (UGC) in allowing the University of Pune (UoP) to conduct the State Eligibility Test (SET) twice a year has resulted in the wannabe lecturer candidates being forced to wait till January 2009 for their next chance. Had the UGC conveyed its decision at least by August-end, the university would have been in a position to conduct one exam next month.

As a result around 25,000 aspiring college lecturers across the state will have to wait another four months to sit for the SET.

The UoP had asked the UGC to grant the permission for taking SET twice a year considering the huge number of candidates appearing for the exams. The vice-chancellor Narendra Jadhav had recently told the media that as a special case, the UGC had granted permission to the UoP to conduct the SET exams twice a year.

The UoP had sent the proposal to the UGC in May 2008 after the results of this year's SET exam, conducted in February, were declared. The UGC replied only in the first week of September when the next exam date (January 18, 2009) was already declared and sale of application forms was started.

"If the UGC would have replied earlier, say till July, we would have been able to conduct one more exam this year probably in October," said N N Godbole, coordinator of the SET exam centre.

"We waited for the clearance of UGC till August-end to declare the next dates of the exams. But we could not wait further as it requires two to three months of preparations for arranging the exams excluding the sale of application forms, which ends on September 18," said Godbole.

"We have to also consider that the dates should not clash with the other competitive exams like MPSC and UPSC as the same candidates usually appear for these exams too," he added. Incidentally, UoP has been conducting the SET twice a year till two years back. But the UGC went to the once-a-year format saying all other centres conduct SET once a year.

But as the average pass percentage of SET is a meagre two, there was a huge demand from the candidates to conduct the test twice a year.

"Moreover, the number of candidates appearing for SET in other states is very low compared to Maharashtra. For example in Gujarat only around 6,000 candidates appear in the exam," said Godbole.

"As the SET papers can be written in Marathi, candidates from rural areas prefer appearing for SET instead of the National Eligibility Test (NET). As UoP is the biggest and one of the best centres in the country for conducting SET for candidates from Maharashtra and Goa, our demand was valid," Godbole added. He also said that the vice-chancellor personally looked into the issue to help the candidates.

SET principle

Clearing SET is a necessary condition to work as a lecturer in any college or university in the state. There is a National Eligibility Test (NET) also, which allows a candidate to work as a lecturer in any college or university across the country. NET is conducted twice a year. If SET is also conducted twice a year, it gives four chances for a candidate in a year to clear either of the exams.

Heading: Government pays up Rs 246 cr for cane dues - Indian Express
Content:
For conservancy staff in Maharashtra, this should come as a just reward for the years of labour put in by them in the most unenviable of conditions. Soon, after spending the entire day cleaning the city's filth, they would at least have the satisfaction of coming home to a place of their own.

On Wednesday the State Cabinet decided to give free houses for conservancy staff of all municipal corporations and municipal councils across the state who have completed at least 25 years in service. This follows a promise made by Chief Minister Vilasrsao Deshmukh on October 19 last year when he had assured free houses, welfare board and free medical treatment in government hospitals for the conservancy staff.

The promise came barely a month after The Indian Express started running reports on the high mortality rate of conservancy staff engaged in the job of cleaning up Pune. The series was kicked off on October 12 with a story titled "227 Pune corporation staff killed cleaning up the city in just over 2 years."

"The government is committed to give justice to each and every person of society. Conservancy staff are also part of society and they have rights to live like others," Deshmukh said after the special cabinet meeting at Aurangabad. He noted that the conservancy staff spent their entire lives in cleaning up work and could not earn enough to even purchase a house.

Thus, the state government has decided to give something for the conservancy staff and free home scheme is one amongst them, Deshmukh said.

Under this scheme, conservancy staff of all municipal corporations and municipal councils across the state will get free houses from state government. The ownership of the house will be given for those completing at least 25 years of service. Around 90,000 conservancy staff in the state stand to benefit.

Soon after the Express series, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) had increased the financial assistance to the kin of deceased employees of the conservancy department to Rs 1 lakh - a life insurance cover of Rs 50,000 and financial assistance of Rs 50,000 from the welfare scheme.

A team of officials led by Union secretary for social justice Arvind Prasad, who visited the city in October last year, had suggested measures to improve the working conditions of the conservancy staff. The committee appointed by the PMC had also concluded that there were insufficient protective gears available for the staff working in high-risk conditions.

The absence of first aid kits, drinking water near the working site and inordinate delay in supplying soaps to the staff were pointed out. It also recommended that the PMC carry out regular medical check up of the staff. Thereafter, the PMC has also initiated many measures to improve the working conditions of the high-risk employees by providing protective gears and other facilities. It also introduced mechanised cleaning by way of two sweeping machines to clean up the streets and is all set to hire machine to clean up the city's manholes. The PMC also made the health check up compulsory for conservancy staff while maintaining the health records of each of its conservancy staff members.

Heading: BSP member gunned down in custody - Indian Express
Content:
Giving a push to disinvestment and privatisation of sugar mills, the state government has released Rs 246 crore as payment for cane dues of cooperative sugar mills of 2007.

A Government Order issued in this connection on Thursday, stated: "In pursuance to disinvestments and privatisation process, the sum of Rs 246 crore is being released to clear the payment of cane arears."

Earlier, on receiving a lukewarm response from investors towards such mills — most of which are sick units — the state government had relaxed norms related to its land use to enable investors to use the adjoining land of the mills for profit-making commercial activities.

The Mayawati government, within a month after coming to power in May 2007, had decided on 100 per cent disinvestment of sugar mills.

The tender process started with inviting the Request for Qualification for the strategic sale of the entire equity of the government in Uttar Pradesh Sugar Corporation Limited, which owns 33 sugar mills.

The process hit a roadblock as only one of the five bidders, submitted financial bid after a physical verification and inspection of the assets and liabilities of the mills. Of the 33 mills of the Corporation, only 14 are functional. The rest were sick (non-functional or defunct) units.

"Even the functional ones do not have the desired capacity," said a Corporation official. Usually, a mill having a capacity to crush 5,000 quintal cane or above on a daily basis, is considered viable. But the Corporation has only one mill with a crushing capacity of 3,000 quintal. The rest are obsolete with less than 1,000 quintal capacity.

"This is why running such mills is a deficit venture for the state government," the official added.

Seeing the delay in the disinvestment process, the government is gearing up to run these mills on its own, as the crushing season is round the corner — from mid-October to first week of November.

"At present, machines are being repaired at the mills," said R B Singh, Joint Managing Director of Uttar Pradesh Sugar Corporation Ltd. "The moment the disinvestment process is complete, we will handover the mills to private companies. But we cannot keep the mills closed waiting for disinvestments to take place," he added.

The Corporation, however, is not expecting much work this year as cane crop — as per their estimate — is 20 to 30 per cent less than the previous year. "Last year, we got 882.81 lakh quintal cane for our 14 functional mills. This year, the target is 655.55 lakh quintal," said an official.

Heading: Tobacco survey set to begin in state from October 2 - Indian Express
Content:
Angry mob resorted to violence in Laxmanpur Mishran village on Thursday morning after the murder of a Bahujan Samaj Party supporter, Manish Shukla, in police custody on Wednesday night. They thrashed the policemen, damaged vehicles and blocked the traffic on the Kannauj-Kanpur Highway for nearly three hours.

Shukla was shot dead by the son of his business partner Vasant Gopal Agnihotri. Since the local policemen were allegedly involved in the murder case, a case under Section 120 B of the IPC has been registered against Uttaripura Chowki In-charge, Hridya Narain Tiwari. He has also been suspended.

Provisional Armed Constabulary has been deployed in the area to prevent any untoward incident. Deputy Inspector General (Kanpur Range) Kamal Saxena said, "Shukla died in police custody. We are investigating the police's role in the murder."

The Bilhaur police has registered a murder case against four persons, including Agnihotri and his three sons Krishna Kumar, Pawan Kumar and Pravin Kumar. Pravin has been arrested while others are absconding.

Shukla, Raja Tiwari and Agnihorti were timber contractors, who had been running the business as partners for the last few years. Recently, Shukla and Agnihorti came to loggerheads over a financial dispute.

On Wednesday evening, Tiwari and Shukla went to Agnihorti's house. Shukla and Tiwari entered into a scuffle with the family members and ransacked the house before leaving the place.

Following which, Agnihotri's sons lodged a complaint against Tiwari and Shukla at the Uttaripura Chowki. Subsequently, Hridya Narain Tiwari, along with two constables, went to Shukla's house and arrested him at 11.30 pm. The police has also arrested Tiwari.

While the police were taking the duo to the police station, Agnihotri and his sons attacked them. Before the police could take any action, Pravin fired two bullets at Shukla that killed him instantly. The assailants fled away instantly.

Shukla's elder brother, Rajole said, "Hridya Narain Tiwari was involved in the conspiracy. Agnihotri and his sons murdered my brother in connivance with him." He alleged that the police had allowed Agnihotris to carry out their personal vendetta against Shukla.

On Thursday morning, several locals gathered and forced the closure of shops in Uttaripura and Laxmanpur Mishran villages. When the policemen tried to disperse the mob, they beat them up, injuring a few policemen including constables Ram Dulare and Hari Singh. 

The mob then blocked the Grand Truck Road. DIG Kanpur Range Kamal Saxena, SSP of Kanpur Ashok Kumar Singh and SP (Rural) Lal Bahadur assured that action would be taken against the guilty officers.

Heading: Recruitment scam: Govt yet to allow prosecution of guilty - Indian Express
Content:
Everytime you light up a cigarette, what is the first thought that crosses your mind? Do you prefer to stick to one brand of khaini or does it change? Does the 'No Smoking' banner actually stop you from smoking?

These are some of the questions, which smokers and tobacco consumers of some 70,000 households across the country will be answering.

The Ministry of Health, which is all set to impose a ban on smoking in public places from October 2, is supporting the country's first nationwide survey on tobacco consumption habits, conducted by Mumbai's International Institute of Population Sciences (IIPS). While the survey is already on in most of the states, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh will have the survey from October onwards.

The survey will bring together the first comprehensive data on number of tobacco consumers, male and female consumers and the impact of government's several campaigns.

Director of IIPS Dr F Ram said the survey, which is being supported by Ministry of Health and WHO, will be a three-dimensional survey. "We are targeting nearly 4,000 households from the state. We are looking at three different sets of people — smokers, non-smoking tobacco consumers and passive smokers," Dr Ram said.

The survey will also cater to those who are trying to quit smoking or have already done so, with different data of both men and women.

"We have tobacco cessation clinics in almost all states. We will also look at people who are trying to quit tobacco consumption, asking them how they are trying to do it and where are they getting medical support from," said Dr Ram.

The survey will actually bring out the number of male and female tobacco consumers in the country, he added. The institute has selected agencies, which will be trained for data collection in different states. 

While the agency for the state is yet to be finalised, the Bihar state survey got delayed due to the floods. The target for completion of the survey is March 2009.

Heading: Two weeks on, lawyers of terror accused refuse to come to court - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti-Corruption Organisation (ACO) engaged in the investigation of the police recruitment scam still awaits the state government's nod to prosecute police officers involved in the process.

"Of the 42 boards that had recruited jawans in various units of the UP Police, we have completed our probe into the work of 32 boards. The ACO has sought the government's sanction to prosecute the officers associated with these boards," said Additional Director General (ADG) of Police Ram Lal.

Sources in the ACO said the investigation into the work of the remaining 10 boards is in its final stage. "ADG Ram Lal will retire on September 30. He wants to complete the task before his retirement," said a source.

Home Secretary Mahesh Gupta said the government had sought legal opinion on the issue of giving sanction to prosecute the officers.

While the government takes its time, investigation into the recruitment scam has badly affected the normal functioning of the ACO.

"Unlike in the past, this year, our performance in prosecuting corrupt employees is very poor," said a officer.

"Though the state government had provided additional officers and infrastructure for the investigation, most of the ACO's staff is still engaged in the probe," he added.

Heading: Pension scheme at bay as govt takes no step for implementation - Indian Express
Content:
For the second time in a week, none of the Lucknow-based advocates defending terror accused, turned up for hearing in 12 cases at the special court in Lucknow District Jail on Thursday.

The advocates have been staying away ever since two of them — Mohammad Shaoib and A M Fareedi — were attacked by a group advocates in the civil court on August 12. The lawyers had objected to Shaoib and Fareedi taking up the cases of the terror accused. After the attack, the administration had decided to shift the special court to the jail.

On Thursday, while a few of the terror accused appealed to the court to provide them advocates, others urged the court to ensure the presence of the defence lawyers.

The court directed the jail superintendent to write to Fareedi — who is defending a few of the accused — to appear before the court on September 25, the next date for hearing.

Fareedi and Shoaib have also moved the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court, seeking a security cover. Uttar Pradesh Bar Council president Bansi Dhar Singh said: "If any lawyer feels threatened, it is his right to seek a security cover."

Heading: 20 more IIITs on the cards, states yet to be finalised - Indian Express
Content:
The contributory pension scheme introduced by the state government has hit the wall, as no step for its implementation has been taken up as yet.

The Centre had launched the scheme on January 1, 2004. Soon, the state government promulgated an ordinance to implement it from April 1, 2005.

Later, the ordinance was replaced with an Act of the Assembly, but the state government issued the necessary order in this connection only on August 14.

Under the scheme, the employees contribute 10 per cent of their salary and DA to the pension fund and the government contributes an equal amount to the employees who joined on or after April 1, 2005.

Till date, neither a fund manager has been appointed nor the employees been issued index numbers that will register them under the scheme. As a result, the government as well as the employees are expected to face a difficult time as and when these formalities are completed.

Owing the delay, once the scheme becomes operational, the government will have to pay the arrears to the employees with an interest of eight per cent. Further, the government will also have to recover the arrears of the contribution made by the employees.

The arrears are mounting as the index numbers have been issued only to 200 employees and primary teachers.

Deductions from the salary cannot begin unless an employee gets the index number. This is bound to draw flak from the employees' unions.

"With the delay, the burden of the arrears on the government and the employees is mounting. The employee's contribution will have to be deducted from his salary from his date of joining the service," said H D Singh, Director of Pension. 

At the Centre, a Pension Fund Regulatory Development Authority Bill (PFRDA) is pending in the Parliament, although the UPA government has set up the regulatory body by issuing an ordinance.  

The law provides for a "Central Record keeping Agency" and the National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL) has been appointed for the job. The NSDL will convey the trustee bank, which is the Bank of India, about the total available funds and the bank will convey this to the PFRDA.

The regulatory body will then decide on the proportionate distribution of funds among the fund managers. The Centre has appointed SBI, UTI and the LIC as the pension fund managers.

"The UP government has the option of adopting the pattern of the Centre and appoint the three financial institutions as fund managers, or create a separate institutional framework which entails creations of the regulatory body by an Act of the Assembly and the appointment of the fund managers," added Singh.

Heading: Arrest warrant against Mitrasen - Indian Express
Content:
The country will soon have 20 more state-of-the-art Indian Institute of Information Technologies (IIITs).

The Strategic Operation Group (SOG) — a body formed to finalise the setting up of the proposed IIITs — is supposed to submit the final recommendations to the Ministry of Human Resource Development (HRD) on September 20.

The ministry has decided to set up the IIITs in almost 20 states of the country. The names of the states are yet to be finalised by the ministry.

Chairman of the SOG and the director of Allahabad-based Indian Institute of

Information Technology (IIIT-A), Dr M D Tiwari said the members of the core group would submit the report to the ministry within the stipulated time.

He said: "Major issues like funding, industry support, percentage of budget to be allocated by the Centre, specific areas of information technology (IT) education to be focused upon by the new IIITs as well as land and other resources are being finalised. These institutes would be at par with international standards."

The Centre, in an effort to bring regional balance in the field technical education, has planned to set up IITs, IIMs, IISc and IIITs in all major parts of the country.

"Deliberations were also made on some intricate issues like selection of industries for raising funds from private sectors. The members were unanimous over the need of introducing application-based IT course in the proposed IIITs so as to tap the skills of industry while earning revenues from the private sector," explained Dr Tiwari.

These proposed IIITs would be based on the Public-Private-Partnership model. The members also discussed whether the proposed institutes should be given the status of a deemed university or not.

The Centre has almost finalised the detailed blueprints of the 20 new IIITs.

The committee, comprising eminent experts from the field of technical education and IT industry, has been working for the last one year after the formal allocation of budget for the proposed IIITs by the finance minister for fiscal 2008-09.

The core group had met in the second week of September and discussed the details of the proposal, Dr Tiwari added.

Heading: LDA plans refund for plot allotment, allottees refuse - Indian Express
Content:
An arrest warrant was issued against Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) MP from Faizabad, Mitrasen Yadav, on Thursday in a case of attempt to murder.

Chief Judicial Magistrate of Faizabad Shailesh Kumar Tiwari directed the Faizabad SSP and the Station Officer of Inayatnagar police station to arrest the MP immediately.

Besides Yadav, his MLA son Anandsen, and the latter's driver Vijaysen are the other accused in the case.

The case was registered following a court order in August 2000, after one Suraj Karan Pandey had filed an application alleging that the three had made an attempt to kill him.

Mitrasen said the case was "false" and he had filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court against it.

He added that on the day of the alleged attack, he was in New Delhi to attend a meeting of the Samajwadi Party.

Heading: Delhi blast victim: LU refuses permission to hold peace march - Indian Express
Content:
After 17 years, the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) has come up with a proposal to refund the money paid by 538 allottees of Nehru Enclave. This proposal has been strongly opposed by the allottees.

The LDA had launched the scheme in 1991 and had planned to develop over 800 flats and 538 plots.

They completed the allotment before January 1993 when the Army claimed ownership of the land. Since then, a case has been pending in the High Court. 

The LDA had already collected the money from the allottees in 1994.

The authority came up with the proposal once they realised that they could not give the possession of the plots because of the dispute with the Army.

On the other hand, the allottees refused to accept the refund on the grounds that real estates prices have shot up, owing to which they cannot buy another plot with the refunded money.

LDA Secretary Mani Prasad Mishra claimed that they had the right to decide whether to give the allottees the plot or refund them the money. 

He said no decision could be taken in the last board meeting because "the interest rate on refund is yet to be finalised. The proposal could now be taken up in the next board meeting."

"We are valid allottees and not defaulters. So the LDA cannot cancel our allotments. When the plots were allotted, the cost varied from Rs 85,000 to 2.25 lakh," said Anand Kumar Tiwari, secretary of the Sangharsh Samiti of Nehru Enclave Allottees.

Samiti joint secretary Anil Kumar Khare said: "The LDA proposal to refund the cost of plots is arbitrary. We have been waiting for 17 years." The LDA should provide us with alternative plots in places like Gomti Nagar, he said.

While announcing the scheme, the LDA had promised a variety of plush services like jogging track, lush green lawns, swimming pool, sports club, and even a cinema hall.

"But LDA did not develop any of these facilities ever. Nehru Enclave is the best example of high promises, and no performance on ground zero," Khare said.

Heading: CPM ’s UP unit snaps at Mayawati ’s heels - Indian Express
Content:
Teachers, students and employees of the Lucknow University's (LU) department of business administration were refused permission to take out a peace march on the campus on Friday in memory of their alumni Vikas Anand, killed in last Saturday's blasts in New Delhi.

Vikas Anand had completed his MBA from LU in May and used to work as an assistant branch manager at IDBI Bank's Connaught Place branch.

"The department had planned a peace march on Friday between 2 and 3 pm. But the vice-chancellor denied us permission, citing security arrangements being made for the President's visit on September 23," said B L Bajpai, head of the business administration department. Disappointed with the turn of events, Bajpai said: "Now, we plan hold the march after the special convocation." President Pratibha Patil will be conferred DLitt at the special convocation.

LU Vice-Chancellor A S Brar said: "In view of the President's visit, no procession could be allowed. Any undesirable element can take advantage of the situation and spoil the atmosphere." "Once the convocation is over, I will consider granting permission for the peace march," Brar added.

Heading: HC issues showcause notice to Ghazipur ADJ for granting bail to murder accused - Indian Express
Content:
After the exit of SP from the exercise of forging a third alternative, the efforts towards that goal seems to have received another setback with the Uttar Pradesh unit of the CPM on Thursday announcing its decision to launch a statewide movement against "anti-people and pro-capitalist" policies of the Mayawati regime.

Of late, the BSP and the Left party were seen coming closer to forge a Third Front with Mayawati and CPM general secretary meeting and sharing dais.

Uttar Pradesh secretary of the CPM S C Kashyap said, "The CPM is working for an electoral understanding with the BSP with the objective of forging a Third Front ahead of the next Lok Sabha election, but the party and the government were different things. We supported the UPA government for over four years but we always opposed the anti-people and pro-West policies of the government."

On the concluding day of its two-day state committee meet, the party adopted a resolution to oppose forcible land acquisition for the Ganga Expressway and other mega projects.

It accused the Mayawati government of compromising the interests of farmers and the poor in general.

"Privatisation has become the order of the day in Uttar Pradesh, and whosoever raises his voice against the wrongdoings of the government is subjected to the most cruel treatment," Kashyap said, citing the recent police action against farmers in Noida as an instance.

The district units of the party have been instructed to chalk out their agitational plans against the government's anti-people policies, he added.

Heading: In UP, 10-yr-old booked for being ‘habitual offender’ - Indian Express
Content:
The Allahabad High Court issued a showcause notice to Shailendra Nath Singh — the Additional District Judge (ADJ) of the Ghazipur court — on Thursday for granting bail to the two accused in the murder of BJP legislator Krishnanand Rai.

Justice Vinod Prasad has wanted to know why Singh's termination should not be recommended. Singh has also been asked to appear in person before the High Court on September 29. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) had moved an application for cancelling the bail granted to the two accused — Ramu Mallah and Rakesh Pandey. The CBI counsel stated that the ADJ had gone ahead and granted bail even though the Supreme Court had stayed proceedings in the case.

However, the SC had directed that the bail application of Afzal Ansari may be considered by the lower court. Ansari is the brother of mafia-turned-politician Mukhtar Ansari, MLA from district Mau.

Krishnanand Rai and seven others were murdered near Goundour village, Ghazipur district, in November 2006. A case was lodged at Bhavarkol police station against Mukhtar Ansari, Afzal Ansari and several others. Later, a Division Bench of the High Court ordered a CBI investigation in the case after the deceased MLA's wife filed a petition.

Heading: ATS seizes heroin worth 5 crore, STF arrests two drug peddlers - Indian Express
Content:
With an aim to maintain law and order, the Bulandshahar police has now declared a 10-year-old boy habitual offender and initiated proceedings to book him under Section 110 (G) of CrPC.

Under Section 110 G, a person has to give an undertaking of good conduct, backed with two sureties, which can be forfeited in the event of violation of the undertaking.

The matter came to light during tehsil diwas held in Khurja area on Tuesday where the District Magistrate and the Senior Superintendent of Police were attending to the complaints of the residents.

District Magistrate (DM) Shashi Bhushan said: "Virendra Singh of Jarara village appeared before us along with his son Harish (10) and showed a notice issued from city Magistrate's office. The notice stated that Harish had to appear before the magistrate under Section 110 G."

The DM said he was surprised to see the notice. The police initiated these proceedings against the boy, who is a student of Class IV, which are usually initiated against a habitual criminal.

The DM asked the SSP to conduct an inquiry.

Circle Officer (CO) of Khurja Ram Kala said another villager, who had a rivalry with Virendra Singh, lodged a complaint of assault against Harish on June 22 mentioning his age as 18.

Following which, Sub-Inspector Bachchu Singh, who was asked to look into the matter, never visited the village to verify the facts and recommended that the accused be booked under Section 110 (G) in August, the CO said.

Heading: ‘Illegal’ stall owners slapped fine - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) of Uttar Pradesh Police seized heroin worth Rs 5 crore from a gang of five, while the Special Task Force (STF) team arrested a Nepalese national and a Bihar-based drug dealer with charas worth Rs 50 lakh in separate catches in Lucknow on Thursday.

The Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) ATS, Rajiv Sabbarwal, said the racket came to light while they were collecting information regarding anti-national activities.

Initially, the ATS arrested Rakesh Kumar of Kanpur City, Ghulam Mustafa of Lucknow and Nirikesh Yadav of Azamgarh carrying the consignment of heroin in Gomti Nagar.

The trio revealed that they received the drug from Chandan Lal and Wali Mohammad of Barabanki. Following this, the policemen later nabbed the two from Satrikh and Jaitpur in Barabanki.

Sabbarwal said Chandan and Wali converted the raw opium into heroin and other drugs after processing it at their respective houses.

Others arrested received the heroin from the two Barabanki-based dealers and catered to the retailers in various cities, the SSP said.

The STF team led by Deputy Superintendent of Police Arvind Chaturvedi, meanwhile, arrested Chandra Bahadur Thapa of Kathmandu and Mohammad Abu Jaan of East Champaran, Bihar from Chinhat area.

The policemen laid a trap following a tip-off and arrested the duo while they were on their way to Kanpur.

Chaturvedi said the drug dealers had concealed 39 kgs of charas in a specially assembled cavity inside the car's boot space.

Thapa told the police that he sold charas to dealers from various cities across the country.

The Bihar-based man was an accomplice of Thapa and used to accompany him during dealings with clients in Uttar Pradesh.

The Deputy Superintendent of Police said Thapa has confessed to have supplied about one quintal of charas to a client in Sri Lanka and had received $3,000 for the consignment four months ago.

Heading: New variety of rice, some free time bring farmers to PAU Kisan Mela - Indian Express
Content: The Municipal Corporation slapped fine on 8 stall owners for putting up seed stalls on Ferozepur Road, opposite Gat No. 1 and 2 of the PAU without prior permission from the authorities. The MC is said to have collected Rs 10,000 as fine from the stall owners, who had put them up on account of the Kisan Mela in PAU. The owners, meanwhile, maintained they are exempted from giving any type of fee to the corporation. An official of the tehbazari team, however, said that anyone who puts up a stall on the MC land has to pay at the rate of Rs 5 per square feet.

Heading: Revamped letter boxes to adorn city after rains - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) witnessed an unprecedented rush of farmers from all over the state who thronged the main campus to attend the two-day Kisan Mela. Insiders on the campus said they have seen such a rush after a gap of seven years. Farmers from as far as Muktsar, Abohar to Patiala or as near as Jagraon and Mullanpur, dressed in spotless white kurta pyjamas, colourful turbans and riding on SUVs dotted the campus on the first day of the mela on Thursday.

Dr N S Malhi, Director Extension, PAU, said: "We do not have mechanism to count the number of farmers who come to the mela. Yet today's rush has been a great motivator for all of us."

A reason for this rush, Dr Malhi said: "The release of new variety of wheat is one major reason. The second reason could be the fact that because of the delay in sowing paddy this year, farmers all over Punjab are relatively free at this time and have come for the mela. In the past few years, farmers were already busy sowing farmers during this time of the year and were too busy to even spare a day."

Jang Bahadur Singh Sangh, Member, PAU Board of Management, is delighted with the footfall. "It is great to see that despite being criticised from all section, PAU enjoys a huge amount of trust amongst its clients that are the farmers. The turnout at the mela says it all."

The mela is thus a runaway hit... nearly 300 agri-industrials stalls, plant clinics, a huge plant demonstration route, free plants distribution, so much so even the DMC Hero Heart Care Centre had put its stall for the farmers.

Citing the success of campaigns to manage mealy bugs in cotton, late blight in potato, water saving, popularisation of nutritional gardens, he said the PAU organises campaigns on emergent issues from time to time. In his thanksgiving address, Dr P S Minhas, PAU Director of Research, said the university has evolved technologies with focus on resource conservation, profitability enhancement and environment protection.

This year, Punjab has contributed 99 lakh tonne of wheat to the Central pool as compared to 69 lakh tonne last year (increase of nearly 40%). The other states have observed this increase from 30 to 120 lakh tonnes (400% increase). This scenario necessitates fresh thinking as far as contribution of Punjab is concerned, said Dr Minhas.

Heading: Lobbying begins for last phase of PU Senate elections - Indian Express
Content:
The OLD cylindrical shaped red-coloured letter boxes are in for a makeover. They will soon be replaced with large rectangular-shaped pillar sized post boxes at about 20 places across the city.

Carrying the new colourful logo of the Postal department, the pillar letter boxes will not only facilitate the public but also enhance the beauty of the city, claimed V K Raizada, Senior Superintendent, Post Offices, Ludhiana. He said: "The logo of the Postal department has also changed now. The pillar letter boxes will carry this new logo — a bird symbol in yellow and red. They will be installed after the rains."

He said the boxes will be installed at main locations where posts are received in bulk. Another employee of the department said: "We will install these at places like Mini Secretariat, near the Government College for Boys, Fountain Chowk and Extension Library among others."

At present, the city has about 350 letter boxes of the old shape, with many of them in dilapidated condition. The SSPO said: "We are just waiting for the end of the rainy season. Afterwards, we will repair the broken ones and paint all of them with new logo."

Heading: MC: No more tubewells, live with what you have - Indian Express
Content:
The PU Senate election fever for the fourth and last phase for the largest graduates' constituency has gripped the five contenders from the city who are vying for place among the 15 seats of the constituency.

One of them, who claimed to be the only one to have come up with a manifesto, held a press conference on Thursday and disclosed his agenda.

The five candidates who are in the fray from the city among the overall 42 contenders in the constituency have been trying to make their presence felt to the over 4 lakh graduate voters who will decide the fate of these candidates on September 21.

They are Dr Madanjit Kaur Sahota, principal of Master Tara Singh College for Women, Jagpal Singh, Head of Political Science department at SCD Government College, Lakhvinder Singh Bedi, Head of PG department of English at GGN Khalsa College and Rajeev Bhasin and Praveen Sharma from Arya College.

Lakhvinder Singh Bedi, who held the press conference today, said: "If I am elected as the member of the senate, I would like to sensitise the youth in the emerging education scenario, orient them towards rural education, redrawing the education and administrative dimensions of Panjab University Regional Centre in the city." Bedi, who fights from ballot number 20, added that he would also work towards setting up vocational and guidance bureaus in the colleges.

Some other candidates, meanwhile, are employing the traditional methods to reach out to the voters. "I have been working day in and day out to visit every corner of the society and meeting the voters," said Dr Madanjit Kaur Sahota, a sitting senator who had contested from the principal's constituency last time. As she feels that women empowerment needs to be given more importance, she would stress to make women education better, besides working to bridge the gap for opportunities for rural students, especially boys.

Praveen Sharma, who has started canvassing heavily with the help of banners and posters, said, "I am a known person in the senate and therefore I do not think there is much need to introduce myself to them. I have anyhow started campaigning with letters as well as posters."

He said he would like to emphasise the importance of modern professional courses and the need to implement them in an effective way by providing all facilities. Jagpal Singh, another old member of the Senate, said that the issues related to the students like fees hike or problems in re-evaluation or late results would be his top priority.

Heading: Poor among Marathas should get reservations: Sena - Indian Express
Content:
The city already has 700 tubewells and submersible pumps. Thirty more tubwells are in the pipeline. This is enough keeping in view the depleting water level and the residents should learn to live within this system.

The Operation and Maintenance Cell of the Municipal Corporation has given this clear message to the residents and the area councillors who, they say, keep demanding more tubewells every passing day.

The same has even been conveyed by the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) — the fact that Ludhiana is over exploited area in terms of water depletion and hence for every new tubewell, the authorities are supposed to take prior permission from the CGWA, with whom will rest the final decision to grant permission to install new tubwells.

Apart from the 450 tubewells and 250 submersibles in the city, the residents are said to be blatantly installing their own submersibles for personal use in homes or factories, further depleting the groundwater level.

K S Dhillon, Superintending Engineer (SE), Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Cell, said: "We have been conveying the same to the area councillors as well that no more tubewells can be dug in the city and the residents should learn to live within the existing system. If all the tullu pumps are switched off from the consumers' houses, the existing network is more than enough and the residents will not face any water scarcity. It is being so difficult to make the consumers understand this."

Sources said that apart from the 30 new tubewells in the pipeline, the councillors are still coming up with more demands, which the O&M Cell is politely denying. The authorities are, however, not adopting a set policy to refuse the installation of new tubewells.

The Newsline team, meanwhile, found an illegal submersible pump being set up on the Gill Road, the digging for which continues on Thursday. The MC authorities, however, are unaware of the development, exposing the concern it has to maintain the water level. Ironically, the MC zone C office is also located in the vicinity of the site. Dhillon said: "I am not yet aware of this submersible and will stop the operations immediately."

Heading: 10,000 children trafficked into NE annually - Indian Express
Content:
Shiv Sena came out in support of the demand that the Maratha community be included in the OBC category.

Maratha is considered to be the 'ruling caste' of the state, yet demand for inclusion in OBCs has been gaining strength off late.

Sena mouthpiece Saamana, in Friday's editorial, said, "As there are super-rich Marathas, there are also those who are driven to suicide because of the poverty. Sena has always been of the view that poor from all the communities should get benefit of reservations."

Maharashtra Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh, had recently assured a section of Maratha leaders that their demand would be dealt sympathetically.

Referring to NCP leader Arun Gujarathi's recent statement, 'poor among the Marathas should be included in OBC category', Sena said, 'There need not be two opinions on this.'

However, the editorial cautions that the issue of granting OBC status to Marathas should not divide the state.

"Mali community has already opposed inclusion of Marathas in OBCs. In Rajasthan, the state was on the boil due to the Meena-Gujjar strife. It should not be re-enacted in Maharashtra," it says.

The editorial also states that while Kunbi community is a part of the Marathas, it has been granted OBC status, but Marathas have been kept out of the reservation net.

The edit refers to stated position of Sunil Pawar, a leader of Maratha Mahasangh that reservations should be on basis of financial condition, not the caste.

"This position is important from the viewpoint of maintaining solidarity of Maharashtrian society," the editorial says.

Heading: Karnataka Bajrang Dal convener arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Not less than 10,000 people, mostly children, are trafficked into the Northeast with a good number smuggled in from Bangladesh, Nepal and other South East Asian countries, surveys by NGOs reveal.

Most of those trafficked are then engaged as cheap labour in coal mines of Meghalaya, tea gardens in Assam and prostitution.

"The region, besides being a transit point of human trafficking, has also emerged as a destination point. We have rescued a number of children hailing from Nepal and Bangladesh in Assam and Meghalaya who were trafficked and to work as cheap labour," says Hasina Kharbhih, Team Leader of Impulse NGO.

"Cross border trafficking is very much relevant in NE, with the region sharing borders with five countries. Some large international trafficking gangs are operation in the region," she says.

A Nepali minor girl, who was trafficked to Assam along with three others, was rescued by Impulse from a house in Assam and repatriated home on September 17.

Two other boys, who were trafficked from Bangladesh and were working in the coal mines of Jaintia Hills in Meghalaya were also been rescued and were likely to be sent home soon. While trafficked children are often booked under the Illegal Migration Act, Impulse feels the Juvenile Justice Act or the proposals of the SAARC Convention on Trafficking could be applied to repatriate the victims to their homes, the NGOs say.

Many of these children are trafficked in connivance with their parents.

It is estimated that Nepalese children constitute 20 per cent (40,000) of the estimated 200,000 Nepalese prostitutes in India.

"It is estimate that some 6,000 to 10,000 girls are trafficked annually from Nepal to Indian brothels and a similar number are trafficked from Bangladesh. 27,000 Bangladeshi women and children have been forced into prostitution in Indian brothels," a Childline India Foundation report says.

The average age of girls trafficked from Bangladesh and Nepal into India has fallen over the past decade from 16-18 to 10-15 years.

With India sharing a 4,222 kilometre border with 28 districts of Bangladesh, most of it open with rivers criss-crossing it, traffickers take advantage of this to smuggle in their hapless human cargo.

Heading: Indian forward post fired at along LoC - Indian Express
Content:
Karnataka convener of Bajrang Dal Mahendra Kumar was on Friday night arrested by the police in connection with the spate of attacks on churches and prayer halls in parts of the state.

"Mahendra Kumar has been arrested tonight," Western Range Deputy Inspector General of Police A M Prasad said.

Soon after the attacks on churches on September 15 in parts of Mangalore and Udupi in coastal regions and in Chikamaglur in Malnad area, Bajrang Dal owned responsibility for them, claiming that incidents of forced conversion had prompted them.

With attacks on churches continuing unabated, the Centre on Friday issued a strong advisory asking the BJP government in the southern state to take immediate effective steps to check the violence, which it said was a "breach" of the Constitution.

In the advisory to Karnataka, the second in 24 hours, the Union Home Ministry brought to the notice of Karnataka government that elements behind such incidents continue to roam freely.

The advisory was, however, not sent under the emergency provisions of the Constitution (Article 355).

On its part, the Karnataka government described the advisory, the second to be issued, as "hasty and unwarranted".

"It is a hasty step. The Centre should have waited for some more time. Our government has already brought the situation under control. There are no casualties in the attack on churches in the state," Karnataka Home Minister V S Acharya said.

Heading: Advisory issued to K'taka over attacks on churches - Indian Express
Content:
An Indian forward post was fired upon from across the border in Poonch district of Jammu and Kashmir.

"There was firing from the Pakistan side across LoC on our forward post Copra in Sabzian sub-sector of Poonch district last night," a senior army officer said on Friday.

But there was no loss of life or injury to anyone during the firing, he said, adding that Indian troops guarding the LoC observed total restraint and did not retaliate.

Ruling out ceasefire violations along LoC from Pakistani troops, he said militants may have fired at the post.

Since January, Pakistani troops have violated the five-year-old ceasefire agreement 32 times and provoked reactions from Indian troops, though the latter refused to retaliate on most occasions. Seven incidents of ceasefire violation in Poonch-Rajouri sector were reported during August and September.

The army's Director General of Military Operations had strongly protested to his Pakistani counterpart on several occasions over the ceasefire violations, especially during the Tangdhar firing and the Nowgam LoC breach.

Violations of the ceasefire by Pakistani troops have been reported from Jammu, Samba, Rajouri, Tanghdhar and Poonch sector this year during which a large number of militants have tried to infiltrate into India.

The army has assessed that the firing occurred whenever militant groups were making attempts to infiltrate into India and ceasefire violations could be a tactic being adopted by Pakistani troops to distract Indian forces.

Increased infiltration bids by militants were witnessed in the summer months this year with the state Assembly scheduled to go to polls. Close to 110 infiltration bids were reported in the last eight months as militants felt that the summer months were the best time of the year to augment their depleting strength in the Valley.

Heading: Tough terror laws need of the hour: Bedi - Indian Express
Content:
Perturbed over attacks on churches in Karnataka, the Union Home Ministry on Friday put the state on alert and directed it to report to the Centre on the steps taken to deal with the situation.

Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta said an advisory has been issued to the state government asking it to take effective measures to bring the situation under control.

He said that the Karnataka situation was being closely monitored by the Home Ministry and that the state government has been told to report back to the Centre on the steps to check attacks on the churches and prayer Halls.

Asked whether the Centre has decided to invoke Article 355 of the Constitution, a provision rarely used, he declined to reply.

The Centre on Thursday night decided to send an advisory to the state following attacks on churches and prayer halls in the BJP-ruled state.

Mangalore has been the epicentre of attacks on the churches in the state.

Karnataka Home Minister V S Acharya said Thursday night that state government would endeavour to maintain law and order in the state and ensure safety of everyone including churches and Christians in the state.

Heading: Flood fury claims 9 in Orissa - Indian Express
Content:
Can stringent laws slash the spurt in India's terror graph? Well, political parties may have varied opinions on the issue, but India's first woman IPS officer feels 'it's the need of the hour'.

"Our laws are weak. We need strong laws to reign in the terrorists. Laws of the land must keep pace with the new challenges posed by terrorists," Kiran Bedi said.

However, according to her, stronger laws should be supplemented with faster legal process. "Terrorists know that it can take up to ten years for a case to be settled in the court of law. So, judicial system needs to be expedited."

Bedi, who also served in the United Nations as the Police Adviser to the Secretary General in Department of Peace Keeping Operations, is also in favour of a federal agency to tackle terror in the country. "It's long overdue," she rued.

Known for her courageous act of towing away of the car of the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in 1983, Bedi feels that India's basic fundamentals of policing are too weak to tackle terror and crime.

"We have no fundamentals in fact. We have structures only. Fundamentals come through human resource management, which unfortunately, is the weakest in our country. When 80 per cent of your constabulary is neglected, than you are bound to be the targets. So, get your basics right first," she said.

Bedi, now retired, also differs on the 'notion of being tough or soft on acts of terror'.

"Basically, we have never addressed the issue of terrorism with desired will and efforts. Our policies are soft on crime and violence with a tradition of breaking laws, than how can you tackle terror," she said.

A recipient of Ramon Magsaysay Award (1994) for her reforms in Tihar Jail, she has also expressed disappointment with the equation between police and citizens.

"There should be 'inclusive policing' and citizens should be co-opted by police. If you do not make them partners in peace, than how can you think of their support in times of war," she said.

Heading: Flood situation in Orissa turns critical - Indian Express
Content:
Nine persons lost their lives as the mighty Mahanadi river rose menacingly and other rivers were in spate on Friday, triggering a major flood situation in Orissa as a high alert was sounded in four coastal districts, official sources said.

With other rivers such as the Subarnarekha, Baitarani and Brahmani in spate, one person was feared drowned in flood waters of the river Tel in Sonepur, while two flood and rain related deaths each were reported from Mayurbhanj, Bhadrak, Jajpur and Kendrapara districts, official sources said.

"We are apprehending a major flood in the Mahanadi system as a huge volume of water is heading downstream," Chief Secretary Ajit Kumar Tripathy told reporters in Bhubaneswar.

Tripathy said more than 14 lakh cusecs of water was expected to reach the Naraj delta head near Cuttack on Saturday as 22 sluice gates of the Hirakud dam on the Mahanadi were opened this afternoon after the water level in the reservoir touched 629.97 feet, almost near its capacity of 630 feet.

While 4.2 lakh cusec of water was entering the reservoir, 3.59 lakh cusec was being released through the gates, and more gates were likely to be opened in view of heavy rain in catchment area in Chhattisgarh, a senior official said.

The embankments of the Mahanadi and its branches criss- crossing the coastal deltaic plains have a capacity to contain about 12 lakh cusecs of water, he said.

The present flood situation in Mahanadi was similar to the one faced in 2001 when 14.8 lakh cusec water passed through the plains. Earlier in 1982, 15.80 lakh cusec of water wreaked havoc, he said.

Heading: Delhi Govt plans nine new 'forest cities' - Indian Express
Content:
Surging waters of mighty Mahanadi river hit the downstream belt engulfing vast areas aggravating the flood situation in Orissa with other major rivers in the state also in spate.

The state government sounded a high alert in four coastal district of Cuttack, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Puri in view of the flood which has claimed nine lives so far.

Evacuation operation has been launched on a big scale to shift the residents of low-lying areas to the safer places.

As many as 26 gates of the Hirakud dam on Mahanadi have been opened for quich discharge of water as the level in the reservoir reached its full capacity of 630 feet, official sources said.

Inflow of water into the reservoir was recorded at 4.6 lakh cusec this morning, while an equal volume was being drained out through the sluice gates.

With heavy release of water from the Hirakud reservoir, the flow of water at Khairmal was recorded at 14.38 lakh cusec while it was 13.66 lakh at Munduli this morning, they said. A major flood in Mahanadi was thereby threatening the delta region as huge volume of water inundated the plains.

Mahanadi waters have already inundated several low lying areas of Cuttack district including Banki, Athgarh and Narsinghpur, besides Athamallick, Boudh and Sonepur.

The embankments of the Mahanadi and its branches criss-crossing the coastal deltaic plains have a capacity to contain about 12 lakh cusecs of water, a senior official said.

The present flood situation in Mahanadi was similar to the one faced in 2001 when 14.8 lakh cusec of water passed through the plains. Earlier in 1982, 15.80 lakh cusec of water had wreaked havoc in the area.

As several other rivers like Brahmani, Baitarani and Subarnarekha were also in spate, one person was feared drowned in swirling waters of Tel in Sonepur, while two flood related deaths were reported each from Mayurbhanj, Bhadrak, Jajpur and Kendrapara districts, official sources said.

The fury in Mahanadi appeared more menacing due to heavy rains in lower catchment area below the Hirakud dam spread over the undivided Kalahandi and Balangir districts, they said.

All major tributaries of Mahanadi including Hati, Tel and Udanti also witnessed flood due to the heavy precipitation in the lower catchment areas, they said.

As vast parts of Boudh were inundated, the civic polls there scheduled for today have been deferred to September 22.

In a bid to tackle floods in Mahanadi delta, the water resoures department has been directed to immediately attend vulnerable points on river embankments and take the required steps forthwith, sources said.

The state government has sought 30 boats from the Centre for undertaking relief and rescue operation in flood affected areas, while two helicopters have already been kept ready to deal with the situation.

The district administration in Kendrapara has evacuated over 5,000 people from low-lying areas and shifted them.

Schools in the four coastal districts have been closed and readied for use as temporary shelters for people along with the large number of cyclone shelters built after the super cyclone of 1999.

Heading: CPM concerned over Singur impasse - Indian Express
Content:
Expanding the green cover in the vicinity of the national capital, the Delhi government has ambitious plans to develop nine new "forest cities" by next year.

Around 220 hectares of land belonging to east, northwest and southwest districts of the city have been identified under new forestation plan, environment secretary J K Dadoo says.

"As part of our CLEAN India campaign, we have planned to develop nine forest cities this year which will be in addition to the 23 existing cities in Delhi," Dadoo said.

The department, which claimed to have planted 1.8 million saplings during last year, have set the same target for this year too under its Community Led Environment Action Network (CLEAN) India campaign.

"The forest wealth of Delhi has increased considerably during the last two years. Having good monsoon this year after a long gap is a good sign amid fears of global warming," Dadoo says. "Total forest area in the capital has increased from 26 sq km in 1998 to 300 sq km in 2008," he adds.

The forest department, which developed nine "green cities" last year on the land given by the Revenue department wants to bring 33 per cent more area under the forest cover as envisaged in the National Forest Policy, the official claims.

"Besides involving 18 government agencies and some NGOs, the forest department also distributed 5 lakh saplings through 606 outlets last year," he says.

Heading: Five detained from Jamia Nagar after encounter - Indian Express
Content:
The CPI-M on Friday expressed concern at the Singur impasse, saying those opposing the Tata Motors small car plant should realise that the people of West Bengal wanted the project to come up there.

"We are concerned. The people of the state should know who are against development," CPI-M state secretary Biman Bose told newsmen after the party's state secretariat meeting.

Referring to the 'pro-Nano' rally organised by CPI-M-led Left Front at Singur on September 15, Bose said the massive turnout on the day indicates that people of West Bengal wanted the Tata Motors plant to come up there.

"Our Bardhaman district committee secretary Amar Halder was leading a big procession to the rally, but it was stranded on the Durgapur Expressway owing to the massive turnout of people. Such an enormous crowd would not have been possible if people did not want the plant at Singur," Bose said.

Asked to comment on the Karnataka government's offer of land to Tata Motors for relocating the small car plant, he said, "It is not impractical. Those who want to set up industry can decide where they will look for land."

Taking a dig at the Trinamool Congress leading the anti-land acquisition agitation at Singur, Bose said, "The people of the state should think and decide what is to be done about those who do not want the state to prosper."

Bose said that he was not aware of Leader of the Opposition Partha Chatterjee meeting Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi.

Heading: Delhi encounter: ‘It all started at 10.30 am’ - Indian Express
Content:
Police on Friday picked up five residents of Jamia Nagar for questioning after killing two militants in a gun battle in the area.

The owner of the house where the five militants were holed up has been detained along with four others of the locality, a senior police official said.

The official said they were being questioned to know more about the militants who were residing in the area for about a month.

Heading: Patil mulls giving more teeth to police - Indian Express
Content:
Tensions ran high in the Jamia Nagar locality of South Delhi as news of one religious place being transgressed reportedly by police came, during the encounter with militants on Friday.

The house where militants were holed up lies very close to a religious place. Once firing stopped, large number of people thronged the narrow lanes of the area and shouted religious slogans. "We are all against terrorism, then why was our religious places places targeted," said one of the residents.

Refuting any such news, DCP South Delhi HGS Dhaliwal clarified that no religious place was used during the encounter. "The firing was done from a place near the religious place," he said.

The tensions were fuelled by rumours that the operation was concocted by police and no fire was shot from inside the house.

Meanwhile, one media personnel, who was informing his office about the encounter, was abused by the local residents. They claimed that no shot were fired from inside the house and the encounter was a blatant lie.

Neighbours of the house where entire operation unfolded, however, confirmed that gun shots were fired from both sides.

"It all started at 10.30 in the morning. We were preparing to go to our work when some police people came in the area," said an eye-witness who refused to disclose her identity.

Heading: Delhi encounter hero dies, 2 militants killed - Indian Express
Content:
A winner of seven gallantry medals, Delhi Police Special Cell officer Mohan Chand Sharma passed away after receiving several bullet injuries during an encounter with terrorists in South Delhi on Friday.

Sharma, 41, who led the police team against the terrorists in Jamia Nagar area, was operated upon at the Holy Family hospital in New Delhi to remove bullets from his body.

The officer received 'firearm' injuries on his upper abdomen, upper arm, left shoulder and right hip, the hospital said in a medical bulletin.

Delhi Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal said that Sharma was a highly decorated police officer and had won seven gallantry medals including a President's award.

He was instrumental in the killing of 35 terrorists and the arrest of another 80 militants, police sources claimed, adding he had killed 40 inter-state gangsters and arrested another 129.

"The officer was rushed to the hospital this morning at 11.15 am and he was bleeding profusely," Reverend Arthur Pinto, the hospital's Director said.

According to Pinto, Sharma had 'no pulse' and was immediately administered blood pressure raising medicines.

Following this, the officer was shifted to the operation theatre where surgery was done to remove his bullets, Pinto added.

The medical bulletin said that throughout the surgery he was in a critical condition.

Sharma joined the Delhi Police as a sub-inspector in 1989 and got an out of turn promotion in 1995 when he was elevated to the rank of an Inspector.

Heading: Manmohan, Sonia condole Sharma's death - Indian Express
Content:
Winner of seven gallantry medals, Delhi Police Special Cell officer Mohan Chand Sharma who was critically injured on Friday in an encounter with Indian Mujahideen militants in New Delhi died after battling for life for nearly eight hours.

Sharma (41), who led Friday's daring encounter at Jamia Nagar where five terrorists linked with the recent serial blasts in the country were holed up, had received three bullet injuries on his abdomen, thighs and right arm.

The inspector, who was bleeding profusely, was rushed to the nearby Holy Family hospital where he was operated upon and later put on life support systems.

After battling with his injuries for nearly eight hours, he was declared dead at 7 pm in the evening.

"We have lost our best man," Joint Commissioner of Police (Special Cell) Karnal Singh said.

Sharma, who is survived by his wife and two young children, had won seven gallantry medals including a President's medal in 2008.

He joined Delhi Police as a sub-inspector in 1989 and was instrumental in the killing of 35 terrorists and the arrest of another 80 militants, police sources claimed, adding he had killed 40 inter-state gangsters and arrested another 129.

Home Minister Shivraj Patil said the example set by Sharma was 'very rare' to be seen.

"I have asked the Police Commissioner (Y S Dadwal) to do whatever is needed to help the family of this brave officer," Patil said after visiting the hospital.

He said the Home Ministry will offer all support to the officer's family.

Delhi encounter: 2 militants wanted in blasts killed

In a brush with terror in the capital for a second time in a week, two militants of the 'Indian Mujahideen' allegedly involved in the serial blasts in Delhi and other places including Ahmedabad, were killed in a fierce gunbattle that also left an Inspector seriously wounded in Jamia Nagar in South Delhi on Friday.

One of the two killed was identified as Atif, a prominent operative of the Indian Mujahideen who is believed to have played a 'key role' in the blasts in Delhi as well as in Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Bangalore, Delhi Police Commissioner Y S Dadwal said on the shootout that lasted about an hour.

Atif's accomplice Sajid, also a member of the Indian Mujahideen which is a shadow outfit of the banned SIMI and Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT), was also killed while police nabbed Mohammed Saif who was injured in the gunbattle in 'Batla House', a four-storied building.

The militants fired eight rounds during the gunbattle while police retaliated with 22 rounds, Dadwal said adding police also recovered an AK-47 assault rifle along with two 0.30 pistols and a computer from the L-18 residence where the militants were staying for the past two months.

Atif is said to be a close associate of Mohammed Usman Qureshi alias Tauqeer, the elusive mastermind behind the serial bomb blasts in various parts of the country in the recent past and had travelled to Ahmedabad on July 24, two days before the serial blasts in that city, Dadwal said.

Heading: Oil rises above $98 on supply concerns - Indian Express
Content:
Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on Friday said Delhi Police officer M C Sharma, who died after sustaining injuries during an encounter with terrorists had shown exceptional courage and was an inspiration for the security forces.

The PM condoled the death of Sharma, an officer with the Delhi Police special cell.

"He has shown exceptional courage and is an inspiration for our security forces," he added.

Sonia Gandhi expresses distress over policeman's death

Congress president Sonia Gandhi expressed deep distress over the death of Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma of Delhi Police, who succumbed to injuries during an operation against terrorists in New Delhi.

In a condolence message she said that Sharma battled with the terrorists valiantly and sacrificed his life in the service of the country.

"Our battle against terrorism will continue with full resolve," she said.

Heading: Rupee up by 7 paise against US dollar - Indian Express
Content:
Oil rose for a third day on Friday, edging above $98 a barrel on growing US and Nigerian supply concerns even as the dollar jumped on an emerging US government plan for a comprehensive solution to the financial crisis.

Central banks around the world have pumped billions of dollars to credit markets and US authorities are working on a plan to mop up bad debt after previous actions including bailouts failed to restore market confidence, aiding commodities that have been hammered by a flight from risk.

US light crude for October delivery rose 23 cents to $98.11 a barrel by 0319 GMT, tempting a third day of gains as prices rebounded from a seven-month low of $90.51 a barrel on Wednesday in the aftermath of Lehman Brothers' collapse, the near failure of insurer AIG and takeover of Merrill Lynch.

London Brent crude fell 4 cents to $95.15.

While the financial crisis roiled markets from stocks to bonds to foreign exchange, some oil traders were shifting their focus back to fundamentals, with worries over falling US inventory levels and Nigerian attacks aiding a $7 recovery.

"I think the fundamentals are still fairly supportive for oil," said Gerard Burg, a resource analyst at the National Australian Bank in Melbourne.

But analysts said ructions on Wall Street would still be a key factor.

The US dollar rose against the yen and recouped most losses against the euro on Friday on reports Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson is considering a comprehensive solution to the current financial crisis, curtailing oil's earlier gains.

"Traders will continue to alternate focus between the financial markets, which could result in further demand destruction, dollar movements as well as production out of the US Gulf of Mexico," Burg said.

Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke and Paulson plan to work through the weekend with Congress on a comprehensive plan to deal with toxic bank assets choking the financial system, a Treasury spokeswoman said on Thursday.

Some 93 percent of the oil production in the Gulf of Mexico, source of a quarter of the nation's crude output, remained idled on Thursday along with about 14.5 percent of the nation's refined fuel capacity.

Analysts said rising tensions in Nigeria's crude-rich Niger Delta region will also lend support, with militants threatening to broaden their "oil war" to offshore oil fields.

The Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta has cut one-fifth of OPEC member Nigeria's oil output.

Oil market participants were also keeping a close eye on No. 2 US investment bank Morgan Stanley -- a major player in energy markets -- which was said to be in advance talks to be bought by US retail bank Wachovia Corp.

Morgan Stanley withdrew from a half-hour oil trading window, used to assess benchmark prices, after pricing agency Platts placed it under review because of counter-party concerns over its credit status, although the move does not stop Morgan Stanley from trading as normal in the open market.

Heading: Oil, gas hunt: ONGC to put Rs 19,338 cr - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian rupee on Friday moved up by seven paise to 46.34/35 against the US currency after surrendering major part of early gains in late morning deals.

Smart rally in the benchmark Sensex by nearly 379 points at 1030 hrs mainly helped the rupee to open stronger at the Interbank Foreign Exchange (Forex) market at 46.15 a dollar from overnight close of 46.41/42.

However, dollar buying by oil refiners pushed the rupee down to quote at 46.34/35 in late morning deals.

Spurt in local equities was attributed to sharp rebound in world stock markets. Most of the Asian indices were up by 3.0 per cent to 9.4 per cent following steep rise on Wall Street last night.

US government's comprehensive approach, with the help of other major central banks, to stabilise the financial crisis helped the stock markets to regain from their lows.

Reassuring comments by the Finance Minister P Chidambaram about the financial health of the Indian financial lenders also partly aided the rupee sentiment at early stages.

Global crude oil prices were quoting slightly higher at USD 98.22 a barrel this morning in Asian trade.

Sustained by foreign funds from equity markets also weighed on the rupee sentiment.

Heading: Inflation coming under control: PM's aide - Indian Express
Content:
Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) on Friday said it would invest Rs 19,338 crore in oil and gas hunt during the current fiscal, about 10 per cent more than Rs 17,651 crore in the previous year.

"Improving the reserve replacement ratio by intensifying exploratory efforts is company's first priority," Chairman R S Sharma told company shareholders.

"Improving recovery factor, arresting decline in mature fields and expeditious development of discovered fields are the other priorities," he said.

ONGC declared Rs 14 per share final dividend for 2007-08, which is over and above Rs 18 per share interim dividend in December.
