Heading: Cell Membrane - Indian Express
Content:
After recording with Carlos Santana and making music in LA for over a decade, composer Sanjay Divecha is all set to release his first album exploring Indian sounds

In a musical career spanning over two decades, guitarist and composer Sanjay Divecha spent 15 of it in Los Angeles. And every time he composed a song, the sound of India went missing. But all of that was until 2003, when 40-something Divecha decided to return home to Mumbai, explore the sounds of Indian languages and compile it all in an album, Full Circle. The album, brought out by Blue Frog, releases on September 24.

"This album, as the title says, is a sum of all my musical influences over the years. And the Indian sound, which was absent in my earlier compositions, is present here and that has made it special, giving me an identity," Divecha says about the 11-track set. The lyrics are in Hindi, Tamil and English, apart from a smattering of Sanskrit shlokas, and the sounds are myriad — Hindustani folk and Carnatic rhythms, apart from Latin American and African sounds, R&B, jazz and gospel rock.

Divecha, who has strummed the acoustic guitar with Carlos Santana for the Beninese singer Angelique Kidjo, and with others such as drummer/composer Dave Weckl and renowned bassist Louis Johnson, has also played the guitar for the soundtrack of Penelope Cruz starrer Woman On Top and scored for films like Leela. He has been busy in Bollywood as well, having worked with music directors such as Vishal-Shekhar and

Salim-Suleiman and playing in the forthcoming Ru Ba Ru by Arjun Chandramohan Bali and Aashayein by Nagesh Kukunoor.

This time, for the album, Divecha has collaborated with 20 musicians, including Kailash Kher, Kunal Ganjawalla, Ranjit Barot, Karl Peters and Vivek Rajagopalan. "Collaborations are common, but my compositions have got the artists to do something they have never done before," says Divecha, who has composed and produced all the tracks in the album. Artists like Kher, for instance, have taken to a westernised singing style.

"The journey of making this album and exploring India has been a learning experience and even a lifetime doesn't seem enough. This is what I will continue doing," he smiles. He has indeed come a full circle.

Heading: Jamia nagar morning mayhem - Indian Express
Content:
Dressed in a faded T-shirt and her hair braided back, 44-year-old Stella seems most content as she cajoles children in a sparsely furnished room. Even though the caption underneath her image reveals that the Zambian has been under trial for six years, the smile on her face appears genuine and it is hard to imagine her behind the bars. But, then, the same holds true for most Tihar inmates who find a place in the photographs of The Indian Express principal photographer Renuka Puri (inset), which are on display at the exhibition "In the Shadows of Walls" at The Ashok till today.

"Bollywood presents a very sad picture of life in prison. I wanted to show that the stereotypical notion is incorrect," says Puri, as she points to the photograph The Bar Dancer that has bar dancer Meena practising for an Independence Day function at the Tihar Jail. Across the hall are several black-and-white photographs taken by Puri over the past four years. There is no formal categorisation, but each cluster of photographs focuses on a particular aspect — from children living in Tihar to inmates deep in prayers. If The Photobook has the room of a British inmate with walls pasted with pictures of Princess Diana along with pages from glossy magazines, in The Eyes that know the darkness and can't forget, Puri zooms in on a five-year-old clutching the prison bars. The colour may be missing from the prints, but Puri assures that the grim life inside the prison has its colourful moments.

Heading: Injured cop now stable - Indian Express
Content:
-Sheila, Patil, LG Khanna meet to firm up security in Capital

In the wake of the blasts last week and reports of CCTV cameras not functioning properly, Chief Minister Sheila Dikshit has asked for a special committee to be formed to monitor the functioning of all CCTVs installed in the Capital's public spaces.

According to a senior official, while Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil had called a special meeting to discuss the implementation of the security plans of Delhi in a time-bound manner, Dikshit and Lieutenant Governor Tejendra Khanna had raised the matter of CCTVs not functioning in the city's markets.

"The chief minister went with a one-point agenda of beefing up the Capital's security and with existing CCTVs not functioning properly, she has asked for a special committee of officials to be formed to ensure smooth functioning of these cameras," said an official.

Following the blasts on Saturday, the New Delhi Municipal Council has commissioned a set of 43 Internet Protocol (IP) cameras for CP and Palika Bazaar and the government has identified 58 markets where CCTV cameras must be installed.

"The idea of the meeting was to see how the decision taken by the Union Cabinet could be implemented in a time-bound and well-coordinated manner," said Home Secretary Madhukar Gupta after the meeting got over at Patil's residence.

Gupta added the government was also planning to utilise retired personnel from the army and other paramilitary forces to fill up vacant posts in the police force.

Heading: Dowry crimes top list in UP ‘badland’ - Indian Express
Content:
Thirty-five-year old Balwant Rana, Head Constable with the Special Cell of the Delhi Police, was caught in the gunfire between terrorists and the police on Friday morning at Jamia Nagar. The constable sustained a bullet wound in his right arm and was rushed to the AIIMS Trauma Centre for surgery, where he is now recuperating.

"Balwant's condition is stable, he has a gunshot wound in his right arm and we will operate on him soon. There is also a possibility that the impact of the bullet could have fractured his bone," Assistant Professor of Surgery at the AIIMS Trauma Centre said.

Rana's elderly father was in Bulandshahar in UP when he heard that his son had been injured, "I did not get a call from anyone and only got to know that Balwant was injured when the news was flashed on television. I called up my elder son, who is also with the Delhi Police, and then rushed to Delhi. I have been informed that he is not in danger," Kumar Pal Singh told Newsline.

"My son was very brave today," he added.

Heading: Grappling with stereotypes, these women wrestle for a future - Indian Express
Content:
Long infamous for making abduction and contract killing almost a cottage industry, Ghaziabad, that 'bright' spot on the badlands map of western Uttar Pradesh, is gaining notoriety on another front: dowry cases. As many as 130 in a list of 280 criminals on the district police's most-wanted list are wanted under the Dowry Prohibition Act.

Senior Superintendent of Police (Ghaziabad) L Ravi Kumar admitted that there is a "large number" of bad characters wanted in dowry-related cases, but "I don't have the exact figures right now".

Kidnapping, long considered a 'booming industry' in western UP, is placed second in the police list, with 81 alleged criminals wanted under such cases.

Of 130 alleged criminals wanted under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 13 are wanted under Section 304(B) — which relates to dowry death — and 117 are booked under other Sections like 498 (A), in which a relative or family member (primarily victim's husband) are accused of subjecting her to cruelty. "Once a complaint is filed under the Dowry Prohibition Act, a chargesheet has to be filed against the accused. The court then takes up the case," SP (City) Vijay Bhushan said.

The reason for the fat in the list of accused in dowry-related cases can be attributed to the fact that four or five relatives are "generally named in an FIR registered under the Dowry Prohibition Act," a police officer said. "And each one has to be arrested, though most of them flee before the police get into action."

Many officers believe that complainants often misuse the Act. "There have been cases where we know that the allegations are wrong," a police officer said, "but going by the Act we have to take action against the accused named in the complaint."

Heading: Textbook controversy: SC asks DU to submit report - Indian Express
Content:
Delhi man's Olympic bronze medal later, a look at city's only akhada for women

Tall, fair and pretty, Sonika Raman looks anything but a wrestler. But when Raman, 25, pins her younger brother to the mat, you know you are facing one tough woman: the recipient of "Mahila Bharat Kesri" award in the 75-kg category, the biggest achievement for women in the sport.

And her playground for the past 10 years is the 12x12-metre mat at Chandgi Ram akhada, the Capital's only akhada for women in North Delhi. "I took up wrestling after finishing Class X. My father encouraged me to take it up since there was not much being done for women's wrestling in the country," says Raman, currently undergoing physiotherapy for spinal injury. "Now I want to fulfil my father's ambition of India producing a champion woman wrestler."

She and 14 other women train at the akhada under the watchful gaze of Padamshree Chandgi Ram, a 1970 Asian Games gold medallist in wrestling. But these days only a few are seen practising — some are either recovering from injury or are away at the 2010 Commonwealth Games camp in Patiala.

Raman says the average training day is broken into halves: three hours each in the morning and evening. The coach is a strict disciplinarian: "We do a 10-km jog, 100 push-ups, and then walk on our hands," Raman, seniormost wrestler at the akhada, says.

After that comes wrestling — always on the mat, for this akhada does not allow wrestling on sand. "We hone our skills on mat since international wrestling is done on that," Raman says.

Though not many in the country still associate the sport with women, wrestling was a conscious decision for many who joined the akhada. It was a "natural choice" for Sonu Verma, 20, from Bhiwani in Haryana, now made famous by the boxers. "My father was a professional wrestler, and since I was always a tomboy, he encouraged me to take up the sport," says Verma, who participated in 2006 junior nationals in 52-kg freestyle.

Others like Panipat resident Rekha Kaliyan, 20, took up wrestling to face challenges. "My brother was a wrestler and seeing him pin opponents to the ground, I wondered whether I could do the same," the bronze medallist at 2006 senior nationals (55kg freestyle) says.

Among the akhada's illustrious trainees are Neha Rathi, 2007 Asian Championships winner, and Kavita Sharma, the bronze medallist at the same event.

Raman says wrestling gives respect incomparable to any other profession she could have opted for (she wanted to be a doctor): "It feels nice when parents come and tell me that I inspired them to put their daughter into wrestling. And it's nice that they choose wrestling as a career for their daughters rather than, say, tennis." While Raman is employed with MTNL, others, too, hope to get a stable government job some day.

Heading: Man killed as two vehicles collide - Indian Express
Content:
Certain paragraphs in a textbook by historian A K Ramanujam prescribed for the second year BA (Hons) History syllabus adopted in 2005, which allegedly show Ramayana and its characters Lord Hanumana and Sita in bad light, were brought to the attention of the Supreme Court on Friday.

The apex court directed the Delhi University's expert panel to consider the views of petitioners before it submits its final report.

Opposing the inclusion of the said chapter on the Ramayana, certain educationists including, Dinanath Batra, opposed the book on the ground that it allegedly gives an interpretation of the epic that is different from the one popularly accepted.

Senior advocate M N Krishnamani who appeared for the petitioners said, "It was a distortion of the Ramayana to hurt religious sentiments of the Hindus who worship the characters in the epic as god and goddesses."

The bench headed by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan expressed reservations in passing any directions at the outset. However, the counsel submitted that a different yardstick is adopted if something relating to other religions causes controversy. "It is because Hindus are tolerant and considerate that anything can be allowed to be published against their faith and religion," he argued.

The bench, also comprising Justices P Sathasivam and J M Panchal, directed the university's five-member expert committee to consider the views of petitioners while giving a report to the Vice Chancellor for clearance by the Academic Council. It also gave liberty to petitioners to approach the court again if the report fails to address their concerns.

Heading: The Hero: ‘Mohan has shown the way to Delhi Police’ - Indian Express
Content: A man was killed when two vehicles collided with each other and one of them rammed a Delhi Metro contractor's trailer truck in the Capital. The accident occurred on Thursday night when the two cars were coming from Jangpura at high speed. The injured were taken to Moolchand Hospital, police said. One of the drivers succumbed to his injuries, they added.

Heading: A call caught: day after, Sharma’s team smoked the terror men out - Indian Express
Content:
Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma's family, friends and colleagues stood at the Holy Family Hospital on Friday evening and quietly watched the officer lose his battle with life. But grief came second to pride.

The police officer passed away at 7 pm, grievously injured in the gunbattle at Jamia Nagar on Friday morning. His colleagues had rushed to the hospital's intensive care unit for one last glimpse. His relatives, his wife Maya and daughter were there too. But the last glimpse was too brief. Maya and the young daughter were almost immediately taken back to their Dwarka home amid security concerns.

Unfortunately, Sharma's school-going son could not be with his father in the last hours. He was home with dengue.

BJP leaders L K Advani and Narendra Modi visited the hospital to pay their last respects. So did Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil.

President Pratibha Patil conveyed her condolences and Prime Minister Manmohan Singh wrote in his letter to the grieving family: "I was shocked to know about the sad demise of your husband, Inspector MC Sharma, who laid down his life in defending the security of our country. He was an exceptionally brave officer and had shown exceptional courage throughout his career. He was an inspiration for our security forces in his life and will continue to inspire them after demise too. It is officers like your husband who make us all feel confident that our security is in safe hands. Your husband's passing away is a great loss for our country and society."

The inspector's uncle Puroshottam Sharma spoke strongly of his nephew's courage. He said: "Mohan has always led from the front. He has shown the way to the Delhi Police. We were proud of him and he will always live among us." Sharma's sister Heera Devi stood nearby, too choked for words.

Sharma's colleagues paid glorious tributes. Additional Commissioner of Police Karnail Singh said: "Sharma was a very brave officer. His feats have been an inspiration to the force." One of his colleagues said: "Many had doubted the authenticity of today's operation.

But Sharma's wounds stand testimony to it all."

Sharma's body was shifted to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences later on Friday evening for the postmortem. The officer will be cremated with full state honours on Saturday afternoon.

Heading: The house: L-18, Jamia Nagar - Indian Express
Content:
OnThursday, officers at the Delhi Police's Special Cell office on Lodhi Road had reasons to cheer for first time since Saturday's serial blasts across the Capital. A call intercept had just given Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma and his team the first vital leads about suspects of the serial blasts.

The calls were made from few numbers in Uttar Pradesh and Mumbai. Immediately, a meeting of all key officers were called in: among them were ACP Sanjeev Yadav, ACP L N Rao and ACP Ravi Shankar.

Thursday's call intercepts were culmination of a week's hard work: the Special Cell's three units (New Delhi, Southern and Northern ranges) had put about 15 cellphone numbers under surveillance since Saturday. These numbers under surveillance, the investigators found, were from phones in Jamia Nagar, near Batla House.

Special Cell sleuths had been doing rounds of the area ever since Saturday.

Thursday's meeting went on till 3 am and thrashed out minute details of the raid at Jamia Nagar, to be done on Friday morning: teams were formed, and each assigned their positions and tasks. This time, Special Cell officers knew that they had genuine information that could yield results. Delhi Police and central agencies also informed the National Security Guards (NSG) about the operation, and all officers part of the action were given bullet-proof jackets.

Since Jamia Nagar area is a communally sensitive area, the Special Cell asked the local police to remain on alert.

At 3 am, the officers finally retired for a quick nap and change of clothes. They were back at the Lodhi Road office a few hours later.

Some Special Cell officers went on a reconnaissance of the Batla House area around 7.30 am — in plain clothes, they identified the building.

The real operation began in another couple of hours, when the first policeman reached L-18 around 9.45 am. He spoke to the residents and the area outside was cordoned off. The encounter had begun.

Heading: Youths in next flat detained for hours - Indian Express
Content:
The five alleged militants who had a gun-battle with the police this morning had moved into the fourth floor of L-18, Jamia Nagar, two-and-a-half months ago. Police sources said the main accused, Atif, alias Bashar, and Sajed were killed in Friday morning's encounter.

One Mohammed Saif was injured and arrested, while two others escaped, police officials said. All five were said to be in their mid-twenties. The two who managed to escape have not been identified yet.

Other than Atif, the four others were enrolled in spoken English courses in private institutes, police sources said. A builder flat, the fourth floor of L-18 was sold to one Raeez Ahmad. The five alleged militants had rented flat number 108 from Ahmad, a police officer said.

"The three identified militants are from Sarai Meer area of Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh," the officer said. "Their leader, Atif, had left his hometown and came to the Capital for further studies. The five were responsible for manufacturing bombs used in Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Delhi blasts."

Police sources said according to information, 12 people regularly visited the apartment, and the five "more or less" resided in the place.

Residents of the area, however, denied the presence of more than five people in the apartment. "They always carried books and other study material; they looked like proper students," Maseeh Alam, a lawyer who lives in the same block, said. "They did not create any disturbance and kept to themselves.

"No one in the area had any problem with them."

A few first-year Jamia Millia Islamia students, who live on the first floor of the building, told Newsline that the five had moved in barely two months ago. "All I know about them was that they were students," one student, who did not want to be named, said. "One man visited them regularly — he looked like a maulana.

"The lights in their apartment often stayed on till about 3 am. But that did not seem out of place since a lot of students live in this area."

Heading: Jamia Nagar holds its breath as it struggles with the ‘terror tag’ - Indian Express
Content:
After Friday morning's encounter, Special Cell sleuths took back to their office six cousins from flat number 107, the apartment opposite the one housing the alleged militants. Family members claim the police whisked away the youths without informing them.

The five were detained at the Special Cell office on Lodhi Road till late Friday evening, police sources said.

Senior officers refused to comment on the issue but police sources said as per information, a 13-year-old boy was believed to be part of the gang. The boy allegedly played a vital part in making bombs set off across the city on Saturday. Officers said the six were detained to find out whether they knew anything about "this boy".

The six detained are: Shahbaz Hussain (a Class XII student), Rooni (Class X), Amir Khan (Class XI), Abu Jaleel (Class X), MBA student Karamat Khan, and Sohail Anwar — who had undergone special studies in The Quran at Saharanpur. Relatives said Anwar had come to Delhi to lead special Ramzan prayers (taraveeh).

According to sources, they were taken away at 11.30 am — at about the same time the police whisked away Mohammed Saif, the alleged militant arrested.

The police could not detain their cousin and flatmate, MBA student Shakeel Ahmad, since he had left for classes at 8.30 am. Ahmad said his cousins were "fine" at the time he left in the morning. "But there was heavy police presence in the area when I returned," he said. "The house (L-18) was cordoned off.

"I could not find my cousin brothers anywhere. I went and asked some of their local guardians in the area but they also did not know anything."

He said the police did not inform relatives about their detention. "They (relatives) had to make a lot of effort to get information that the six had been taken for questioning," Ahmad said. "The police called it protective detention but their families claim they were taken away from the building after the encounter." Sources said the youths were asked what they knew about their neighbours.

One Saad Ahmad, a software professional settled in New Zealand, is their relatives and pays rent for L-107. Their immediate families are based in Gaya, Bihar.

Heading: SP leader, 3 others booked for murder - Indian Express
Content:
The fourth-floor flat of house L-18, Jamia Nagar was out of bounds in the afternoon.

Its verandah wore a dishevelled look, with pieces of smashed flower pots and glass strewn all over. A black shirt fluttered from a hanger outside, a pair of blue jeans lay folded on the floor. The door that led into the balcony had religious verses pinned on it. This was where the two alleged terrorists were shot dead in a mid-morning encounter by the police.

Nearby the building stands the Khalilullah Mosque and in its shadow a lattice of narrow lanes. Most houses on them are tall, but neck-to-neck.

The closeness of the homes helped the police on Friday. They clambered on the upper floors of the house opposite — L-10 — and started throwing flower pots at the fourth-floor balcony where the men lived — to test if the men were inside.

A resident here Saba Israr said: "By 10.15 am they had opened fire and it continued for sometime. I read my namaz at home today." Locals said the five alleged terrorists were students of the Jamia Millia University.

The bang of the guns drained peace from the area on Friday, the holiest day of Ramzan. Not many ventured out to the mosque, schoolbuses refused to drop home students and people seemed disconcerted — will this area get a terror tag? As Israr put it: "We are looking at the credentials of our tenants. How could this have happened in our locality?"

The people here mention three places to identify where they live — Khalilullah, Batla House and Okhla. These areas might be geographically separate, but the combined address established their reality — the religious splendour of the mosque, the familiarity of Batla and the opulence of Okhla.

The residents also fiercely guard the reputation of that address. It was not a happy experience to see Zeba Siddiqui — a student of Class XII — being picked up by her father because the school authorities would not send the bus on Friday.

Thirty-two-year-old mother of two Sheeba Naqvi shifted to the Khalilullah area a few months ago. "We lived in Zakir Nagar, but this locality, with its robust service class, appealed to us. It is not congested and the people are liberal," Naqvi said. Her children study at Frank Anthony School in Lajpat Nagar. But Naqvi sounded tentative too: "Did we make a mistake by coming here? I am so scared."

Third-year student at Kamala Nehru College, Saba Siddiqui said: "Khalilullah is a better address than Batla House or Zakir Nagar. Batla is very congested. Here people want to be something."

There are some who are irritated at the secrecy of Friday's operation and are scared of being branded fundamentalists. Mehtab Khan, 51, said: "I came here from Bihar because I wanted my daughters to get a good education. This is the best locality to live in, but I have second thoughts now. Shouldn't the police talk to us, tell us where their suspicions lie?" One of his girls is in Jamia while the other is a budding fashion designer.

On Friday, their father kept them home.

Heading: ‘Questionable deals were approved by previous CMCH director’ - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after a Shiv Sena leader was arrested for murder, the Shimlapuri police have booked another politician — Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Taranjit Singh — for murder. Singh, who was recently appointed as SP's district youth wing president, is absconding.

On Wednesday evening, Singh and three of his supporters — Pappu, Neetu and Jyoti — allegedly shot at Vikash Kumar Sharma (22) and Gurmail Singh while celebrating his appointment as president. He was reportedly in an inebriated state.

Sharma, who was admitted to Satguru Apollo Hospital, succumbed to his injuries on Thursday afternoon. The condition of Gurmail Singh, who was shot in the leg, is stated to be stable.

Station House Officer (Shimlapuri) Pawanjit said: "Efforts are on to nab all the three accused."

Heading: 20 more dengue cases surface - Indian Express
Content:
The report of the fact-finding committee hints at several questionable deals concerning the financial matters of the Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMCHS) Society," said CMCHS chairman Dr Rajinder Giani on Friday.

The six-member fact-finding committee was constituted on March 14 (at an emergency Governing Body meeting) to investigate the role of the previous management, headed by former CMCH director Dr John Pramod, in some institutional matters. A private firm had been hired to look into the alleged financial irregularities.

"We had received complaints about the previous management from two organisations. One was the CMC Sangharsh Samiti and the other was a group of senior faculty members of the institute," said Dr Giani.

"Some decisions taken by the previous director are definitely questionable. The matter of taking a loan of Rs 60 lakh for a hostel is clearly wrong. Also, an architect, who is Dr Pramod's father-in-law, was hired at Rs 75,000 per month— this salary cannot be justified," he added.

Investigations are still on as the committee is yet to go through some documents allegedly withheld by a few management members in an effort to obstruct scrutiny. "The Wolkhardt Heart Centre project was scrapped — the hospital has been drawn into legal hassles now as Wolkhardt has filed a case and the matter is subjudice. The Regional Cancer Centre project was abandoned by the House as we could not find the MoU that had been signed in that regard," said Dr Giani, hinting at non-cooperation of the members.

Asked about the present financial status of the hospital, he said the institute was doing better than before. "CMCH has been able to clear most of its debt and revenue has also increasedm," said Dr Giani.

On the other hand, Dr John Pramod had answers for all allegations. "The loan was clearly not for myself, but to provide accommodation to the students of Post Graduation and Dental College. Even now, students are residing in that very hostel. The loan amount was to be repaid in installments and will be recovered easily."

"On the architect issue, I would like to clarify that my father-in-law was hired by the previous director. I only allowed his services to continue. Also, the money paid to him was to be adjusted in the final fee for various projects, as agreed upon earlier," he said.

He added that the committee was given full co-operation in the investigation. "I possess no documents," he said.

Heading: SSA projects affecting class teaching in schools, rue teachers - Indian Express
Content:
Twenty more cases were added to the total tally of the confirmed cases of dengue in the district so far this season, taking the total number of dengue patients to 49, said health department report today.

District Health Officer, Dr S.S. Dhir said that the number of cases increased suddenly as pending reports of some cases were received today. He however added there was no need to panic. "There is nothing to fear but the residents should take care to avoid mosquito bites," he said.

Different hospitals in the city are also registering an increase in the number of suspected cases of the disease. The total number of suspected cases registered from different hospitals so far has also crossed 200 mark.

Meanwhile All Indian Congress Committee Rajiv Gandhi Panchayat Raj Sangathan today expressed concern over the rising number of cases of dengue in the city. A statement issued by the Sangathan said that it was an alarming situation and therefore the health department should not indulge in suppressing the number of the patients afflicted with the disease.

Heading: Students display Gujarat art in their creations - Indian Express
Content:
All the government primary schools in the district have been running three projects of Sarv Shiksha Abhiyan simultaneously. These important projects are being run on regular basis and thus the class-wise syllabi to be taught to the students is being ignored.

The teachers teaching in these schools are a worried lot as regular studies, especially of senior classes is getting affected.

Said a group of teachers, "The school starts at 8 a.m. It takes about half an hour for morning prayer and marking the attendance. Then, starts "Padho Punjab"- the first project of SSA in collaboration with Pratham, an NGO. Under this, students are taught Punjabi and mathematics from 8:30 am to 10:30 am. After that, a 15-minute break is given to the students which is followed by 'Mid-day meals,' the second project of SSA. It takes about one hour to finish with this. And then starts the third project of SSA i.e. learning through radio. It starts at 12:05 and concludes at 12:35 p.m. It is followed by discussion between teacher and the students as what did they learn from that lesson. Afterwards, we have to write the feedback about radio learning programme. And the school gets over at 1:30 p.m."

The teachers said that they were left with no time to teach students anything from the recommended syllabus. A teacher from the rural area school said, "We feel that studies of class IV and V get affected maximum. We also brought it in the notice of District Education Officer (Elementary)."

Amarjeet Kaur, District Education Officer (Elementary), said, "Teachers told me about this problem and in the meeting of October 10, we will bring it in the notice of higher authorities."

Meanwhile, through Edusat Block Resourcepersons and Block Master Trainers are being made aware about different schemes of SSA. Today they were told about "Padho Punjab," an initiative of SSA with Pratham. This training through Edusat will continue till September 25.

Heading: City doc attends ‘Dialysis Con 2008’ - Indian Express
Content:
Mixing the traditional art of villages of Gujarat in their modern and appealing creations, 20 students of third semester of fashion designing of Sportking Institute of Fashion Technology, who visited local artisans of Gujarat to learn from their art, showcased their articles in an exhibition here today.

With the use of intricate designs on modern clothes and dresses in an attempt to save the dying art forms like 'Rogan' and 'Namdah', the students not only impressed the visitors but also raised the issue of saving the traditional artisans from penury by roping in their talent to occupy share in the modern apparel market.

"We tried to learn from them in our 22 -day stay in Gujarat wherein we visited various villages and some famous and some unknown artisans of the country. But, we observed there that in spite of all the progress in the industry, somehow it is not being transferred to them," said Sonali Jain and Sakshi Sachdeva, members of one of the four groups of the students who visited Gujarat in June-July.The students worked on these designs after their visit as part of their curriculum and organised an exhibition titled "Varsghat" today.

They said that they would like to tap this potential in their future projects and might come up with commercial products designed on the traditional art.

Heading: Flaws in family planning drive discussed - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Rahul Kohli, Consultant Nephrologist, SPS Apollo Hospitals, attended National Conference of Dialysis -''Dialysis Con 2008" as chairperson. He chaired sessions on management of patients on peritoneal dialysis.

This year for the first time the combined meeting of 11th Annual conference of India Society of Peritoneal Dialysis (ISPD) and 3rd Annual Conference of Indian Society of Hemodialysis (ISHD) was hosted at Sanjay Gandhi Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow as Dialysis Con 2008 . The scientific programme of this meeting included one day Symposium on Reneal Nutrition, followed by the scientific sessions of ISPD and ISHD.

According to Dr Kohli, 'Dialysis Con 2008' is a platform to discuss and deliberate issues related to dialysis and renal nutrition with emphasis on India perspective . A galaxy of national and international faculty participated in the meeting.

The scientific programme is a reflection of the new emerging and unresolved issues in the areas of dialysis renal nutrition related to clinical care, research , development and manpower.

Heading: Seminar held on Kashmir - Indian Express
Content:
The Department of Pharmacology, Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, today organised a symposium on the topic "Contraception" under the aegis of Association of Physiologists & Pharmacologists of India (APPI), Ludhiana branch, and Punjab Medical Council.

Dr Daljit Singh, Principal, DMCH, Dr S.C. Chopra, Dean, Academics and Dr Balbir Shah, Member, Punjab Medical Council, inaugurated the symposium by lighting the lamp. Dr Daljit Singh delivered the inaugural address and emphasised the importance of "contraception," which is the need of the hour in India.

The symposium was attended by about 100 delegates from all the medical institutions of Ludhiana.

Dr Sangeeta Gupta described the physiology of menstrual cycle. Dr Shivani Tandon discussed the hormonal and non-hormonal contraceptives while Dr Monica Aggarwal highlighted the clinical considerations while selecting the appropriate contraceptive for a woman. This meeting was accredited by the Punjab Medical Council for 2 CME hours.

The discussion focussed on drawbacks in the current awareness campaigns which have failed to check the population explosion. The emphasis was laid on the importance of a small family, which results in the overall prosperity of the nation.

Heading: SN Vohra hockey from Sunday - Indian Express
Content:
Panchand Research Institute, Ludhiana chapter, organised a seminar on "Kashmir - Kal, Aaj aur Kal." Radheshyam Sharma, former Vice-Chancellor of Makhan Lal Chaturvedi University of Journalism, Bhopal, addressed the seminar.

Addressing the gathering, Radheshyam Sharma said, "Nationalistic forces have recorded their victory in Jammu and Kashmir in Shri Amarnath Yatra land transfer dispute. This dispute has brought into focus the pseudo-secularism being practised by so-called secular parties of our country. The episode has shown that only an organised protest can compel the leaders to honour people's sentiments."

By tracing out the 333-year-old history of Kashmir, Sharma, said, "It is a matter of grave concern that on one hand we call Kashmir as Paradise of India. While on other hand the issue of Kashmir has been lying pending for so many years."

Heading: Sub-registrar arrested for accepting bribe - Indian Express
Content:
The 38th edition of SN Vohra's All India Gurmeet Memorial Hockey Tournament will start from September 21 at Hockey Stadium, Sector 42.

Addressing a press conference, Chander Shekar, president, Chandigarh Hockey Association said the tournament will see the participation of top teams from all over the country and the teams have been divided into four pools. Air India, Punjab Police, BSF, Jalandhar, BSF, Mohali, ONGC, Western Railways, SRC, Hyderabad, RCF, Kapurthala, Corps of Signals and EME, Indian Overseas Bank, Punjab National Bank, CISF, IAF, PSEb, Ropar Hawks, COE, Patiala, CHFA and Chandigarh XI are the teams which will vie for the top honours. The winning team will get a cash reward of Rs 70,000 while the runners-up team will get a cash prize of Rs 45,000.

Heading: Kisan Mela: Day 2 turns out to be a damp squib - Indian Express
Content:
The Vigilance Bureau arrested a sub-registrar, Arvind Verma, after he was caught red-handed accepting a bribe of Rs 10,000 from an NRI on Friday. Two others, identified as Parminder Pal Singh (cashier) and Harjinder Singh (police constable), were also arrested. The sub-registrar's reader, Gopal Krishan, is absconding.

"NRI Barjinder Singh Lalton wanted to register a power of attorney favouring one Baljit Singh of Baddowal and approached Verma. The accused demanded Rs 15,000 as bribe. Later, the deal was settled at Rs 10,000. After this, Lalton filed a complaint with us," said Senior Superintendent of Police, Vigilance Bureau, Kanwarjit Singh Sandhu.

A Vigilance Bureau team, led by Deputy Superintendent of Police Rav Charan Singh Brar and Deputy Superintendent of Police Gurcharan Singh, laid a trap for the sub-registrar. After Lalton delivered the cash, it passed from Verma to Krishan to Parminder Pal Singh and finally to Harjinder Singh.

The Vigilance Bureau also conducted a raid at Verma's house in Jalandhar and seized Rs 1.59 lakh, 47 bottles of Scotch whiskey and two unlicensed rifles. The Jalandhar Police has registered two cases, one under the Excise Act and another under the Arms Act, against Verma in this regard, said SSP Sandhu.

Verma had replaced 'most honest' officer

Sub-registrar Arvind Verma had replaced Mukesh Kumar, who was presented the 'Most Honest Officer' award by Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal, about four months ago.

Heading: Salt Lake in dengue grip, residents blame KMC - Indian Express
Content:
After getting off to a great start on Thursday, the Kisan Mela at Punjab Agricultural University seemed washed out on its second and concluding day.

The incessant rains, lashing the city since early morning, forced the fair to an early closure with many winding up their stalls even before lunch. The main pandal, where several industrial houses had put up their stalls, resembled a pool of slush.

A prize distribution ceremony, meanwhile, was held at Pal Auditorium, where PAU Vice-Chancellor Dr Manjit Singh Kang awarded progressive farmers and agricultural entrepreneurs for the 'Best Produce' and other competitions. Prizes were also given to different firms for 'Best Exposition' at the mela.

Congratulating the winners, Dr Kang urged farmers to adopt technologies recommended by the PAU to enhance their profitability.

The first prize for 'Best Display in the Agro-Industrial Exhibition' was given to the Department of Plant Breeding, Genetics and Biotechnology, PAU, while Department of Entomology and Department of Plant Pathology bagged the second and third prizes respectively.

In the category of 'Best Field Demonstration', the Department of Plant Pathology was adjudged first and Department of Entomology and Soils followed with second and third positions respectively.

Heading: 7 found guilty in Roma Jhawar abduction case - Indian Express
Content:
Five days ago, Abir Roy Chowdhury, a resident of ward number 10 at BF block in Salt Lake complained of high fever. He was quickly admitted to a private hospital and was found to be suffering from dengue.

Earlier, dengue cases have been reported from the FE block of Salt Lake and Purbachal Housing Estate.

On Friday, Roy Chowdhury was discharged from the hospital. But the seven dengue cases reported from Salt Lake in the last three months have angered the residents.

According to locals, there has been a huge negligence on the part of the municipal authorities. "When the Bagjola canal used to be desilted and water flowed through it steadily, the mosquito menace was greatly reduced. The situation, however, deteriorated after winter, as water stagnated and the place became a breeding ground for mosquitoes," said B K Pal, a resident of Salt Lake.

Though locals alleged that the civic body begins to act only once there is a outbreak of the disease, the municipal authorities have claimed that they had been keeping a constant vigil to check the spread of the diseases.

The Bidhannagar municipality has earmarked Rs 25 lakh as its budget for eradicating diseases this year.

"We have been taking preventive measures, including spraying mosquito-killing oil, clearing bushes, distributing leaflets on awareness and monitoring health of all local people," said Nandogopal Bhattacharya, member, municipality's chairman-in-council (Health).

"Whenever dengue cases are reported we take measures to treat them. There is no specific reason why such cases have been appearing from July. However, all such cases have been cured," he added.

KMC's notice to police: Don't make stations a breeding ground for mosquitoes

KOLKATA: The Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) will serve notices to police stations asking them to keep its premises clean.

The civic body will also send similar notice to Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority directing them to keep its water tanks clean since these places have become breeding places for mosquitoes.

"The police stations of the city are ideal breeding ground for mosquitoes. We have asked the authorities several times to issue a circular to all the police stations regarding this but to no avail. Moreover, Sahidul Islam, joint Municipal Commissioner also had a discussion with the police commissioner over this issue," said Subodh De, MMiC, Health.

This year 24 cases of malaria have been reported from the city, so far. Among them, Rajanath, a resident of Sarsuna (ward no 127), died of Falcifarum Malaria on Wednesday but the KMC took three days to confirm the cause of death. According to a health official, the open trench dug by the Kolkata Environment Improvement Project (KEIP) workers on Biren Roy Road (west) near Sarsuna, has become an ideal breeding zone. Moreover, the surface drains are choked by workers while carrying out the developmental work but they have not been restored.

"We do not have inter-departmental coordination. We repeatedly asked the KEIP to restore the drains so that water does not get stagnated there, but nothing yielded," added De. — ENS

Heading: ‘Cops demanded Rs 1 lakh for my son’s early release’ - Indian Express
Content:
The two security guards at the victim's house have been acquitted

The Barasat court held seven people guilty and acquitted two others in the 2005 abduction case of Roma Jhawar, a college student.

Additional District Sessions Judge Justice Samaresh Prasad Chowdhury convicted the main accused, Gunjan Ghosh, and acquitted two security guards of the Jhawar household, Damodar and Dasarath Yadav. The sentence will be declared on Saturday.

On February 4, 2005, Roma, daughter of a businessman Satyanarayan Jhawar, was abducted when her car stopped at a traffic signal in Salt Lake.

A van blocked the car in which she was travelling. Four miscreants got off and kidnapped her at gunpoint. The following evening, the CID traced Roma.

Around Rs 19 lakh ransom money had been recovered from the possession of the accused in the course of the investigation.

Gunjan Ghosh was aided by his accomplice Munna Sau. While the other accused, Vikas Sau, was driving the car, Dinesh Yadav was guarding the Kankurgachi garage in which Roma was kept. Ramachandra Singh who on occasions drove the family's car also passed on the information to the abductors.

Sukumar Mondal, the driver of the car in which Roma was travelling during the abduction, was also found guilty. So was Mukesh Singh, the driver who had provided the car to Gunjan in which Roma was taken away after abduction.

Gunjan Ghosh's advocate said they were going to move the High Court.

Heading: HC asks state to make Land Transfer Act effective - Indian Express
Content:
The family of Mohamad Azharuddin — the jail inmate who died in the clash with security personnel of Presidency jail on Wednesday — has alleged police officers had demanded Rs 1 lakh for his early release.

A frequent flier to Hong Kong, 24-year-old Azharuddin was detained by the Anti-Rowdy Section of Kolkata police in 2006 for snatching a cellphone.

"It was four days after his arrest, a policeman came to me and demanded one lakh rupees for the speedy release of Azharuddin," alleged his father Sheikh Fakiruddin.

"Ninety days later, we found that the police had framed a lot of cases against him, including those of extortion, and they even got fake witnesses for the identification parade," he said.

According to an officer of the Anti-Rowdy Section, Azharuddin used to procure visas for 14 days and visit Hong Kong at least once in two months.

"From there he used to bring foreign goods and sell them to his clients in Kolkata. He had been doing this for the last few years till he was arrested," the officer said.

Azharuddin's family said that he used to earn about fifteen thousand rupees every time he went abroad. "He saved a large part of it for his sisters' marriage," said Fakiruddin, who sells second hand clothes, at his Ibrahim Street residence in Elbalpore.

On September 17, the day Azharuddin died, Fakiruddin was informed over phone about the incident.

When he went to the Presidency jail, he found his son dead with at least 19 stitches on his head. B D Sharma, I G (prisons), who was present in the jail, informed Fakiruddin that his son had died after being hit by police batons.

Congress leader Subrata Mukherjee, meanwhile, visited Azharuddin's family.

"I called up the jail minister and asked him why the jail superintendent, against whom a complaint of murder was registered, could still continue in the office. He could not answer," Mukherjee said.

He threatened to begin a hunger strike at the gates of Presidency jail if the state government did not take appropriate steps.

Heading: At JU, 10,000 students jostle in 100 acres - Indian Express
Content:
A division Bench of the Calcutta High Court has set aside a notification that made a 1993 Act on land transfer ineffective since its issuance in 1998.

During the hearing of a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by a Kolkata resident, Himangsu Haldar, the bench comprising Chief Justice S S Nijjar and Justice Sanjib Banerjee on Friday also directed the state government to formulate rules and schemes to revive the Act again.

The West Bengal Land (Regulation of Transfer) Act, 1993, was introduced by the state government to regulate all kinds of land transfer in a legal manner. But the Act had become ineffective after the government issued a notification on March 23, 1998.

Advocate General Bolai Roy admitted that the notification was wrongly issued. He sought three months time from the court to formulate rules and schemes to make the Act effective, which was allowed by the Bench.

This year, Haldar filed a PIL challenging the notification in connection with transfer of land in Salt Lake. Anirudha Chatterjee, counsel of Haldar, said the notification should be treated as illegal, as it could not supersede an Act which was passed by the Assembly.

HC orders demolition of a temporary market at Salt Lake

KOLKATA: A Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court comprising Chief Justice S S Nijjar and Justice Sanjib Banerjee on Friday directed the Bidhan Nagar Municipality to demolish the portion of the temporary market that was being constructed in the excess area of the park at BD block in Salt Lake. The bench has directed the civic body to complete the demolition work within 10 days.

Advocate Biswajyoti Bhattacharjee, the special officer, told the Bench that over 50 per cent area of the park was used by the municipality for shifting the market and it had also constructed a building. The court had earlier asked the Bidhan Nagar Municipality not to use more than 40 per cent area of the park for temporary use of the market. — ENS

Heading: Wholesale giant plans to pull out of Bengal - Indian Express
Content:
Jadavpur University, the name synonymous with top-class education in West Bengal, is reeling under a severe space crunch.

The university has about 10,000 students enrolled in the three faculties of engineering, science and arts. All of them, however, have to remain cramped together in just two campuses, which do not even come close to 100 acres when put together.

"We are facing a shortage of space in the university. In many departments, there is not enough space for the students to even sit properly," said Pradip Narayan Ghosh, the Vice Chancellor of the university.

The university has appealed to the state government for about 100 acres of land for another campus at Baruipur in South 24 Parganas but there has been no response from the government. The National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) team that had earlier visited the university described the infrastructure of the university as 'obsolete and outdated'.

Although the university has been rated as one of the best universities by NAAC, experts feel there is an urgent need of expansion for proper growth. The university had secured 3.61 points on a scale of 4, and The University Grants Commission (UGC) had promised to double the grant to the university for the 11th plan period. In that case, the university is likely to get an approximate grant of Rs 20 crore, which experts opine, should be properly utilised in solving the issue of space crunch.

The university is now eyeing a piece of land in the vicinity of the campus. The abandoned land of National Instruments — a central undertaking — is located a stone's throw away from the university.

"We are waiting for the response of the central government. The team has already visited and we can get a reply any time," said the Vice Chancellor. The land of the abandoned National Instruments is, however, only eight acres, and experts feel that the space will not solve the space crisis the university is facing. Only some research facilities can be shifted to the new found space.

The UGC team that visited the university a few months ago also suggested to go for academic and infrastructure expansion. "There is much demand for courses offered by the university. Sometimes, there are 5000 applications for 50 seats," a member of the UGC team said. The university is now planning to start two new departments in Geography and Education from the next session. The university is also keen on starting a school of nuclear engineering and a post graduate course in the subject.

State to get two more medical colleges

Kolkata: The state will soon have two more medical colleges at the ESI hospitals at Joka in South 24 Parganas and Baltikuri in Howrah. The colleges will be funded by the ESI and application for granting them recognition has been sent to the Medical Council of India (MCI). The number of seats in both the colleges has been fixed at 100. While candidates who have cleared the Joint Entrance Examination will be taken in, some seats will also be reserved for children of those covered by ESI. Students who pass out from these two colleges will have to work in their respective colleges for the first five years, the official said. The state government is also planning to introduce PG courses in medicine at Maniktalla ESI hospital and application for granting it recognition has been sent to MCI.

Heading: Ride your way to Puja pandals in AC comfort - Indian Express
Content:
The German wholesale major, Metro Cash & Carry, has decided to pull out of the state after the state government cancelled the Agriculture Produce Marketing Committee (APMC) licence of the firm.

The decision has left the fate of 700 people, including 350 employees, and many farmers and suppliers hanging. The wholesale giant, which was set to open before the Pujas, had already booked several farmers as its suppliers and issued many personalised cards to its customers as well.

The state government is now in a fix. "Discussions are on at various levels. We are expecting that the issue will be resolved by next week. We are trying to come up with some solution," said Naren De, state agriculture minister.

The Forward Bloc, which leads the APMC authority, had protested against the launch of the Metro Cash & Carry on grounds that it would affect livelihood of poor farmers and small shop owners. But there is a difference in opinion within the government.

"If the store is allowed to open then the poor farmers and the small retailers will benefit. The farmers will get rid of the middlemen," said Kanti Ganguly, Minister, Sundarbans affairs. "In the agreement, the firm has assured that it is not going to take up retail business." added Ganguly.

The state government in 2005 granted the APMC license to Metro. It was subsequently renewed in 2006 and 2007, which was valid till March 2008. The license was, however, cancelled by the APMC authority in June 2007 citing that the company had not started its work within the given time. "We have been trying to obtain a fresh license but to no avail, which led to the company 's decision to pull out," said an official of Metro Cash & Carry.

Heading: After Uttar Pradesh, Bengal, Tamil Nadu also receive ‘not usable’ JE vaccines - Indian Express
Content:
With Goddess Durga all set to arrive in Kolkata, the city is gearing up to provide a memorable experience to tourists, both domestic and foreign, who wish to get something more than just a "Puja feel" this autumn.

Soon after tourism minister Manabendra Mukherjee announced that the department was eyeing major private investment in the tourism sector of West Bengal, the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation (WBTDC) has come up with attractive packages for tourists.

"This time we have tried to design packages in such a way that there is something for everyone. It is a government initiative, as many outsiders feel safe to book packages with the WBTDC," said MD WBTDC, TVN Rao.

The WBTDC is offering a two nights/three days stay at a four star hotel for revelling in the Durga Puja celebrations in Kolkata at Rs 21,000 plus taxes. This package will include conducted tours around the city, pandal-hopping and various other Puja attractions. Many such trips and packages are in the offing between October 4 to 11.

For people who are unable to spare time during the four days of the Durga Puja, WBTDC will be organising pre-Puja tours on October 4 and 5. While travelling in the comfort of an AC buses would cost Rs 600 per head, that in a non-AC bus would be Rs 400. It will roll out special Puja trips to traditional Puja pandals outside Kolkata, like Goswami Barir Puja in Serampore, Sheoraphuli Rajbari and the terracotta Naba Kailash temple in Kalna. These are likely to come with a price tag of Rs 1,200 for each day. The government and private tour operators have also organized cruise rides on the river.

The charges for the morning trip will be Rs 500 while the evening ride will cost Rs 100 extra. The vessels will depart from the Outram Ghat jetty.

And it is not just the state government that is offering special packages. Vivada inland waterways has also arranged for a four nights/five days package in its vessel MV Parmahansa for Rs 34,000 per person.

The accommodation will be provided in the vessel itself that will stay afloat in the Hooghly during the four days of the Puja.

Each day will be based on a certain theme with traditional food and folk dances from different parts of Bengal. "On Mahastami, tourists will be taken to Belur Math for the Kumari Puja. Tourists are free to board the vessel anytime during Saptami and the tour will end with the immersion ceremony on October 10," says R Sushila, executive director of Vivada inland waterways.

Heading: ‘Post transfer, shoot feature films too at Technicians’ - Indian Express
Content:
After Uttar Pradesh, the governments of West Bengal and Tamil Nadu have complained to the Centre that the stocks of Japanese Encephalitis (JE) vaccines sent to them recently was not usable.

The serum has lost its efficacy because of exposure to heat.

Following this, the proposed JE vaccination drive, which was to be undertaken as part of routine immunisation in 38 districts across 10 states, has been put on hold.

The Centre has now ordered an inspection into its Karnal-based Government Medical Store Depot (GMSD), the main storage house of such vaccines. Experts are likely to visit the GMSD on Saturday. "We have received some complaints and will conduct inspections in Chennai and Kolkata, like we did in Uttar Pradesh. We will inspect the stock of vaccines kept at Karnal and decide the future course of action," said Dr S D Khaparde, Deputy Commissioner, Infectious Disease, Government of India.

The vaccines that have been sent to West Bengal and Tamil Nadu had reached stage III and IV of damage, which renders them not usable. Vaccines can be used only if the exposure is up to stage II. The damage can be seen by the change in the colour of a heat-sensitive sticker pasted on the vaccines.

On September 12, the Bengal government had written to Naresh Goyal, Assistant Commissioner for Universal Immunisation Programme, Government of India, about the vaccines. The letter stated that 1,44,845 doses of vaccines that the state had received on that day were in stage III of exposure. Only a day before, Director of Public Health and Preventive Medicine in Chennai had written to Goyal that the stock of 85,700 vaccines received from Karnal's GMSD, was found in stage III and IV of exposure.

Kaparde said the vaccines supplied to Tamil Nadu and Bengal were not from the same batch as that of Uttar Pradesh, which had received more than 4.5 lakh defective vaccines last week.

After the Uttar Pradesh government's complaint, a team of Central officials had visited Lucknow, inspected the stock and said the vaccines were still in stage II and therefore, usable. The UP government, however, refused to buy this. "Whatever they have to say, they should inform us in writing. As of now, we want fresh stocks," said Dr M L Khatloiya, Director General, state Family Welfare department.

This particular batch of JE vaccines to UP, Bengal and Tamil Nadu was dispatched on September 10.

The Karnal GMSD receives the vaccine from China. While the Kolkata GMSD caters to the northeastern states, Chennai GMSD caters to the southern states.

Heading: Not really worried about Bagan trio: Booth - Indian Express
Content:
A group of artistes representing the Artist's Forum and Technician's Forum met the principal secretary of the Information and Cultural Affairs department, Dilip Chakraborty, on Friday and submitted a deputation on the transfer of Technicians Studios to private hands.

The group, which included Gautam Ghosh, Rituparno Ghosh, Jeet, Prosenjit, Swapan Saha and Soumitra Chatterjee, alleged that the 33 offices located on the premises of the Technicians Studio had been asked to vacate and given a month's notice without being given any alternatives.

"We want to know what will happen to the 33 offices located within the premises of the studio. Also, we do not want the studio to be used only for serials and telefilms shooting but also for feature films," said Gautam Ghosh.

Technicians Studio, a government-aided studio till even a year back, made headlines when the government decided to hand it over to Zee Telefilms for Rs 41 crore. Though initially the decision had been opposed from various quarters, the final transfer has been made.

Dilip Chakraborty, said: "Nine floors in the studio will be used for the making of telefilms while two will be used to make feature films." On the question of finding an alternative site for 33 offices , Chakraborty said it would not be possible.

Heading: Kolkata set for a date with Arshavin - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai FC coach banks on Hammond and his youth brigade

Mumbai FC coach David Booth is all geared up for the upcoming I-League and doesn't feel that his side would start their campaign as underdogs against Mohun Bagan at Barasat Stadium on September 27.

The Bagan upfront has the likes of Baichung Bhutia, Jose Barreto and PC Lalawmpuia — a combination that can give sleepless nights to any coach. Booth, however, appears unperturbed. Rather, he is a tad apprehensive about whether his young boys would be able to produce their best in front of a packed house that would go ga-ga to see a Bagan win.

"I'm only thinking about whether the youngsters would be able to handle the pressure. It's not easy to play in front of thousands of partisan fans. If they don't choke, they would give Bagan a run for their money," Booth told The Indian Express.

"I'm not really worried about Bagan's strengths. They have quality players, but my job is to help the boys perform to their potential," he added.

The British coach is not really happy with the fitness level of his players. According to him, that was the reason why the team couldn't put up a decent performance in the Durand Cup and was eliminated in the quarterfinals.

"Personally, I didn't want to participate in the Durand Cup. Instead, my idea was to go for an intensive training programme. But we had to participate (in the Durand Cup). So, I chose a line-up comprising basically the juniors.

"I'm not too unhappy with their performance, though there's always room for improvement, especially on fitness count. We have been working to improve their fitness level," Booth observed.

As for the I-league, the new Ghanaian recruit Abel Hammond, fresh from his stint with the Italian third division club Brescia FC, is going to be his trump card.

"Given a choice between Barreto, Yakubu and Hammond, I would choose the latter," Booth said.

Hammond didn't play in the Durand Cup. But his performance in warm-up matches, have impressed one and all.

Said midfielder Noel Wilson: "I don't want to say much at this moment. If Hammond stays fit, he will set the I-League on fire."

The Ghanaian would be paired up with Nigerian Felix upfront. The latter has also impressed his coach with his showings in the I-League qualifiers and the Durand Cup.

In Kalyan Chowbe, Noel Wilson and Sanjoy Parte team has experience. Booth wants a perfect blend of experience and youth which, according to him, would be the key to success.

It would be baptism by fire for Mumbai FC who are playing the I-League for the first time. For a newcomer, to bump into four tougest teams of the tournament in first four matches is certainly not a very welcoming prospect. Coach, however, keeps his fingers crossed.

"Our first four games are against Mohun Bagan, East Bengal, Mahindra United and Dempo SC. The outcome of these matches would decide our fate in the I-League," Booth concluded.

Yakubu cleared

East Bengal have finally roped in Yusif Yakubu who was today released by Salgaocar for a transfer amount of Rs 17 lakh. A Salgaocar official, however, claimed that they took Rs 7 lakh from the player. Yakubu, who had earlier signed a contract with the Goans, sent a letter of apology to Salgaocar management.

Heading: Sambaran appointed chairman, Devang in panel - Indian Express
Content:
If everything goes to plans, Andrei Arshavin and his club Zenit St-Petersburg would be seen in action in Kolkata. It is learnt that the state sports ministry is planning to organise a mega football event in the city in January. Along with Zenit St-Petersburg, a top club from Turkey is also expected to play.

The three city giants — Mohun Bagan, East Bengal and Mohammedan Sporting and an outstation I-League side will make the list in this proposed six-team tournament. The tournament will be named after Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and is likely to start on January 23, Netaji's birthday.

The 27-year-old Arshavin was the undoubted star of Russia's march to the Euro 2008 semifinal. Earlier, he helped his club to first Russian Premier-Liga title last year. He is also Russia's first ambassador for the Fifa SOS Children's Village Charity Project for child orphans.

The state sports minister Subhas Chakraborty plans to organise the tournament after the first phase of the I-League. There would be a few days' gap before the second phase starts. If the plan materialises, the city will once again witness top quality soccer action.

Kolkata's tryst with top class football stars is few and far between. Pele came here in 1977. Then Roger Milla of Cameroon paid a visit in 1990. Last in the list was Bayern Munich goalkeeper Oliver Kahn who played his farewell match against Mohun Bagan last May.

Heading: Aandrita bags singles title - Indian Express
Content:
Sambaran Banerjee has been appointed as the chairman of the Bengal senior selection committee. This was decided in the CAB working committee meeting today. Banerjee, who replaced Arup Bhattacharya, will be assisted by Devang Gandhi, Sharadindu Mukherjee and Kalyan Chowdhury. Barun Burman will head the junior selection panel which will also have Sumit Shome, Farasutullah Khan and Dipankar Sarkar as the other selectors. Mithu Mukherjee will lead the women's selection committee.

The CAB pulled off a surprise by appointing Gandhi as a selector. The former India opener was in the running for the post of senior Bengal team coach. Utpal Chatterjee, however, edged past him in the final selection.

Meanwhile, the CAB Challenger Tournament will be played from November 16-26. The Bengal Ranji probables will represent the three sides, similar to that of the BCCI's Challenger Trophy. The winners will get a prize money of Rs 1.5 lakh, while the Man of the Series and Man of the Match will be richer by Rs 20,000 and Rs 10,000 respectively. The tournament has been named after SK Acharya.

About the renewal of the lease of the Eden Gardens, CAB president Jagmohan Dalmiya said: "We expect to get the renewal by October."

On the pending accounts issue of the IPL, he said: "We are yet to get the details of the amount distribution and an expense worth about Rs 7.26 crore has to be met. We don't want to be out of pocket. Recently, we got a communication from the Kolkata Knight Riders and then we have written to the former office bearers to give us the account summary so that we can recover it."

Heading: Redemptive Pattern - Indian Express
Content:
Aandrita Deb bagged the women's open singles title, while Manoj Kumar Sewa and Saurav Panja paired up to win the men's doubles crown in the Calcutta Hardcourt Tennis Championship at the Calcutta South Club today. Heading: Mamata meets Governor, makes no headway - Indian Express
Content:
Film: The Lives of Others

Director: Henckel von Donnersmarck

Cast: Sebastian Koch, Martina Gedeck, Ulrich Muehe

Rating: ********

Running at: Inox (City Centre,

Forum)

Sometimes, cinema ends up being redemptive. It delivers audience from the overwhelming brutality of history. Through instances of kindness, like in Schindler's List and The Pianist, which talked about amazing survivor tales during the Nazi regime, it humanizes harrowing experiences. The 2006 Oscar-winning film The Lives of Others, which finds a rather late release in Kolkata halls, explores similar territories but its narrative is styled more as a psychological thriller, where characters and not their immediate history, shape the proceedings.

It's East Germany in the mid 1980s, where the oppressive Stasi police rounds up hapless youngsters suspected of helping friends escape to the more liberal West Germany. Fear lurks in every corner, freedom of expression is limited to secret societies of subversive writers who smuggle their works out to the west. In such a world, Georg Dreyman (Sebastian Koch), is a smug, successful writer, who hides his ideals behind the psychophanitc relationship with the government. He seems to have found a perfect balance — he refrains from making direct attacks at the regime in public and the Stasi keeps out of his business. Almost. His passionate affair with a temptuos stage actor, Christa-Maria Sieland (Martina Gedeck), invites the wrath of a senior Stasi official, who is conducting an exploitative affair with her too. A spy is quickly deployed by the government, who with a team of specialists bugs Dreyman's house. The surveilence officer in charge of the case, Gerd Wiesler (Ulrich Muehe) is a cold-blooded monster. He leads a life of a zombie, walking to a bare apartment every night and feeding on the fear of the victims he grills. But light comes to his life in the form of Dreyman's idealism. As he monitors the writer's life, he slowly succumbs to his convictions. He buys their dream of a free world. Ironically, the victims are struggling with their own demons—Dreyman is torn between his life of comfort and the perilous path of his beliefs while Christa is tired of making compromises in her career.

Henckel von Donnersmarck's triumph as a director lies not in the fact that he manages to convince us about Wiesler's transformation, but in the way in which petty incidents have walloping consequences in the film. Yet, the ironies are as delicately layered and delicious as they could possibly be without a hint of preciosity.

Incidentally, in India, which seems to be in a grip of voyeuristic reality television shows, the release of The Lives of Others, couldn't have been better timed. It illustrates in the most potent way, the happy consequences of voyeurism.

Heading: 11 Singur farmers get cheques, 40 in queue - Indian Express
Content:
As the Singur stalemate remained unresolved, Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee met Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi to vent her grievances against the state government.

Banerjee had threatened to start her agitation afresh as the government was not complying with her demands and had "deceived" her.

In her one-hour-twenty-minute meeting, she failed to convince the Governor — mediator between the protestors and the state government on the Singur issue — that the state government betrayed her. On the other hand, the Governor insisted on the state government's version on the issue.

The Trinamool leader refrained from talking about Tata and the various offers made to the Tata

by the Karnataka and Uttarakhand government. She once again chose to reiterate her old stance that her party wanted both agriculture and industry to survive and prosper together. "We want quick and sure solution to the issue. We hope for the best," she said.

According to Trinamool sources, it was evident after

Friday's meeting that Banerjee was entrapped in the situation where very little option was available to manoeuvre.

Earlier, she had hopeed that the Governor would take a U-turn and be on her side.

As the situation unfolded, it was realised that the representatives of some of the key constituents of the 21 party coalition formed by Banerjee for the Singur issue were not present at the meeting.

Leaders like Purnendu Bose also gave the meeting a miss. Banerjee was accompanied by Partha Chatterjee, Dinesh Trivedi and Manik Mukherjee.

Buddha refuses to bow down

KOLKATA: Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee today made it clear that the state government was not ready to make any further concessions to the Trinamool Congress on the issue of the Tata project at Singur. "On the basis of the talks held in front of the Governor between the state government and the opposition, the state government brought out a compensation package for the dispossessed. The problem can only be solved if the Opposition accepts this package," read a statement issued by the chief

minister. — ENS

Heading: Discharged from hospital, Basu talks development, cooperation - Indian Express
Content:
Terror loomed large in the villages of Singur as 11 unwilling farmers accepted compensation cheques on Friday. At least 40 others submitted papers, applying for compensation and formally giving land for the Tata small car factory.

The process will continue till September 22. District Magistrate Neelam Meena said the exercise will continue uninterrupted over the weekend as well.

The state government has marked three spots for receiving applications from farmers and issuing cheques to them. These are Singur's BDO office and Chinsurah's SDO office and DM's office.

Chinsurah being 40 kms away from Singur, the distance has proved an impediment, especially for the aging people.

But things are little better in Singur, where the BDO office also being the office of the Panchayat Samiti, currently controlled by the Trinamool Congress. Most farmers are wary of going there to apply for compensations, said an official of district land acquisition department, the nodal agency responsible for issuing cheques.

Besides, there is a general fear of retaliation keeping some of the farmers from putting in their application. Most are consciously avoiding media glare and the watchful eyes of Trinamool supporters.

Avoiding the BDO office which is closer home, one of the farmers, Dilip Barik, had gone to the DM's office in Chinsurah on Friday. His father Sanatan Barik is due to receive a cheque of nearly Rs 50,000 for their land tomorrow.

He confessed that his entire family had ardently opposed the land acquisition for the Tata motors plant. "At the time, the pressure was such that we had no option but to join the resistance movement," said Dilip Barik. "The pressure is still there, which is why I had to be careful to avoid the eyes of the party strongmen."

The DM is also aware that terror is keeping many farmers from putting in their applications.

"This is why we are not disclosing the names of farmers who have put in their application," said Meena.

Becharam Manna, Mamata Banerjee's pointsman in Singur, meanwhile, said they were not terrorising unwilling farmers. It was the CPM which was forcing farmers to put in applications at gunpoint.

"Our party has also filed an FIR in Singur police station in this regard," he said. But police sources said it was a complaint from a political party, no individual has put forth any such complaint.

"We have forwarded it to higher authorities," said a senior officer of Singur police station.

Heading: After 8 years, GMADA says 15 colonies illegal - Indian Express
Content:
In the first public comment since his discharge from hospital, former chief minister Jyoti Basu has asked the Opposition to coordinate with the government over the Singur issue.

He said those who have halted work at Tata Motors should keep in mind that the revised compensation package will benefit the disposed farmers there.

"If the Singur project is allowed to go ahead, it will mean industrial and financial development for Bengal. More investors will be encouraged to come to the state and the job market will grow. The Singur project is for the people, not against them. To make it a success, we need cooperation from all sections of people," Basu said in a statement.

The CPM, meanwhile, expressed concern over the Singur impasse, saying the people there wanted the Nano factory to stay. Addressing the media after the CPM state secretariat meeting, party state secretary Biman Bose said: "We are concerned. The people of the state should know who are against development." He said the considerable turnout at the Left Front pro-Tata Motors rally in Singur on September 15 was an indicator of it.

"Amar Halder, our Burdwan district committee secretary, was leading a big procession, but it was stranded on the Durgapur Expressway owing to the massive turnout of people. Such an enormous crowd would not have been possible if people did not want the plant," Bose said. He said the Karnataka government's offer of land to Tata Motors is not impractical. "Those who want to set up industry can decide where they will look for land. The people should decide what is to be done about those who do not want the state to prosper," he added.

Heading: No agency has attempted to tap phones of HC judges: Punjab Govt - Indian Express
Content:
It has taken nearly eight years for the authorities to realise that fifteen colonies in Zirakpur and Kharar are illegal.

Nearly 70 per cent of these colonies are infact developed with people residing here for the last six years.

For the residents, the news has come as a shock as all the plots in these colonies are registered and house maps have been cleared by the local bodies.

The issue came to the fore when the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) recently swung into action on a petition filed in the Punjab and Haryana High Court pertaining to the Singhwala choe that starts from Panchkula in Haryana and enters Punjab at Zirakpur. The High Court gave a notice to the GMADA to identify the parties who were polluting the choe and the authorities zeroed in on the fifteen colonies.

"We examined the matter from the legal angle and after receiving field reports, we concluded that these colonies have been developed without the approvals from competent authorities," said GMADA Additional Chief Administrator Balwinder Singh Multani.

He added, "The colonisers have been booked under the Punjab Apartment and Property Regulation Act (PAPRA) and FIRs have been lodged against these developers. These colonies have been sheltered by the Municipal Council."

Multani further said that each developer has been asked to install a separate sewerage plant and stop polluting the choe.

The developers, meanwhile, have a different take on the issue. "No clearance from anybody was required at the time when we started developing these colonies in 2000. Now we are asked to establish our own sewerage plant, which would cost anywhere near Rs 40 lakh depending upon the number of houses," said the spokesperson of Krishna and Lakshmi Enclave in Zirakpur.

The spokesperson added that of the total 400 plots, hardly 150 are lying vacant without any construction and that even today, people are constructing houses on these plots,

Nearly 2,000 plots in Zirakpur alone are claimed to have been sold without the permission of GMADA. The present rate of these plots in Zirakpur ranges between Rs 8,000 to 13,000 per square yard.

"It is a matter of concern that local bodies like the Municipal Council and City Town Planning have passed the layout plans for the houses on these plots, which is termed as the legal stamp. Of the fifteen colonies, nine fall under the GMADA and six under the concerned local bodies," said Deputy Commissioner (Mohali) Rahul Bhandari.

Blamegame

Additional Chief Administrator GMADA Balwinder Singh Multani has his justifications ready. "Action is only taken when things come to our notice. The local bodies are to be blamed for sheltering these colonies."

Heading: Secretariat staffer held for taking bribe - Indian Express
Content:
