The Punjab government, on Friday, filed its reply in the Punjab and Haryana High Court submitting that no agency of the Punjab government has ever attempted to tap the cellphones of High Court Judges.

The reply was filed in wake of a suo moto notice issued by the Punjab and Haryana High Court on the basis of a news item which had appeared in an English daily. The news item had highlighted that post the judge-bribery case, some judges of the High court expressed suspicion of their phones being tapped.

Notices had been issued to the states of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh. While law officers for Haryana and Chandigarh sought time to file replies, the counsel of the Punjab government filed its reply on Friday.

It was further submitted that the Government cannot do so as it does not have any authority for the same.

While the issue was first raised by judges nearly a month ago, several judges had consequently decided to hang up on their existing service providers and go in for new numbers. Similar apprehensions have also been aired time and again by advocates handling "anti-establishment" cases.

Heading: Minor boy among three held for stealing vehicles - Indian Express
Content:
The Vigilance Cell of the UT Police arrested an employee with the Jail and Judicial Branch of the Haryana Civil Secretariat on Friday after he was caught red-handed accepting Rs 2,000 as bribe.

The accused, Jag Mohinder Singh, an assistant, was caught after the police laid a trap on the complaint of Rajinder Kumar Bawa, Additional District Attorney (ADA) in the Fisheries Department at Panchkula.

Bawa wanted a transfer to Hisar to be with his father who is 107 years old. After he appealed to the department in this regard, Singh allegedly demanded Rs 3,000 for handing over his transfer orders.

Bawa told the Vigilance Cell that he had paid an advance of Rs 1,000 a day before and was to hand over the rest of the amount on Friday.

A trap was then laid by the police and Jag Mohinder Singh was arrested under Section 7 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

DSP (Vigilance) Promod Kumar said the accused was caught red-handed while accepting the bribe.

"Jag Mohinder had asked Bawa to give a missed call on his mobile phone to call him from his office. He was to hand over the orders in exchange of the money," he said.

The Vigilance Cell has started conducting raids at his residence for more clues.

Heading: ‘It appears UPA is the Oppn, not the ruling party’ - Indian Express
Content:
The police arrested three persons on Friday, including one juvenile, from Sector 51 for their alleged involvement in a number of motor vehicle thefts in the city.

The arrested have been identified as Varun (21), Tafuzzal alias Bittu (19) and a 16-year-old boy, all residents of Dadumajra colony. According to the police, Varun had been arrested a few years back when he was a juvenile. He is now said to be the gang leader. Two Maruti cars were recovered from their possession.

On Thursday, the police received a tip-off which led to the arrest of the gang. During interrogation, the accused confessed to snatching a purse containing Rs 800 from one Ved Parkash, resident of Colony Number 5 near the Sector 20 Gurdwara a few months back.

The gang is said to have spread its wings in various states. The police said the arrested used to make master keys and lift cars at night. A case has been registered with the Sector 34 police station.

Heading: CII for more industry involvement in checking AIDS - Indian Express
Content:
The decision taken by local members of the Congress on Thursday, to meet UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and complain against the attitude of the officials of the Administration including Administrator Gen S F Rodrigues (Retd), has invited flak from different political corners.

Former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) parliamentarian Satya Pal Jain alleged complete failure on part of the Congress and local MP Pawan Kumar Bansal.

"People voted for them and brought them to power. The Administrator is appointed by the Centre. They are now trying to disassociate themselves with the functioning of the Administration," said Jain.

He added, "The Congress is trying to befool the people. They have not achieved anything substantial in the past four years. The party is shirking its responsibility by blaming the officials and the Administrator."

Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) convenor Harmohan Dhawan shared similar views.

"It appears the Congress is the opposition and not the ruling party. The Opposition makes various demands, not the ruling party while the MP here is writing letters to the Centre putting forward his demands," said Dhawan.

He added, "Their party is in power at the Centre and the MP should talk to the Home Minister and get things done. Bansal cannot escape his duty. At the fag end of the term they are trying to hide their failures."

Dhawan further stated that if the Congress feels that the officials are not listening to them, the MP should resign.

The tussle between UT Administrator and Pawan Bansal has been continuing for some time. A few months back, trouble arose when Mayor Pardeep Chhabra's name was not included in the list of invitees for the inauguration of the Solid Waste Management Plant

Heading: To discourage encroachment, MC to give new look to rehri markets - Indian Express
Content:
"Educating the masses is the only solution to check the growing number of AIDS patients."

This was stated by Atul Gupta, member of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Chandigarh Council and chief executive officer, Red Alkemi, while addressing an Infotainment Session on "Global Crisis — Local Action" organised by the CII on Friday.

The objective of the session was to spread awareness on Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) at the workplace, reduce stigma and discrimination and encourage blood donation.

Discussing CII's initiatives in the area, Gupta added that the Confederation of Indian Industry has taken on the mandate of catalysing the involvement of industries in India's social development agenda, particularly regarding AIDS.

Dr Suvir Saxena, deputy director, Blood Safety- State AIDS Control Society, said the focus is to galvanise awareness and support of the industry towards the issue.

Breaking the myth on blood donation, Dr Saxena said, "It is actually beneficial for the donor as new cells are formed after donation, which have better efficiency. There is no chance of acquiring any infection as single use needles attached to the blood bag are used."

A film based on the myths and misconceptions related to AIDS was also screened.

Heading: Ravinder gives in, says he sent no money - Indian Express
Content:
In A proposal mooted recently, the Municipal Corporation (MC) has decided to beautify the rehri markets across the city.

Officials say the main aim behind the drive will be to send out a clear message to the encroachers to steer clear the markets of choked bylanes and corridors. The proposal is a fresh attempt by the MC to remove encroachment from the rehri markets. Earlier, imposing fine, impounding goods and issuing challans to defaulters bore no fruit as encroachers returned soon after the drives ended.

In most of these markets, the corridors have been encroached upon. Due to this, the passages are choked and have space for only one person to pass at a time. Experts say the situation can prove dangerous in case of a fire as the encroachments leave no space for people to escape. There is also a danger for the fire to spread quickly. And above all, there is no space for fire tenders to enter.

Keeping these aspects in mind, a proposal was mooted during the meeting of the Fire and Emergency Services Committee. As per the proposal, the passages in the markets will be beautified and laid with tiles.

Additional Commissioner P K Sharma said: "The beautification drive will be carried out in a phased manner. A meeting was held with the presidents of the market associations recently, who were asked to voluntarily clear the passages for us to start work. The drive will start within the coming week. After this, it will be convenient for the people to shop."

M P S Chawla, chairman of the Fire and Emergency Services Committee, said the proposal is a positive approach to clear such corridors of encroachment. Whenever an encroachment drive is organised, shopkeepers offer resistance and feel that the enforcement staff is forcibly taking away their belongings, he said, hoping that since force failed to work, the novel idea might show results. Other members of the committee feel that the violations would be reduced substantially if the corridors are given a new look.

In the past few months, the Enforcement Wing has collected lakhs of rupees through anti-encroachment drives and challans. The results were not encouraging, however, as there was no substantial decrease in the number of encroachments.

Heading: Addiction is a way of life with city youth: survey - Indian Express
Content:
CASH at judge's door: Dramatic surrender surprises all: Will be in CBI remand till September 23

Evading arrest for more than a month in the cash-for-judge scam, Delhi hotelier Ravinder Singh surrendered before the Special Court of CBI Judge Jagdeep Jain on Friday. Giving a twist to the case, Ravinder flatly denied sending any money though Sanjeev Bansal, former Haryana Additional Advocate General, to be delivered at the house of any judge.

Ravinder's stand is at complete variance with that of the other accused arrested in the case — Sanjeev Bansal, Nirmal Singh, Parkash Ram and Rajiv Gupta. In their statements to the investigating agency, all four accused had said the money belonged to Ravinder.

His surrender, though looked well-planned, surprised everybody present in the court, including the judge. Ravinder had been reportedly roaming around in the District Courts complex since morning.

Minutes after the court had turned down his application for an identification parade, Ravinder offered to surrender. He was already sitting in the court along with his wife. The naib court (court assistant) was then asked to inform the CBI, which had no clue about the surrender. Its officials came to the court within 20 minutes.

Attired in a blue striped T-shirt and grey trousers, Ravinder was sporting a blue cap and not a turban. Sources said the application seeking permission to surrender before the Special Magistrate, CBI, in Delhi was a ploy to deviate the attention of the CBI so that he could quietly surrender in Chandigarh.

Appearing before the judge, Ravinder said the packet containing Rs 15 lakh in cash, which was wrongly delivered at the residence of Justice Nirmaljit Kaur, did not belong to him. He, however, admitted to close association with Bansal and Justice Nirmal Yadav. He was remanded in the custody of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) till September 23.

'I did not try to conceal identity, do I look clean shaven?'

Demanding police remand for 14 days, the CBI public prosecutor contended that the High Court had given Ravinder an opportunity to surrender, but he did not do so. Thus, he added, the interim relief given to him earlier, allowing the presence of Ravinder's counsel during his custodial interrogation, stood cancelled. In the September 5 order, the HC had also said in case Ravinder surrendered, he would not be subjected to third degree methods of interrogation.

The prosecutor requested the judge to record his observation that Ravinder had tried to conceal his identity by cutting his hair and beard. Both Ravinder and his counsel objected to the remark angrily. "Do I look clean shaven to you? I am not wearing a turban because I know you would have arrested me," said Ravinder, taking off his cap to show his hair was intact.

Contesting the police remand sought by the CBI, the defence counsel said since the final order of the High Court, dismissing Ravinder's anticipatory bail plea, did not make it clear as to whether the interim order stood cancelled, he should be awarded the interim relief.

Demanding 14 days' remand for Ravinder, the CBI took the plea that the motive and purpose of fabrication of documents by the accused was to be ascertained. Moreover, they needed to find out the nexus between Ravinder, other co-accused and higher members of judiciary, read the application filed by the CBI.

Counsel to remain present during interrogation

The CBI prosecutor added that Ravinder might have to be taken to Delhi in relation with the case. The judge said in case the two local counsel were not available there, a Delhi-based lawyer could meet Ravinder and remain present during the custodial interrogation.

The court also held that a medical examination of Ravinder would be done after every 48 hours. Ravinder, who has been a patient of diabetes for the last 17 years, requested the court that some medicines prescribed to him be made available to him in the custody, which was granted.

The court directed the CBI to conduct a medical examination of Ravinder Singh either in the Government Hospital-16 or at GMCH-32, by a doctor who was already on the panel of Director, Health Services.

The counsel for Ravinder Singh were allowed to remain present from 5 to 6 pm during custodial interrogation. They can also meet him between 6.30 and 7.30 pm.

Hotelier admits to close association with Bansal, judge

Taking to Newsline, Ravinder said he had known Sanjeev Bansal for the last seven years. He said he was introduced to Bansal through a common friend, Andy, in Sector 17, Chandigarh, at a function. Ravinder admitted to sharing close family ties with Justice Nirmal Yadav too for several years.

He denied any relation or acquaintance with Justice Nirmaljit Kaur, and preferred silence when asked if he knew more HC judges.

Corroborating Bansal's statements to the CBI, Ravinder confirmed that the two had lunch together in Delhi on August 13, the day the packet was delivered to Justice Kaur, but categorically denied sending any money to Chandigarh.

When confronted as to why Bansal was naming him, Ravinder said: "Sanjeev Bansal would know (that) better." Denying any role in the case, he said: "All allegations levelled against me are false. I am being implicated."

He, however, failed to give a convincing reply when asked as to why was he being targeted.

Ravinder said he had been in the hotel business and that of import-export for the last 15 years.

Heading: 20 mm: Season’s heaviest rain has city running for cover - Indian Express
Content:
Consumption of alcohol or drugs is indicative of maturity, feel nearly 53 per cent of youngsters living in the city. A recent survey conducted by Dr Avnish Jolly, resource person with UNAIDS India, Godwin Society and Theatre Age, found that only 2 per cent of the youth were aware of the potential addictive nature of painkillers, sleeping pills and cough syrups.

The survey was conducted on 500 youngsters in the city in the age group of 18 to 20 years.

The format of the survey was based on the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime.

Dr Jolly says: "Painkillers or sleeping pills are commonly available at home. Youngsters tend to consume these without realising that they can get addicted. Parental guidance is essential as they should check whether their child is consuming these medicines in excess."

As many as 82 per cent youngsters admitted in the survey that alcohol was being consumed by people in their age group.

The sample survey found that nearly 46.6 per cent youngsters took to drugs owing to a negative family environment, while around 28 per cent gave in to peer pressure and another 22 per cent saw addiction as a relief from boredom and stress.

In terms of de-addiction, the city youths were found to be under the grip of various misconceptions. Nearly 24 per cent youngsters feel de-addiction is not possible for women while there are others who believe that de-addiction is possible if the period of abuse is less than five years.

According to Dr Jolly, students feel that taking drugs is a way of life.

"A committee for drug abuse control at all levels is required to expedite drug elimination tasks, which should be carried out at home and in cooperation with the international community," he adds.

Heading: NIIFT student shoots self in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
The city experienced its wettest 12 hours of the season as rains that started on Thursday evening lashed the region till Friday morning.

"These weather conditions are likely to continue till the end of the month. The rainfall was above normal till the morning hours today and we are recording the afternoon and evening data to make a comparison," said a Met official.

With the department recording 20 mm rains from 8.30 pm on Thursday to 8.30 am on Friday, the temperature saw a dip of 6 degrees. The mercury plummeted to 23 degrees as compared to 29 on Thursday.

As a result of the incessant rains, the bridge at Bapu Dham collapsed in the evening, though no one was hurt in the incident.

Water entered some portions of the emergency area in PGI. Patients and their attendants at GMSH-16, bore the brunt as the registration counter and the emergency block remained under water.

"It rained very heavily and water entered some parts of the building. We are in the process of renovating the old building which will solve the problem of waterlogging," said a PGI spokesperson.

At the Government Model Senior Secondary School, students and teachers had a narrow escape as a portion of the roof collapsed around 11 am due to the heavy rains.

"Luckily, none of the students was sitting under that portion of the roof which collapsed," said a teacher.

Karamjit, a parent, told Newsline, "The authorities should look into the matter and take corrective measures as soon as possible."

Education Secretary Sanjay Kumar, meanwhile, said, "We will get the building inspected and take the required corrective measures."

Heading: Raninder to present file of atrocities on Congmen to Rahul - Indian Express
Content:
Mystery shrouds the death of a 25-year-old student who allegedly shot himself in Mohali on Thursday night. Police said Lovejot Singh, who was pursuing BSc in Fashion Technology from the Northern India Institute of Fashion Technology (NIIFT) in Mohali, used to keep weapons as he was "very fond of them".

The police did not confirm if it was an accidental firing or a suicide. They are also yet to ascertain whether the 9 mm pistol used in the shooting was licenced or not.

Harbir Singh, Station House Officer (SHO), Phase I, said the incident took place around 8.30 pm on Thursday. Lovejot was found dead in his Hyundai Verna outside his rented accommodation in Phase VI.

His father Pritpal Singh, who lives in Jalalabad in Ferozepur district, had come to meet his son on Thursday. Around 8.30 pm, he told the police, he asked Lovejot to bring the car inside the compound and park it. Standing on the balcony of Lovejot's first-floor accommodation, Pritpal said, he saw Lovejot going towards the car. He started watching television, but when Lovejot did not return even after half-an-hour, he went downstairs to find him lying in a pool of blood inside the car, the police said.

The SHO said a loaded pistol was recovered from the car. A single shot had been fired that had hit Lovejot on his left temple, piercing through his head.

During preliminary investigations, the police said, it was found that Lovejot was very fond of weapons, which he used to possess and kept changing from time to time.

A postmortem was conducted on Friday after which Pritpal took his son's body to Jalalabad for last rites, said the SHO.

The police said they were clueless about the reason or provocation behind the drastic step. Inquest proceedings under Section 174 of the CrPC have been initiated.

Heading: Irregularities alleged in lecturers’ selection - Indian Express
Content:
Crying hoarse over the alleged vendetta by the SAD (B) in Punjab ever since there was a change of guard in February 2007, the Punjab Congress is getting ready to take the fight against "atrocities on workers" to the Centre through MP Rahul Gandhi.

In a press conference held here today to spell out the objective and itinerary of Rahul's Punjab visit, Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) general secretary Raninder Singh said a heap of files on atrocities on Congress workers would be placed before Rahul Gandhi. "Forty-eight Congress workers were murdered, of which 11 were from Bathinda. We will present their children and family members before him," said son of former Punjab CM Capt Amarinder Singh. Accusing the law and order machinery in the state of not listening to the grievances of Congress workers, Raninder, who was flanked by Indian Youth Congress president Ashok Tanwar, Talwandi Sabo MLA Jeet Mohinder Singh Sidhu and Punjab Youth Congress president Vijay Inder Singla, said IPS officers should not forget that they were under the Ministry of Home Affairs and it was the Congress-led UPA that was at the helm of affairs at the Centre.

Tanwar said Rahul would boost the morale of the Congress workers. He highlighted the case of Congress supporter Ranjit Sharma of Jalal village in this district who was allegedly beaten up by some Akali activists yesterday and sustained injuries.

About selecting people for the cadre, Tanwar said Punjab was chosen as a model state, as its youth were dynamic.

Heading: Facing corruption? Log on to MLA’s website - Indian Express
Content:
Irregularities have been alleged in the appointment of lecturers at Government M R College, Fazilka, as guest faculty.

A resident, M L Baghla, in his complaint to the DPI (Colleges), alleged that in gross violation of the Punjab Civil Service Rules, 1994, some less qualified candidates were appointed on August 12.

"In case of physical education and Punjabi lecturers, candidates who had passed UGC National Eligibility Test were ignored, while others were selected," alleged Baghla. The lecturer appointed for English has not even qualified Punjabi test in class X, which is a pre-requisite, Baghla said, adding that for a history lecturer's post, a candidate with UGC-NET and 12 years of experience was overlooked.

"When I asked for records of appointment under the RTI Act, the college provided information on August 20 sans details of the application of the candidates. But later, when the same record was provided in response to another application on September 5, details were provided. This implies that the record was tampered with," said the letter.

When contacted, principal of the college Kulbir Singh said, "We had set certain criteria for selection. There is no question of any partiality. This is an effort to malign the image of the college."

Heading: One sentenced to death for killing wife, two kids - Indian Express
Content:
Is corruption the most important issue affecting the common man in Punjab? Asks Qila Raipur MLA's website, www.saveourpunjab.com, which is an e-redressal centre for complaints regarding corruption in government departments.

MLA Jassi Khangura said, "This site was launched last week and I am sure that it will get popular within few weeks. In the assembly session, I had asked the Chief Minister whether his government has any proposal to receive confidential information by phone, post, internet or e-mail from government employees and the public who wish to report acts of corruption. But the question was disallowed. So, I decided to create my own website."

"Whatever complaints we will receive, will be forwarded to the department concerned. We will post complaints on our website after scrutinising the contents," he said.

However, Khangura kept mum when asked whether he would post complaints of his party's ministers also on the site. He claimed that his e-complaint centre would become a big hit during the Lok Sabha election season.

Heading: Indian politicians tog up in Pak designs - Indian Express
Content:
A man was here today sentenced to death by the court of District and Sessions Judge Gurdev Singh for killing his wife and two children on September 21 last year.

The convict, Tarsem Singh, in an effort to project the deaths as an accident, had set his own house on fire after killing his wife Binder Kaur (32) and two sons Gurvinder (10) and Parwinder (8). Tarsem had also got injured in the fire and was admitted to the Civil Hospital. The villagers had informed about the incident to the police, who smelled a rat after examining the spot.

During the interrogation, he had confessed to having murdered the three in a fit of rage over a petty domestic row.

Heading: Hearing on Jagjit’s bail plea on Monday - Indian Express
Content:
The chic clique that walks the corridors of power in India gets its wardrobe from Pakistan. The Indian politicians form the major part of the clientele of Pakistani designers, who eye the country as a prospective market.

In the past one year, many designers have made frequent trips to the metros of India, especially Delhi. Hina Anjum, who claimed that she was flooded with orders from politicians in Delhi, has made over four business trips to India in the past six months, focusing mainly on Delhi and Punjab.

Though she talks excitedly about the offers, she prefers not to disclose the identities of the clients. "It is a professional secret. But I have to admit that I have got maximum response from politicians," she said.

She said the orders that she had received during her recent exhibition in Delhi outnumbered what she received in two months. "I have been flooded with offers of designer suits, especially those that can be given away as gifts," she said, adding that Pakistani fabric was not only attractive, but also durable.

She said trade exchanges could help build strong bridges of trust between India and Pakistan. Among other top Pakistani designers who have visited India include Asiya Malik and Nadiya Lakdawala.

Heading: Illegal sale of wheat seed goes on unabated - Indian Express
Content: The hearing on the bail application of former local bodies minister Chaudhary Jagjit Singh in the case of illegal construction on public land at Kitchlu Chowk would be held on September 22 in the court of Additional Sessions Judge NK Gaur.  The Vigilance Bureau had booked Chaudhary Jagjit Singh, former assembly Deputy Speaker Darbari Lal, his two sons and an executive engineer of Patiala Municipal Corporation, besides others, on charges of violating the norms for registration of 633-square-yard plot and its land-use change.

Heading: Capt to return on Monday, will attend Rampura Phul rally - Indian Express
Content:
Illegal sale of the much-in-demand PBW 550 variety of wheat seed by private sellers is going on unchecked right under the nose of the government authorities. On paper, however, the seed is available only with PAU, Punseed and the Department of Agriculture.

Released by PAU at the recent kissan mela here, the seed is still in multiplication stage and has not been given to any private dealers, as that the state has only 20,000 quintal of the seed at its disposal, sources said. But the ground reality is that private seed dealers, operating outside PAU, are selling the seed openly and the officials of the Department of Agriculture are doing little about this.

The dealers are, in fact, selling the seed at double the price. "PAU is charging Rs 800 per kilogram, while private sellers are making a killing at Rs 1,600," complained Kuljit Singh, a farmer.

Another farmer, Hardeep Singh, said, "The seed sellers are not providing any invoice or bill. We are forced to buy the seed from them as PAU does not have enough and we have to stand in long queues to get it."

When contacted, Yadwinder Singh Chhinna, District Chief Agriculture Officer, denied any such illegal sale.

When told that banners inviting buyers were dotting the Ferozepur Road, Chhinna said, "We saw the banners and talked to a few sellers. They told us that they are simply advertising the new variety for the benefit of the farmers."

Heading: Patiala segment: Is Rakhra SAD choice? - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Congress has put efforts in top gear for the Rampura Phul rally, which will be addressed by Rahul Gandhi on September 22.

Former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh is expected to return from the UK on Monday and participate in the rally, sources said. For the Congress, Rahul's visit will sound the bugle for the parliamentary polls, though it has been planned to boost the membership drive of the party, which will eventually lead to the election of the new body of the Youth Congress.

Vijay Inder Singla, president of the Punjab Youth Congress, said, "This is the first time that the organisation elections are being held for the Youth Congress. Prior to this, the post was nominated. Punjab is the first place to have democratic system of electing youth leaders," Singla said.

Besides, this will be the first show of strength by the Congress which will see the party's "iconic" youth leader sharing stage with Amarinder after he was made chairman of the election campaign committee.

Congress MLA Jeet Mohinder Singh said, "People from all over the state are expected to turn up."

As per the schedule, Rahul is expected to tour various areas in Punjab, including Mohali, Patiala, Mansa, Bathinda, Gidderbaha, Gurdaspur, Jaito and Amritsar, for three days, Jeet Mohinder said. The Congress has chosen Bathinda as the venue for the rally, for there have been talks that MP Sukhbir Badal will contest from here.

Recently, Amarinder had organised a rally in Chief Minister's home constituency Lambi.

Legal tangle

The expulsion of former Chief Minister Capt Amarinder Singh from the state assembly might kick off a new legal debate. Amarinder's Delhi-based counsel Atul Nanda today said the Election Commission of India (ECI) may question the Patiala by-election since the resolution of unseating the former CM does not mention a breach of privilege. "Till the court decides the matter, I feel the ECI will not interfere."

The ECI has maintained that the Vidhan Sabha has the powers to expel an MLA and the commission has to hold the by-election unless stayed by the court, after the seat is declared vacant. What is now being debated is that if the court stays Amarinder's expulsion after he or someone else gets elected in the by-election, a situation could arise wherein the Patiala Assembly seat will have two MLAs. Jeet Mohinder Singh said, "It's a constitutional matter which requires deliberation by legal experts, the process of which is already on."

Heading: On way to Nanded, one pilgrim killed, 21 injured - Indian Express
Content:
In the run-up to the polls, former SAD MLA from Samana Surjit Singh Rakhra is taking the credit for getting funds for the city by apprising Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal of the dilapidated infrastructure.

Sources said he may be the SAD face for the Patiala by-poll. However, former MP Prem Singh Chandumajra is also in the list of the candidates who can challenge the might of the Congress in the royal town.

Sources said Rakhra was close to Badal and has the support of traders.

Over 20 councillors from the city, including SAD district president Indermohan Singh Bajaj and Patiala Deputy Mayor Anil Bajaj, today attended a function to thank Rakhra for bringing grants to the city. "I was perturbed to see Patiala neglected, so I asked Badal to come to the city and hear the grievances of the people," he told The Indian Express. "I am not doing this to get a SAD ticket. Besides, such decisions are taken by the party," he added. He, however, said, "Badal sahib had asked me to fight the coming Lok Sabha polls from Delhi, but I want to work for the state."

Heading: Baba Sheikh Farid fest starts - Indian Express
Content: A pilgrim was killed and 21 others injured when a truck ran over them near Kankar on the Agra-Mumbai National Highway on Friday, the police said. The mishap occurred in the wee hours when about 500 Sikh pilgrims were going to Nanded from Fatehgarh Sahib on foot and were hit by a speeding truck. The deceased has been identified as Harpreet Singh (35) of Ludhiana. The condition of the five injured was stated to be serious, and they have been admitted to the district hospital here, the police said, adding that the truck has been impounded and the probe was on.

Heading: Grievance panel meet sees chaos, protests - Indian Express
Content:
The 23rd Baba Sheikh Farid Aagman Purb, a five-day festival showcasing heritage, commenced today at Gurdwara Tilla Baba Farid with the recitation of Sri Sukhmani Sahib.

On the occasion, a blood donation camp was organised by an NSS unit in cooperation with Sahara Club and State Bank of India at Government Brijindra College. Faridkot Deputy Commissioner VK Meena, who inaugurated the camp, said the donors would be honoured in a special district-level function. The Aagman Purb Baba Farid Arts Society also organised a state-level painting workshop and exhibition in Sanjeevani Hall of the college. Tournaments of cricket, hockey, football, basketball, handball and volleyball also started today. A body-building championship was also held. A three-day Punjabi drama festival also kicked off.

Heading: BJP, INLD get closer, pact for LS polls likely - Indian Express
Content:
Vandalism and chaos, followed by slogan-raising, marred the functioning of the grievances committee, formed under Haryana Health Minister Kartar Devi, to redress a land dispute pending for the past couple of months. Residents of Dhani Mohabbatpur, which falls under the Adampur Assembly constituency, got angry over the delay in the solution of a dispute over panchayat land. The one-kanal land, which links the village to the adjoining village Darola, has allegedly been encroached upon by relatives of Bhattu Kalan MLA Kulbir Benewala.

The villagers, numbering around 100, raised slogans against the district administration for its failure in freeing the passage from the possession of encroachers even after directions were issued to this effect by the Punjab and Haryana High Court. They alleged that the administration was favouring the relatives of the MLA and was intentionally delaying the implementation of the Court's orders.

The BDPO, Rajesh Koth, who was supposed to get the possession of land from the encroachers, said that standing crop on the land in question was stopping the authorities.Deputy Commissioner O P Sheoran's assurance of getting the land free from encroachments too failed to pacify the agitating villagers following which, police force was deployed. The protesting villagers were then forcefully taken away by the police personnel. The whole drama continued for an hour.

Heading: State to be dotted with agro malls, Gurgaon next - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP and the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) seem to be veering towards each other for an alliance. INLD supremo and former chief minister Om Prakash Chautala gave an indication to this effect when on the invitation of BJP MP Navjot Singh Sidhu the other day, he attended a special film show of "Mera Pind My Home" in the presence of top BJP leaders L.K. Advani, Rajnath Singh and Sushma Swaraj. Chautala is also reported to be in touch with BJP leaders in the past.

However, none of the parties has yet made up its mind on the alliance issue since they are also weighing other options, such as a possible pact with the BSP or the Haryana Janhit Congress (BL).

One thing is certain though. Despite all its bravado and talks of the past, the BJP is not going to contest the next Lok Sabha elections alone.

Having seen the damning result in the three byelections, the party high command now seems to be clearly in favour of an alliance, possibly with the INLD.

The working committee of the Haryana BJP will meet in Sonepat on September 26 to discuss the current political and law and order situation in the state.

Former BJP president Venkaiah Naidu, in charge of party affairs in Haryana Vijay Goel, and joint in charge Harjit Singh Grewal will also take part in the meeting, according to a senior leader of the party.

"In this meeting, the party will also not just discuss holding of the BJP's sankalp rally in Ambala on October 8, but also mull the issue of a pre and post-poll alliance with other political parties for the forthcoming Lok Sabha and Assembly elections in the state,'' said the BJP leader.

The BJP is divided over seeking support from the INLD or some other party. Krishan Pal Gurjar, Rattanlal Kataria and Sudha Yadav seem to be in favour of the BJP, while BJP state president Atam Prakash Manchanda and Ram Bilas Sharma seem to favour the Kuldeep Bishnoi's Haryana Janhit Congress.

According to sources, BJP's high command is in favour of an alliance with the INLD despite the BJP's bitter experience in the past. The INLD is keeping its cards close to its chest for the time being.

Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, however, pooh-poohed the possibility of a coalition between the INLD and the BJP. "Many a time they have joined hands and then parted company.

They neither have any interest in development of the state, nor the welfare of the people,'' said Hooda.

Heading: 29 cases of power theft detected - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board (HSAMB) has decided to set up air-conditioned agro malls for the sale of all kinds of agricultural based products, food products and other allied products at various places in the state. To be developed on the pattern of international supermarkets, two such malls have already been launched at Panchkula and Karnal.

Disclosing this here today, Haryana Agriculture Minister H S Chatha said the board had also approved an agro mall at Gurgaon to be set up over an area of approximately 4.7 acre, at an estimated cost of Rs 44.85 crore. The construction work of this proposed mall would be started shortly, he said.

The specialty of the agro mall would be to lay special emphasis on organic food and direct marketing of agriculture products from farmers by the sellers.

The mall would be fed regularly by a chain providing grading, sorting, packaging and ripening facilities, which would be located in the newly developed vegetable market in Gurgaon.

Heading: Heavy rain disrupts life across state - Indian Express
Content:
Intensifying its campaign to curb the pilferage of power, the Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam has detected 29 cases of theft of power Yamunanagar district and for the first time, 100 per cent of the penalty amount has been recovered from the erring consumers.

Giving details, a spokesman said here today that the teams constituted by the Nigam conducted surprise checking of 1,231 consumer premises in Yamunanagar, Jagadhri and Naraingarh and found 26 domestic, one non-domestic and two AP tubewell consumers stealing power.

In most of the cases, the metres were found tampered with, he said.

A penalty of Rs. 5.61 lakh had been imposed on the erring consumers and the full amount has been recovered from them after serving them the required notices. The connections of these consumers have also been disconnected by the nigam.

Heading: Protesters against Una SEZ storm meet in Shimla - Indian Express
Content:
The heavy rain spell that started since Thursday evening has disrupted normal life throughout the state. Though all major highways across the state remained open for traffic till today evening, many link roads were closed down due to landslides and fallen trees.

The most affected have been the apple growers of Kinnaur district. The movement of apples had just started from here in the beginning of this week, but with the NH 22 getting blocked at various points due to landslides beyond Wangtoo and the road leading to Pooh sub-division being cut off for vehicular traffic near Spillo, the transportation has come to a halt.

The cold wave has also intensified with snowfall on higher reaches. Kinnaur today received fresh snowfall, with Chitkul and Masterang receiving three to six inches of snow.

In Shimla, four deodar trees fell near the high-security Raj Bhawan, besides landslides at various points.

Kinnaur Deputy Commissioner P.S. Draik said NH-22 was blocked at Powari due to a landslide and traffic could only be restored by Saturday morning. He added that the movement of apple-laden trucks was not very heavy so far.

During the past 24 hours, Arki in Solan district received the heaviest rainfall of 152.7 mm, Shimla received 42.8 mm and Sangla in Kinnaur received 62 mm rain.

The met department's forecast for the next 24 hours also warns of heavy rainfall at many places. Director of the met department Manmohan Singh said the weather is expected to clear up after September 22, but till then higher reaches would continue to get snowfall and the lower hills would receive heavy rainfall accompanied with strong velocity winds.

Heading: IT services to get people-friendly - Indian Express
Content:
"The Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in the present scenario would reverse what was achieved over decades through implementation of land reforms to re-distribute over two million hectare of land to the landless." A national conference on economic and social perspectives of SEZs at Indian Institute of Advanced Study (IIAS), Shimla, opened on Thursday morning with this statement made by president of Indian Academy of Social Sciences, Allahabad, S.P. Shukla.

By evening, the academicians got an opportunity to get a first-hand account of threats to people facing displacement through SEZs when a group of people who are agitating against the proposed SEZ at Gagret in Una talked to them through the same platform.

Narender Parmar, legal advisor of Matribhumi Sangharsh Samiti of Una, said the government was not presenting a true picture about the number of farmers who would be displaced by the proposed SEZ of SKIL Infrastructure Limited.

"We have sought information under the Right to Information in which it is clearly mentioned that the SEZ and airport proposed in Una would require 11.5 thousand acres of land, whereas the survey has only been done of 4,000 acres," said Parmar.

Heading: ‘Hard work, focus and determination go hand in hand’ - Indian Express
Content:
Himachal Pradesh, the state with highest tele-density and optical fibre cable (OFC) cris-crossing its length and width, is all set to take a new leap forward in the information technology (IT) sector to offer web-based services to its citizens.

At a summit of IT investors and leading professionals, Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal rolled out his vision of making Himachal an IT hub, both by attracting new investors and also by providing IT-based services to its 65 lakh citizens.

Dhumal said, "The Himachal government is exploring possibilities of creating a citizen-based repository of database to deliver them all government services on web. There is a plan to provide every citizen a unique ID code and linking every department for sharing the database. This will also enable the government in better planning and monitoring of the schemes, beside offering citizens easy access to government e-services."

The day-long summit -- IT@Himachal 2008 -- organised by Wisitex Foundation in collaboration with the state's IT department, was addressed among others by Nash Narasimhan of Hewlett and Packard; Vinnie Mehta,

Executive Director of Manufacturers' Association of Information Technology, and B.K. Aggarwal, Secretary, IT, Himachal.

In 2001,Himachal had started "Lok Mitra" Kendras on pilot basis in Hamirpur.To extend the same concept further, the state is in the process of setting up 3,366 Common Service Centres all over the state.At least one such centre is proposed in each gram panchayat in association with private players.

Responding to Vinnie Mehta's offer to woo some of the leading foreign IT players who are moving out of China, the Chief Minister said he has already given the necessary instructions to Aggarwal to tie-up with Mehta for facilitating foreign investments in the IT sector.

Dhumal said the state provides an ideal environment for the IT sector as it has been amongst the leader states to set up statewide area network. The focus, however, has been on taking IT services to the people.

Vinnie Mehta also raised the issue of e-disposal and advised the government to frame a policy on e-disposal as part of e-procurements, wherein the company should be asked to handle safe disposal of the e-waste.

At this, Subhashish Panda, Director, IT, said the policy is already under formulation and will soon be finalised. Himachal has been a pioneer on environmental issues and this aspect has already been taken care of, he said.

Heading: 2 yrs on, multi-level parking project fails to take off - Indian Express
Content:
For Arshmeet Singh, a Class IX student of KBDAV, success comes easy if one is determined and focused in life. An all-rounder in the true sense of the term, Arshmeet says he takes life as it comes and believes that hard work, focus and determination go hand-in-hand.

After winning laurels for his performances in badminton championships, Arshmeet is busy playing for the under-sixteen badminton open tournament at the state-level.

Besides sports, Arshmeet has done well in academics as well. In Class VIII, he secured the second position in the city by securing 96 per cent in the final examinations.

Arshmeet's biggest motivation in life is his family and he maintains that it is because of their support that he has been able to achieve whatever he has till now.

Besides badminton, Arshmeet is passionate about dancing and singing, which he says he enjoys the most.

Talking to Newsline, Arshmeet said: "Badminton requires a lot of concentration. To focus and keep myself free of stress, I take lessons in dancing and singing to help me feel refreshed."

What further makes Arshmeet popular in the school is his willingness to participate in every tournament — be it at the school-level or the inter-school level. In future, Arshmeet aims to join IIT and become an engineer like his parents.

"There are times when one really feels low and thinks that nothing is going right in life. But these are the times which make one tough and a better person," he says.

His final take on life — Do not give up and strive hard till you get what you want in life.

Heading: Movie Reviews - Indian Express
Content:
The Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh had proposed a multi-level parking lot in Sector 17 around two years ago, looking at the increasing problems of parking in the area. While the problem has now assumed almost alarming proportions, the project is yet to see the light of day.

Not only Sector 17, with the number of vehicles increasing by the day, lack of parking space is one of the biggest problems in all sectors. Though paid parking lots are being increased and proposals are being studied to tackle the problem, the measures are not proving adequate.

The plan to build a multi-level parking in Sector 17 has not even been approved yet.

The project plan, with a provision for parking of 1,200 cars, submitted by a Delhi-based company had been rejected, as it did not conform to the bylaws. According to the plan, there were three storeys for basement parking and one for surface parking. There would have been two more storeys for commercial activity, with shops and a food court.

The Administration has recently asked the Delhi-based company to submit plans according to new terms and conditions.

While it is yet to be seen what the new plan will hold, the MC has planned to construct additional parking lots to ease the chaos at present. The work will be started in full swing after the rains.

With Sector 17 being the hub of commercial activities, the area sees a large number of vehicles. A multi-level parking is expected to solve the problem of parking to a great extent.

"The final plan for the multi-level parking lot is yet to be approved. Once that is done, it will take another two years for the parking to become functional. It will ease the congestion in the market," says an MC official.

Heading: Heavy rain in Patiala, part of historic gate crumbles - Indian Express
Content:
Welcome to Sajjanpur

CAST: Shreyas Talpade, Amrita Rao, Divya Dutta, Yashpal Sharma, Ravi Kissan, Rajeshwari Sachdev, Ila Arun

DIRECTOR: Shyam Benegal

Welcome to the return of Shyam Benegal. The director, who's been meandering for some time with stodgy biopics and moral science lessons, is back doing what he is best at: creating life-like characters to tell life-like stories.

Sajjanpur is a modern-day, hovering-on-the-edge-of-prosperity Indian 'gaon', where 'bijli' and 'pani' have made inroads, as well as 'kutcha' roads and rattling buses. But illiteracy is still rampant. Which is why Mahadev (Shreyas), the village's only 'padha likha' young fellow, hangs up a shingle under a 'bargad' tree, and makes a living writing letters. And reading them out, also for a charge.

All kinds of people wash up under that tree: a loony aunt (Ila Arun) worrying about her 'manglik' niece (Divya), a lovelorn wife (Amrita) waiting to hear from her husband, away for four years in Bambai, a local 'neta' (Yashpal) who can easily pass off as a goon, a compounder (Ravi) in love with a pretty widow (Rajeshwari).

Welcome to Sajjanpur stays quirky and engaging even when the pace flags, and the rural accents turns faux, because of the felt screenplay and superbly robust, earthy dialogues by Ashok Mishra (this is a U/A film). The fact that the village is really a set is evident too, but you overlook it all when you see how skilfully Benegal brings up the ills that beset us still, after all these years. If a girl is unlucky, marry her off to a dog. If a eunuch stands for election, get rid of her.

But none of these 'issues' are in your face, and the film is saved from becoming the sort of dreaded preachy treatises that the director has been delivering of late. And a large part of that has to do with Shreyas Talpade, who wears his writer-of-letters-and-arbiter-of-lives role like a second skin: comforter of the lonely wife, his thoughts lead him astray, but his heart stays steadfast. But the real hero of the film is the village and the way it melds the past and the present: the profusion of all the Rams (Ram Ashrey, Ram Khilavan, Ram Singh), the references to Sita, and 'Kalyug', as well as the acknowledgment that a cell phone text message is also a letter!

The village had all but disappeared from Hindi cinema. Welcome to Sajjanpur.

Hulla

CAST: Sushant Singh, Rajat Kapoor,

Kartika Rane, Vrajesh Hirjee

DIRECTOR: Jaideep Varma

This is the week of the small film doing big things. Hulla, directed by debutant Jaideep Varma, is another welcome step towards getting back to celluloid centre-stage real people, real motives and real problems.

Smart broker Raj (Sushant) moves in with his wife Abha (Kartika) to a far-flung but nice suburban housing society. That's not enough for her South Mumbai parents, but she's fine till he's fine. And then one fine day, he's not. The building's night watchman whistles too loudly. Raj can't sleep. He petitions the society's self-important secretary Janardhan (Rajat) to get the fellow to stop. He acquires dark circles and a pounding head. He tries explaining his troubles to a colleague and friend (Vrajesh), to his irate boss, to a cop at the local police station, to anyone who will listen. And finds only noise.

Hulla reminds you of the middle-of-the-road cinema that lit up the 70s: it has a very Sai Paranjpye-ish feel to it. The plot's simple. But the treatment makes it a whimsical, affectionate study of people. As they are, and as they'd like others to see them. The film does slow down in the second half, and gets a tad repetitive, but keeps you with it.

And it brings to your attention the actors who never get their due in today's mainstream cinema. Kartika is fresh and perky. Sushant Singh is very good. But the real surprise in this package is Rajat Kapoor, who delivers a pitch-perfect performance as a man whose identity depends upon his designation, on what he can paint on his entrance plate below his name.

Jaideep Varma took many years to get this one out. His second should be sooner.

Saas Bahu Aur Sensex

CAST: Kirron Kher, Farooq Sheikh, Tanushree Dutta, Ankur Khanna, Lilette Dubey, Masumeh

DIRECTOR: Shona Urvashi

Can women understand the complex world of finance, stocks and shares, and the Sensex? Or should they be confined to watching 'saas bahu' serials?

Shona Urvashi's second film has a whopper of an idea. And stalwarts fronting it. Kirron Kher is the divorced, desperately-in-need-of-money Binita Sen, who lands up at the door of Feroz Sethna, an eccentric out-of-work stock broker (Farooq Sheikh). He is rude and brusque. She is angry and annoyed. And then it turns into a profitable partnership, professional and personal.

The interplay between these two consummate actors could have taken Warner Brothers' first Indian production Saas Bahu Aur Sensex to an interesting place. But the director sends out confusing signals by gathering up a bunch of kitty-party aunties, converting them from couch potatoes to eager Economic Times-reading stock hounds, and then letting them slip, and lose money. What is she trying to say: can they or can't they? "Aaj sharad purnima hai, aaj toh Sensex zaroor upar jayega", intones Mrs Sen. Leaving the irascible Mr Sethna beaming, and, horrors, agreeing.

So is greed good? Mrs Sen, who's been picking up all the rising stocks unerringly, suddenly becomes all over-pious, and rants on about the evils of wanting to make money. Huh? In between, youngsters working on today's jobs crop up. Tanushree and Ankur are call centre execs, refining their Yank accents. Masumeh is a femme fatale, who wants 'moneh', not love.

In the end, it's so all-over-the place and indeterminate that you couldn't be bothered. What makes up for the rest is watching the inimitable Farooq in a full-fledged role, and Kirron as a non-stereotyped Bollywood mom, both after a long time.

Heading: Bull murder: MC strike on, ultimatum on snapping power, water supply deferred - Indian Express
Content:
Heavy rainfall in Patiala for the last two days has severely hit normal life. The impact has been so bad that the Sunami Gate near Modi College collapsed today. There were also reports of some minor breaches near Patran, resulting in water entering fields.

While various residential colonies struggled to drain out excess water, business remained shut across the city due to heavy rainfall.

A part of the historical Sunami Gate crumbled days after the Municipal Corporation passed a resolution to demolish the structure. The decision was taken despite the fact that the state government and the Patiala administration had decided to conserve heritage buildings of the city.

"The MC House had passed a resolution to demolish of the gate after Mayor Ajit Pal Singh Kohli claimed it to be unsafe. A section of the media had criticised the mayor for deciding in favour of the demolition and the plan had to be postponed," deputy mayor Anil Bajaj said.

Meanwhile, Mayor Kohli visited various parts of the city to take stock of the flood-like situation. "The former government did not do anything and instead covered all the nullahs, resulting in waterlogging," he said.

"The sewage water entered houses in the low-lying areas of the city. The government is sleeping over the situation and not taking any steps," angry residents told Newsline.

"The whole area is under water and if it rains in the night, we would have to shift to the first floor of our house," said a resident of Model Town area.

Meanwhile, incessant rain has thrown life out of gear in Mohali and Kharar as well. With several areas inundated and water entering into houses and shops, the link roads to certain villages in the district were also snapped on Friday. No loss of life or property due to heavy downpour was yet confirmed.

The rain, which started on Thursday morning, was continuing till the filing of this report on Friday night.

To avert any possible loss arising out of heavy downpour, the state government has asked all the Deputy Commissioners, Senior Superintendents of Police and Sub-Divisional Magistrate to remain in their respective headquarters and monitor the situation in the respective jurisdictions.

The situation in several villages like Dharak, Majat, Landran, Santemajra, Chapparchiri, Nawanshaher, Badala, Desumajra, Bhagomajra and Balongi was alarming with reports of major parts of the link roads being under knee-deep water. Even the concrete roofs of several houses could be seen leaking.

The potholed roads in Mohali and Kharar besides the cracked patches of the busy NH-21 gave a tough time to motorists as vehicles were trapped in deep potholes becoming invisible with the filling of water. The standing water in the markets of Ambala City also damaged a large portion of the paddy lying in the open. – With inputs from Mohali, Kharar and Ambala

Heading: ‘No ration card, no LPG’ in Parwanoo - Indian Express
Content:
In protest against the FIR registered against their men following the death of a stray bull in Mohali on Wednesday, the employees of the Mohali Municipal Council (MC) continued their indefinite strike on the second consecutive day on Friday.

Hundreds of MC employees staged a dharna outside the MC office in Sector 68 and denied public entry to the office. In the evening, a delegation of the MC Employees Union went to meet Deputy Commissioner Rahul Bhandari, who was, however, not available.

They later met Additional Deputy Commissioner Jaspal Mittal, who bought time till Monday for the fulfillment of their demands. The protestors called upon SP (City) Varinder Pal Singh, who was entrusted with the investigation in the case, and demanded the cancellation of the FIR against them.

The agitating civic staffers, however, deferred the ultimatum to snap the power and water supply in the entire city till Monday. They had threatened on Thursday to suspend emergency services in Mohali from Saturday if the FIR registered against the MC employees was not cancelled today and the residents of Lambian village, whom they accused of assaulting the MC staffers and obstructing them from discharging duty, were not arrested.

"On the assurance of the ADC, the agitating employees decided to wait till Monday but if till then the FIR is not cancelled and those accused of assault are not arrested, all the employees of the government departments in Mohali will strike and suspend essential public services like supply of power, water and cleanliness services," said municipal councillor Harman Preet Singh.

Payal Sodhi, founder trustee of the Chandigarh chapter of People for Animals (PFA), has meanwhile sought appointment from the deputy commissioner to press for their demand to arrest the MC employees accused of the bull's murder.

Heading: Karva Chauth gift for jailbirds: no bar on meeting wives - Indian Express
Content:
Severe shortage of LPG cylinders has been reported in Parwanoo with gas agencies stating that only ration card holders will be given refill cylinders. The Vikas Gas Agency of Indian Oil even presented an order issued by the Director, Food and Civil Supply, Himachal Pradesh dated August 6.

This new rule has created panic among the residents. Inderjeet Singh, a resident of Sector 4, said he has been living in the town for the last 15 years but does not possess a ration card. "How will I run my household now," he asks.

Deputy Director, Food and Civil Supply, Liak Ram said the rule has been misinterpreted. "The consumers will have to provide proof of residence, whether a ration card or another document. Our aim is to ensure that customers' LPG is not be used for commercial purposes."

Heading: Jalandhar Mail - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government is determined to rehabilitate criminals lodged in jails across the state, said Jails Minister Hira Singh Gabria on Friday.

Addressing the media at the SAS Nagar Press Club, Gabria said special initiatives were being taken to make jail inmates good citizens during their stay behind bars.

For the purpose, he said, discourses of different religious leaders and yoga camps were being held inside the jails. Special arrangements have also been made for the live telecast of Gurta Gaddi Diwas in jails from October 29 to November 3.

For the first time ever, the inmates will be free to meet their wives inside the jails on karva chauth from 9 am to 6 pm.

"We intend to help women whose husbands are behind the bars. Our aim is to change the notion that jail inmates can only be punished," said the Jails Minister.

Gabria, who also holds the Tourism, Cultural Affairs, Printing and Stationery portfolios, said besides creating three new jails in Nabha, Faridkot and Kapurthala with the capacity of 2,500-3,000 inmates each, Rs 201 crore would be spent to enhance the capacity of 4,000 inmates each at the existing jails besides providing better facilities for the inmates.

Regarding the fire incident in Central Jail in Amritsar on August 28 wherein the Nihang chief of Taruna Dal Ajit Singh Poohla was allegedly burnt alive, the Jails Minister said that the departmental inquiry into the case was complete and the judicial probe was on to find out the reasons and nab the culprit.

"We will not spare anybody found guilty in the case," he said.

Gabria said after the Amritsar incident, he was inspecting all the jails in the state personally to address the problems and demands of the inmates. The Minister also announced Rs 1 lakh for the building of the Press Club. Later, the Press Club office-bearers honoured Gabria with a memento.

Heading: Reel success - Indian Express
Content:
A new show on television brings in a truckload of stars to the city. There's veteran actor Ranjeet dropping his mean streak, Rakhi Sawant's boyfriend making an identity, Baba Sehgal doing what he's best at....JAGMEETA THIND JOYbrings a roundup

Till now all the joint families that you've probably caught on television have a) squabbling mother-in-laws b) forever plotting daughter-in-laws c) basically, a lot of unpleasantness. In an effort to make the audience out there less skeptical about joint set-ups, SAB TV has brought in the Bhalla parivaar. This is one happy Punjabi family from Jalandhar complete with the Bauji, his bossy-yet-affable wife and a couple of doting sons and their better-halves. Coming from the Tony and Deeya Singh stable (the makers of Left Right Left, Jassi Jaisi Koi Nahin), the show 'Jugni Chali Jalandhar' is being pegged as a one of a kind comedy soap which stars a couple of veterans alongside a bunch of new comers. There's veteran actor Ranjeet and Alka Sachdev as the elders, Baba Sehgal and Rakhi Sawant's down-to-earth boyfriend Abhishek Avasthi as the sons and newcomer Karan Godwan and Muskan Mehani as the love-struck couple. Quite like the downpour we had on Friday, these stars poured in the city along with the biggies from the channel. Here's a who-said-what of it all.

* MEAN NO MORE: Minus a few giveaways on his face that show he's aged, veteran actor Ranjeet looks exactly like how we've seen him onscreen. "Only now I am not running after a woman trying to molest her," the actor laughs in his stride. Having played the really bad man in films, Ranjeet has turned a new leaf with his foray into television. "The concept really appealed to me and that's what got me to sign up. As far as acting goes, I don't find any difference in the two mediums," says the actor who plays the Punjabi patriarch who doesn't like educated women! "Otherwise I have no such issues," he laughs. On a more serious note, he's not yet doing a Bollywood flick for "I am not ready to do tit-bit roles." But there's a movie in the pipeline and he's the one directing it.

* STEPPING OUT OF THE SHADOWS: Even though Abhishek Avasthi brought home the ZEE Cinestars Ki Khoj title, it's taken him long to find his feet as an actor in the industry. The fact that he's Rakhi Sawant's boyfriend has much to do with it. "I think I have had my share of dance shows and I now want to concentrate on my acting career," admits Avasthi who plays a brawny Maninder Bhalla on 'Jugni Chali Jalandhar'. And unlike his controversial girlfriend, Abhishek wants to play safe. "This is a great debut for me on television. The banner's good and so is my role," he answered. The fact that his love life has been much explored by the media, Abhishek's not cribbing. "We are celebrities and such things are bound to happen." Bring up Rakhi and he mellows down even more. "She's been misunderstood. In reality she's very down to earth and helpful person," the boyfriend shares.

* DREAM DEBUT: Until now, 20-year-old Karan Godwan was used to being in the background. This former dancer from Shiamak Davar's team finally decided to step out. "I have schooled in Spain and came back after finishing high school," informs Karan who plays the youngest son Vicky. With no connections to pull, this newcomer decided to give it all. "I must have given a million auditions and then Jugni Chali Jalandhar came my way," Karan's happy to have made it finally. On the show he's pairing up with Muskan Mehani who plays the lead as Jugni. Muskan's not new to television, having done shows like Dil Mil Gayee and Mamta.

* SECOND STINT: The last time we bumped into singer and once-in-a-while actor Baba Sehgal, he was busy crooning on NDTV Imagine's show 'Dhoom Macha De'. While Jaspinder Narula went on to win that, Baba Sehgal has emerged once as an actor on 'Jugni Chali Jalandhar'. "I am a Punjabi and what better way to show it off than by acting in such a soap that brings out the best of a Punjabi family," mentioned the singer who even gets to rap while playing his character of Balwinder Bhalla. With an album in the making, he has enough to keep him busy and us too!

Heading: Star gazing - Indian Express
Content:
TV's most sought after producer-couple Tony and Deeya Singh is now looking at making a film

Their work speaks for them. For 15 years, producer and also a couple, Tony and Deeya Singh have dished out delectable entertainment on television. Be it the truly ahead of its time Banegi Apni Baat or the immensely popular Jassi Jaisi Koi Nahin to their just wrapped up Left Right Left, the producers have scored aces each time. "Yes, our USP has been our ability to make shows that are for a varied audience," admitted Deeya Singh who was in the city to formally roll out their new show 'Jugni Chali Jalandhar' on SAB TV. Also accompanying Deeya was N P Singh, Chief Operating Officer of Sony Entertainment Television. This time around, the producers have gone all Punjabi. "Being a Punjabi it all came easy," smiles Deeya who feels it's tough making the viewer laugh every day. "But then there's so much negativity elsewhere that we decided to do this." Interestingly, they have a whole gamut of shows across all channels. "The only thing we haven't touched upon is reality and that's something we really want to do," mentioned Deeya who also lets out a special something. "We are all geared up to make a film now," says the producer. So what genre are they looking at? "All round entertainment. We are looking at a four-ticket movie," signs off Deeya.

Heading: The Write Stuff - Indian Express
Content: Saas, Bahu aur Sensex may be a small-budget movie, but this did not deter Bollywood stars from making it to its premiere. The star cast of the movie —the elegant Kirron Kher, Tanushree Dutta in a little red number, Masumeh Makhija and glamorous Lilette Dubey were seen mingling with everybody. Parvin Dabas and Sanjay Suri were spotted together on many occasions involved in animated conversations. Anupam Kher and son Sikander were also present to cheer for Kirron. Rahul Roy with wife Rajlaxmi (with layers of make-up), Bobby Darling, Shahana Goswami, Sudhir Mishra and Sonu Sood were among others at the venue.

Heading: Foot Loose - Indian Express
Content:
Australian filmmaker Megan Doneman on her documentary on Kiran Bedi

There was enough of India in Toronto last week — from the slums of Mumbai and the sets of Kaun Banega Crorepati? flickering on Danny Boyle's Slumdog Millionaire to the razzmatazz of Punjab in Singh is Kinng. And then there was Kiran Bedi — in Australian filmmaker Megan Doneman's compelling feature-length documentary, tongue-in-cheekily titled Yes Madam, Sir. The story of the first woman IPS officer, narrated by Academy Award-winning Helen Mirren, was screened as part of the Toronto International Film Festival's Real to Reel section that showcased 20 of the finest non-fiction films of 2008.

Doneman first read about Bedi when she was just 13 in a newspaper article her mother brought home from India. "The story was headlined 'Kiran Bedi: India's First Woman Police Officer Doing it her Way!' Even as a young girl, I knew how significant and bold that was," says Doneman, who next spotted her on television. She watched in disbelief the programme on Bedi introducing Vipassana meditation in Tihar Jail. "About 1,000 prisoners practised Vipassana in complete silence for 10 days and emerged from the experience weeping in the arms of the stoic prison guards, repenting their criminal behaviour. It was unbelievable," reminisces Doneman.

Nine years ago, Doneman began e-mailing Bedi, hoping that she might agree to let her do a film. "Bedi is one of these fascinating people. What motivates her to live her life the way she does? What drives her to continually oppose the status quo in the face of huge adversity and personal consequence? I had to know," says Doneman. Even as she pursued Bedi over the years, Doneman, a graduate of business communications and film at the University of Technology, Sydney, worked as assistant editor in Mission: Impossible 2 and The Lord of the Rings trilogy's The Two Towers and The Return of the King. But Yes Madam, Sir was to be her directorial debut. Doneman is not surprised by that. What she wondered, instead, was why did Bedi decide to go with an "unknown girl from Australia after turning down offers from esteemed filmmakers for 15 years". Finally, when Bedi invited her to fly to India, Doneman put the question to the top cop. "She replied, 'Because I am going to enjoy watching you struggle and fight to somehow pull this off.' I guess she had done that all her life," smiles Doneman, who watched Bedi at home and at work for months and pored through archives. And she found the clue to her character. "The true drama lies not in Bedi's extraordinary courage, but in the inherent contradictions in her character," says Doneman. "The very qualities that allow her to triumph could ultimately lead to her undoing." Bedi wouldn't disagree.

Heading: Ain’t nothing but a number - Indian Express
Content:
Smart Package
For the consumer who wants it all in one package, Sony India has introduced the Bravia series T, an LCD TV range. This new series provides a combination of high quality images with powerful side speakers for a complete entertainment experience. Available in three models, the T series are designed specially for the Indian market, post a consumer research undertaken last year. "Consumer insight represents a key focus area in Sony's product development plans and we are delighted to introduce for the first time an LCD TV that marries perfect audio pleasure with visual splendour," mentioned Sunil Nayyar, General Manager (Sales) with Sony India. The audio credentials do not end with the inclusion of speakers. The series features a built-in FM Radio as well as a highly customizable 5-Band Graphic Equalizer. Based on three preset modes (Dynamic/Standard/Clear Voice), the equalizer function allows users to enjoy richer sound according to their preferences and choice of content. The new Bravia Series T will be available at Sony owned stores, select national retail partners, as well as select Sony authorized dealers across the country.

Heading: Reely worth - Indian Express
Content:
Kareena Kapoor's birthday plans

If you ask us, we'll tell you she's ageless. But the blithe Kareena Kapoor adds yet another candle to her cake on September 21. As she turns 28, Kapoor insists she will be busy shooting for Raju Hirani's upcoming 3 Idiots in Ladakh.

"I don't intend celebrating my birthday with Saif since I will be shooting with Aamir Khan for my upcoming film," she says of her much-watched relationship with Saif Ali Khan. If only we didn't know the spontaneous Khan better, we'd believe that. It is also rumoured his sister Saba will be designing jewellery for Kapoor's birthday. A fact the actress considers too personal to be discussed.

As we catch up with Kapoor at the opening of a spa, the lass says: "The slimming equipment here is non invasive. Personally, I love yoga and I've controlled my weight by turning vegetarian. I encourage you to do the same," she smiles.

On the movie front, Kapoor has had some disappointments of late with the debacle of her last release, Tashan. But now, Kapoor will lend her voice to an animation film Roadside Romeo, about a spoilt dog roaming Mumbai streets. And as her beau is lending his voice to the film as well, Kapoor can't stop smiling. "I am looking forward to do an animation character. It is nice to know how people associate your voice with a particular character. Since Saif is with me in this project, it's even better," she blushes.

Heading: Father accuses ashram of indoctrination after sons refuse to visit ailing mother - Indian Express
Content:
City-based director Nikhil Mahajan's short film Antahasthiti revolves around the mystery of immaculate dreams

Dreams pass into the reality of actions and from the action stems another dream. Although we can resonate it in either ways, the connection between reel and real has always been strong. Unleashing the common ties between a world of dreams and intelligent cinema, and raveling the emotions of a young boy, city-based director-writer Nikhil Mahajan, in his first short film Antahasthiti –Inner Spirit, frames a tale of innocent dreams.

"Antahasthiti is a dark psychological thriller about Damodar, a young boy who lives in a place in Konkan and is out to solve the mystery of his dreams and in the process he unwinds a deep dark secret of life. The story revolves around an eight-year-old Damodar, who is breaking into adolescence as he is juggling amidst a bunch of emotions and deals with depression, desires and dreams. The entire film has been shot in Malvan in Maharashtra," adds Mahajan, a student of Sydney Film Institute.

This 35-minute film is Mahajan's first tryst with the big screen. Elaborating on the concept he adds, "Antahasthiti is a very intelligent film, it is layered with lot of metaphors and sentiments. It can be a little difficult to decipher and many times people have been questioning me on the concept."

Mahajan plans to screen the film at various international festivals. "I have always wanted to make a film on a boy in this kind of a dilemma. I am sure it will be perceived by people of various cultures, the issue has a universal appeal. Aniruddha Deodhar has played the role of Damodar, the kid in the film and is extremely talented. Anirudha Harip and Rutuja Patil, the lead actors, have done a fantastic job," he adds.

Mahajan is at present working on his first feature film Hawa Mahal. Talking about the film he says, "It is a fantasy fairy tale set against a rural background and on a realistic backdrop. It revolves around three characters that meet accidentally. It is a commercial movie and in Hinglish. Although I have grown seeing Shahrukh Khan and always had a like for Indian films, Sydney has given me the platform and exposure I needed. There I got to learn about the various different cinemas of the world and interact with different people. I believe I am blessed with a vivid imagination and my films are going to be invariably fictions."

(Antahasthiti will be premiered at the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) today at 3.00 pm)

Heading: Not many takers for CM’s charity plans - Indian Express
Content:
A retired army man from Agra came to Gujarat seeking custody of his two adult sons who are inmates of two different ashrams run by Asaram Bapu in Ahmedabad and Surat.

Jagramsinh Chauhan (70), a resident of Durga Palace, Devri road in Agra had submitted an application to the DIG of Agra to get the custody of his two sons Dharmesh (29) and Vivek (26) who are in the Asaram ashrams in Motera in Ahmedabad and Jehangirpura in Surat. The sons meanwhile have refused to meet their father and have even told the police that he could harm them if they returned home.

Chauhan added in his application that his wife Vimladevi is bedridden and wants to see her two sons. Agra DIG transferred the application to Gujarat, following which Chauhan came to Ahmedabad and handed over the application to the CID, seeking custody of Dharmesh from the Motera ashram.

Chauhan, along with Inspector Himmatsinh Rajput (CID) met Dharmesh after obtaining permission from the ashram in-charge Yogeshbhai. Dharmesh is a BE in Electrical engineering and has been living in the Motera ashram for six years.

Dharmesh made a call to his brother Vivek in Surat and told him that their mother Vimladevi is bedridden and that their father has come to take them back home. Vivek agreed. He has been an inmate of the Jehangirpura ashram for the last eight years now.

But in a surprise move on Friday morning, Vivek handed over an application to Surat police commissioner and a Rander inspector stating that his father will come to the ashram, take him back home and will kill him, as he had lost his mental balance. He pleaded for help and said he did not want to go with his father.

In the afternoon, Chauhan, with two of his relatives, went to the Surat ashram. But Vivek gave him the shock of his life by refusing to come with him. Rander police arrived after learning about Chauhan's arrival at the ashram. They recorded the statements of both father and son and took them to Rander police station for further questioning.

In presence of Inspector R H Hadiya, Vivek repeated his decision about not going back home.

"I have come here to take my sons home. My wife Vimladevi is bedridden. Both Dharmesh and Vivek have not come home for the last seven years. They (ashram authorities) have brain-washed my sons. How can one change his mind overnight? We suspect that the ashram in-charge Amar Yadav and others might have pressurised him not to go with his father, by making him believe that Asaram Bapu was 'present in them' and that there was no place for any relative or family in their life," said Chauhan.

He added: "I will not leave Surat without Vivek. If he is not willing to come home for good, he can come for just five days. He can return after seeing his mother's condition."

Vivek, however, stuck to his decision. However, later in the evening, Chauhan again went to the ashram and talks were still on between father and sons till the time of filing this report.

"I have been in the ashram for the last seven years and I am enjoying a holy life with the blessings of Asaram Bapu. I don't want to go back home, as I am scared of my father. He is a retired army man and has come in contact with those who are anti-Bapu. They will kill me," said Vivek.

Meanwhile, Amar Yadav has said that the ashram is not pressurising Vivek. "We have done nothing to him. He had sent an application to the police commissioner and Rander police seeking police help.

Hadiya said, "Vivek is mature enough to understand what is good or bad for him. I have asked him to visit his mother and then return to the ashram."
