Heading: Something is fishy about it: Govt does away with fishing tenders, cites religious beliefs of Jains - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Secretary is opposed to govt's plan of seeking a share of PSEs' profit for welfare of weaker sections

Even as Chief Minister Narendra Modi has called a meeting of chairpersons and managing directors of state-run profit making public sector enterprises (PSEs) next week, Chief Secretary Manjula Subramaniam is learnt to have opposed the government's plan of seeking 30 per cent of the PSEs' annual profit before tax (PBT) for the welfare of weaker sections of the society.

Sources in the CMO said on Friday that the chief secretary, at an official meeting held recently in the Sachivalaya, had opposed the government's plan, arguing that while there is no harm in seeking funds from the state-owned unlisted PSEs, asking the six listed PSEs, where private investors have also put in their money, to contribute from their profits, would not only have an adverse impact on the functioning of these companies, but also harm the interests of private investors. A 1972 batch IAS officer, Subramanium will retire from service at the end of this month. She was of the view that the listed PSEs would have to obtain an approval from their respective boards of directors, and also a nod from private shareholders at their AGMs before seeking funds from these companies to fulfil their corporate social responsibility (CSR). "The government overruled her opposition," said sources.

Earlier this month, MDs of some of the listed government companies had reportedly expressed their reservations about the government's move. The most vocal among them was the CMD of GNFCm, Sudha Anchaliya, a 1972 batch IAS officer who is learnt to have told the government that asking the PSEs to contribute from their profit as part of their CSR might adversely affect their expansion plans due to reduced liquidity. However, the babus of these government-run entities fell in line after they realised that their political bosses were more than keen to implement this move.

Meanwhile, Arvind Agrawal, the Commissioner, Bureau of Public Sector Enterprises, Government of Gujarat, told Newsline on Friday that the chief minister would call a meeting of chairpersons and MDs of all profit making state PSEs — both listed as well as unlisted — sometime next week, to deliberate on how they could set aside funds for the government to carry out programmes for the socio-economic upliftment of the poor. He said the government would go ahead with its plan and "request" letters have already been dispatched to the PSEs. He agreed that the listed companies would have to obtain a nod from their respective boards of directors and private investors before setting aside the funds.

On Thursday, a meeting of the secretaries of all departments concerned was called by Additional Chief Secretary (Finance) D Rajagopalan, where they were asked to expedite the process of preparing reports on the various projects proposed to be implemented in the social sector, like health, education, drinking water, sanitation, tribal development and so on, Agrawal said.

After this, the projects will be sent to the Centre for approval. The Gujarat Socio-Economic Development Society headed by the CM will then apply for income tax exemption for funds to be diverted by PSEs to the government. The 16-member society having ministers and secretaries of the departments concerned has been constituted to ensure proper utilisation of funds to be diverted from the PSEs.

Heading: Nanavati report: Yet to win the trust of kin of the accused - Indian Express
Content:
Fishing contractors knock at court doors, file PIL seeking cancellation of contracts given away on the quiet

The Gujarat Government claims to have done away with the practice of floating tenders to award fishing contracts worth crores in the state's reservoirs this time. This has been done mainly to avoid hurting the "religious sentiments" of communities like the Jains whose religious beliefs do not support catching or killing fish.

For the first time, the state government has done away with the Government Leasing Policy for Reservoirs of Inland Fisheries 2004, which insists on tenders by fixing contracts on the basis of upset prices (lowest price at which an item of property may be auctioned or sold).

This has come as a shock to the Muslim community, which used to bag the fishing contracts, given for a period of five years.

Fisheries Minister Purushottam Solanki told Newsline that the step has been taken to provide equal opportunities to all castes. "Communities like the Jains have protested against these tenders. In order to avoid hurting their religious sentiments, we have decided to do away with the practice of inviting tenders, and instead, award them on the quiet."

Many contactors have now moved the High Court seeking cancellation of the contracts given away without floating tenders. As many as five cases and one PIL have been filed against the state government's decision.

Responding to a plea filed by Birsa Munda Matsya Udhyog Mandali (Wankaner) on July 20, the Gujarat High Court had issued a notice on September 18, asking the state government to justify its action and decision on September 26.

In a counter affidavit filed in the case, the government cited nine reasons for not following the tender system.

The chief among them was that the religious sentiments of certain communities was hurt when tenders were floated to award fishing contracts in the state reservoirs. Another justification was that the tender process favours financially strong groups and thus poor people are not able to compete in the process with high bids.

Heading: A case of too little, too late... - Indian Express
Content:
Most believe culprits will not be brought to book

A day after the first part of the Nanavati Commission's report on the Godhra riots was handed over to Chief Minister Narendra Modi, the kin of the accused seem to have a general lack of faith in it. Most believe that the real culprits will not be brought to book.

A Godhra Municipal Corporation corporator, who was also summoned by the Special Investigation Team, refused to share his views on the report, saying he would talk "openly" later.

The families of two POTA accused—Maulana Hussain Umarji and Ibrahim Dhantiya alias Kachuka — remained tightlipped. While Dhantiya is in Pakistan and reportedly struggling in Karachi by selling gutkha, Umarji is in Sabarmati Jail.

Arif Kachuka (23) hung up on the phone as soon as the word 'riot' was mentioned. "Kya chahiye aap logon ko? (What do you want?) Mere abba ke bare mein pooch rahe ho to mujhe kuch pata nahi. (I have no clue where my father is.)

Heading: Two drown in flood waters; three go missing as tractor overturns - Indian Express
Content:
It's been more than six years when the S-6 coach of Sabarmati Express was torched on February 27, 2002. And, while everyone is keen to know about the contents of the Nanavati-Mehta inquiry commission report, which was submitted to the Gujarat CM on Thursday, the kin of those who were burnt alive in the coach, think it is now too late to make a difference in their lives. Time has healed their wounds.

Gayatri Panchal (23) is the youngest of the Panchal sisters, who were orphaned when their parents, Harshad and Meeta and two sisters, Prateeksha and Chayya died in the incident. She said, "It's been more than six years now and we have learnt to live without our parents. We have come a long way and the report will hardly make a difference to us."

Gayatri, who had survived the incident, is now pursuing a post-graduate degree in Indian Culture. "I saw my parents and two elder sisters being charred to death right in front of my eyes. I want to forget it. We sisters have learnt to survive in this world without any support. We want justice. If the judiciary cannot provide it, God will," she added.

A resident of Amraiwadi, Vilas Yadav (35), whose father, Sadashiv Yadav (55) was among the 59 Karsevaks killed in the carnage, said, "I hope the report brings out the truth and the guilty are punished."

When asked if he is anxious to know what is there in the report, he said, "If the submission of report can make news headlines, its content will do the same. We will come to know about it (content) too."

Heading: MSU computers ‘bugged’, over 300 systems are out of order - Indian Express
Content:
At least two persons have died and three others have gone missing in the flooded waters of Surendranagar and the adjacent district of Ahmedabad rural in the last 48 hours.

While the two people who have died in Surendranagar are yet to be identified, the three who have gone missing in Fedara village of Ahmedabad have identified by the Dholera police officials as Jaypalsinh Rana (24), Haresh Rathod (28) and Annabhai (40) -- all residents of Fedara village. The three had gone to distribute food packets to people stranded near Fedara village when they were washed away in the floodwaters.

Police sub-inspector S T Kharadi said five villagers had gone on a tractor to provide food packets to passengers of five luxury buses stranded in flooded waters near Fedara village on Thursday, when their vehicle overturned in the water.

Kharadi said, "Only two among them could be rescued, who were shifted to a local hospital. The other three could not be traced. A search operation was launched with the help of the Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services and other agencies."

Kharadi said even though search operations are still on, there is a very remote possibility of the three being alive. Dholera police have registered a missing complaint in this regard.

Meanwhile, with their being less rain in Surendranagar since Thursday evening, the flood situation has improved. District collector J D Bhad said, "The situation is fast returning to normal. We plan to help the evacuated people return home in a day or two after giving them adequate ration."

Meanwhile, the authorities have recovered bodies of two unidentified men. "The two were washed away in the floodwaters when they were on their way from Morbi to Ahmedabad on a motorbike. We had been looking for them since Thursday," Bhad added.

Heading: VMC offers third alternative to Station-Sashtri Bridge area shopkeepers - Indian Express
Content:
'It is true that we have been facing connectivity problems ever since the VMC carried out digging near the faculty. We had complained about this a month ago but nothing has been done so far'

M S University (MSU) has a new problem to contend with—over 300 computers in the varsity are down with virus. And surprisingly, the varsity administration is yet to take note of this problem.

The MSU alumni, who had formed the Technology Promotion Trust (TPT), had drawn up a sustainable module to boost the Internet connectivity of 2,000 computers in 13 faculties in 2002. They had spent over Rs 10 crore to install an optical fibre system of Internet connectivity. The TPT, which is presently managing the interlinking of the system, has expressed their willingness to hand over charge to the university this year. The MSU, however, has not made any concrete effort to this end.

With the first rains in the city, Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) carried out digging work near MSU Faculty of Social Work (FSW), damaging the optical fibres and affecting more than 20 computer systems in FSW.

"It is true that we have problems in connectivity after the VMC's digging near the faculty. We had complained about this a month ago but nothing has been done so far to restore connectivity," said Aruna Khasgiwala, the FSW dean.

The optical fibres imported from the US in 2002 were encased in a special material to minimise chances of system failure. Nevertheless, wires are seen hanging outside the faculties of Education and Psychology. This might lead to a total break down of the system, said a few lecturers on the condition of anonymity.

Rumi Mistry, a TPT trustee, said, "After our work gets over, we will hand over the task of interlinking the computers to the varsity authorities."

The TPT had spent around Rs 12 lakh to ensure that bandwidth is properly managed for four years. In 2007 the varsity took up the responsibility of bearing the expenses required to maintain 4 megabytes bandwidth, to provide air-conditioners and support to the Hansa Mehta library, university office, technology faculty and other areas within the campus. However, the TPT is still managing the system.

Prof Ramesh Goyal, MSU Vice Chancellor, refused to comment on the management system. He said, "In our meeting, we have decided to come up with a unique IT policy, where a computer will be allotted to one person and only he/she will be allowed to handle it."

An anti-virus software will also be installed.

Heading: Mystery shrouds girl’s death due to allergy - Indian Express
Content:
After shop owners expressed their disapproval with Kishanwadi and Manjalpur lands, VMC has proposed a 9000 sq-ft plot at Chaani Jakatnaka

The tussle between shop owners in the Station-Sashtri Bridge stretch and Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC), which has been going on for a year and eight months now, finally seems to have reached a conclusion. For, the VMC has offered a third alternative to the 140 shop owners for their encroached cabins, which were demolished by the Corporation on February 4, 2007.

After the shop owners expressed their disapproval on being offered a substitution at Kishanwadi and Manjalpur, the standing committee has proposed a 9000 sq ft plot at Chaani Jakatnaka. The earlier proposed land at Manjalpur saw a stiff opposition from the leaders of the opposition party. "The Manjalpur plot is used during Navratri. The leaders opposed the proposal, as the plot is situated near residential areas and the shop keepers have been demanding for a land within two kilometres of the station area, which is not logically possible," said B M Pardesi, Director, Encroachment and Security, VMC.

He added: "Plans for widening the road are being discussed for the last 12 years. We had offered them the option of plots at Kishanwadi and Manjalpur, but the shopkeepers never heeded to the proposal and we finally had to take action."

While the shop owners completely rejected the plot at Kishanwadi, they did subsequently agree to the Manjalpur land. "We have lost our businesses. Most of us are working from rented cabins in non-profitable areas or from roadside handcarts. But we gave a nod to the Manjalpur plot half-heartedly, as we were devoid of any better choice," said Kishor Chandwani, who owned three electronic shops at Station road. The Chaani jakatnaka plot, if approved by the shop owners as a better business undertaking, will act as a substitute for the encroached plot as per the High Court judgment.

"We expect that the shopkeepers will accept this new plot. Once approved, the proceedings will be completed within a fortnight," said Pardesi.

Heading: BSP to organise protest rally over suspension - Indian Express
Content:
The mystery surrounding the death of 30-year-old Sumitra Baria from Koyari village of Tilakwada taluka in Narmada district on Wednesday has deepened further with her viscera being sent to the Surat Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL). Baria had reportedly died of an allergic reaction to a medicine that had accidentally fallen on her body.

Medical experts at Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL), Narmada Yojana Hospital said the viscera was sent to the FSL because of the want of a proper medical history of the deceased.

"Prima facie evidence suggests that Baria developed an allergic reaction after a bottle of medicine accidentally fell on her when she was cleaning the house on Tuesday afternoon. However, we have not been able to figure out if she had a history of allergies," said Dr Radhika Devi, from SSNNL, Narmada Yojana Hospital.

Heading: BSP to organise protest rally over suspension of Borsad Municipal Hospital doctor - Indian Express
Content:
Supporters of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) will take out a rally in Anand district on Sunday to protest against the suspension of Borsad Municipal Hospital medical officer Dr Ashok Mehta.

Dr Mehta, who has been serving in the hospital for the last seven years, was allegedly suspended by the Borsad municipality in August without the two thirds majority vote of the municipality board members.

Dr Mehta had filed an atrocity case about a month ago in Borsad police station. However, the police have not taken any action yet.

Around 500 people are expected to take part in the protest rally organised by BSP, said Rajendra Makwana, BSP General Secretary, Anand district. "Borsad Municipality Hospital is in a bad condition. There is a shortage of staff in the hospital. Dr Mehta had just complained about this to the municipal authorities when he was threatened by some goons," he added.

Heading: UGC committee’s queries too tricky for Gujarat University heads - Indian Express
Content:
The General Elections are due for next year, but it seems the Congress has already started wooing its tribal vote bank.

On Friday morning, senior Congress leaders embarked on the Gujarat Nirman Rath Yatra rally to promote the Central government's schemes in Nanod taluka of Narmada district.

While a separate programme for Chhota Udepur and Naswadi in Vadodara district is already underway since September 17, it will be also carried on simultaneously in all the 24 Lok Sabha constituencies in Gujarat in the coming months, said senior Congress leaders.

Dhirubhai Bhil, Naswadi (Congress) MLA told Newsline: "The rally has been conducted in more than 150 tribal villages of Vadodara and Narmada districts. For every tribal taluka, we are taking at least two days to promote Central government schemes. It has been noticed that state government is taking advantage of the schemes actually started by the Centre."

The rally started two days ago in Chhota Udepur Lok Sabha constituency, where Congress MP Naran Rathwa has won the last four terms consecutively. It will be organised in all the Lok Sabha constituencies in the state.

Heading: GU teacher submits confidential report to UGC committee - Indian Express
Content:
Heads of several departments fail to answer questions about their own demands; non-teaching staff stage a demonstration after being barred from meeting the committee

More teachers, better labs, laptops and better infrastructure — the Gujarat University (GU) was ready with its wishlist for the University Grants Commission's (UGC) XI Plan Expert Visiting Committee, which visited the varsity on Friday. However, the heads of several departments of GU failed to answer the team's questions regarding their own demands.

A senior GU official said on condition of anonymity: "The UGC committee was surprised to see the demand of Rs 120.31 crore made by GU for the XI five-year plan."

The heads of several departments could not answer the UGC team's queries about the need for a separate computerised library and computer laboratory when the University Central Library and Rollwala Computer Centre are already in place, the official said.

"The UGC team is in no mood to approve the demand of a separate computerised library and computer laboratory for different departments," the official added.

Meanwhile, around 100 non-teaching employees of the university staged a demonstration after their plea to meet the UGC committee was rejected by GU Vice-Chancellor (V-C), Parimal Trivedi. Shreekant Vyas, one of the non-teaching staff, told Newsline: "After protesting for about an hour, we finally managed to meet Dr Reddy, one of the committee members. He allowed us to present our demands and praised us for showing concern for the development of GU."

Problems like violation of the UGC norms related to the RTI Act, Promotion Act, Minimum Wages Act, Factory (Press) Act, Contract Laws, and Roster were discussed between non-teaching staff members and the UGC committee.

Brain teasers for GU heads

* How many books are there at the University Central Library relating to the respective departments?

* How many books, journals and magazines are there in the department libraries?

* Why is there a need of a separate computerised library and computer laboratory when the University Central Library and Rollwala Computer Centre are already in place?

* The contribution of your department in the past five years?

* Why is the syllabus not revised every year?

Key issues discussed between UGC committee and non-teaching staff

* The violation of the Executive Council (EC) rules and regulations by the Vice Chancellor

* The violation of the RTI Act

* Wrong and less information provided to the applicant by the Public Information Officer (PIO)

* The current in-charge Registrar of GU not up to the marks

* The violation of Promotion Act, Minimum Wages Act, Factory (Press) Act, Contract Laws

Heading: Right to inaction: GPCB ignores obligation to provide information under RTI Act - Indian Express
Content:
A senior Gujarat University (GU) teacher on Friday submitted a confidential report to the visiting University Grants Commission (UGC) team, compiling the academic and financial anomalies of GU authorities.

According to sources, the report points out that after allotting grants to GU, the UGC does not conduct checks on the university.

Several complaints about administrative, academic and financial irregularities have been made to the Higher Education Department, Governor, Chief Minister, State Education Minister and the Chief Education Secretary of the state. Despite this, the UGC has not taken any steps.

Some of the important points mentioned in the report are: no recruitments have been made even after three years after GU had released an advertisement in October 2005; the present Chief Accounts Officer, Minesh Shah, was appointed in 2004 even though he did not possess the required qualification as per UGC rules; and no suggestions have been proposed by the UGC even after the report was submitted by the National Assessment and Accreditation Council two years ago.

Heading: Blasts case: Four arrested sent to police custody for 10 days - Indian Express
Content:
An RTI application filed in the Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB) seeking details about all the RTI applications filed in GPCB till August 31, 2008 and the responses given to them, has thrown light on how the Act has been dishonoured

Mahesh Pandya of Paryavaran Mitra, the organisation which filed the RTI, said: "We had filed more than 50 RTI applications with GPCB, but their response was shocking. Neither was the stipulated 30 day time limit followed nor the information supplied was correct. It was inadequate, false and misleading. In some cases, GPCB took 2 years to reply to our RTI pleas. So, to trace a pattern, we asked them to tell us about all the RTIs filed and their responses to them. The facts are now out in the public domain."

A close examination of the GPCB reply raises several issues. As per GPCB, it has received 85 RTI applications during the above mentioned time period. In 25 of them, the appellate authority has provided information after the expiry of the stipulated period of 45 days. Section 19 of the RTI Act clearly enlists the procedure for appeal if the information supplied by the Information Officer is deemed inadequate. "Since the law is silent on the penalty if the appellate authority delays the reply, GPCB has exploited it to the maximum. Also, the RTI replies do not mention where to appeal if the applicant is not satisfied with the appellate authority's response, creating further confusion," said Pandya.

GPCB has also disallowed 10 RTI applications, without specifying any reason, in direct contrast to section 10 of the RTI Act. Another major issue concerns the provision for providing third party information under sections 8 and 11 of the RTI Act. Paryavaran Mitra alleges that GPCB has rejected several RTI pleas under the garb of 'third party information'.

"In some cases, we have observed that even before seeking a mandatory submission by the third party for the disclosure of information, GPCB has rejected RTI pleas. The Gujarat High Court has recently interpreted section 11 of the RTI Act, but the ambiguity still remains," Pandya added.

Heading: Militants killed in Delhi encounter may have planted bombs in Surat - Indian Express
Content:
Emails sent by Abbas, Nagori may contain more information about SIMI and the Indian Mujahideen

The designated Metropolitan Court hearing the Ahmedabad blasts case and the Surat bomb case has remanded the four accused — rearrested on Thursday — in police custody for 10 days, even though the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) had requested for 14 days remand.

Naved Kadri, Javed Sheikh and Abbas Samjea, who had been arrested from Bhuj on September 5, had been earlier sent on 14 days remand for their alleged role in the Civil Hospital blasts, while Aiyaz Saiyed, a resident of Vatva, had been arrested in connection with the Naroda Gam blast case. The four were rearrested after their initial 14 days remand in the Civil Hospital case elapsed.

The DCB had submitted an application seeking their remand to probe their role in the blast conspiracy, the SIMI meetings attended by them and their role in providing logistical support.

More specifically, it states that Aiyaz needs to be questioned about his links with Abu Bashar and Abdul Subhan alias Tauqeer, who is believed to have sent the terror emails prior to the Ahmedabad and Delhi blasts.

According to the remand application, Aiyaz is close to Tauqeer, and he was the one who had arranged for the rented house in which he (Tauqeer) had stayed with Bashar.

Abbas, who was arrested from Bhuj, is wanted for further questioning with respect to the SIMI operations in Kutch.

The DCB has also stated that it wants to find out the details of the emails sent by Abbas and Nagori from Bhuj, where they had organised SIMI meetings.

According to the DCB, the emails may contain more information about SIMI and the Indian Mujahideen, which has claimed responsibility for the Ahmedabad and Delhi blasts. During the hearing of the remand, advocate I M Munshi presented an application before the court seeking permission to meet his clients in the absence of police personnel. The court offered him a meeting with his clients but with the rider that the police personnel would be five feet away from them.

This was, however, not accepted by Munshi and the court too, rejected the application on the ground that such a meeting would give rise to security issues.

Heading: Modi watches from air, a flood-ravaged Gujarat - Indian Express
Content:
The Delhi Police on Friday shot dead two Indian Mujahideen (IM) militants in an encounter and nabbed another injured militant. Suspicions are rife ever since that they could be among the four unidentified 'outsiders' mentioned in the records of Surat police, who are wanted in connection with the live bombs found in the diamond city.

Surat Police Commissioner R M S Brar said that his force would investigate the matter thoroughly and try to ascertain if the dead terrorists had visited Surat earlier.

The Surat top cop's statement was based on the Delhi Police Commissioner Y S Dadhwal's hour-long press briefing in Delhi after the encounter. Dadhwal told the media that one of those killed, Atif alias Bashir, had travelled to Ahmedabad on July 24 with 10 accomplices and returned on July 27 along with 12 others. Two of them had arranged for the car found laden with explosives in Surat.

Incidentally, SIMI activists Tanveer Pathan and Zahir Patel, who are presently in the custody of Surat police, are also accused of helping four unidentified 'outsiders' who stayed in Surat at around the same time. These four men are accused of purchasing vehicles and later using them for planting bombs in Surat.

"Residents of Surat, Pathan and Patel are accused of helping these four men with logistics. During his interrogation, Pathan told us that he even arranged for a house for these four men. The duo in our custody, however, can identify those persons only by their faces. Whether the IM terrorists killed in Delhi were among the four wanted by us can be established only during investigations. A police team will be sent to Delhi soon," Brar said.

Atif had also been with the Mumbai-based SIMI activist, Tauqeer, who is the alleged mastermind behind the serial bomb blasts in various parts of the country, including Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Delhi. The other militant killed in the Delhi encounter has been identified as Sajid, a member of the IM, a shadow outfit of the banned SIMI and Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), police said. Both Atif and Sajid hailed from Azamgarh in eastern Uttar Pradesh.

The arrested terrorist has been identified as Mohd Saif who has been taken by the Special Cell sleuths for questioning. Sources in Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB), said that a team of DCB may leave for Delhi to interrogate Saif.

Heading: Hoax e-mail on bombing rly stations came from Rajkot - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Narendra Modi on Friday did an aerial survey of the flood-affected villages in Ahmedabad and Surendranagar districts. Over 10,000 food packets and drinking water pouches were air-dropped in 30 worst-affected villages of Dhandhuka taluka, which are still marooned although it has stopped raining after monsoon clouds moved towards UP.

Modi later held a meeting with his ministers and senior bureaucrats for carrying out emergency relief and rehabilitation works like distribution of cash doles and initiating measures to prevent spread of diseases post-floods.

According to Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Anandi Patel, a total of 79 persons have died owing to heavy rains this monsoon and 20,000 people have been evacuated. A survey about crop loss and payment of compensation to the farmers would be carried out as soon as the water recedes.

There is a drinking water crisis in 98 villages of Rapar taluka, as water cannot reach due to a breach in the Narmada canal. The Kutch district administration has now arranged for tankers to supply drinking water.

As many as 35 state highways and 208 other roads have been closed to traffic in the last couple of days due to floods. The most prominent of these is the Madhavpur-Porbandar coastal highway. The state government has also pressed into service 22 water lifting pumps in Nadiad and seven pumps in other areas to clear rain water from the low lying areas.

Energy minister Saurabh Patel said that power supply to the flood-hit villages in Lakhtar and Patadi talukas of Surendranagar has been restored since Friday morning.

Meanwhile, Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee president Siddharth Patel visited four worst hit villages of Lakhtar taluka including Kadu, Barwada and Lakhtar proper on Friday. Congress MLA Shailesh Parmar and others accompanying him arranged to distribute 20,000 food packets in Ahmedabad and Surendranagar districts.

Heading: Contour mapping OK’d, forecasts on floods next year? - Indian Express
Content:
Meanwhile, ATS collects documents bearing Tauqeer's handwriting to check if Al-Arbi signature in terror mails is by him

A day after security at railway stations in the city was beefed up after a news channel received an e-mail regarding planned bomb blasts at Churchgate station, Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus and Borivali railway station, the state Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) on Friday said that the source of the e-mail, which turned out to be a hoax, was traced to a location in Rajkot. The ATS also stated that further inquiries in the matter would be conducted by the Gujarat Police.

"The e-mail sent to a news channel yesterday, and later forwarded to us, has been traced this afternoon to an IP (Internet Protocol) address in Rajkot. We are not going to send a team there, as the case will be investigated by the Gujarat Police. It does not seem like this e-mail was sent by the same group who have been sending out the Ahmedabad and Delhi terror e-mails," said Joint Commissioner of Police (ATS) Hemant Karkare.

The e-mail had been sent from the account 'almujahidin2001@yahoo.com', and warned of bomb blasts at the three major suburban stations between 8 pm and 10 pm, on Thursday.

Karkare also stated that no Mumbai links had been found yet to the militants killed in the encounter at Jamia Nagar in New Delhi.

"We have been constantly in touch with the Special Cell of the Delhi police after their operation, and so far we have not got any information cocerning possible local links to the militants involved," said Karkare.

Meanwhile, the ATS has collected certain documents bearing the handwriting of SIMI activist Abdus Subhan Qureshi alias Tauqeer, the alleged mastermind of the Ahmedabad and Delhi serial blasts, in order to match them with the handwritten  signature 'Al-Arbi' in all five terror e-mails sent out by the Indian Mujahideen.

"We have some documents that serve as samples of Tauqeer's handwriting. We have submitted them to handwriting experts, to see if they actually match with the signature on the Indian Mujahideen e-mails. However, we are yet to receive an opinion from the experts," said Karkare.

Heading: All the property you own, detailed in a digital card - Indian Express
Content:
Two years after the Chitale Committee, the fact-finding team studying the 26th July deluge of 2005, first recommended a contour mapping exercise for the city, the crucial topographical maps will finally be ready by the next monsoon. The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's planned 'flood modelling' system depends on the contour maps, which show topographical features of land in greta detail. A flood modelling system, in turn, will help the civic body predict and plan for major flood situations in the future.

After rejecting the demand for low-flying aerial photography — a necessary prerequisite for the contour maps — owing to security reasons, the Ministry of Defence has now given its approval to conduct the exercise. However, high risk areas like the naval base, Mumbai Port Trust, the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre and the international airport will not be included in the final maps.

The MOD approval, with certain conditions, came on September 17. Work will begin in the next few days. "The base maps will be ready by next year and so will the contour maps. We are trying to meet the target of monsoon 2009," Additional Municipal Commissioner R A Rajeev.

Contour mapping is the most important element of a flood modelling system, as it shows points of elevation (height) of valleys and hills, and the steepness of slopes by using a curve connecting points. The mapping requires low-flying aerial photographs which will be taken from a height of 1,000 metres , with a high resolution of 1 is to 50. The distance between two points on each curve will be 20 cm, which means the maps will be adequately detailed so as to enable the plotting of minor storm water drains, river tributaries and even every manhole on the maps. The civic administration has selected private company MWH - Mumbai and ORG Informatics, Gurgaon, for the job.

Officials from MWH - Mumbai said that representative from the MOD will be present when photographs are being taken. "They will scan all the low-flying areial photographs and the contour maps and only after their approval will the civic administration be handed over the final maps," a spokesperson said.

Through a series of reports, Newsline has reported on the delays in the BMC's implementation of contour mapping and the consequent delay in flood forecasting.

* Flood modelling is done with the assistance of digitised maps of the city. A flood situation in a certain area of the map can be predicted depending on the quantum of rian and the locality's drainage capacity.

* Flood modelling is a system accepted worldwide in predicting floods. It helps in developing an online real-time system with the help of geographical information on low-lying and steep areas.

Heading: Mumbai Airport still at birth-pang stage: Yechury - Indian Express
Content:
The City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharahstra Ltd (CIDCO) became the first government agency in the country after it launched digital property cards on Friday.

The digital cards in the form of smart optical cards would be the certificate of property and have all the necessary information of the particular property. Four property owners were handed over the new cards by Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh in Mantralaya on the occasion of the launch of the digital cards by CIDCO.

The cards made of PVC polycarbonate have embedded microprocessor chips of 4 KB with 1.5 MB optical strip for storing data. "The digital cards eliminate the need to carry paper documents. They are safe and easy way of retaining important property papers," the vice-chairperson and managing director of CIDCO G S Gill told the newsline. "There won't be excuses of untraceable files (by officials) as the property owners will carry their own files."

Gill said that the scheme, applicable to CIDCO properties only, was voluntary. "For obtaining such card a property-holder has to pay Rs 1,000. We have not made it compulsory, eventually people will switch over to the new system," he said.

The CIDCO has leased over 1.50 lakh apartments and about 40,000 plots to various buyers. According to officials, the digital card would also help CIDCO in preventing multiple mortgages of property with financial institutions without its permission. The information that the card stores includes allotment letter, lease agreement, details of payment, transactions with civic bodies and banks.

They also claim that the cards are tamper-proof and data once stored cannot be deleted, making it an authentic and permanent source of information on a particular property.

Heading: Mangrove wetland centre at Navi Mumbai: Master plan in 12 more months - Indian Express
Content:
Rajya Sabha MP and CPI(M) Politburo Member Sitaram Yechury, who is the chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism & Culture, said today that "though things look chaotic at Mumbai Airport at the moment, the future looks pretty good on paper". In the country's commercial capital along with 13 other members of the 35-strong committee to assess the airport's ongoing privatisation process, he said, "The airport is going through a phase of birth pangs."

The privatisation process is facing several controversies, from opposition by the Airport Authority of India Employees' Union (AAEU) to questions on rehabilitation.

Apart from these issues, the House panel also discussed with employees' representatives the merger of Air India and Indian into National Aviation Company of India Ltd (NACIL). Representations were made to Yechury by AAEU and NACIL's union under the umbrella Joint Action Committee (JAC). "There are some decisions that have been taken in the past, which cannot be reversed," Yechury pointed out, referring to the privatisation of the Mumbai and Delhi airports on the basis of the operations, management, development agreement (OMDA), which is yet to be recognised by the 15,000-strong AAI union. "However, there is still scope for development of facilities while working within the constraints... on that we have made suggestions to the government," he added.

He said that while Mumbai Airport has been privatised, there is no question of privatising Air Traffic Control (ATC) operations as that would involve security issues.

Yechury, however, made it clear that the suggestions made by the House committee could not be disclosed.

The committee members met Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) officials to discuss the fate of over 40,000 slum dwellers around the airport. Yechury said that the BMC officials cited land constraints to their full relocation but the committee maintained that information available with them indicated that there is enough land to settle all slum dwellers. "The BMC initially plans to relocate 20,000 slum dwellers. Plans for the rest need to be worked out," Yechury said.

While the committee is empowered only to make non-binding recommendations to the government, Yechury pointed out that the objective of such a panel is to question the government on certain matters and bring all relevant issues into the public domain.

Commenting on the fact that AAI holds a 26% stake in the Joint Venture Company (JVC) MIAL while AAI employees are working for the JVC, Yechury said, "This is an unprecedented thing... Union members are employees of the Government of India (GoI) and not of a private company. Even if facilities are privatised, the people cannot be."

Heading: Underground scanner on faults in pipes - Indian Express
Content:
Forest Department, CIDCO and Conservation Action Trust sign MoU in CM's presence; CIDCO to bear cost of project

After the inauguration of the Mangrove Wetland Centre in Bhandup in March, a similar proposal has been chalked out for Navi Mumbai. Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh today oversaw the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the three parties involved in the setting up of the Centre.

The tripartite agreement was signed by Chief Conservator of Forests Shree Bhagwan from the Forest Department, City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Ltd (CIDCO) Managing Director G S Gill and Debi Goenka of the Conservation Action Trust.

"The master plan for the Mangrove Wetland Centre in Navi Mumbai will be ready in 12 months, with CIDCO bearing the cost of the entire project," said Mangrove Wetland Centre Director Vivek Kulkarni. A structured committee, called the Project Steering Committee, will be set up to oversee the planning and execution of the project.

The committee will be chaired by the CIDCO MD and include secretaries and senior officers from the government, along with non-governmental organisation (NGO) representatives.

"CIDCO recently declared an area of approximately 277 hectare for the development of mangroves. The idea is to protect and conserve mangroves while simultaneously promoting tourism," said Gill.

Of the land being used for the project, 5 hectare will lie outside the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) and mangrove. "The building and Centre will come up within the 5 hectare, after the Forest Department makes sure that there is no violation," informed Kulkarni.

The facility has a carrying capacity of around half a million people a year, and will have elevated bird walks and watch towers. The Centre is being planned by a Singapore-based architect, along with local architects.

While the design for the Centre is still being prepared, a marine aquarium is also being planned. "The Centre will have various trails but none of them will cause any harm to the existing mangrove population. We have modelled our Mangrove Wetland Centre on the lines of the ones in Singapore and Hong-Kong — as opposed to London's Eco-Park — as their climate is somewhat similar to ours," explained Gill.

"Subject to approval, we are looking at February 2011 as a possible inauguration target. Some centres may open earlier, to cater to education groups, students etc," said Kulkarni. Planning for the project began over three months ago, he added.

"It is a four-pronged system, beginning with conservation and proceeding to education, research and recreation in that order of priority. Each one has a 10-year plan that is being written by the Forest Department," said Kulkarni.

The Forest Department believes that this is one way to ensure people's participation in mangrove conservation. "We want to create awareness among people so that it becomes something they discuss within their households," said Kulkarni.

Heading: BMC to strengthen security measures at hospitals - Indian Express
Content:
Civic body plans to use ground penetrating radars to detect leakages in pipes and drains

With Mumbai's crumbling and old underground utilities resulting in leakages and roads caving in—three days ago a part of a road at Jacob circle caved in killing three— the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) is planning to purchase Ground Penetrating Radars (GPR) which will enable it identify leakages without actually digging roads.

There are a number of utility lines- water, storm water drains, sewerage which were laid during the British rule. Also there are cable lines of service providers. However, detection of the crumbling old pipelines becomes difficult due to heavy traffic and layers of Cement Concrete or asphalt. With the help of a GPR, leakages can be identified by just moving the machine on the surface.

Additional Municipal Commissioner, (Projects), Anil Diggikar said the civic administration is in discussion with a few companies. He said, "We will be given a demonstration in a few days which will enable us to know how efficient the GPRs are in locating leakages." If the use of the machines is feasible, BMC will take the opinion of experts and IIT- Bombay, after which tenders will be invited. If approved, then BMC may purchase around six GPR machines to be used in six zones across the city at a cost of around Rs 60 lakh each. GPR uses radar pulses to image the subsurface through electromagnetic radiation in the microwave band (UHF/VHF frequencies) of the radio spectrum, and detects the reflected signals from subsurface structures.

Municipal Commissioner, Jairaj Phatak said that since the island city—Colaba to Mahim— was made by reclaiming land and has utilities from the British era, the incidents of leakages are high there. "This problem is not as much in western and eastern suburbs as the utilities are newly laid," he said.

There is around 2000-2,500 km of underground water pipeline network in the island city, which was laid in the British era. Officials from the water department said it becomes difficult to verify which underground utility has a problem. "GPR gives a radar-gram as its result in which the underground utilities conditions are depicted and leakages are identified," said Deputy Municipal Commissioner (Water supply), Pramod Charankar.

He also pointed out that GPR will only be able to provide a rough indication.

"The GPR data will have to be correlated. The machine will only gives us radar-grams of all utilities but which utility actually has leakages will still have to be determined," he added.

Heading: No discrimination against HIV-positive man, say JJ Hospital authorities - Indian Express
Content:
Keeping in mind the ongoing threat perception in the city and the terror strikes at hospitals in Ahmedabad last month, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) on Friday decided to step up security at civic hospitals. The civic body on Thursday recognized the need of special squads which will look into the identification of visitors and relatives, crowd control and vehicle checking. "The need of the hour is tight security in hospitals. For this, the BMC consulted medical representatives from the three civic hospitals and have come up with short and long term goals," said Additional Municipal Commissioner Madhav Sangle.

As part of their short-term goals, the civic body has decided to issue stickers and identification cards to all staff members. "We will issue stickers and identification cards to our staff and their vehicles. This is to regularise traffic and identify staff vehicles from the rest, for now these stickers will be plain stickers but by 2009 we will have bar coded stickers which will further tighten out security measures," said Sangle.

BMC has also decided to regularize parking places inside hospital premises. Additional Municipal Commissioner Kishore Gajbhiye said, "As of now parking places are scattered around the premises, now we will club all these points and have one or two parking places inside the hospital meant only for the staff, visitors' vehicles will be parked outside unless it is carrying a patient."

BMC has also planned to install metal detectors and door frames at entry and exit points for screening visitors and their belongings. Also CCTVs will be installed within a month's time. As part of its crowd control measures, the civic body has decided to restrict the number of visitors with patients to one or two. "We will ask patients and visitors not to come in groups. We will also strictly ask them to follow the timings. Though these norms are there no one practices them. We will also install bells inside the hospitals to warn visitors of the time limit," said Sangle.

The civic body has decided to increase security personnel at police chowkies manning the hospitals and provide them with equipment for faster communication. "There will be an increase in the number of security staff manning the police chowkies, we will also provide them with walkie-talkies so there is easy communication among the staff," added Sangle.

At present, the BMC has decided to adopt these measures at the main civic hospitals-KEM, Sion and Nair Hospital. "We will first adopt these measures at the main civic hospitals, after gauging their performance we will replicate the measures at the periphery hospitals," said Gajbhiye.

Heading: Scrap dealer held for passing off Buddha idol as smuggled antique - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the Supreme Court asked the Centre Health Ministry and the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO) to reply to the petition filed by a HIV positive person in Mumbai, the JJ hospital Anti Retroviral Treatment (ART) chief Dr Alka Deshpande refuted that such discrimination would occur on caste, creed or region lines in the hospital. She said the hospital authorities must have communicated the formal guidelines laid down by the NACO about extending the second line of drugs to patients from medical colleges in Mumbai, as it was a pilot period.

Drawing the attention of a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan, Senior Advocate Colin Gonsalves on Thursday sought immediate intervention from the court, which has posted the matter for further directions on September 29.

The senior counsel appearing for a patient who's a native of Bihar, told the court that the state did not have the requisite drug and line of treatment for such patients. Coming to know of this, the HIV-infected person moved to Mumbai. But, the city's JJ hospital allegedly refused treatment on the ground that he was not a Maharashtrian, the court was informed.

"I don't think that this patient approached us as we have no data about him. A relative or someone on behalf him might have approached us. We tell all the patients hailing from outside Mumbai that the second line of drugs are being given to patients from the four medical colleges in Mumbai as per the NACO guidelines," said Dr Alka Deshpande, ART chief at the JJ hospital. "Moreover, one of the conditions in the guidelines is that the patient must have been under Anti Retroviral Treatment (ART) for six months and he/ she should come through the respective NACO-run ART centre."

Dr Deshpande further elucidated the examples of patients from Ratnagiri and other parts of the state. She said they were not allowed to take second line of drugs as the pilot is only for Mumbai colleges.

As per the current guidelines, HIV positive persons are selected for second line of drugs after thorough evaluation by a team and they fulfill all the conditions for starting the treatment.

Heading: Six burglars arrested - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Thursday arrested a scrap dealer for attempting to cheat people into buying an idol of the Buddha for Rs30 lakh by passing it off as an antique. The police are now on the lookout for the man from whom the scrap dealer sourced the idol.

The arrested accused has been identified as Mallaude Saifuffin Ansari (30), a resident of Bainganwadi in Govandi. He was arrested by the Ghatkopar Unit of the Crime Branch. The Buddha idol has been seized. "Crime Branch officers received specific information that someone was trying to sell an antique idol that had been smuggled in from Kathmandu for an amount of Rs 30 lakh. We put forward a dummy customer who approached Ansari and told him he wanted to buy the idol. They negotiated the price and it was brought down to Rs 25 lakh. Ansari asked the dummy customer to pay Rs 5 lakh , and pay the remaining amount the following day. Our officers then moved in and arrested him," said Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime, Rakesh Maria.

According to the Crime Branch, the seized Buddha idol is nine inches high, and weighs 9.35 kg. The police had sent it to the Archaeological Survey of India for an expert opinion. "The experts told us that the idol was made of copper and bronze. It's only worth between Rs 30,000 and Rs 40,000. We're on the lookout for one Raheem Shaikh who sold the idol to Ansari," Maria said.

Heading: Anti-smoking law highly impractical: Civic body - Indian Express
Content:
The Goregoan police arrested a gang of five burglars along with their ringleader recently. According to the police, the gang operated mainly in Goregoan (east) and used to steal spare parts of vehicles from the godowns in the area. At times, they also targeted homes mostly in the Virvani Industrial area, said the police.

"They used to gain entry into the godowns by breaking the locks with iron crowbars. Their ringleader Muhammed Younis Aka Laden was arrested from the Kurla Bus Terminus on September 8, while he was boarding a train to his hometown Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh. As many as 18 housebreaking cases are registered against him," said the police.

During his interrogation, we came to know about his associates Firoz Khan(20), Muhamad Khan (22), Vajid Khan (21) and Durgaprasad Gupta (24) and arrested them from their houses near Ambedkar chowk in Goregoan, said the police. According to the Goregoan police, they have seized brass, copper and iron spare parts worth around Rs 7,21,628 from the accused.

" There are 15 cases registered against Laden in 2008. Three other housebreaking cases were registered against

him in 2007 also. Many similar cases have been registered in police stations like Dindoshi and we suspect the same gang's involvement in them. After Laden's arrest, we could arrest other accused also," said Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 12) Ajit Patil. According to him, the gang members used to sell these spare parts to various scrap dealers and earn money.

"We have recovered the stolen materials from their houses as well as some scrap dealers' houses," added Patil.

Heading: Yashaswini provides market interface to women living below poverty line - Indian Express
Content:
In less than a month, the much awaited law against smoking at workplaces and public places will come into force and according to a survey commissioned by Healis- Sekhsaria Institue for Public Health, over 96 per cent of people want a smoke-free Mumbai. The new law will come into force from October 2.

However, Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has a different take on the issue and feels that the implementation of the law will be highly impractical.

Even though the anti-smoking laws exist in the country, the government has struggled to enforce them. "Problem is that a vast area is to be covered. With the given infrastructure, it is not possible for the BMC's health department to implement the law," said Dr Jairaj Thanekar, executive health officer, BMC. If someone is caught smoking, the person would be made to pay a fine of Rs 200 as per the National Tobacco Control Act.

The law does not include parks, beaches and roads as these are open spaces. Even as doctors welcome the regulation, they admit that the quantum of the fine is less. "If one carefully interprets the law, even if the smoker gets away by paying a paltry amount Rs 200 at a hotel, hotel managers have to pay Rs 5,000 for each incident of smoking at the prohibited area of hotel or restaurant," said Dr Shastri who was one of the key persons in framing the law.

However, Mumbai's masses, as the survey shows, think otherwise. The survey encompassed smokers and non-smokers and was carried out in Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.

The survey was conducted on a randomly selected sample of 1030 Indians aged between 15 and 64. They were interviewed in the month of August. "Eleven per cent of the total interviewed persons were smokers and majority were males. All were in favour of the law," said Dr P C Gupta, director, Healis- Sekhsaria Institue for Public Health.

Mumbai along with Delhi and Chennai will also kick start a 'smoke-free Mumbai' campaign. Tata Memorial Hospital, the premier cancer institute in Asia, funded by Bloomberg Foundation has planned a number activities to make Mumbai smoke free as a run up to the 14th World Conference on Tobacco and Health scheduled in March next year. "Apart from other campaigns, advertisements in newspapers and electronic media will be issued in public interest," said Dr Surendra Shastri, professor and head, department of preventive oncology, Tata Memorial Hospital.

The dos and dont's

Effective from October 2, the new law banning smoking in public places and workplaces will be applicable to hotels, restaurants, coffee houses, pubs, bars, airport lounges, workplaces shopping malls, cinema halls, educational institutions, libraries, hospitals, auditorium, open auditoriums, amusement centers, stadium, railway stations, bus stop. Individuals in charge of public places and workplaces will be held responsible for complying with the law.

They need to ensure, smoking is permitted in rooms physically separated and surrounded by full height walls. The rooms should have an entrance with doors that close automatically and an air system that is exhausted directly outside.

The rooms should have negative air pressure in comparison to the remaining part of the building and no food and beverage should be served there.

All designated smoking areas should be prominently placed away from entrance and exits of building also signages on smoking restrictions need to be prominently placed.

No ashtrays, matches and lighters to be provided.

Persons authorized for collecting fines-

Public places: Tax inspectors, health directors, central/ state administration heads, anti-tobacco nodal officers.

Railways: Station leaders

Government officers: Gazettes officers

Hospitals: Hospital heads

Poast offices: Post masters

Private offices/workplace: Office head (managers, administration heads)

Educational institutions: Principals, teachers

Libraries: Library heads, assistants and librarians

Airports: managers, airport/ airline officers)

Heading: Govt backs BMC on killing stray dogs - Indian Express
Content:
It is not only the MBAs who are benefitting from the new retail chains, women mostly in their thirties united by their miseries are tasting success like never before.

Women's self-group manufacturing and selling home made masalas, hand pounded rice, amla candy and a variety of pappad surviving on a shoestring budget and a multi-million mega retail chain seems like two ends of a spectrum. However, the twain has met with the Project Yashaswini, an initiative by Member of Parliament Supriya Sule under the banner of Yashawantrao Chavan Foundation. "We have tied up with Big Bazaar, which, besides showcasing the products manufactured by the self-help groups, has also placed major orders worth Rs 3.5 crore," said Supriya Sule. There are about 220 self-help groups spanning all the districts of the state engaged in producing food and non-food products. According to Damodar Mall, group customer director of Future Group, the company promoting Big Bazaar, the retail chain in its first order has procured from the self-help group what the women would have taken a year or more to produce. The retail chain hosts yatras four days in a month where about 35 self-help groups get an opportunity to showcase their products."Big Bazaar provides the self-help groups the platform to showcase their products in a highly competitive environment. We place orders for products that get good response," said Mall.

The retail chain ensures that the self-groups meet the high standards of quality of content and packaging. Women's self help group in all districts in the state are getting an opportunity to showcase their products at Big Bazaar four days in a month. "There is a big demand for traditional and regional food. As life gets busier, modern women only yearn for traditional food. On the other hand there are housewivies who have knowledge of traditional recipes. Big Bazaar connects the two worlds together," said Mall.

"This is an unique initiative where all the districts in Maharashtra, including women from nomadic tribe in Vidarbha, to women living below poverty line in Mumbai, get an opportunity to validate their work. This initiative provides them a market interface like never before," said Tejaswini Adhikari, a former TISS faculty and human resource analyst for Yashaswini.

Infact the tremendous response received by the initiative in Maharashtra is making Big Bazaar consider taking up such initiatives in other states such as Tamil Nadu and Gujarat. "The beauty of the project is that it enables the empowerment of women in a holistic manner. Women self-help groups do not require charity. They need avenues to showcase their abilities. Yashaswini precisely does that," said Sule.

Heading: Delight at dusk - Indian Express
Content:
The state government has extended support to the BMC regarding validity of the BMC Act which gives them powers to kill stray dogs. According to provisions in section 191 B A (2) of the Municipal Corporation Act, the Municipal Commissioner at his discretion may sell, provide shelter or even destroy stray dogs. BMC had earlier stated that it had the powers to kill stray dogs.

Today, the BMC also stated before a full bench of the Bombay High Court about the huge financial constraints connected with the rehabilitation of stray dogs in dog shelters. BMC also contended that there is no need for additional dog shelters as they have kennels and dogs can also be given for adoption.

However, the NGOs and animal activists contend that the provision under the Corporation Act is against Article 51 A (g) of the Constitution of India which says that it is the fundamental duty of every citizen be compassionate to animals.

The court has adjourned the hearing till September 30.

Earlier, an affidavit filed by joint executive health officer G T Ambe had stated that "Maintenance of stray dogs in the dog shelter would involve huge expenditure running into crores of rupees which would be a huge financial strain on the MCGM. It is questionable whether MCGM should spend crores of rupees on feeding stray dogs when we do not do so for the poor in Mumbai, who are starving."

Ambe further stated that "Municipal Corporation feeding dogs certainly does not deserve more priority than the poor people of Mumbai." The court was also informed that as per the dog census of October 2007, there are 70,182 stray dogs in Mumbai and 26,900 are pets.

Heading: Meal ticket - Indian Express
Content:
Iftaar not only brings family and friends together but also offers a range of mouth-watering delicacies

As the day draws down and the muezzin's azan resonates, the crowd in its devout grandeur gathers in various locales breaking the fast among the scrumptious delicacies and in the most tempting atmosphere. Peer into the inner lanes of the city, where the waft of tasty foods and lip-smacking delicacies await. Be it roasted chicken, seekh kebabs or malpoaa, every dish would definitely get your taste buds dancing. The holy month of Ramzan signifies supplication, upholds charity and inquests delicacies.

The Babajaan chowk, Sharbatwala chowk, the Poona college vicinity and Mominpura are some of the prime areas of hustle and bustle during the month of Ramzan. People from across the city assemble not only to relish but also vend their wares.

As one walks into the lanes of Mominpura, a queue of food-vendors is ready to take you for a treat. The counter of Rahil Caterers, one of the oldest eatery in the area, you surely cannot resist your temptation to eat. "For Ramzan we have a special stall and menu, the buzz starts at around 5 pm and we are open till 2 am. The most popular dishes are chicken tandoori, chicken cutlet, kadi ghosht, chicken dum biryani and most important the various kebabs. Dalcha khana is our speciality. My grandfather first started it here. We are into this business since the last 30 years," says Shaik Ali Abdul Karim, the owner of Rahil Caterers, as he unremittingly takes the orders.

Drinks and shakes also form one of the hors d'oeuvre, with strawberry and chocolate flavoured milkshakes, falooda and so on. Tahura Cold Drinks is one of many stalls that sell the most novel Hyderabadi cold drink. "It is a popular drink during Ramzan. A lot of youngsters come here. It has been there for the last 15 years," says Shaikh Azhar.

Mohammad Shafiq sells samosas on Kasbapeth throughout the year however during Ramzan the stall shifts its location as well as the content. "I sell dates during Ramzan. I have ten different varieties from Iran, Saudi, Medina, Arab and so on. The price varies from Rs 50 - Rs 250 per kg," adds Shafiq.

The dusk also calls out the family members to assemble to proffer prayers and indulge into the cuisine that the women have been cooking through the day. Anjum Shaikh, HR, Fortune Placement, is joined by 10 other kin during the Iftaar. "The white cloth-dastarkhan is spread on which we have the grand dinner. Dates are a must while we break the fast, which are at times replaced by salt. There are two to three delicacies every day in addition to the main course. Starters have to be kebabs, potato wedges or any fried stuff. Biryani follows and the most preferred desserts are malpoaa, sheera and sevai. We may stuff ourselves throughout the night but the day begins with nothing more than a cup of tea and toast or plain coconut water," adds Shaikh.
