"It is always hard to score consistently but I am hoping for the best. My batting has improved a lot nut like I said earlier I still need to work out on my weakness. It's good to know that I was the top scorer in last year's Ranji trophy. There's still one month left for the Ranji Trophy to commence. I will definitely try to carry my form in Buchi Babu ahead," says the prolific scorer who has been praised my veterans like Dravid and Kiran More.

Always a future prospect, Cheteshwar came into the limelight with a mammoth unbeaten 306 (540m, 516b, 36x4) in a West Zone Under-14 match against Baroda in 2000-01. Runs followed from his willow and soon he was the mainstay of the Saurashtra team which had an impressive run last year; all due to Cheteshwar who emerged as the highest scorer in the Ranji Trophy. "People think that I am more suited to Test than ODIs but let me clear one thing that I was the highest run scorer in Under-19 World Cup in Sri Lanka (he was the player of the tournament) and last year also I scored in excess of 450 odd runs. I have also talked to many coaches to improve my batting in ODIs. Besides that Ihave also done well in Twenty20 cricket," says Pujara.

His team mates from the World Cup team, Piyush Chawla and Rohit Sharma has already made it into the Indian team. Even Virat Kohli has donned the Indian colour. So doesn't he feel left out or dejected? "It's the selectors' decision. They did well and got the reward. It's not late for me. I am performing well and if I continue this way then I have got enough chance to play for the Indian team. I am waiting for that opportunity," says the right handed batsman and a part time bowler.

Apart from Ranji Trophy, it is the New Zealand series that he is looking forward to. 'Apart from the Ranji Trophy and New Zealand series in 2009 I haven't thought about anything," adds Pujara. The IPL enigma is something which he still hasn't been able to figure out. "I don't know what went wrong last year. I didn't get a chance to play any game. Hopefully this year will be different," says Pujara who signed three year contract with Kolkata Knight Riders last year.

Heading: Punjab Gold Cup 4-nation hockey approved by FIH - Indian Express
Content:
Olympian Sushil Kumar was felicitated by 'Gulzar Akhara' near Zirakpur on Saturday. "Sushil has not only brought laurels to the country but inspired the younger generation to take up wrestling and make a name for them in this sport." said Ranbir Singh Kundu, organiser and coach of Gulzar Akhara.

Sushil was accompanied by two coaches Ram Chander and Yashbir Singh of Satpal Akhara. As many as 40 wrestlers from the akhara welcomed their hero on an open jeep. The function was attended by many persons from adjoining villages. Apart from the akhara, State Bank of India also honoured the star grappler with a memento and a bouqet. Sushil also interacted with the wrestlers shared tips with them. The akhara has been a nursery for the budding wrestlers and have produced wrestlers who have done well in various junior international tournaments.

Heading: Carmel Convent, GHMS paddlers clinch TT titles - Indian Express
Content:
The International Hockey Federation (FIH) has accorded approval to the Punjab Gold Cup Men Four-Nation Invitational Double Leg Hockey Tournament to be hosted by the Punjab Sports Department from February 5 to 14 next year.

According to Punjab Sports Director Pargat Singh, FIH General Manager Christophe Troendle has conveyed the sanction to ad hoc committee of the Indian Hockey Confederation. Besides hosts India, Pakistan, Holland and German teams would be seen in action in the double leg to be played at the Sector 42 Hockey Stadium in Chandigarh and the second leg, classification match and final will be staged at the Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar.

The Punjab Sports Department will provide to and fro air fare for 22 members, including one umpire of each team, free board and lodging and local transport.

Pargat Singh said that the double-leg series would be professionally managed. Expert agencies will be associated for the smooth and professional conduct of the tournament. Expert agencies would be associated and the matches would be telecast live.

Meanwhile, the Punjab Sports Department has also requested the International Hockey Federation through Mrs Amrit Bose of Indian Hockey Confederation, for sanction to organise an invitational Four-National Women hockey tournament in the last week of April, next year.

Besides hosts India, three national teams from Argentina, Australia, New Zealand, Australia, Holland and Germany will compete in the double-leg tournament in Jalandhar.

Heading: Wong to meet Tushar in boys’ u-10 final - Indian Express
Content:

Carmel Convent defeated KC Public School of Jammu by 3-1 in the girls' under-19 final. GHMS-38 also recorded an identical 3-1 verdict against DAV Public School, Sector in the boys' under-19 team championship final.

Rajeshwari stole the show in the girls' Under-19 team championship final against KC Public School as she won both her matches. She prevailed over Tanvi by 11-4, 10-12, 11-4, 11-6 to give her team the lead. Harjasleen then defeated Lavanya by 11-9, 11-4, 11-9 in the second singles. However, Ishita lost to Sandeep 3-11, 6-11, 5-11. That was the only game the Jammu and Kashmir school won in the final. Rajeshwari then wrapped up the final with a fluent 11-6, 11-9, 11-3 against Lavanya as Carmel Convent registered a 3-1 win. SD Public School of Ambala Cantonment blanked Bhavan Vidayalaya of Panchkula by 3-0 to finish third in the girls under-19 team championship.

Dev Saini performed well as he won both his matches to enable GHMS-38 defeat DAV Public School, Sector 8 by 3-1 in the boys under-19 team championship final. Sameer Singla put GHMS in the lead by beating Rajan Mahindra by 11-8, 8-11, 11-9, 11-6 in the opening singles match.

Heading: After the deluge, the damage - Indian Express
Content: The 15th All India J P Atray Memorial Cricket Tournament is likely to get underway on Sunday with LIC Cricket Club taking on Rajasthan Cricket Association at PCA Stadium, Mohali, Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association locking horns with BPCL at Sector-16 Cricket Stadium, and Moody ICL taking on MRF at DAV Sector-8. Heading: FAR too good: More height, floor area for multiplexes - Indian Express
Content:
After a record 181 mm of rain lashed the tricity in the last two days, only damaged and potholed roads greeted the residents on Saturday. Although, the showers subsided, sporadic spells of rain continued the entire day. Exposing the shoddy repair work recently carried out by the Engineering department, cracks appeared at several places in the road leading from the Tribune roundabout to the Transport chowk.

UT Chief Engineer S K Jaitley told Newsline: "It will take at least 10 days to repair the damage. We had filled the cracks in the roads just a few days ago. The material apparently did not bind well and with the continued onslaught of rain, potholes have cropped up."

To the chagrin of daily commuters, traffic snarls were the order of the day. A road in Industrial Area Phase 1, near the CTU workshop, was closed to traffic to carry out repairs. But as the authorities neglected to put up a diversion sign in advance, the harried drivers traversed the full distance of the broken road only to realise it was closed.

"After the rains, the city seems paved with mud. The Administration must make preparations to deal with the rains in advance. The monsoon is not new — it hits the city every year and the authorities should know what to expect," said Rajiv Dutta, a resident of Sector 29.

Meanwhile, work to repair the Kishangarh bridge and Bapu Dham bridge, which had collapsed on Friday, continued till 7 pm today. "Water is also being drained out from houses in the colonies and slums," said MC Chief Engineer S K Bansal.

Panchkula

* The low-lying witnessed major waterlogging with Sectors 2,4, 10, 12, 12-A, 16, 17, 19 and 21 being the worst affected.

* Water entered several houses in Rajiv colony, Indira colony and Kharak Mangoli.

MOHALI

* Several areas were submerged under knee-deep water and several old buildings were damaged.

* Deep potholes and cracks have appeared on the busy Mohali-Kharar National Highway-21.

* Several villages along the Sutlej-Yamuna Link Canal flooded.

KHARAR

* Angry residents of Ward 5 in Kharar blocked traffic on the Kharar-Banur road on Saturday morning to protest the flooding of their locality. Municipal councillor Jai Bhagwan Singla promised immediate relief to the residents. Consequently, an hour later civil officials reached the spot and drained out the excess water.

* The bridges on Patiala Ki Rao and Jayanti Ki Rao in Mullanpur Garibdass, Kharar and other villages in the district also developed cracks and were closed for vehicular traffic.

Heading: ChaTtbir Zoo A den of problems - Indian Express
Content:
In a decision that will leave several cinema hall owners (who have approached the authorities for converting the theaters into multiplexes) smiling, the UT Administration has fixed the height of multiplexes at 62.3 feet. An additional Floor Area Ratio (FAR) of 50 per cent (taking the figure to above 2) was also approved.

Most of the existing cinema halls in the city are around 55 feet in height and have an FAR between 1.5 and 2, said an official. The modalities of parking are still being worked out with the likelihood of allowing two vehicles for every 15 seats, he added.

UT Chief Architect, Sunita Monga, told Newsline: "Requests had been consistently pouring in from multiplex owners to allow them the additional height and FAR. The decision will apply to all halls that go in for conversion now. A drift from these parameters will be allowed only if there are special architecture concerns, as in the case of KC cinema."

In Industrial Area, the multiplexes and malls enjoy a lower margin — the Administration has allowed the multiplexes to go up to 100 feet in height.

Heading: Cong files complaint, says babus siphoned off NREGS funds - Indian Express
Content:
The sight of a solitary lion lounging in one corner of the 18-acre Lion Safari at Chattbir Zoo, located on the outskirts of Chandigarh, sums up the state of affairs inside.

Once a delightful experience for visitors, India's largest fenced zoological park now sports a deserted look.

For long having served as home to over a hundred big cats, today their number has fallen to 11, most of them aged and ailing.

The zoo, spread over 505 hectares, houses several rare species including white tigers, horned antelopes, a lion-tailed macaque and a jaguar.

Dying animals

The incidents of animals dying have become far too frequent in the recent past raising questions about the prevailing state of affairs in the zoo.

On Sunday, a tigress was found dead in its enclosure. A few months ago, an ailing old Asian lion breathed his last.

In September 2006, two Royal Bengal white tigers died one after the other due to a parasite infection.

The decline has largely been attributed to inbreeding — a practice that was overlooked by officials when the lion population was swelling at the zoo. "Inbreeding eventually led to biological deformities in several lions. It was then decided to sterilise the entire lot to prevent further damage," said a zoo official.

Chief Wildlife Warden of Punjab, M P Rai, said: "Mortality is a natural phenomenon. Most of the lions were aged and had lived their life. The death of a few was the fallout of inbreeding."

Zoo officials claim tigers are immune to the ravages of inbreeding, still retaining the distinction of being genetically pure.

Acute staff shortage

Staff shortage has hit the upkeep of over 966 animal and bird species inside the zoo. Against the sanctioned posts of 21 zookeepers, there are just 15 zookeepers managing 19 animal complexes on the premises.

Part of the zookeeper's job is to let the animals out into the wild every morning and as sun sets, to ensure all are inside their complexes. Also, a veterinary doctor is supposed to physically scan all animals for injuries every evening. "The exercise is invariably lax. Many at times, the zookeepers double up as vets as well," said an official.

The lacuna has taken its toll. In April, a Rosy Pelican died after its backbone broke after a zookeeper tried to push it inside its enclosure at dusk. The zookeeper, temporarily assigned the task, was later suspended.

Elephants are taken care of by mauhawats, who are half their sanctioned strength. "The zoo has an annual budget of about Rs 3.5 crore, a major part of which is spent on paying salaries," said an official.

2003 probe

In 2003, questions were raised on the quality and quantity of meat supplied to the zoo as well as the procurement cost. A probe was ordered and Zoo Director, Dr Vinod Sharma, was booked for the alleged irregularities. The case is still pending in court.

Heading: Falling wires have claimed over 1,000 lives in two years - Indian Express
Content:
Seven principal secretaries and the chief secretary of the Uttar Pradesh government have been accused of misappropriating and siphoning off Rs 350 crore allotted for a special plantation project under the NREGA.

In a complaint lodged by UPCC president Rita Bahuguna Joshi with Hazratganj police station on Saturday, principal secretaries of department of forest, housing, public work department, irrigation, power, panchayati raj and horticulture have been named as the accused.

The state-level NREGA monitoring committee of the Congress claimed to have found serious irregularities in the implementation of the Act in the seven districts of the Bundelkhand region — Jhansi, Chitrakoot, Banda, Lalitpur, Mahoba, Hamirpur, and Jalaun. Names of the district magistrates, chief development officers, divisional forest officers of these districts along with commissioners of Jhansi and Chitrakoot have also been included in the complaint.

Terming the plantation project as fake, Joshi said, "Our committee has counted the trees and found that the government has planted only 30 to 50 per cent plants out of the total 10 crore plants stipulated by the government order."

The state government, through a May 14 government order, initiated the special plantation project, pegged at Rs 413 crore. The state government has already availed Rs 219 crore from the central government under the NREGA.

"We found that the minimum wage provisions of the NREGA were being openly flouted by the officials. The labourers were paid Rs 20 to 30 per day for digging 66 cubic feet surface as against the minimum wage of Rs 100," Joshi said.

The committee claimed that their complaint is backed by video recordings of the interviews of villagers who were paid only a fraction of the wages they were entitled to. "Since more than half of the plants have not been planted, the scam amounts to around 200 crores and another 100 crore come out of the deflated wages paid to the labourers," Joshi said.

Further, she alleged that the ministers concerned were also involved in the irregularities. "We will meet Governor T V Rajeswer on Sunday and will present our report to him," she added.

Heading: Rain claims 42 lives in Sitapur - Indian Express
Content:
The death of an employee of Lucknow Electricity Supply Administration (LESA) on Friday, while he was repairing a traffic light amid rains, has again brought in to focus the risk-prone conditions in which these electricians work.

Rameshwar Shukla is not the first casualty involving LESA employee or a commoner in the state capital. In the last two years, there have been 2,572 accidents in which 1,090 people have died. [see box] While the LESA authorities are passing the buck claiming that Shukla was not asked to repair the traffic light, the city is witness to a number of such electrocution incidents in which innocent people fall prey to the carelessness of the part of the authorities.

Majority of these cases are due to breaking of overhead high tension electricity line. In 2006-07, accident caused by overhead lines stood at 404. This year the number has already risen to 409.

An official study revealed that the increasing number of fatal accidents due to breakage of electrical wires is due to the substandard material which various governments have purchased over the years without following standard design specification norms and safety norms. The fact was revealed from an official study conducted by the Equipment Quality Control Committee and Investigating Authority comprising experts from IIT Kanpur and officials of the UP government.

On Saturday, LESA Chief Engineer KB Ram said the contractor, for whom Shukla was working, would pay the family of the victim Rs 50,000. The compensation, however, for such victims is Rs 1 lakh. If a person is badly injured or disabled, then also a compensation of Rs 1 lakh is to be awarded to the victim's family. In case of animal deaths, the compensation is Rs 5,000.

The family of Shukla, meanwhile, remained inconsolable and blamed the authorities for his death. "It is nothing but the fault of the administration. I do not want any compensation. It will not bring my husband back. How will I raise my children without him? We neither have any property nor any other source of income," said Sita Devi, Shukla's wife.

Heading: International fake currency racket busted, 6 held - Indian Express
Content:
The incessant rain on Friday claimed 42 lives in Sitapur district. The deceased included seven women and five children. The district administration has announced a compensation of Rs 1 lakh to the family of each of the deceased.

District Magistrate of Sitapur, Mritunjay Kumar Narayan, said: "Majority of the deaths were caused by wall collapse in different areas of the six tehsils in the district. The incidents took place late on Friday night. The administration is providing food packets to the affected families."

The staff of the community health centres has been instructed to visit the villages in their respective areas and take stock of the situation, Narayan said. The details with DM office stated that the areas where the deaths occurred were —Mishrikh, Biswan, Laharpur, Reusa, Sidhauli, Rampur Kala, Mehmoodabad, Sadarpur and Thangaon.

Superintendent of Police, Sitapur, V K Dohre said they came to know about the toll on Saturday morning and immediately sent police teams for the rescue work.

Heading: ‘Bell Bajao’ campaign hits Lucknow roads - Indian Express
Content:
In a major breakthrough, the Allahabad police on Saturday busted an international gang involved in the supply of fake currency notes.

The cops arrested six persons, including the alleged kingpin, Shamsul Haq, and recovered fake currency notes of face value Rs 1, 50, 800. Five stolen motorbikes, one computer and other fake papers related with vehicle and life insurance schemes were also seized from them.

In a pre-dawn raid, a police team led by Kareli police station officer K K Mishra arrested Haq from Karamat Ki Chauki. Based on the information given by him during interrogation, the police later arrested Sameer alias Tabraiz of Gorakhpur, Satish Sharma of Pratapgarh, Firoz Ansari and Mohd Yusuf of Colonelganj, Allahabad and Atiqur Rehman of Kareli.

The police said during interrogation, the accused confessed that they were in contact with gangs operating in Pakistan, Bhutan, Nepal and Bangladesh and had been supplying fake currency in Allahabad, Pratapgarh, Gorakhpur and other surrounding districts.

The police recovered 69 notes of 1,000 denomination, besides 146 notes of 500 denomination and 88 notes of 100 denominations from their possession.

Senior Superintendent of Police Lalji Shukla said fake notes were printed in Nepal and Pakistan and were supplied into India through the bordering districts of Behraich, Gonda, Sidharth Nagar and Gorakhpur. Shukla also announced a cash reward to the police team.

Heading: Number of dengue cases spirals in the state, touches 158 mark - Indian Express
Content:
What do you do when you hear your neighbour beating up his wife? Or you notice a woman crying for help from a house as you pass by? Most of us reply "nothing" or just say — "Why should I interfere in other people's lives?" In the last two weeks, over 3,000 Lucknow residents have been told that they can contribute towards curbing domestic violence by simply ringing the doorbell of the victim's house.

Delhi-based organisation 'Breakthrough Communications', which has also made a video titled Mann Ke Manjeere featuring Mita Vashisth, launched Bell Bajao campaign in Lucknow and nearby areas on September 7.

The campaign, which has also been launched in Karnataka and Maharashtra, informs people that by just ringing a doorbell one can make a difference in curbing incidents of domestic violence. The Bell Bajao van doing the rounds of the city uses street plays and films to make people aware of the need to stop domestic violence.

"Once you ring a doorbell, incidents of domestic violence is likely to come down. You can then move inside the house telling the family members how domestic violence can lead to a jail sentence," said Anuj Gopal Dubey, a volunteer of the campaign.

He said that every day on an average three to five women, who are victims of domestic violence, share their woes with them.

"We have realised that despite being the state capital, Lucknow has reported high incidents of domestic violence. We not only try to counsel the victims who

turn up to share their problems with us, but also give them references of organisations who can help them.

We will be personally following up these cases with the organisations as well," Dubey added.

From September 21, the campaign will focus on suburbs like Sarojini Nagar block, Malihabad and Kakori. "We will also take the campaign to a large number of cities like Moradabad, Aligarh and Muzzafarnagar which report highest incidents of violence against women in UP and even North India," said Priyanka Sarkar of Breakthrough Communications.

Heading: Class VIII girl raped by 2 classmates - Indian Express
Content:
With the number of dengue cases touching 158, a rising trend of the disease has been noticed in the state based on the threefold increase in the number of patients in the last one week.

As compared to 67 cases recorded from various districts on September 12, the statewide tally touched 192 today. Of them, 158 patients are from the state while the rest (34) are cases from other states but diagnosed in the state.

Notably, about half the cases reported to the Integrated Disease Surviellance Project by various district surveillance units have come from Ludhiana where 77 cases of dengue have been identified so far.

Various major hospitals in Ludhiana have so far recorded over 200 suspected cases of dengue, the confirmatory reports of which are still awaited. While the Christian Medical College and Hospital has registered 70 suspected cases of the disease so far, Dayanand Medical College and Hospital has recorded 180.

"The rising trend means that there can be a substantial addition to the figure in the days to come. Till October 15, nothing can be precisely predicted," a health expert noted. Ludhiana is followed by Mohali with 33 cases and Patiala with 18 cases.

In 2006, only 28 cases of dengue were reported from the state as per the Integrated Disease Surveillance Project (IDSP) statistics. In 2006, however, the number had crossed 1,000 mark and had settled at 1152.

Project Coordinator of IDSP, Dr Deepak Bhatia said that the rising trend was a cause for concern and therefore the report is being sent daily to the central unit of the project of the Government of India, which in routine is sent weekly.

"Although the number of cases is not alarming, there is definitely a cause for concern as the number is rising every day," said Dr Bhatia, who added that the most cases were being reported from Ludhiana as the city is an industrial town and the stagnant water is also a problem in the urban areas.

"As compared to the number of cases of dengue in the rural area, the most number of patients of dengue are reported from urban areas because there is more filth in the urban areas," he added. Asked about cases of gastroenteritis, he said that it was well under control.

Heading: Kids show the literacy path to their parents - Indian Express
Content:
A student of Class VIII was reportedly raped by two of her classmates today. The crime took place in the ground of the Government College for Boys.

The Division Number 5 police have arrested one of the accused and registered a rape case. The hunt to nab the second accused is still on. According to information, the incident occurred this afternoon when the victim was coming back from her government school in the Civil Lines area after taking her exams. The police sources said the duo met the girl on the way. They enticed her and took her to an isolated area of the ground of the Government College for Boys where they raped her. Sources said that while one boy raped her, the other boy gagged her so that she could not raise an alarm.

After committing the crime, the duo fled from the spot after giving Rs 10 to the victim. They also threatened her with dire consequences if she reported the matter to anyone. They left the girl in a critical condition as her private parts were bleeding and she could barely walk. Some students of the college spotted the girl with her tattered clothes. The girl was rushed to the Civil Hospital and the police were informed.

The Division number 5 SHO Shavinder Singh Dhillon told Newsline one accused has been arrested while the hunt to nab the second accused is on. He added that the medical examination had confirmed rape.

According to legal experts, as both the accused happen to be minors, their case will be tried by a special court meant for juveniles.

Heading: Here residents are charged for throwing litter in MC dump - Indian Express
Content:
Although shopkeepers at the Akalgarh market have been told to remove their illegal encroachments, no action has been taken against them till date. This has been admitted by deputy commissioner Sumer Singh Gurjar while submitting an affidavit in response to a PIL in the High Court. Gurjar has clearly stated that a three-member committee comprising of SDM (East), MC joint commissioner and the SP City had asked the shopkeepers to remove the encroachments from the market. The matter had been resolved but later the shopkeepers again made illegal encroachments in front of their shops.

In addition to this, the affidavit also states that there is no parking facility in the market, which has over 840 shops, a hospital running in a basement and a gurdwara. He also stated that it is the duty of the MC to issue notices to shopkeepers to remove such encroachments.

Meanwhile, Kartar Singh Patna, chairman of Akalgarh Market Bachao Sangarsh Committee alleged that no action is being taken against the violators due to political pressures.

Heading: Indians have outdone Chinese in English proficiency - Indian Express
Content:
When it comes to removing garbage from various sites in the city, everyone acts arbitrarily. The residents of about 13 localities in the city such as 9 blocks of BRS Nagar, Aggar Nagar and few other colonies are facing serious garbage problems these days. The residents used to throw garbage at a common MC dump site located on the Ferozepur Road. However, for the last one week, the incharge of this site has refrained private workers from throwing garbage here. Reason: they have been asked to pay Rs 400 per rehra as the charge for throwing garbage.

MC authorities, meanwhile, have expressed surprise over this move as no charges have been levied for throwing garbage at the approved MC sites.

Kuldeep Singh, Zonal Commissioner, Ludhiana Municipal Corporation, said, "The Ferozepur Road site has been covered so that garbage can be thrown in an organised manner. Because of this, workers may have been told not to throw garbage at the site for a few days. I am not aware if anyone is asking for money. This is totally illegal and if the complaint is genuine, action will be taken against the concerned sanitary inspector."

While the residents are paying between Rs 30 and Rs 50 per month to private workers for removing garbage, private workers are a surprised lot over the diktat of the MC employees who are not allowing them to throw garbage at the approved MC site. "MC employees cannot charge for throwing garbage at the MC site," fumed a garbage collector of BRS Nagar while talking to Newsline. The workers added that for the past one week they are facing problem due to which they also have to face the ire of the residents.

Zonal commissioner, meanwhile, suggested the residents to get garbage bins placed in every block. He added, "No one wants to get a garbage bin placed near their houses. Still the problem of money being charged will certainly be cross checked and the guilty will be punished."

Heading: 13 from district in race for PU Senate elections - Indian Express
Content:
"Indians are by far ahead of the Chinese when it comes to proficiency in English language. They not only perform better in the IELTS (International English Language Testing System), but the statistics reveal that their average level of proficiency is much higher than their Chinese counterparts when it comes to clearing the English language testing exam."

Kevin Mclaven, First Secretary (Education Services), British Council division of the British High Commission, said this in an exclusive interview with Ludhiana Newsline on Friday, while praising the expertise of Indian students in English language.

According to the British diplomat, the average band score of Indian students is slightly above six on the IELTS rating scale of nine bands, which indicates that most of the users of the language are better than the average users.

"Indian students form the second largest market for IELTS, second only to China. But when it comes to proficiency in the language, Indian students score better than Chinese students," he remarked. The IELTS exam is recognised by universities in different English speaking countries for admission to foreign students.

Kevin said he was in Punjab to celebrate the fact that the largest chunk of students taking the IELTS annually is from Punjab. "Punjab contributes to as many as 30 per cent of the students who take the exam in the country every year," he said.

Presently, more than 6,000 educational institutions, faculties, government agencies and professional organisations around the world recognise IELTS scores as a trusted qualification to communicate in English. The IELTS exam is taken in 120 countries across the world every year. "Last year, about 1.1 million students took the exam globally of which 1.6 lakh students were from India," Kevin claimed, adding that about 80 per cent of Indian students take the exam in the academic version while the rest take it under the general training version.

"This indicates that most of them are taking the exam for pursuing further studies abroad and going by the present trends, most of them aim to go to Australia," he said. Manish Joshi, the North India Head of Examinations Services, was also accompanying Kevin. They were in the city to participate in the 'Train the Teacher Programme' being held in the state for the first time.

Heading: Police bust gang of thieves - Indian Express
Content:
The fate of thirteen candidates from the district, who are in the fray for three different constituencies - graduates, principals and lecturers - in the fourth phase of Panjab University Senate Elections, is going to be sealed in the ballot boxes on Sunday.

Over two lakh voters are expected to exercise their franchise to elect the senators of the PU Senate in the elections being held in various affiliated colleges of the university.

While Praveen Sharma, Rajiv Bhasin, Jagpal Singh, Lakhvinder Singh Bedi and Madanjit Kaur Sahota are contesting in the graduates' constituency from the district, the principals constituency includes Dr Satish Sharma, Dr Varinder Kaur Thind, Dr Narinder Singh Sidhu, Dr RS Jhanji and Dr Rekha Bhardwaj from the district.

The lecturer constituency has Mukesh Arora, Harpreet Dua and Kuldeep Singh in the fray.

"I am quite hopeful of winning the elections. Though I have not even sent a single letter to the voters seeking their support or spent any extra money on the campaign, except for phone calls, I am still sure that I will win with a huge margin," said Prof Mukesh Arora, of SCD Government College, who is also a three-time winner in the senate elections.

"I have tried to live up to the expectations of the voters who voted me to be the youngest senator in the house last time. Therefore, I am hopeful of winning this time around too," was how Harpreet Dua summed up his chances of being a senator again.

On the other hand, a principal constituency candidate Dr Varinder Kaur Thind, principal of Khalsa College for Women, who is contesting the elections for the first time, said, "As it all depends upon one's personal relations, I am positive about winning," she beamed.

There are 42 candidates - five of them from Ludhiana - vying for 15 seats in the largest graduates' constituency wherein over two lakh voters are expected to cast their vote.

There are about 4.15 lakh registered voters in the constituency.

In the lecturers' constituency, out of the total of 12 candidates who are in the fray, three are from the district.

They are contesting for eight seats to be voted for by 2200 voters.

The principals' constituency has 13 principals contesting for eight seats. There are five candidates from the district alone in the constituency with an electorate strength of 70.

Heading: First ‘no job’, now PU students’ mired in litigation web - Indian Express
Content:
The Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) II claim to have busted a gang of motorcycle thieves on Saturday.

The police have arrested three members of the gang and claim to have recovered 13 stolen motorcycles from them.

A police party led by the CIA II Incharge Sub-Inspector (SI) Dilpreet Singh arrested three persons from the Tibba Road following a tip-off.

The arrested persons have been identified as Devinder Kumar alias Lovely, Tari Singh and Ravi Singh.

Initially, the police party had seized three stolen motorcycles from them but when the police questioned them, they revealed that they had hidden 10 more stolen bikes in a house in Amarjit Colony.

According to the police, these bikes had been stolen from different cities.

The police have also recovered a master key from Devinder Kumar, who is said to be the leader of the gang.

The gang members used to open the bikes with this master key and steal them, the police claimed.

Heading: Man from Haridwar alleges castration by eunuchs - Indian Express
Content:
It has been nearly a month since the job placements for students at the University Business School, Panjab University, was held up following a petition filed by the management students at the PU regional centre, Ludhiana. The students have suffered another jolt with legal experts suggesting that the lawyer hired by these students to represent their side cannot interfere in the case going on in the High Court. Consequently, nearly Rs 1 lakh paid by the students to the lawyer has also apparently gone down the drain.

The management students at the PU regional centre at Ludhiana had recently filed a case against the Panjab University demanding to hold their placements along with the students at UBS Chandigarh. While the case was still pending in the court, the authorities at the department were misinformed that the placements of the students of UBS Chandigarh had been stayed as a result of which, the placements were halted for the students.

Without cross checking, the department halted the placement procedure and instructed its students to stop communicating with companies regarding job placements till the said case was resolved.

Chairperson, UBS, Dinesh Gupta said, "We have been advised by our varsity counsel to halt the proceedings and that is what we have done". Clarifying his stand Anupam Gupta, UT Counsel, said, "We are doing what we can and it is out of the technicalities involved that I have advised the department to halt the placement procedure. Students need not worry as we will do our best for them."

Looking for a solution, the panic-stricken students approached a city-based lawyer, Sanjeev Walia, who was incidentally the father of their batchmate, Sangam Walia.

Talking to Newsline, one of the students from the department said, "We were worried after students from Ludhiana filed a writ petition and our placements were stopped. Sangam told us that his father was ready to fight our side but would charge Rs1,50,000."

After negotiations, the deal was settled around Rs 1 lakh with the 150 students paying Rs 700 each.

Walia, however, maintained, "It's after the students approached me that I decided to take up their case and they paid the fee on their own. I have made these students a party to the case and shall be fighting their case". On meeting the vice-chancellor on Friday, the students were politely refused any help and were told that the matter would be dealt with by Dean University Instructions (DUI).

Heading: Company secretaries seek posts in MC - Indian Express
Content:
A youth was allegedly castrated by some eunuchs on Thursday and has been admitted to the Civil Hospital in a critical condition. However, the police claim to be unaware of the matter.

Nikhil Sharma (18), a migrant from Haridwar, was presently living in the city in Threeke village. Talking to mediapersons from the Civil Hospital, he said that as he was unemployed, he used to play musical instruments with a group of eunuchs to earn his livelihood.

Nikhil alleged that the eunuchs had urged him to start performing with them but he refused to do so. He further said that on Thursday evening, these eunuchs took him to a place in Haibowal and offered him a cup of tea. He fell unconscious after drinking the tea, he claimed. He said that when he regained consciousness, he found himself thrown in an area near Chaand Cinema. He alleged that he saw blood oozing out and realised that he had been castrated. He called out for help when some passersby rushed him to the Civil Hospital.

When contacted, Division Number 4 SHO Pardeep Sandhu, under whose jurisdiction the area falls where Nikhil was thrown, said, "We have not received any such information. Also, this crime had not been committed in our area." When some mediapersons brought the matter in the notice of SSP R K Jaiswal, he said that he will get the matter investigated.

Heading: State Vigilance depts should be made independent bodies - Indian Express
Content:
The Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) has asked for the constitution of a post of a company secretary (CS) in the Municipal Corporations of Punjab to ensure better governance. The members submitted a memorandum to the Local Bodies Minister Manoranjan Kalia on Saturday, who was present at the inaugural function of the 4th Punjab State Conference of Company Secretaries at the Friends Regency in the city.

The municipal corporations in Gujarat have already accepted this proposal, said K Bakshi, president of ICSI. He added that apart from this, the CSs also demanded that even they be allowed to audit the VAT of various companies, which at the moment is done only by the CAs.

Kalia said that he would look into both the demands and later also called them for a meeting to Chandigarh.

Kalia further added that company secretaries and others professionals play a vital role in enhancing the productivity, management and marketing skills which boost the profitability of companies.

The minister further said that a new industry policy is being framed by UNIDO, a subsidiary of UNO to facilitate to boost investment in the industry of Punjab.

He said that the recommendations of the repot would be implemented soon.

Heading: Dissolve rights panels or make them more powerful - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti-Corruption Federation of India (TACFI) has decided to file a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in the Supreme Court for declaring the state vigilance departments as independent bodies. This was announced by Neeraj Chawla, the national president of TACFI, while addressing a press conference on Saturday.

Chawla said, "The state vigilance bodies should be made independent just like the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). They should also be trained on the lines of the CBI." The vigilance bodies presently work under their respective state governments.

When asked if the state governments were using the vigilance departments as a tool for setting scores with rival political parties, he said, "It is quite evident."

He said that corruption had to be controlled from the grassroots level and moreover at an individual level. Chawla said, "Corruption is growing at a rapid pace. TACFI cannot control it all alone."

While Manjeet Singh Komal, the newly elected state president of the federation said, "There is a need to motivate people against corrupt practices."

Heading: Sub-registrar sent to police custody for two days - Indian Express
Content:
Sant Shamsher Singh Jagera, president of the Sant Sipahi Dal, an organisation for the protection of human rights, said that the various human rights commissions in the country were ineffective and were proving to be white elephants.

Jagera said, "The government should either dissolve these commissions or should make them more powerful."

He alleged that these commissions were working under the influence of politicians and for making these commissions more powerful, they should be given equal powers of the judiciary.

He further said that to prevent custodial deaths, the concerned senior superintendent of police (SSP) should also be booked for murder if any custodial death was reported from any police station.

He said that according to the data procured from the National Crime Bureau, over 100 custodial deaths take place every year.

He claimed that many cases of custodial deaths were also going unreported.

Heading: Campaign to promote organ donation gains momentum - Indian Express
Content:
Sub-registrar (tehsildar) Arvind Verma, and two others who were arrested by the Vigilance Bureau on Friday for allegedly taking a bribe of Rs 10,000 from an NRI, have been sent to the police custody for two days for further questioning.

Verma, Parminder Pal Singh (cashier) and Harjinder Singh (police constable) were produced in a local court on Saturday. Accepting the plea of the Vigilance Bureau, the court sent the trio to police custody.

Heading: Encroachments galore in Akalgarh market - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly 1,50,000 patients need kidney transplant every year but only around 3000 transplants are carried out as there are not enough willing donors. With the passing of the Transplant of Human Organs Act 1994, the concept of cadaver organ donation i.e. retrieval of organs from 'brain-dead' persons has become legal, but inspite of that, hardly any cadaver organ donation takes place," said Dr Baldev Singh Aulakh, Chief Transplant Surgeon, Professor of Urology at the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital on Saturday.

He explained that a very large number of patients die every year due to organ failure and transplantation is the only treatment available.

He also said that there are only about 25 organs and tissues like the heart, lungs, liver, corneas (eye), bones, skin etc that can be transplanted.

"Only a few like kidney, blood & a part of the liver can be donated by living persons. Therefore, cadaver donation is the only answer to meet the growing requirement of thousands in need."

Gift of Life Organ Donation Awareness Society (GLODAS), which was launched on July 12 this year by State Health Minister Laxmi Kanta Chawla, is pushing ahead it's campaign to generate awareness about the noble deed of organ & tissue donation to save lives.

Dr GPI Singh, professor and head of Community Medicine at Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, also the vice-president and an active campaigner of GLODAS-India explained the concept and philosophy behind the campaign.

Dr Aulakh also said that GLODAS was planning to hold presentations, seminars and discussions in colleges, schools and organised groups like Indian Medical Association, social service clubs, army camps and so on.

"During such meetings, free literature is distributed and the audience is motivated to sign a donor card after discussion with the next of kin, which he or she should keep on him or her as an expression of wish to donate organs after death," he said.

Heading: Vendors begin supplying Nano parts to other plants - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee met Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi regarding the Singur impasse on Saturday. It is learnt that during the hour-long meeting, Bhattacharjee told Gandhi that there cannot be any further concessions on the land issue, else it would be impossible for the Nano factory to remain in Singur. After the meet, Bhattacharjee briefed top party leaders at the state party headquarters.

The meeting was a follow-up of the Friday's meeting between the Governor and Mamata Banerjee, wherein after giving a patient hearing to her allegations against the government, Gandhi had told her that he would also hear the state's version on the matter.

Party sources said that Bhattacharjee, who went to Raj Bhavan at 6 pm, informed the Governor that the state government was ready to negotiate the fresh compensation package with Banerjee. They also said that the CM had reiterated that only 70 acres of land could be practically returned to the farmers.

Heading: Buddha caused Singur debacle: Dasmunsi - Indian Express
Content:
Pune and Pantnagar receive supplies

With work at the Tata Motors factory in Singur being stalled for over 20 days now, the company has asked the vendors, who supply various components of the small car, to supply the parts to their plants in Pune and Pantnagar.

Delhi-based Sharda Motor Industries Limited, which supplies exhaust systems, catalytic converters, suspensions and seat frames for the Nano car, recently received bulk orders for October. The company is likely to deliver these at either Pune or Pantnagar.

Executive Director of the company, Udayan Banerjee said: "We got orders for various parts including exhaust systems and seat frames."

Sources in the company said the company has received orders to supply 2,500 exhaust systems and 4,000 seat frames. "Due to the protests in Singur, we will supply the goods from our Pune and Nashik units," said Banerjee.

Since last week of August, Gurgaon-based Anand Motors Products Pvt Ltd has been supplying rubber components for Nano. "We supplied the first consignment for 200 vehicles last month. Now we have been asked to send nearly 2,000 sets to Pantnagar," said V S Valia, Director Operations of the company.

Rucha Engineers Pvt Ltd is providing sheet metal components and plastic components for the Nano car. "We are supplying components in small quantities to the Pantnagar unit of Tata Motors. We hope to get a bulk order soon," said MD Umesh Dashrathi.

Another vendor, Biswajit Chowdhury, Vice President (Marketing), Endurance Technologies Pvt Ltd, said: "We are ready to dispatch our components. We have two units in Pantnagar and Pune. Providing supply to these areas will not be a problem for us."

Heading: 7 get life term in Jhawar abduction case - Indian Express
Content:
Union Minister Priya Ranjan Dasmunsi has held Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee responsible for the Singur stalemate.

"The chief minister is singularly responsible for the (Singur) impasse. Before acquiring the land, he had not discussed it even within the Left Front," said Dasmunsi. He was speaking at a convention of the party's south Kolkata unit on Saturday.

He said that Bhattacharjee had misled the Singur farmers, as the government made a promise to return maximum land from the project area to the affected farmers, knowing well that it would not be possible.

"How can ancillary units be saved if land was given from the project site? The chief minister had not done adequate homework in preparing the rehabilitation package before signing an agreement with the Trinamool," said Dasmunsi.

He accused the CPM of neglecting farmers in areas that were not under its stronghold. "The CPM's farmers' wing, the Paschimbanga Krishak Sabha, has remained silent over the plight of Singur farmers," he said.

Heading: Pranab says industrialisation is a must today - Indian Express
Content:
Seven persons, who were accused of abducting Roma Jhawar, were sentenced to life imprisonment by the additional sessions and district judge in Barasat on Saturday. Those convicted are the prime accused Gunjan Ghosh, Munna Shaw, Bikash Shau, Sukumar Mondal, Damodar Yadav, Dashrath Yadav and Ramchandra Singh. While Dashrath and Ramchandra were the drivers, Damodar was the gatekeeper of the Jhawar family.

Jhawar, a teenage girl, was going to college on February 4, 2005, when miscreants stopped her vehicle and kidnapped her at gunpoint in Salt Lake. She was released later, after her family paid a ransom of about Rs 20 lakh. The kidnappers, however, were arrested within four days.

On Saturday, in his plea to the judge to reduce the sentence, Ghosh said he was the only child of his old parents.

"I am the sole earning member of the family," he said in the court. His accomplice, Shaw and other accused also pleaded for leniency.

The judge, however, refused to consider their plea. Lawyers of the convicts said they would appeal to higher court against the judgment. No one from the Jhawar family was present in the court during the hearing.

Heading: No puja off for KMC staff - Indian Express
Content:
Union External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukhrejee said industrialisation is necessary for the state. He, however, said he had no solution for the Singur issue.

The minister was speaking at the 121st Annual General Meeting of the Bengal National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BNCCI) in Kolkata on Saturday.

"The progress of all civilisations has been from agrarian to industrialised societies and any attempt to reverse the order can push us into regression," he said, adding that economic strength is required to gain respectability in the world community.

India is being given importance on global platforms because of its 1 trillion USD economy, said the minister. "We should invest nearly 40 per cent of our GDP. China has been investing 40 to 45 per cent of its GDP over the last 30 years," said Mukherjee.

The GDP growth in India reached nearly ten per cent last year and over the last four years, it has been around nine per cent, he said, adding that in the last 17 years nearly 80 billion USD of investment has been reported in the country. "We now require 10-15 years of sustainable growth and peaceful relationships with China and Pakistan," said the minister.

Mukherjee, who had many stints as finance minister of

the country, said he discussed with Finance Minister P Chidambaram the global crisis caused by the failure of the investment banks in US.

He said: "There is no need to press the panic button in India. Our exposure to these institutions is extremely limited."

The country faced a challenge to undertake investment in areas like health, sanitation, rural development, infrastructure and energy, Mukherjee added.

Heading: 3 killed in accident - Indian Express
Content:
Following scarcity of staff in the health department, the Kolkata Municipal Corporation has decided to cancel Puja holidays for its health workers.

"We don't want the anti-malarial programme to be held over during the Pujas. So we cancelled the holidays for the health workers at the borough level," said TK Mukherjee, Health Executive, Borough VI.

Lack of staff is emerging as a major hurdle in taking anti-malarial measures. At the borough level, there are several vacancies in the posts, including that of health assistants, health supervisor and doctors.

The civic authorities held an emergency meeting to resolve the issue on Saturday. "We are understaffed and overworked. This is affecting our programmes. We have decided to fill up the vacant posts in the health department soon," said Sahidul Islam, Joint Commissioner, Kolkata Municipal Corporation.

Heading: CPM happy as some farmers accept cheques - Indian Express
Content:
Three persons were killed, when a two-wheeler collided with a truck near Sandeshkhali in North 24 Parganas on Saturday morning.

The victims, Dipak Khardin (24), Bapi Bisayee (25) and Amal Sardar (23), all local traders, were travelling in the two-wheeler. The victims were on their way to their shops when the accident occurred. They were rushed to a nearby hospital but were declared dead on arrival.

Locals staged a protest against rash driving and demanded arrest of the truck driver. They blocked the road for two hours and the blockade was removed only after the police intervened.

"We have asked the authorities to construct a speed breaker on the road but the administration never paid heed," said a local. The driver of the lorry is absconding. Bodies of the victims have been sent for autopsy.

Heading: Eyeing Gold - Indian Express
Content:
The CPM is happy that at least some of the unwilling farmers of Singur are accepting compensation cheques. The state secretary of the party, Biman Bose, termed the development as a positive sign in favour of industrialisation.

Bose said: "This shows that the people of Singur are beginning to understand facts. We want to explain why inustrialisation is important. But the Opposition is not allowing us to do so."

Bose said the party is going in for rapid propaganda to create awareness regarding industrialisation. "We want to go to every village and town to explain why this state needs industrialisation," he said.

He alleged that the Opposition is misleading the people of Singur and expressed confidence that once their message reaches the unwilling farmers, they would understand and things would change.

Heading: Hills Beckon - Indian Express
Content:
Sudeep Pakrashi in conversation with Tirthankar Nandy who is on a mission for gold in C'wealth games in karate

He could have been an ace swimmer. He had represented North 24-Parganas at the junior level swimming during his school days. But the pressure of education forced him to quit swimming. He also could have established himself as an actor on the celluoid. For he modelled for a city-based popular garment company for a couple of months. But Tirthankar Nandy didn't want to walk down the streets of glamour and so-called fame.

Nandy can best be described as the lone karateka in the city in recent years who was branded by one of the city's renowned schools in its publicity campaign at the time of its launch at Pailan in South 24-Parganas.

But Nandy, one of the city's popular karatekas in hudokan style, has preferred the way of teaching would-be karatekas. He begun his career with the game in 1986 under Sanchit Saha Nandy and he sharpened his skill and performance in the hudokan style under Chew-Choo-Soot and then under his son Richard Soot through a two-week training in Sydney in 1998. But Nandy is also grateful to Vasant Shetty in Mumbai.

Nandy said: "Shetty, uncle of Bollywood star Suniel Shetty, didn't have a bright career as a karateka. But he was simply brilliant as a teacher. I improved my technique, skill, psychological drill under his careful observation for around four years in Mumbai. I used to travel at that time from Kolkata to Mumbai."

This black-belt karateka who had mastered the art of yoga since 1984 had another wish to work as action director in movies. And he fulfilled his desire in a telefilm named 'Good bad guys' directed by an NRI which was released in the UK also at the end of 90s.

Nandy began teaching aspiring students from 1992 at a small centre in Manicktala. He had only around 25 students. Nandy today struggles to recollect how much fees those students paid at that time.

"It might not have been more than Rs 20 each of those 25 students used to pay," Nandy said.

In the past 16 years, Nandy's work has been hectic, to say the least. Not only has the school in Pailan roped him in as a karate teacher, the pressure from students all over the state has led Nandy to introduce karate in 13 schools in the city. Besides, a new school in Jharkhand has also roped in his services. But apart from his job in the school, Nandy receives the same amount as fees from each of his 5,000 students in the other 14 schools.

He has so far produced nine black-belt holders. Many of his students like Samir Singh, Bijon Fadikar, Kartik Basak have already graced Bengal with their impressive show. But the 33-year-old teacher's aim is to prepare his bright students so that they can earn gold medals in the forthcoming Commonwealth Games in 2010 in New Delhi. Before he signed off, he said: "It will be one of my most cherished dreams even if one of my students can win a gold in the 2010 Games. When I am totally dedicated in my job, can't I expect results from them?"

Heading: Terror abode: Bomb ingredients recovered from deserted house - Indian Express
Content:
Chandranath Das has portrayed one touching point of the mountains — how people's apathy is ruining its natural beauty.
Pragya Paramita talks to the curator-cum-artist

When Chandranath Das, curator of Himalayan Mountaineering Institute (HMI) in Darjeeling recently participated in a group exhibition in Kolkata, many were shocked to hear that the artist had picked up his brush after more than a decade. His deft strokes and intense subject matters give no indication of the fact that the curator-cum-artist had quit art after graduating from art college and was far from being a professional artist.

"There are many young men who join art college but few really make it big in the world of art. Like many young men who join the college, I too enrolled, much against my parents' wishes, but later I got disillusioned with the politics," says Das. While Das may have dreamt of being an artist, he had not reckoned for the politics that they have to face to make it big in that field. Although he gave up his childhood dream of being an artist, he nevertheless got a job that enabled him to pursue his passion — albeit a little differently.

"Joining HMI gave me scope and exposure that perhaps I could not have got as an artist. Though I had quit painting, my job gave me an opportunity to pursue an entirely different side of the subject," says Das. He even went on to acquire an AMA from London, which made him an expert on museums.

But it was only in the last few years that he decided to go back to art and started painting once again and this time it was the Himalayas that inspired him. Being based in Darjeeling, he says, he could not but be touched by the beauty of the hill station and slowly he started painting again, and now he is once again a full-fledged artist.

"The mountains in all its beauty — the tea gardens, the quaint life of the people — they all inspired me to pick up the brush again. His recent exhibition in the city was a testament of that passion. Most of his paintings revolved around the changing seasons in the mountains, flora and fauna and the life of the people.

But what makes him different is that through his works he is also trying hard to show the deteriorating conditions of the mountains.

"Many of my works centre on that as I can actually see how people's apathy is ruining this natural beauty. When tourists come to Darjeeling on holidays, they leave behind a mess caring nothing for the natural environs. Even mountaineers leave behind a mess in the mountains. I hope my paintings are able to throw some light on these issues that need to be tackled," says Das.

While recognition as an artist may have come late to him, Das says he does not regret it.

"I had the scope to study a lot of things that I would not have had I decided to stick to painting. I got the scope to study subjects like restoration of paintings and museology abroad, something that widened my scope as an artist. Museums abroad are very different from their Indian counterparts and one must go there to understand how," says Das.

His late blooming as an artist also gave him the scope to discover himself as an artist. "When I look back at my work, I see how much I have developed in spite of staying away from art for such a long time. I think my long sabbatical helped me to grow," claims Das.

Today, he is being invited to galleries across the country to showcase his works and his talent is being acknowledged by different artists. Busy completing his latest series based on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railways, today he is an artist first and then a curator.

Heading: Now, govt wants corporate houses to imbibe social responsibility lessons - Indian Express
Content:
Suspected bombers killed, arrested in Delhi on Friday, had stayed here in July, say cops

The Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) recovered bomb making materials during a raid on a closed bungalow on the outskirts of the city, late on Friday.

The DCB said at least six terrorists, including the two killed and one arrested by the Delhi Police on Friday in the National Capital, had stayed in the house this July, before the serial blasts.

"At least six terrorists involved in the Ahmedabad serial blasts had stayed in this house between the second week of July and July 26. The temporary occupants of this house were Atif alias Bashir and Sajid, who were killed by the Delhi Police at Jamia Nagar on Friday. This can be established by the fact that their mobile phones were in use during their period of stay here. Mohammed Saif, who was arrested in Delhi on Friday, had also stayed in this house," said H R Muliana, Assistant Commissioner of Police, DCB.

A team of DCB officers raided the two-storey bungalow no 10 at Al-Ahmedi society in Nabinagar, near Narol Circle on the basis of information gleaned from Jahid Sheikh, an accused of the Ahmedabad serial blasts, during his interrogation in police custody.

The police recovered battery cells, timer watches, circuit wires, multi-meters, cello-tapes, hardboards, cloth and plastic bags during a search. Besides, the police also seized used utensils, cycle carriers, car covers, worn out clothes, a table fan, an Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation diary (from which the city map is missing) and maps of some places in the city where bombs exploded on July 26. The DCB said the occupants had used the house for assembling bombs for the July 26 attacks.

While displaying the cache of arms and ammunition before the media, Muliana said that the cars stolen from Mumbai were first brought to this house to be loaded with the bombs and later planted outside the LG and the Civil Hospitals.

He added that the backyard of the house was used for disposing off documents. Muliana said the terrorists had also scribbled something on a wall in Arabic. "Though it resembles the logo the Indian Mujahideen uses in its e-mails, it can be a secret code as well. We are yet to decipher that," he said.

Muliana also spoke about the tip-off the Gujarat police gave to its Delhi counterpart, which led to the Friday encounter. "We had collected call details of the accused of the Ahmedabad serial blasts. While analyzing them, it was found that some calls came from the Jamia Nagar area. This information was immediately passed on to central agencies."

When asked if the bombs used in Delhi blasts were also made here, Muliana shrugged off the question. "The Delhi Police would know about that," he said.

He added that according to preliminary investigations, a nurse at a private hospital owned the house. 'Khokarben rented the house to Sheikh through a private agent for Rs 5,000 a month. Khokarben also took a deposit of Rs 25,000," said Muliana. He said she has now been accused of violating the police commissioner's notification, which says that credentials of the tenants should be verified from the concerned police department prior to renting out property.

Heading: Former bank employee arrested for running hawala racket - Indian Express
Content:
Proposed industrial policy expects more concerted efforts from private players

After asking the Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs) to utilise 30 per cent of their annual Profit Before Tax (PBT) as part of their Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), the Gujarat government now proposes to rope in private corporate houses to undertake the same across the state.

The proposal is contained in a draft industrial policy prepared by the State Industries Department.

The government is expected to announce its new industrial policy at the Science City in Ahmedabad on January 12-13, 2009, prior to the Vibrant Gujarat Global Investors' Summit, a senior official in the Industries Department said on Saturday.

Among other chapters included in the draft document dealing with various incentives and facilities for industries, the one that relates to "Corporate Social Responsibility", says: "By and large, corporates undertake CSR activities. The efforts are, however, scattered and dispersed, because of which the outcome is not visible to the public at large. Hence, there is a need to synergise CSR activities with government initiatives for better visibility, sustainability and outcome."

It is proposed in the draft document that the corporate houses and industry associations may take specific welfare activities in villages, cluster villages and also at the taluka/district-level. The area to carry out such activities may be allocated by the government depending on the size/scale of operation of an industrial unit/corporate house/industrial association.

The government has suggested that a committee consisting of Director, CSR (of a company), an officer attached to the district rural development agency (DRDA) and an officer nominated by the district collector be constituted. This committee may decide CSR activities, allocate funds provided by the corporate groups and government, and monitor the progress of such activities.

It has also been suggested that the corporate houses and industry associations may undertake the various CSR activities.

These may include adopting primary and community health centres on the PPP model, supporting nutritional programmes in villages, enhancing capacities and reach of NGO services, enhancing technical competence and manpower (including vocational training), besides helping the government implement sanitation and environment-related programmes in the state.

Heading: Vadodara’s ‘problem patch’ finally gets a security cover - Indian Express
Content:
SOG, ATS recover Rs 92 lakh; money had come from South African businessman

The Special Operation Group (SOG) from Surat and the Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) from Ahmedabad has unearthed a Rs 92 lakh hawala racket during a joint operation and arrested a retired bank employee and a youth from Surat.

Acting on a tip-off, the SOG and the ATS arrested one Suresh Surti, a retired bank employee from his house in Kathor village of Surat with Rs 82 lakh cash on Friday.

During interrogation, Surti claimed that he had received the money from one Ishaq Ibrahim, a native of Kathor village in Surat, who is a businessman based in South Africa.

He also claimed that the money was to be donated in masjids, madrassas and among the poor Muslims during the month of Ramzan. He also said that he had given a sum of Rs 10 lakh to Kasim Vohra, a resident of Nana Varachha in Surat, following which, the latter was arrested from his house and Rs 10 lakh cash was recovered from his possession.

SOG Sub-Inspector R G Desai said: "Ibrahim regularly sends money to Surti during Ramzan. We have arrested Vohra and Surti and are interrogating them about the source of the money. We are also looking for those people who have been given the money."

He further said that Surthi served in a nationalised bank in Kathor and had retired only a couple of years ago. "He took care of Ibrahim's bank accounts and properties in Khator village. The matter is still under investigation and we will get to the bottom soon," Desai added.

Heading: Verdict in Asaram narco test adjourned till October 4 - Indian Express
Content:
Two-km stretch between Kumbharwada and Champaner Darwaja is prone to communal flare-ups

With the State Reserve Police erecting six tents in the 2-km stretch between Kumbharwada and Champaner Darwaja on Saturday, it seems the city police has finally woken up to the needs of this 'problem patch'.

The area was witness to a communal flare-up after the Ganesh Visarjan celebrations early this week, which led to police firing and the death of one person.

It was on September 18 that Newsline had published an article, "Walled city's two-km stretch too long for Vadodara police," which had highlighted the poor bandobast that had led to the communal flare-up.

"We have set up six SRP camps and also stationed two companies of Rapid Action Force in the area, who are keeping a strict vigil," said City Police Inspector B N Chawda.

The camps have been welcomed by both the communities even though many small-time traders have been asked to shift their businesses to other places to make space for the police camps.

"We are ready to suffer losses, but there should not be any more riots. The camp is for everyone's safety," said Dholabhai Damor, a laari-owner, who has also been asked to shift to an alternate place.

Locals, who have been in this area since long, said, police tents were last erected in Fatehpura Char Rasta in 1986. Akram Timberwalla (42), a local resident said: "This is very similar to what happened in 1986, when there was a camp here (pointing to the crossroads). Even in 2002, when the entire Walled City was burning, they (the police) would frequent the place, even though there was a permanent camp at Hujarat Tekra, about two blocks away."

Local residents also admitted the situation would have been different had the SRP been present here before the visarjan.

"The SRP tents will have an effect on our psyche and habitual miscreants will think twice before indulging in any such act," said another local resident.

Former VMC councillor summoned for questioning

The Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) has summoned former Vadodara Municipal Corporation councillor Kishor Rana from the area for questioning on Friday night. Though DCB officials refused to comment as to why Rana was picked up for questioning, police sources said there were reports about Rana instigating mobs after the visarjan riots.

Heading: Un‘fair’ deal: Pilgrim arrested because of his skin colour - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Metropolitan Magistrate D M Patel on Saturday adjourned the verdict in the narco-analysis test case of two 'sadhaks' (disciples) of the Asaram Bapu Ashram till October 4.

Though no criminal case was registered against Pankaj Saxena and Yogesh Bhati, the two sadhaks, the CID (Crime) had sought permission to conduct narco-analysis tests in a bid to dig out the truth following the mysterious deaths of two minor boys at the Ashram gurukul.

The prosecution counsel contended that it was necessary to conduct the narco-analysis test on the two disciples to unravel the mystery surrounding the deaths of the two children.

The prosecution also contended that there was no need to obtain consent of the suspects. He said the Gujarat High Court, in a recent order in the case of Santokhben Jadeja vs State of Gujarat had held that there was no need to seek consent of the accused to conduct scientific test or narco-analysis.

He was, however, strongly opposed by defence counsels Rohit Verma and Bharat Joshi. They argued that the present case could not be compared to the Santokhben case as the latter was an accused while the two disciples are not. The two disciples had earlier refused to undergo the test.

Heading: Vadodara welcomes M S Dhoni, Mohd Kaif - Indian Express
Content:
BSF took fair-skinned Qureshi, a Jetpur labourer, to be a Kashmiri Muslim

A man arrested by the Border Security Force (BSF) from the Hajipur Shrine on suspicion has been found to be a pilgrim from Jetpur town of Rajkot district.

Soyab Hanif Qureshi (23), the victim of mistaken identity, said: "I was paying my obeisance when a BSF party picked me up from the shrine area who mistook me as a Kashmiri Muslim because of my fair skin. I told them that I was a poor labourer from Jetpur on a pilgrimage to Hajipir baba. But they did not believe me and took me to Bhuj for interrogation and beat me up mercilessly. I have marks on my feet and legs."

Qureshi told this reporter in chaste Kathiawadi: "Saheb, mare Ghar javun chhe. Emne kaho n eke mane juldi this jawade (I want to go home. Please tell them to allow me to go home immediately)."

The BSF, however, denied that they beat up Qureshi.

N D Prasad, Deputy Inspector General, BSF, said: "The man frequently changed his statements during the preliminary inquiry and it was he who had described himself as Pakistani. What can we do? We man the border and have to be alert all the time to ensure that no wrong person is found in the notified area."

Sources, however, said that the shrine of Hajipur was outside the notified area and Soyab was inside the permitted shrine area.

According to sources, after the BSF authorities found out that Soyab was an Indian citizen, they handed him over to the Nara police for further action.

The police said since they had received in writing from the BSF that the man was not a Pakistani national, they have not registered any case against him.

They said they have now contacted Soyab's relatives in Jetpur so that they could take him back.

Heading: Unidentified foreign boat found abandoned near Chorwad - Indian Express
Content:
Barodians cheered the arrival of Indian skipper Mahendra Singh Dhoni and ace-cricketer Mohammed Kaif on Saturday. Fans crowded the entire stretch from the airport to Hotel Welcom just to have a glance of the two cricketers who are in town to play in the upcoming Irani Trophy match between Delhi and Rest of India.

The match will be held between September 24 and 28 at the Reliance Cricket Stadium. Net practice will be held at the IPCL cricket stadium.

The Baroda Cricket Association will host a press conference on Sunday, which is likely to be attended many cricketing stars including Dhoni and Kaif.

Heading: Whiff of freedom: NHL medical college to become autonomous now - Indian Express
Content:
An unidentified foreign boat was found abandoned near the Chorwad coast in Junagadh district on Saturday. The 34-feet-long and five-feet-wide fibre boat had Arabic words scribbled on it.

Chorwad Sub-Inspector F A Karmur said: "The boat has been found between Jujarpur and Khambhaliya coastal village near Chorwad. The boat was empty and nothing objectionable was found from it."

He said they informed the customs officials about the boat, who paid a visit to the site.

He said the officials have opined that the boat might have been abandoned a couple of months ago. "The boat was in a damaged condition, which indicates that it might have separated from its mother ship for some unknown reason. It might also be possible that some sailors or fishermen might have lost their lives in the sea and the stranded boat reached here afloat," said Karmur.

Newborn leopard found in agricultural field

A newborn leopard cub was found in an agricultural field on the outskirts of Mandor village under the Sutrapada taluka in Junagadh district.

According to forest guard C M Rathod, the cub was born just a couple of days earlier and its eyes had not opened properly.

Rathod said the cub was found lying in an agricultural land owned by one Ramshibhai, a farmer. The farmer immediately informed the foresters about the cub, who rushed to the spot. After providing it with initial healthcare, the foresters decided to leave it where it was. Early morning on Saturday, when the foresters reached the place, the cub was missing. "We noticed clear signs of the mother leopard's visit, including the pugmarks of the animal. She must have taken the cub away," he said.

Heading: Two cops depose before Nanavati panel; advocate demands former CBI boss share his SIT probe finds - Indian Express
Content:
New trust to take over control from AMC, 58 granted seats to become self-financed

The standing committee of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) on Wednesday approved the proposal of transferring all medical colleges from AMC's jurisdiction to the newly formed 'Ahmedabad Education Trust.' At present, there are only two municipal medical colleges in the state—the Surat Municipal Medical College and the NHL Municipal Medical College. The former is a self-financed institution and after Wednesday's decision, the NHL Medical College too has attained autonomy.

As a result of the decision, all the 58 granted seats will now be converted into self-financed seats. Pankaj Patel, the Dean of the NHL Medical College, said: "The entire administration, finances and the admission process will now be governed by the education trust, while a state government committee will decide on the admission and fees."

The Ahmedabad Education Trust, which was registered on July 5, will now handle all the administrative, financial and admission issues of not only the NHL Municipal Medical College but also the two proposed medical and dental colleges under the city's LG Hospital.

AMC Commissioner I P Gautam said: "With the NHL Medical College becoming autonomous, all the future medical institutions will also be self-financed. We will, however, withdraw in stages and aim to make all the medical colleges self-dependent. This will result in more such institutions."

The reason behind the decision is said to be the drive to expand the educational set-up in medicine. It is believed that granting autonomy to the colleges will benefit both AMC and the institutions.

"Though we are expanding the educational facilities, we cannot, however, run many institutions. We have hospitals with 2,000 beds under which we can have 2 medical colleges. Even though we have the facilities, AMC cannot involve itself too much in medical education. But at the same time, we do not want education to suffer. The move therefore, would benefit both," said Gautam.

Heading: Rubber problem stretches ACS to its limits - Indian Express
Content:
Two police officers, S M Katara, Deputy Commissioner of Police, Zone II (Ahmedabad) and Inspector H G Baraiya deposed before the Nanavati Commission probing the Godhra and post-Godhra incidents, on Friday.

The two officers were posted in Vadodara's south zone during the riots. It was here that the Best Bakery carnage took place in which 11 people were massacred. While Katara was the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Bariya was an inspector at the Panigate police station, under whose jurisdiction fell the Best Bakery on Dabhoi Road.

The Vadodara police had come under flak for their failure to protect the bakery inhabitants. The then Chief Election Commissioner, J M Lyngdoh, had also made some inconvenient comments about during his visit to the charred bakery at that time.

When contacted, Katara refused to reveal details of the deposition.
