Meanwhile, advocate Hiralal Gupta representing the Congress party, argued in his submissions before the commission that the commission should also call former CBI chief R K Raghavan, who is heading the Supreme Court-constituted Special Investigation Team to re-investigate the 10 most heinous riot cases including Godhra. Gupta said Raghavan must issue a statement regarding the new revelations that might have come during the SIT probe.

Gupta pleaded that the SIT has so far re-arrested about three dozen people accused in different cases that were earlier probed by the local police.

He said he had submitted an application before the Commission in April 2008, beseeching that Chief Minister Narendra Modi, former Health and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Ashok Bhatt and former Home Minister Gordhan Zadaphia be also summoned to depose before the Commission.

"But no decision on the application has been taken so far by the Commission," Gupta added.

Heading: Mind game: A tale of those who lose it despite their best effort - Indian Express
Content:
Call it pressure to achieve golden target or calculation error, society is left with an unmanageable stock of condoms

The Gujarat government has set up several golden targets for itself to achieve by 2010, the golden jubilee year of its inception. Not to be left behind in the Swarnim Gujarat bandwagon, the AIDS Control Society (ACS) too has found for itself, unwittingly though, a golden target of distributing several lakh condoms among the high-risk behaviour persons before their expiry date, which is incidentally, also 2010.

These days, the ACS is facing problems of a different kind. Its office on C G Road is flush with lakhs of condoms it has received from the National Aids Control Organisation (NACO) sometime ago. The entire place, including its conference room, is choc-a-bloc with boxes of condoms. Each box contains 6,000 condoms and several hundreds of such boxes are lying for almost two months here now. The officials also have no idea how and where to distribute them and through whom.

According to ACS director Dr Chirag Shah, there are several reasons for this backlog. One of them being limited storage facility with limited voluntary organisations registered with the ACS for AIDS awareness in the city.

He said the huge quantity was perhaps sent by mistake. "We can clear this in one year," he said.

Dr Shah said that compared to the earlier two dozen odd NGOs, which were working in the field earlier, there are only two NGOs now in accordance with the latest guidelines. He said this has had an impact in the mobilisation of volunteers and had made the distribution process rather slow.

He said the distribution of condoms has also suffered an impact because Ahmedabad city has less concentration of high-risk local populace and high migration from other areas. He said, compared to Ahmedabad, there is a high prevalence of HIV/AIDS in other districts like Surat, Surnedranagar, Amreli and Mehsana. These come under the care of Gujarat AIDS Control Society (GACS), he added. Dr Shah said he plans to distribute the condoms before more consignments are expected. According to estimates, the annual requirement in Ahmedabad is one million condoms for an approximate 2.5 million population of high risk individuals.

Heading: Croc Chronicles: VMC refuses to house homeless crocodiles in Ajwa Sarovar - Indian Express
Content:
Mental health, a neglected branch of health sector, needs urgent attention

* Mohan Makwana (40) from Ganeshpura village near Odhav set himself afire on Wednesday night. The police said he was suffering from a mental illness for the last four years. In his dying declaration, he said illness was the only reason for him to attempt suicide.

* In Bapunagar area, a 39-year-old woman committed suicide by hanging herself from the ceiling fan, allegedly due to a mental illness. The police have registered a case of accidental death.

The above incidents took place in the eastern part of the city last week. There is, however, a common link in the two cases — 'mental instability' allegedly drove the two to take their own lives.

With a steady rise in suicide cases over the years, the need for a better-equipped mental health apparatus has been felt for long. Between 2002 and 2004, the Indian Institute of Management- Ahmedabad (IIM-A) had prepared a mental health mission report for the mental health support project of the Department of Health and Family Welfare of the Government of Gujarat. The report had widely hinted on the grey areas and on capacity building and strengthening.

Dr. R H Bhakre, the then Programme Officer of the Mental Health Cell, who was also part of the short-listing committee of 'Mental Health Mission Report', said: "On the basis of the report, seven different projects related to women's issues, children, service delivery in tribal areas, traditional health practices and rehabilitation were taken up. While the projects are running, it is only after the report that several NGOs shed their reluctance to venture into this sector. Prior to that, there wasn't a single NGO working in this area. Public-private partnership and linkages in the sector have also grown over time."

In another major move, the six government medical colleges undertook a statewide project named 'Distress and Suicide Prevention for Medical Students': a helpline targeting to lower suicide attempts among medical students.

Ritambara Mehta, dean of the Psychiatric Department of the Government Medical College, Surat, said: "Mental health remains a largely neglected branch in all government hospitals, while private hospitals and individual psychiatrists provide 80 per cent of the services in the mental health sector."

Ajay Chauhan, the Superintendent of the Ahmedabad Mental Hospital, said, there has been inadequate government funding of the projects and researches to this end. "Manpower in this sector is a major hindrance in developing a proper support system. There are not more than 250 psychiatrists in the state, which effectively means that one psychiatrist has to cater to a large number of people. Many cases have to be handled by a few clinical psychologists, nurses and social workers. Moreover, there is no course to cater to the professionals interested in specialisations." he added.

Heading: MSU dept hit by ‘Toonami’, courtesy Sudhir Tailang - Indian Express
Content:
A Vadodara Municipal Corporation notification preventing the release of rescued crocodiles in Ajwa Sarovar has stirred a fresh controversy. Forest officials and crocodile rescue organisations are reportedly unhappy over the move.

The VMC has claimed that the decision has been taken after considering the safety of the workers who are engaged in the maintenance of the reservoir. But at the same time, the municipal body, in its communication with the forest department, has claimed that the carrying capacity of the reservoir has exceeded, as the number of crocodiles in the reservoir is already 340 and it is not possible to include any more. The Forest Department has replied that the crocodiles should be released in Ajwa, as other reservoirs are far away.

As per VMC's August census, Ajwa Dam shelters approximately 340 crocodiles. Rajendra Vasava, Deputy Engineer, Ajwa Dam, said: "The restriction was imposed years ago, but the rescued crocodiles are still released here. We have our people working in the dam for cleaning. While Ajwa crocodiles are quite harmless, the security of the people working here and also of the neighbouring village will be threatened if crocodiles from outside are released."

With over 45 people working in the dam, authorities say that around 10 to 15 people get into water twice a day for cleaning purposes.

The notification has come as a blow for the crocodile rescue organisations and the Forest Department. "We have been informed by VMC that Ajwa reservoir has crossed the carrying capacity of crocodiles and that they have to be released elsewhere," said Nayan Desai, District Conservator of Forest.

The homeless crocodiles will now have to be housed either at Dev Dam, Sukhi Dam or at Karjan.

"The alternatives are far away. We have to release them in other reservoirs. We have written to the commissioner requesting him to allow the release of the crocodiles at Ajwa itself," Desai added.

The city NGOs and the Forest Department rescue approximately 10 to 15 stray crocodiles every month from across the city. "This happens the most during monsoon. Some of them come from Ajwa. They enter the city when the sluice gates are opened during heavy rains," said Ashok Pawar of Late

Rohan Crocodile Charitable Trust.

Heading: VMC seeks Sardar Sarovar’s help to meet city’s water demands - Indian Express
Content:
A bachelor degree in science has helped me in the profession

A riot of caricatures of politicians and film stars mesmerised everyone at the M S University's (MSU) Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) department on Saturday, as cartoonist Sudhir Tailang stole the show.

"Cartoonists always make sketches of famous personalities. One of the most amusing and famous personalities is Modi. In the Gujarat Assembly election, he had shouted a slogan—mujhe fansi de dena, agar main maange na poori karoon (hang me if I don't fulfil the goals). I drew a cartoon strip where Modi is shouting and Manmohan Singh is running away," Tailang said.

Tailang began early, at the age of 10. Till now, he has covered around 10 Prime Ministers right from Mrs. Indira Gandhi to Manmohan Singh. He has an educational background in biology. "A bachelor degree in science has helped me in the profession. As a biologist, I dissected living beings including many frogs. Former prime minister Late P V Narasimha Rao had certain frog-like features," he said with a smirk.

He said further, "Science makes one's mind analytical and English literature makes an individual philosophical. Several such things make a cartoonist."

Tailang said that no professional degree could make a cartoonist. "I always make caricatures that are for the common man, he said.

Tailang will be releasing a compilation of 150 cartoons on Manmohan Singh in his book 'No Prime Minister'. "It takes six months for a prime minister to be a cartoon material. Everyone including Manmohan Singh has passed that acid test. I have invited Mr Singh to release the book and comment on the caricatures. It will be interesting see his comments since all of them are controversial," Tailang added.

Heading: MSU girls’ hostel officials worried about rising incidents of theft - Indian Express
Content:
The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has approached the Sardar Sarovar Narmada Nigam Limited (SSNNL) for additional supply of water, as it fears a water crisis to hit the city in future.

The water supply will come at a cost of Rs 37.69 lakh under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) project.

The decision has come after the widening of VMC jurisdiction following water scarcity in many parts of the city.

"The city limits are increasing and more villages are coming under the purview of the corporation. Water will be one of the major concerns in the future, which should be addressed soon," said P M Patel, executive engineer.

At present, the city requires 750 lakh gallons of water per day. While water from the Mahi River meets most of the requirement, Ajwa caters to the eastern part of the city.

"Almost 75 per cent of the supply comes from Mahi. Four new overhead water tanks have come up in different parts of the city. While the regions nearer to the tanks receive a generous quantum of water, the pressure staggers at the peripheral regions from the tanks," said Hemant Jaradi, executive engineer, water supply distribution.

SSNNL will supply water in two parts: while 160 MLD of water will be supplied till 2025, another 300 MLD will be supplied to the city by 2040.

Though SSNNL authorities have sent a letter of confirmation to the VMC, the logistics will be decided on Wednesday.

Heading: 57 Candles - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Sayajigunj police have not made any headway in the laptop theft case that took place in MSU's Kasturba Gandhi Halls of Residence three days ago, hostel authorities have admitted to an increase in theft cases and also pointed to the role of insiders.

Manisha Chaudhary, warden of Kasturba Gandhi Halls of Residence, said: "We suspect it to be the handiwork of some insider. After the serial blasts in Ahmedabad, as a precautionary measure, we have stopped students from going to each other's hostels. But I have checked all the rooms in KG Hall and found nothing."

Pointing to the theft statistics, MSU hostel authorities have said that they received more complaints of small-time thefts like that of food and clothes from the girls hostels.

Speaking to Newsline, D P Barambe, chief warden of MSU Halls of Residence said: "The incidences of theft are more in girls hostels as compared to the boys. In the last one-year, more than six cases of theft have been reported from the girls hostels. The matter must be given serious thought since most of the girls involved in these cases do not come from poor families."

On being asked as to what steps have been taken for this, he said, "We counsel such students and inform their parents." He added that a few months ago, a girl from Pandita Gargi Halls of Residence had picked up her roommate's ATM card and withdrawn a sizeable amount."

Commenting on this issue, Dr B H Buch, a city-based psychiatrist said: "We find more kleptomaniacs among the females of our species due to their urge to own something. It is not a matter of being rich or poor, but it is generally an urge to get something at a specific time."

Heading: Small wonder - Indian Express
Content:
The panel discussion for Screen's The Big Picture (our third edition this year) was attended by eminent personalities from the Hindi film industry who exchanged their views on various issues related to cinema. An elite panel of eight film industry professionals discussed the topic 'New, Improved Bollywood: Are we ready to take on the world?'. The panel included eminent names like writer-lyricist Javed Akhtar, actor-director Anupam Kher, actor Farooque Sheikh, writer-lyricist Prasoon Joshi, director-turned-actor Farhan Akhtar, actor Shiney Ahuja, Saurabh Varma, Chief Marketing Officer, Reliance Big Picture and Pankaj Khandpur, Creative Director, Visual Computing Labs, Tata Elxsi. They discussed film industry trends and achievements, which excited an audience that comprised a combination of both film and media personnel.

After a stimulating experience for the grey-cells, it was time to hit nightclub Enigma at the JW Marriott for a grand celebration. Amitabh Bachchan cut the anniversary cake and what followed was a pulsating evening that celebrated the success of one of the film industry's most respected publications.

Bollywood celebrities attended the evening with great enthusiasm and their presence added glamour to the evening. Film legends, popular TV artistes, dashing newcomers and popular filmmakers were all part of the celebration. The guest-list included Shatrughan Sinha with Poonam Sinha, Manmohan Shetty, Govind Nihalani, David Dhawan, Poonam Dhillon, Anu Malik, Sanjay Gadhvi, Sanjay Gupta and Madhur Bhandarkar, Kailash and Arti Surendranath, Sachin Pilgoankar, Renuka Shahane and Ashutosh Rana, Shankar Mahadevan, Pritam, Aadesh Srivastava, Sajid Khan, Lilette and Ravi Dubey and young guns like Arjun Rampal, Sonu Nigam, Himmesh Reshammiya, Luke Kenny, Purab Kohli, Nishikant Kamat, Sikandar Kher, Meera, Ronit Roy, Manasi and Rohit Roy, Sonal Chauhan, Mughda Godse, Vidya Malavade and many others.

A successful and engaging discussion on the happy developments in the film industry followed by a merry evening of glamour and glitz—it was a perfect way to bring in Screen's 57th year in business.

Heading: Up and down - Indian Express
Content:
Movie name: Welcome to Sajjanpur

Directed by: Shyam Benegal

Cast: Shreyas Talpade, Amrita Rao

Showing At: City Pride Kothrud, City Pride Satara Road, E-Square, Fame Akurdi, Gold Adlabs, INOX , Mangala

Welcome to the return of Shyam Benegal. The director, who's been meandering for some time with stodgy bio-pics, and moral science lessons, is back, doing what he is best at: creating life-like characters to tell life-like stories.

Sajjanpur is a modern-day, hovering-on-the-edge-of-prosperity Indian village where electricity and water have made inroads, as well as kutcha roads and rattling buses. But illiteracy is still rampant. Which is why Mahadev (Shreyas Talpade), the village's only 'padha likha' young fellow, hangs up a shingle under a bargad tree.

All kinds of people wash up under that tree: A loony aunt (Ila Arun) worrying about her manglik niece (Divya Dutta), a love-lorn wife (Amrita Rao), waiting to hear from her husband, away for four years in Bambai, a local neta (Yashpal Sharma) who can easily pass off as a goon, a compounder (Ravi Kissen) in love with a pretty widow (Rajeshwari Sachdev).

Welcome to Sajjanpur stays quirky and engaging even when the pace flags, and the rural accents turns faux, because of the felt screenplay and superbly robust, earthy dialogues by Ashok Mishra (this is a U/A film). That the village is really a set is evident too, but you overlook it all when you see how skillfully Benegal brings up the ills that beset us. If a girl is unlucky, marry her off to a dog. If a eunuch stands for election, get rid of her.

The film is saved from becoming the sort of dreaded preachy treatises that the director has been delivering of late. And a large part of that has to do with Talpade who wears his writer-of-letters-and-arbiter-of-lives role like second skin. But the real hero of the film is the village and the way it melds the past and the present: The profusion of all the Rams (Ram Ashrey, Ram Khilavan, Ram Singh), the references to Sita, and Kalyug, as well as the acknowledgment that a cell phone text message is also a letter.

The village had all but disappeared from Hindi cinema. Welome to Sajjanpur.

Heading: After US fiasco, India Inc ready for HR challenge - Indian Express
Content:
Movie Name: Saas Bahu Aur Sensex

Directed by: Shona Urvashi

Cast: Tanushree Datta,Ankur Khanna, Kirron Kher, Farooq Sheikh, Masumi Makhija, Lilette Dubey

Showing At: City Pride Kothrud, City Pride Satara Road, E-Square, Fame Akurdi, Gold Adlabs, INOX Pune, Mangala

Can women understand the complex world of finance, stocks and shares, and the Sensex? Or should they be confined to watching saas bahu serials?

Shona Urvashi's second film has a whopper of an idea. And stalwarts fronting it. Kirron Kher is the divorced, desperately-in-need-of-money Binita Sen, who fetches up at the door of Feroz Sethna, an eccentric out-of-work stock broker (Farooque Sheikh). He is rude and brusque. She is angry and annoyed. And then it turns into a profitable partnership, professional and personal.

The interplay between these two consummate actors could have taken Warner Bros' first Indian production Saas Bahu Aur Sensex to an interesting place. But the director sends out confusing signals by gathering up a bunch of kitty party aunties, converting them from couch potatoes to eager pink paper-reading stock hounds, and then letting them slip, and lose money. In between, youngsters working today's jobs crop up. Tanushree Dutta and Ankur Khanna are call-centre execs. Masumeh is a femme fatale, who wants money, not love.

In the end, it's all-over-the place and indeterminate. What makes up for the rest of it is watching the inimitable Farooq in a full-fledged role, and Kirron as a non-stereotyped Bollywood mom.

Heading: 85 per cent of WiFi lines in the city insecure, say experts - Indian Express
Content:
Positive changes on the cards, call to redefine role of HR managers

Even as the world is feeling the heat of the collapse of three major financial Institutions in the US, India Inc is ready to face the emerging challenge in a positive manner. That's the good news emanating from the finance and insurance sector in the country. India Inc is analysing the situation closely and is ready to bring in some positive changes, particularly in the working of human resource management.

Many in the industry feel that from mere pay roll managers and recruiters, the function of HR managers in the country should be shifted to that of advisories and providers of leadership development.

Speaking to The Indian Express on the sidelines of Tatva-2008, the annual HR summit of National Insurance Academy School of Management at Balewadi on Saturday, Sanjeev Kumar Jindal, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Finance, said what went wrong in the global financial market ought to be found out. "The reasons for this need to be studied. It is also an HR challenge," he said. The global finance sector was in turmoil. In the country, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority will step in to protect the interests of the policy holders and regulate orderly growth," he said. "HR is the face of the company...there are areas yet to be tapped."

G Srinivasan, chairman and managing director, United India Insurance, said in changing global scenario, the role of HR managers should be re-defined. "HR officials should be adept at managing changes. Managing talent is critical but HR officers also should start developing business acumen," he said. Agreeing, Vikram Mehmi, president and chief executive officer of Birla Sun Life Insurance, said that they should have a keen understanding of the business.

Industry leaders also feel that some of the tasks like recruiting should be outsourced so that the main role of the HR practitioner will be strategic planning.

According to Sanjay Kedia, managing director and country head of Marsh India Insurance Brokers Pvt Ltd, the outsourcing of some of the HR functions had already started in the industry. "It is still early to comment on the reason for the financial crumple that took place in the US. But in strategic issues, HR has a key role to play that should be utilised maximum," he said.

While S Krishnamurthy, chief executive officer, TTK Healthcare TPA Pvt Ltd, observes that there is less number of CEOs from HR stream. "There are CEOs from finance and production side but a CEO from HR stream is rare. This is an indicator. The mindset of HR has to be changed and it in itself has to act as a change agent," he said. Experts in the field also feel that HR practitioners have a role even in the vision statement of a company. Jacob Mankidy, Mankidy Associates Centre of HR Solutions, said with emerging global scenario a paradigm shift in HR was the need of the hour. "All easy-to-do task should be outsourced. HR practitioners should have a vision and should function to advice the company,'' Mankidy said.

Heading: Four, not two-year training for teachers proposed - Indian Express
Content:
The WiFi connections in the city have drawn serious objections from ethical hackers and computer experts, who, strongly believe that 85 per cent of them are "insecure." The lack of mechanism to record the identity of the persons using the WiFi network is another major problem, the experts point out.

Investigative agencies have found that members of Indian Mujahideen, the terrorist outfit that claimed the responsibility of recent serial blasts, broke into the "insecure" WiFi networks in Mumbai for sending the terror mails.

Such "insecure" systems are aplenty in Pune, experts stress. The Pune Municipal Corporation, as a part of its "unwired Pune" project has provided WiFi Internet zones at J M Road and Bund Garden Road. PMC's chief information officer Anupam Saraph admits that as of today the facility is available free of cost to all and no password is required to get into these

WiFi systems.

Internet security expert, Proshanto Mitra, who is chief technical officer of Balasai Net Pvt Ltd said, "Every IT Company here has a WiFi network. Almost 50 per cent of other corporate firms with broadband internet connections have acquired wire free technology. The number of individual internet users going for WiFi routers at home is increasing."

Mitra said that 85 per cent of the WiFi networks in the city are not protected. "Forget about precautions, a majority of WiFi users are not even aware of the risk. I have an access to five WiFi networks in my residential complex itself. There is no security installed and a person with criminal intention can easily hack these wireless network for dangerous purposes," he said.

Sudam Choure, chief co-ordinator of Pune Police Cyber Committee said, "Incidents in Mumbai are alarming. WiFi network of a college was hacked for sending a threat mail. Many colleges, hotels, cafeterias, shopping malls in Pune have WiFi connections and are allowing easy log-ins. There is no administrator to record the identity of those using the WiFi networks," he said.

"When I sit in my cabin, I have an access to a WiFi network of a hotel located in the adjacent building. Application of proper security measures can avoid other machines getting into your WiFi. But along with it, we also need to have a mechanism for identifying the person getting into the WiFi system. If this mechanism is in place, possibility of breaking into the wireless network would be less," he said.

"A major awareness drive is needed for securing the WiFi connections in the city. The issue was included in the action plan of cyber committee and was submitted to the former police commissioner Jayant Umranikar. We suggested the police to form a policy for commercial, corporate and home WiFi users that would enable identification of the internet user," he said.

The Pune police have however not taken any proactive measures yet. When contacted, deputy commissioner of police (cyber cell) Rajendra Dahale said, "We plan to hold a meeting of internet service providers for sensitising them about WiFi security. The formalities for organising the meeting are on."

Rohit Srivastva, an ethical hacker and founder of Club Hack, said, "Terrorism is not the only threat due to insecure WiFi network. There are other dangers like an attacker can read your confidential mails, credit card details and even chat with your girlfriend posing as you," he said.

Steps to protect your WiFi

* Go for WPA (WiFi protected access) or WPA2 (advanced version) security.

* Set complex passwords

* Change router login password and WPA/ WPA2 password frequently

* If you have three machines at home, create an IP pool for three IPs only

* Configure Media Access Control (MAC) binding so other machines could not connect to your WiFi

Courtesy Club Hack

Heading: Citizens urged to remain alert - Indian Express
Content:
Pointing at the commercialisation of teachers' training courses (BEd and DEd), Sharadchandra Beher, former chairman of National Council for Teachers' Education (NCTE), has proposed a four-year integrated programme in teachers' training instead of the present two-year format.

NCTE based in Bhopal is a regulatory body, which grants permission and regulates the teachers' training programmes run by various universities in the country. Beher pointed out that the NCTE has become only a permission granting authority for teachers' training courses instead of regulating them.

"The BEd and DEd courses are mushrooming in the country and various educational institutes start the courses with a purpose of making money," he said. Beher was speaking to this paper on the sidelines of a book release function in the city where the work of renowned educationist J P Naik was unveiled in the form of three books. He said the teachers' training job is crucial but the present quality is not up to the mark. "I have proposed an integrated four-year course in the teachers' training on the lines of engineering and medical courses," said Beher.

Incidentally, the state government has recently taken a decision to restrict the growth of BEd and DEd colleges in the state. "The decision may stop mushrooming of colleges but it won't serve the purpose. The quality factor is still important, which is not being taken care of," said Beher.

Beher also said that if any university shows willingness to start four-year integrated teachers' training course, the NCTE would be ready to give the permission.

The Indian Institute of Education (IIE) started by educationist J P Naik will start DEd course from the next year. "The institute is in the process of making proposal to the NCTE to take permission for the course," said Gautam Sen, director-general of IIE. IIE is a renowned institute in the state, which is actively involved in various aspects of education. UNESCO has placed the institute in the honour roll of 100 World Educators. The Institute is a non-government organisation, a public trust of which the dominant intention is public service through "Education for All' and "Health for All." "Considering the reputation of IIE, we want to create a role model for the other DEd colleges to follow," said Sen. He said that the institute would be running the same syllabus but the methodology would be different and practical oriented.

Heading: Five arrested for kidnapping law student, friend - Indian Express
Content:
Citizens should remain alert and must not hesitate to inform and cooperate with the security forces in case they encounter any suspicious object or person, Lt Gen R K Chhabra, chief of staff, Southern Command, said on Saturday.

"Our cities are being targeted by terrorists. With several serial blasts occurring across the country, it is vital that people remain vigilant to potentially dangerous situations and also be willing to help the armed forces in every possible way," Chhabra told media persons on the sidelines of a demonstration organised by the 203 Bomb Disposal Company (BDC), a unit of the Southern Command that specialises in bomb and Improvised Explosive Devices (IED) disposal, at its premises in Khadki.

"There is an urgent need to create an awareness among the public about the kind of bomb detection and disposal capabilities the Indian army has, which is the purpose of this exercise," he said. Asserting that the army was in a 'constant state of readiness' to counter any emergency or hazardous situation, Chhabra said, "The Indian army is equipped with several advanced technological counter measures. However, experience, training and awareness are key factors in combating the IED menace." Senior army officers will coordinate with the police to counsel citizens, especially college students, to be vigilant, as part of 'Mission Mritunjay' project launched recently by city police commissioner Satyapal Singh, Chhabra said.

Earlier, braving heavy rain, a team of army personnel attached to the 203 BDC, also known as the 'Khadki disposers,' put up an organised and professional display of the drills and actions taken by a counter IED squad to safely dispose of an IED, in the presence of several senior army officers. According to Lt Col M M Swamy, commanding officer, 203 BDC, the unit is equipped with state-of-the-art technology and 'counter IED' equipment such as explosive detectors, fibre optic surveillance devices and remotely operated vehicles.

"The remote-operated vehicles enable us to take X-ray images of a suspicious object and to carry it to a safe disposal area," Swamy said. He pointed out that the BDC had participated in the 1965 and 1971 wars against Pakistan and now provides training to army as well as police personnel at the security training centre in Ramtekdi.

Heading: Now, CYG to take the green route - Indian Express
Content:
The crime branch police on Saturday arrested five persons, including two history-sheeters, for allegedly kidnapping a law student of Bharati Vidyapeeth and his friend for a ransom of Rs 50 lakh.

The suspects have been identified as Vaibhav alias Pintya Manohar Choudhary (26) of Sahakarnagar, Lokesh Uttam Pulawale (29) of Chavannagar, Amjadkhan Pathan (28) of Shivdarshan, Rupesh Sable (22) of Bibvewadi and Mangesh alias Munna Pulawale (20) of Chavannagar. Vaibhav and Lokesh were reported to be history sheeters. Sheshzad Hussain Bhat (24) of Mahatma society, Kothrud has lodged a complaint with the police.

Police said Bhat, a student of law, was living with a friend Naved Abdul Majid Ali at Mahatma Society for last three years.

"Vaibhav was in love with Bhat's classmate who did not reciprocrate the feeling. So he and his accomplices barged into Bhat's house around 8 pm on Thursday. Flashing a fake pistol, they kidnapped Bhat and his friend Naved in a jeep. They snatched their mobile phones and took them to Khamgaon village on Pune-Solapur Road," said police inspector Vijaysinh Gaikwad.

"At Khamgaon, the suspects asked Bhat and Naved to arrange Rs 50 lakh for release. The suspects then consumed liquor. Interestingly, they consumed so much liquor, that Bhat and Naved gave them a slip and escaped from the spot," the police said.

"The duo then walked for 12 kilometres and then boarded a truck towards Pune. They then went to the Kothrud police station and lodged a complaint," he added.

Acting on a tip-off, the crime branch team comprising inspector Vijaysinh Gaikwad, assistant inspector Ashok Shelke, constables Santosh Kshirsagar, Yogesh Jagtap, Chandrakant Jagtap, Rajendra Marne and Narendra Parkhi nabbed the kidnappers at Padmavati on Saturday afternoon. Police recovered a mobile phone, a fake pistol and a jeep from the suspects.

Heading: Dow row: Warkaris gherao Chakan police station - Indian Express
Content:
The Commonwealth Youth Games is planning to go the green way by using battery-operated vehicles and low-intensity firecrackers to reduce pollution.

Former UN under-secretary general and chairman, CYG green council, Dr Shashi Tharoor who visited the CYG office at Senapati Bapat Road on Saturday told reporters, "Getting people together from 71 countries is a big task. Such mega-events might lead to some negative effects on the environment in the form of high fuel consumption by vehicles, loads of firecrackers etc. So, we are planning to use battery-operated vehicles and low-intensity firecrackers."

It is also likely to compensate the quantum of electricity used at the opening and closing ceremonies of the event. The quantum of electricity utilised will be generated later by a company from renewable sources of energy like solar, wind etc. This will be added to the main power grid later. However, the talks are still underway.

Tharoor also added that they are focusing on a four-point agenda to prevent environmental hazards, the major points of which include reduction of fuel consumption, reduction in the number of vehicles and replacing the energy sources.

MP Suresh Kalmadi, who was present on the occasion said, "We are going to use the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) route for the event," he said despite the fact that there is no BRT route falling on the stretch between Lohegaon Airport to Balewadi.

Heading: Delhi: 3 militants, Batla House caretaker arrested - Indian Express
Content:
Protesting against the arrest of seven warkaris by the Chakan police on Wednesday, over 200 warkaris on Saturday morning gheraoed the Chakan police station. The Pune rural police subsequently arrested as many as 115 warkaries, including 46 women, and their leader Banda Tatya Karadkar.

Earlier, the police had arrested seven warkaris for allegedly pelting stones at a Dow Chemicals engineer and setting fire to his jeep.

Claiming that the warkaris had nothing to do with the attack on the Dow engineer, over 200 activists of Warakari Sampraday, Vyasan Mukta Yuvak Sangh and villagers from Shinde gaon staged protests at the Chakan police station. Singing kirtans and raising slogans against Dow Chemicals, the warkaris demanded the release of the seven arrested.

Deputy Superintendent of Police (Khed division) Shrikrishan Kokate and other senior officers reached the spot. But when the warkaries refused to pay heed to Kokate's appeal to calm down, he ordered their arrests. They were shifted to an unknown location.

Vilas Javle, leader of Vyasan Mukta Yuvak Sangh said that the agitation will continue till the police release the warkaris.

Heading: Fierce gunbattle between militants, troops on LoC - Indian Express
Content:
Three more suspected 'Indian Mujahideen' militants allegedly involved in the Delhi serial blasts and the caretaker of a house where some members of the terror module were staying, have been arrested, police said.

A day after Delhi Police claimed to have identified 14 members of the module and arrested two of them, sleuths nabbed three others identified as Zia-ur-Rehman, Shakir Nishar and Shakil, who were on the run since the September 13 blasts.

Seven people are still at large and a hunt is on to catch them, a senior police officer said, adding the three arrests were made from a south Delhi locality.

Police had killed two terrorists, including Atif, the 'main man' of the Indian Mujahideen and alleged mastermind of recent serial blasts in several parts of the country, in a gunbattle in Jamia Nagar on Friday morning while two others were arrested the same day.

Police also arrested Abdul Rehman, the caretaker of the Batla House, where Atif and four others were staying on fake documents. The encounter had taken place in that house.

The officer said Zia and Shakeel were also allegedly involved in the July 26 Ahmedabad serial blasts that claimed more than 55 lives.

During the interrogation of Mohd Saif and Zeeshan who were arrested on Friday, police claimed that they told investigators that Shakeel had planted the bomb in Gaffar market in Karol Bagh.

The Delhi police had yesterday claimed that they have uncovered the conspiracy behind the attacks in the capital and in Jaipur and Ahmedabad saying they were carried out by terrorists of Indian Mujahideen and SIMI in league with Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba.

Heading: Terrorists planned to explode 20 bombs in Delhi: Police - Indian Express
Content:
A fierce gunbattle broke out on the Line of Control (LoC) between Indian troops and militants, who entered the country under the cover of firing from Pakistani side, in Poonch district of Jammu and Kashmir.

"A group of armed militants entered the Indian territory from Kabaristan post of Pakistan and were trapped by troops close to Kalash Indian Post between Zeroline and border fencing along LoC in Poonch district today," defence officials told PTI.

The gunbattle is still on, they said, adding that infiltration of militants followed the heavy cross-border firing on Indian positions along LoC since yesterday.

Heading: Suspense over N-deal: PM leaves for US, France on Mon - Indian Express
Content:
With the arrest of three more militants of the Indian Mujahideen allegedly involved in the serial blasts here, Delhi police today claimed that the terror module was planning to explode at least 20 bombs in several places in the national capital, including Nehru Place.

The IM militants were planning to strike terror by exploding bombs in Nehru Place, a locality which houses several multi-storeyed buildings, and other parts of the capital, Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) H G S Dhaliwal told reporters.

Zia-ur-Rehman, Shakir Nishar and Mohammad Shakil were arrested early this morning from Jamia Nagar, the locality where two terrorists, including the "main man" Atif were killed in a gun battle with police on Friday.

Police also arrested Abdul Rehman, the caretaker of Batla House where the terrorists were residing on charges of cheating and forgery. Rehman, the father of the arrested Zia allegedly forged the signature of the owner of the house. The encounter had taken place in that house.

During the interrogation of Mohd Saif and Zeeshan who were arrested on Friday, police claimed that they told investigators that Shakeel had planted the bomb in Gaffar market in Karol Bagh.

Dhaliwal said Zia and Shakeel planted bombs in the

Maninagar area in the heart of Ahmedabad during the July 26 serial blasts.

The Delhi police had yesterday claimed that they have uncovered the conspiracy behind the attacks in the capital and in Jaipur and Ahmedabad saying they were carried out by terrorists of Indian Mujahideen and SIMI in league with Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba.

Heading: Nepal: 21 killed in floods, landslides - Indian Express
Content:
Armed with an NSG waiver, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh embarks on a 10-day visit to the US and France on Monday amid mounting suspense over the Indo-US nuclear deal clearing the final Congressional hurdle in time for President George W Bush to toast the landmark accord.

Singh's first diplomatic engagement abroad after the crucial waiver that ended the countrys 34-year nuclear isolation may also see India and France firm up an agreement on civil nuclear energy cooperation after summit talks with President Nicholas Sarkozy in Paris on September 30.

With just three working days left for the US Congress to take a call on the 123 agreement to clear the decks for the nuke deal in its last lap, the White House is optimistic of wrapping up the pact during Singh's working visit to Washington on September 25 for a meeting with Bush.

In the backdrop of a string of terror attacks in India, Terrorism will be high on Singhs agenda in his parleys with Bush and bilateral meetings with world leaders on the sidelines of the 62nd annual session of the UN General Assembly in New York.

Singh is expected to firmly convey Indias strong concerns over cross-border terrorism and remind Pakistan about its commitments in this regard at his first meeting with President Asif Ali Zardari who has just spoken about the need for bilateral ties to be "creatively reinvented".

A meeting with Chinese premier Wen Jiabo has also been scheduled during which the two leaders are expected to put behind the strains in bilateral relations following Beijings perceived negative role at the Nuclear Suppliers Group(NSG) meet in Vienna.

Singh, who had last addressed the UN in 2005, will be in New York from September 23 to 27 after an overnight halt in Frankfurt. He will be attending the Indo-European Union(EU) Summit in Marseilles in France on September 29.

At the UN, Singh is expected to make a strong case for the expansion of the Security Council and democratisation of the UN systems. He will also touch upon important issues including terrorism, verifiable and comprehensive nuclear disarmament, food crisis and poverty eradication.

Heading: RCom out of top 10 most valued club - Indian Express
Content:
At least 21 people have been killed and thousands displaced due to massive floods and landslides in four districts of western Nepal.

Twelve people were killed in Kailai district, five in Doti and two each in Gulmi and Palpa districts due to floods and landslides as incessant rains lashed the region, police said, adding two dozen others were missing.

Some 3,500 families have been displaced as hundreds of houses submerged in Kailali and neighbouring Kanchanpur districts, officials said.

More than 24 villages were inundated in Kailali district.

In Kanchanpur, more than 50 per cent of villages were affected.

The rescue and rehabilitation work being carried out by the army and police has been hampered due to bad weather.

Heading: Asia Pacific: Indians-10th most intense Net searchers - Indian Express
Content:
Reliance Industries would increase the crude production from the prolific KG-D6 block to 20,000 barrels a day by Diwali, even as its gas output has been delayed till the first quarter of 2009.

The first cargo of oil would go to Hindustan Petroleum's Vizag refinery and the crude was benchmarked on Papis and Nigeria bonny light, an RIL official said. At the rate of 20,000 barrels a day, the total crude output would amount to one million tonnes a year.

The gas production would now start from the first quarter of 2009, instead of the second half of this year.

Heading: PepsiCo to invest $500 mn in India in 3 yrs - Indian Express
Content:
An Indian netizen is hitting the search button on an average 51 times during a month, but this puts them only at the last position among the top 10 countries of Asia-Pacific in terms of intensity of online search.

According to the latest ranking of top internet search figures for Asia-Pacific released by internet traffic tracking firm comScore, Koreans have topped in terms of online search intensity with an average of 102.8 searches per searcher during the month of July.

"Searchers in Korea exhibited the heaviest search intensity with an average of 102.8 searches per searcher during the month, followed by Australia (102 searches per searcher) and Japan (100.8 searches per searcher)," comScore said.

India has ranked after Korea, Australia, Japan, Singapore (91.2), New Zealand (87.2), Hong Kong (81), China (76.6), Taiwan (74.8) and Malaysia (64.2) on search intensity ranking.

India's score of 51 searches per searcher is even lower than the overall average of 80.7 for the Asia-Pacific region.

However, the figures might increase after taking into account traffic from the public computers. The comScore data has been compiled by taking into account all unique internet users aged 15 and above from their home and work computers and it excludes searches from public computers such as Internet cafes or access from mobile phones or PDAs.

However, India fares much better in terms of the number of people searching something on internet as well as in terms of the number of such searches.

Heading: RIL makes history with 1st deep-sea oil - Indian Express
Content:
Global soft-drinks major PepsiCo India said it will invest USD 500 million in India over the next three years to triple its business in the country.

"As a tangible sign of our continued confidence in India, I am delighted to announce that we will be investing USD 500 million in the next three years with the goal of tripling our business here," Pepsico Chairman and CEO Indra Nooyi said.

She said the investment would be made in various activities such as improving market infrastructure and agricultural capability.

The company has been registering double-digit growth both in volumes and revenues, Nooyi said, adding that in the next three years the company expects to generate 50,000 direct and indirect jobs in the country.

Since its entry in India in 1989, the company has become the fourth largest consumer firm in India.

Heading: India's bn-dollar club now half in value - Indian Express
Content:
Reliance Industries has created history by flowing oil from the nation's first deep-sea oilfield but gas production from the eastern offshore KG basin will begin in January, four months behind the deadline.

Reliance began oil production from its predominantlyg as-rich KG-DWN-98/3 or D6 block on September 17 with initial oil flowing at the rate of 5,500 barrels per day, the company Chairman Mukesh Ambani announced today in Mumbai.

Crude oil production will reach 20,000 barrels per day (1 million tonnes a year) in a month's time and the peak output of 40,000 barrels (2 million tonnes) of oil will be achieved in the first quarter of 2010.

Company CEO and President Oil & Gas P M S Prasad said Reliance had internally set 2008 as the target for oil and gas production from D6 but officially it had always stated that gas production will begin in second half of 2008-09 .

Reliance is selling the first oil from D6 to HPCL's Vizag refinery on spot basis and will look for long-term contract when the production stabilises when it reaches peak.

The first cargo of oil would go to Hindustan Petroleum's Vizag refinery and the crude was benchmarked on Papis and Nigeria bonny light, an RIL official said.

The gas output, to begin with, will be around 15 million mmscmd (million standard cubic metres per day) rising to 40 mmscmd in three months.

Heading: RIL to step up oil output to 20,000 barrels - Indian Express
Content:
The ongoing turmoil in equity markets, coupled by the recent depreciation in rupee value, has forced out as many as 87 companies from the elite billion-dollar market value club, while shrinking its overall valuation by nearly half.

There were as many as 226 companies with a market valuation of at least a billion dollar as on January 10 – the day when the stock market benchmark Sensex scaled its life-time peak before falling prey to a bear-run continuing for over eight months now.

However, the size of this elite club has shrinked to just 139 companies now and its cumulative market value currently stands at about 796 billion dollars (Rs 36,62,000 crore), against close to 1,600 billion dollars (Rs 1,60,000 crore) on January 10.

This diminution is primarily caused by a sharp plunge in the stock market that has lost nearly one-third of its value during this period. A steep fall of over 17 per cent in rupee value versus US dollar has also contributed considerably in the shrinking size of this elite league.

The rupee has plunged to near 46 level against the US greenback, against its close to 39.25 level on January 10.

Besides, the Sensex is currently hovering near the 14,000-point level after peaking at 21,206.77 points on January 10.

Those having moved out of this club include Anil Ambani group's Adlabs Films, Tata group's Tata Tea, Naresh Goyal-led Jet Airways, biotechnology major Biocon, IFCI, Max India, HCL Infosystems, Patni Computer, Jain Irrigation, Bajaj Hindustan, Gujarat NRE Coke, Praj Industries, Madras Cement and India Cement.

Heading: Deepa Mehta's 'Heaven on Earth' to open fest in NY - Indian Express
Content:
Victor Hanescu mercilessly crushed India's hopes to make the Davis Cup World Group as he knocked out Prakash Amritraj in the first reverse singles to give Romania an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-match playoff tie.

The Romanian number one outplayed Prakash 6-2 6-3, 6-1 to make the second reverse singles, to be played between Somdev Devvarman and Victor Cruvoi, inconsequential.

Hanescu, world number 67, remained undefeated in the tie as he displayed a solid all-round game and the Indian, ranked as low as 222, had no answer to his powerful game.

A berth in the World Group thus continued to remain out of India's reach and it goes back to the Asia/Oceania Group, where it will once again fight to come back to play the World Group play-offs.

India last played in World Group in 1998.

Hansecu raised the tempo gradually and raised his game to a different level as the match progressed, taking it away from the Indian game after game.

Prakash did play well in flashes but it needed immense talent apart from mental toughness and continued intensity to tame a player like Hanescu.

Early trouble welcomed Prakash as he faced breakpoint in the very first game of the match but saved it via some big serves.

Hanescu continued the way he played on the first day as he served well and used the drop shots brilliantly.

The Romanian number one had pummelled Somdev Devvarman in the singles on Friday but Prakash, India's number one, was determined to give a good fight to his formidable opponent in the must-win match for the visitors.

Heading: Reverse flick: Kaushik sent back to women’s team - Indian Express
Content:
Indian filmmaker Deepa Mehta's Preity Zinta-starrer 'Heaven on Earth', which touches the issues of immigration, isolation and power of imagination will open an annual film festival of Indian and diaspora films.

The film, which was premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival last week, will feature at this year's Mahindra Indo-American Arts Council Film Festival of Indian Independent and Diaspora Films on November 5, where it will be screened at the Lincoln Center Jazz.

The 106-minute film in Punjabi and English revolves around Chand (Zinta), who travels from India to Canada to marry Rocky (Vansh Bhardwaj), a man she has never met.

Her dream of a new life morphs into a nightmare as marriage to Rocky and his family becomes a numbing spiral of confusion and pain.

Chand finds hope in her friendship with Rosa (Yanna McIntosh), a street-smart woman from Jamaica who works with her at a laundry factory.

Rosa gives Chand a magical root and promises that it will make Rocky fall deeply in love with her. The experiment ends in a surreal parallel life that mirrors an Indian fable involving a King Cobra.

Besides, "Little Zizou", written and directed by Sooni Taraporevala, will be the closing film to be screened on November 9. The 101-minute film stars Boman Irani, Sohrab Ardeshir and Imaad Shah among others with John Abraham in a special appearance.

"Little Zizou" is a comedy for audiences of all ages and nationalities. It is the rambunctious and moving story of how two battling Mumbai families finally come to terms with each other.

Heading: Stroke of genius - Indian Express
Content:
Indian hockey continues to amaze. A day after the Indian Women's Hockey Federation (IWHF) protested MK Kaushik's appointment as chief coach of the men's team for two years, he has been 'sent back' to the women's team.

Confirming this, IOA technical director MP Ganesh, who is also treasurer of the IWHF, said that Kaushik will remain with the women's team. "He won't be with the men's team and will continue as the national coach of the women's team. There was some communication gap but it has been sorted out and everything is clear now," Ganesh told The Indian Express.

The IWHF had claimed that it was not taken into confidence by the IOA selection committee before naming Kaushik — who last coached the men's side in 1998 — as the men's chief coach. Kaushik has been working with the women's national team for a long time now. "I don't have a problem with either side. I will work with whichever team I am asked to," Kaushik said, admitting that as of now, he wasn't sure of his role.

Kaushik is awaiting formal announcement of being deputed to SAI till the 2010 Commonwealth Games. "Everything will be clear in a couple of days," he added. However, he hinted that he would prefer to coach the men's side, indicating that there were more chances of success with them.

However, sources said that not only had Kaushik been informed that he will remain with the women's team, he would soon join them at the ongoing national camp in Bangalore.

The IOA ad hoc committee, though, is yet to take a final call on the issue. Ashok Kumar Mattoo, one of the committee members, said that the matter will be resolved in the next couple of days. "Kaushik was picked by the selection committee and now we find that there is a difference of opinion. Hopefully things will be worked out soon," he told The Indian Express. Chairman of the selection committee Ajitpal Singh was unavailable for comment.

If Kaushik goes back, it will again leave men's hockey in the lurch. The selection committee had named a four-member support staff which was expected to submit a detailed coaching and training programme for the team by the weekend. However, with Kaushik now out of the scene, things are back to square one for the men's side which has been sitting idle for almost six months now.

Though there is no information on his replacement, sources say that none of the three coaches named to assist Kaushik — Harendra Singh, Romeo James or Ramandeep Singh — is expected to take charge. Which means the process of appointing a new coach will begin all over again.

If one thought that the former IHF administration was a "mess", things don't seem to be getting any better under the new regime.

Heading: Arsenal power through to the top - Indian Express
Content:
Perhaps it was the big cheers from a group ahead on the sixth hole. Or the little glance he stole at the scoreboard on his way to the ninth tee. Whatever inspired Jyoti Randhawa's sudden burst of form, it was enough to completely turn the third round around at the DLF Masters.

The defending champion's three-under 69 put him at seven-under 209, two shots in front, as overnight leader Gaganjeet Bhullar's double-fumble left him tied second with Shamim Khan. A rainy morning forced Saturday's play to start four hours late, and once the leadergroup had teed off in the afternoon's hazy sunshine, Randhawa took his own time to get going.

A bad lie of his tee shot meant Randhawa reached the green in three, and then missed the par putt to drop a shot on the very first hole. On the fourth, he was again off key with the driver, hitting the rough across the cartpath on the left. Left with a huge putt, he took three tries to hole. And just like that, Randhawa had fallen two-under for the tournament and three behind Bhullar.

A group ahead, Arjun Singh and Shamim were making their moves, Singh stunning with an eagle on the par-five sixth. But that was when Randhawa took charge, sinking a 25-foot long putt on the par-five ninth for an eagle, a three-foot birdie after his breathtaking second shot on the 10th, and an eight-footer for another birdie on the par-three 11th, going from one-over for the day to three-under, and in joint lead with Bhullar on seven-under.

Bhullar seemed to rise to the challenge, his second shot on the tenth matching Randhawa's stunner and giving him the day's second birdie. But the parity was broken on the par-four 13th as Bhullar finally blinked, his ball brushing tree-tops and getting lodged in heavy rough on way to a bogey.

Disaster came in the shape of a double bogey, 3 holes later. An awry second shot on the 17th was lost in the bushes behind the green, a shot penalty and then a two-putt finish had the 20-year-old suddenly reeling three behind Randhawa. Fortunately for him, the round ended on a positive note as he struck his third shot inches away from the pin on the par-five 18th for a birdie. He finished with a second successive level-par round, totalling five-under 211. Shamim's 69 came with six birdies and three bogeys, and the Delhi player will join Randhawa in the final day's lead group.

Heading: New-look Europe cut through US lead - Indian Express
Content:
New West Ham United manager Gianfranco Zola got off to a winning start on Saturday as fellow Italian new boy David di Michele scored twice in a 3-1 home Premier League victory over a ragged Newcastle United, while Arsenal raced to the top of league standings after coming from behind.

Kevin Davies headed Bolton into an early lead but, after Emmanuel Adebayor and Alexandre Song hit the woodwork for Arsenal, before Emmanuel Eboue levelled in the 26th minute and Niklas Bendtner put the visitors ahead a minute later.

Bolton had chances in the second half before Denilson made sure for Arsenal with a goal after another lightning break. Liverpool, who beat Manchester United in their last league outing, spent almost the entire afternoon on the attack against Stoke City at Anfield but, a disallowed Steven Gerrard goal apart, could not break down the promoted side's defence in a goalless draw.

In Saturday's other games Michael Chopra came off the bench to score twice as Sunderland beat Middlesbrough 2-0 and Blackburn Rovers beat Fulham 1-0 with a late goal by Matt Derbyshire.

Heading: India ‘A’ sweat over batsmen’s form - Indian Express
Content:
Even with Sergio Garcia and Lee Westwood reduced to spectators, the Europeans cut into the commanding US lead at the Ryder Cup on Saturday.

The Europeans closed a three-point deficit to 7-5 by winning two matches and halving another at Valhalla Golf Club. Jim Furyk and Kenny Perry gave the Americans their only outright win of the morning alternate-shot matches, beating Padraig Harrington and Robert Karlsson 3-and-1.

Phil Mickelson and Anthony Kim, who played so well for the US on the first day, squandered a 4-up lead after six holes. Henrik Stenson and unheralded Englishman Oliver Wilson closed out the match 2-and-1 when Wilson rolled in a 30-foot birdie at No 17. The Americans knew they had let a big one slip.

Ian Poulter and Justin Rose kept up their solid play, giving the Europeans the first point of the day. They defeated Stewart Cink and Chad Campbell 4-and-3, wrapping it up at No. 15 when the erratic American duo posted their fourth bogey of a round that also included a double bogey.

Heading: Watson best replacement: Ponting - Indian Express
Content:
With the series evenly poised, India A will start their second-half campaign hoping to keep a clean slate against New Zealand A when the two sides lock horns tomorrow.

The second half of the league phase heading to the final of the tri-series, involving Australia-A, New Zealand A and India-A, is well-balanced with the teams having six points each from three encounters.

India A, who defeated New Zealand A by five wickets on Wednesday, would hold an edge over their rivals in the third of their four-match league game tomorrow. The final is scheduled for next Thursday.

However, form of the seniors remains a concern as batsmen like Robin Uthappa, Suresh Raina, Rohit Sharma and Dinesh Karthik are yet to find their usual rhythm having been dismissed cheaply.

With pacers Irfan Pathan, Praveen Kumar and spinners Piyush Chawla and Yusuf Pathan, India's bowling attack looks stronger than the Kiwis who have spinner Jeetan Patel as the main strike bowler having notched up five for 52 from two matches in 12 overs. Although Mark Gillespie (5/71) and Grant Elliot (3/34) were also amongst wickets, they were sent on a leather hunt.

Meanwhile, curator K Parthasarathy predicted a high-scoring match provided the rain does not play spoilsport. "The wicket is firm and hard and it should help the batsmen," he said.

Heading: Presidential intervention in Sri Lanka’s IPL tussle - Indian Express
Content:
Australia skipper Ricky Ponting feels Shane Watson is the best possible replacement for sacked all-rounder Andrew Symonds and has backed him to be in the playing XI during next month's Test series against India.

"Him for Symonds is probably the absolutely likely swap at the moment," Ponting was quoted as saying by The Australian on the eve of the team's departure to India for the four-match Test series.

Ponting feels Watson's all-round ability may have helped him win a place in the side even if Symonds is around. "I think he might have played anyway if Symonds was around, just for that flexibility and what his bowling can offer," the captain said. "I would be surprised if he didn't play in the opening game."

It was Watson's spate of injuries that had opened the door for Symonds to establish himself in the Test side and now Symonds's sacking for indiscipline has presented Watson the chance to do the same.

Noffke lure for cash

Disillusioned at being ignored for next month's Test series against India, Australian pacer Ashley Noffke has warned the national selectors that he might take a plunge into cash-rich Indian Twenty20 leagues for the sake of his family.

"I have told 'Digger' (national selection chairman Andrew Hilditch) that I am totally disillusioned with the way these selections work. I have to now start to think about where I am placed and how much money I can earn to look after my family. There is the IPL and the ICL on my mind," Noffke added.

Heading: Badri: Back by default again - Indian Express
Content:
Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapakse is expected to meet Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) officials and the players, who are refusing to tour England due to clash of dates with the IPL.

SLC Chairman Arjuna Ranatunga has written to players asking them to skip matches of IPL 2009 but the players have contended they have already committed to play in the tournament. "I will call the two sides and look into the matter," Rajapakse had said adding he would take up the matter after he returned from his US visit later this month.

Heading: India’s dual core performance - Indian Express
Content:
Subramaniam Badrinath was in the middle of a dream season when Dilip Vengsarkar took over as the chairman of selectors two years back.

However, Badrinath's 636 runs from seven games in 2005-06 went in vain as the star-studded Indian middle-order had no vacancy. Not quite frustrated by the snub, Badrinath continued to be among the top run-getters in subsequent seasons. But despite several openings in the Indian line-up over a period of time, the Vengsarkar-led selection committee continued to ignore the Tamil Nadu batsman.

Then last month, Lady Luck finally smiled on Badri as an injury to Sachin Tendulkar saw him get a place in the ODI squad for the Sri Lanka series. And as it turns out, in Vengsarkar's final days as the chairman of the national selection committee, Badri has now been picked in the Irani Cup squad. Once again, the reason for this late-inclusion is Tendulkar's lack of fitness.

Being in the Irani Cup squad is no guarantee that Badri will make it to the Test squad for the Australia series to be announced next month, but one thing is clear: The middle-order batsman attracted the selectors' attention by his consistent show on the domestic circuit. Equations will change with the formation of a new selection panel and it will be interesting to see if Badri's new found status is permanent.

When news about Tendulkar's dodgy elbow surfaced on Friday, several cricketers would have fancied themselves as the likely replacement. Among those were Rohit Sharma, who was part of the Test squad that toured Sri Lanka and Suresh Raina after his convincing show in the Sri Lanka ODI series.

But with Badri heading to Baroda now for the September 24-28 game, it is clear that the selectors place him high on the waiting list of second stringers.

When the all-important call came to Badri on Saturday, he couldn't take it since he was busy training for the India A versus New Zealand A game on Sunday. "Vengsarkar had called me, but I couldn't take his call. So he called our coach Dav Whatmore, who relayed the news to me," Badrinath told The Indian Express.

Speaking about the importance of inclusion in the squad, he said, "It feels great that finally my performances have led me somewhere. I did well for India 'A' and this is definitely a result of that. Now what I need to do is to score well in such opportunities."

After the selectors were blamed for ignoring Badri all these years, they have given him that all-important chance while being on their way out. Now it is up to Badri to take make the best of this opportunity.

Shikhar back in Delhi squad

New Delhi: Shikhar Dhawan, who missed the Mohammad Nissar Trophy and the India A Test series due to a thumb injury, will join the Delhi team for their Irani Cup tie against the Rest of India at Vadodara starting September 24.

Dhawan will replace Gaurav Chhabra from the 15-member Delhi squad that was selected for the Mohammad Nissar Trophy.

"Dhawan has confirmed his availability for the Irani Cup and will replace Gaurav Chabbra," Chetan Chauhan, chairman of selectors said on Saturday.

Heading: ‘Dreams are like being on the Internet with God’ - Indian Express
Content:
Leander Paes and Mahesh Bhupathi relied on their experience to keep India afloat in the Davis Cup World Group play-off against Romania as the duo quelled the challenge of Horia Tecau and Adrian Cruciat 6-4, 7-6 (0), 6-4 in the doubles rubber here on Saturday.

The ace Indian pair had to toil hard to defeat the Romanians, who tested their opponents with an all round game but could not stop the visitors from reducing the margin to 1-2 in the five-match tie in close to three hours. The reverse singles will be played on Sunday and Prakash Amritraj and Somdev Devvarman have a daunting task ahead as they seek to steer India to the World Group stage for the first time since 1998.

The Indians saved a break point in the very first game of the match and squandered two on their opponents' serve in the fourth game, letting the scoreline to be 2-2. The Romanians broke in the fifth game, only to be broken back in the very next. Down 30-40, Tecau came up with a brilliant serve and Bhupathi's return could not cross the net as the Romanians saved the first break point. A double fault gave the Indian pair another chance but Cruciat warded off the threat, exploiting the gap between Paes and Bhupathi.

The Indians raised their game and fought back brilliantly in the next game to neutralise the lead. One set up, the Indians were broken in the first game of the second set though they saved four breakpoints as the hosts wrested an early initiative. The Indians got their first chance in the fourth game but the hosts' played well to negotiate the Indian attack.

However, India continued to attack and earned three break points but Tecau once again served brilliantly to save all three. The Indians missed one more break point but converted their fifth chance when Cruciat hit Paes' overhead volley to net, making it 3-3. The Indian pair had a chance to wrap up the second set as they had triple set points in the 12th game but the Romanians managed to stretch it to the tie-breaker.

Once the Indians had got the break in the fifth game of the third set, the Romanians dropped the intensity and the Indians easily won the set. They saved two break points in the eighth game, denying Romania any chance to come back but wasted two match points in the ninth game. Bhupathi then served for the match in the 10th game.

Heading: ‘Atif’s sister was unwell... he was supposed to bring her home’ - Indian Express
Content:
