The Vinod Gupta Charitable Foundation, set up by Gupta's son Vinod Gupta, had renovated the rooms in December 2007. But both stand locked because the university "wants to maintain the prestige and honour of Sharma and Gupta" by allotting the rooms only to meritorious students. Till date, it has not found any, said Chief Provost Nishi Pandey. "In order to get these rooms, a student has to obtain over 60 per cent marks in the Intermediate exams, with a good record in extra curricular activities," she said.

The teachers and students, however, allege

that the university had made the selection procedure complicated.

Giri Lal Gupta, who works as an administrator in a private hospital in Ghaziabad, said he had asked LU to frame rules for selection of students.

"The university may have decided on some specifications, but I do not have any role. Shankar Dayal Sharma was my close friend, so I renovated the rooms in his memory. The university should identify the right candidates and allot the rooms as soon as possible," he added.

Heading: IIM-L set to start global forum of its alumni - Indian Express
Content:
Uttar Pradesh will now churn out pilots. Three flight training academies and an aircraft maintenance engineering institute are coming up on the state-owned airstrips on a Public Private Partnership (PPP) model.

Last week, three flying clubs of the country — Chetak, Ambition and Pioneer — received the No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Director General Civil Aviation (DGCA) to set up their flight training academies on the airstrip in Aligarh.

The Chetak Flying Club is also setting up the Uttarakhand Academy of Aircraft Maintenance Engineering Institute along the airstrip.

Chairman of the club, B P S Yaduvanshi said: "We are the only flying club in the country to have a Cessna 172-R trainer aircraft and a twin engine eight-seater pressurised heavy aircraft Cessna 421-B."

The institutes have initiated the admission process. Rajiv Khandari, the Chairman of Mumbai-based Ambition Flying Club, said: "We began the admission process from September 12 immediately after getting the approval from the DGCA. The training classes started from September 15."

Saroj Joshi, the Chairperson of Delhi-based Pioneer Flying Club and daughter of BJP leader Murli Manohar Joshi, said: "Our institute will become operational in about a month."

In July 2007, the Mayawati government had decided to hand over all the 12 state-owned airstrips to private investors for setting up of flying training academies and aircraft maintenance engineering institutes on PPP model.

The airstrips — located in districts of Ambedkarnagar, Ghazipur, Sultanpur, Aligarh, Meerut, Farrukhabad, Faizabad, Kushinagar, Sonebhadra, Lakhimpur Kheri, Shrawasti and Etawah — used only for VVIP movements till now.

Due to the sporadic use, the infrastructure at most of these airstrips has deteriorated over the years, with an exception being the Saifai (Etawah) airstrip, which was upgraded by the Mulayam Singh Yadav government and was regularly used by him and his relatives. 

Under the present agreement, a private investor is required to pay Rs 3 lakh per year for initial five years to the government, after which the contract will be renewed with a 50 per cent hike in the charges. The state government is providing the airstrips, hangars and terminal buildings to the investors on a 30-year lease. The government has also allowed them to undertake further construction on the premises and add facilities required for setting up of institutes.

Besides the three companies that have started functioning in Aligarh, six proposals from India Pacific, Chawla, Flytech, Manpower Solutions Pvt Ltd, Sultan Education Society and Saraswati Educational Society are lying with the state government for other airstrips.

"The Saraswati Educational Society has opted for the Sultanpur airstrip and is getting the runway renovated as per the DGCA guidelines. The airstrip will soon become operational," said a senior officer of the State Civil Aviation department.

He added that the general recession in the market has affected the progress on other proposals.

Heading: Lucknownama - Indian Express
Content:
To bring together its alumni across the world and create a forum where they can find business solutions, the Indian Institute of Management-Lucknow (IIM-L) Alumni Committee is set to begin a global teleconference network.

Named the "IIM Lucknow Dialogue", the first interaction of this forum will be held on September 27.

In order to connect to the forum, each alumnus will be provided with a toll free number once they register online. At present, over 3,000 IIM-L alumni are working in different fields across the world.

For the first talk, the alumni committee has already received 90 registrations from 15 countries.

"We were expecting around 50 registrations the first time. But the response has been tremendous," said Ashkar Pandey, a coordinator of the committee.

In view of the response, alumni of other IIMs have also been invited to join the forum. Till date, one alumnus from IIM-Calcutta and another from IIM-Ahmdabad have registered for the forum.

Nitin Das, a filmmaker based in Mumbai, will deliver the first speech on "MBAs and Movies — the Bollywood experience".

Heading: Villagers on vigil at mobile checkposts in forests - Indian Express
Content:
Mobile error gets Don moved

Why has don-turned-MLA Mukhtar Ansari been shifted to Agra jail from his hometown Ghazipur? This, even though his brother Afzal Ansari had defied a party whip to vote against the UPA in the trust vote to please Mayawati.

Now, though the Ansari brothers may be behind the bars for the murder of former BJP legislator Krishnand Rai, both have enough clout to enjoy facilities which ordinary prisoners can never dream of. They have been frequently using cellphones. There is talk in certain circles that during a telephonic conversation, Mukhtar Ansari was overheard using inappropriate language to "people who matter". He was promptly dispatched to Agra, where, unlike Ghazipur, nobody holds him in great awe.

Worse for the Ansari brothers, the BSP has made up its mind to field its own candidate, Girdhari Yadav from Ghazipur in the Lok Sabha election.

CMO policing the police

The government has clipped the wings of DGP Vikram Singh. The office of IG (Establishment) that controls non-gazetted policemen, including constables, has been placed under Vijay Singh, secretary to the chief minister, who is an IG-rank officer. This means the CMO is keeping a watch on every little change in the police force.

Moreover, politicians who keep lobbying for transfer and postings of inspectors, sub-inspectors and constables now need not approach the DGP. Technically, Vijay Singh may be under the DGP, but the way things work in the government, the CMO could be introducing changes directly. Now, the police officers are keen to know who is going to be the IG (Personnel) — another important administrative post, which has been vacant since H C Kashyap was sent to Gorakhpur. If the government chooses an officer who is not in the good books of the DGP, that would compound Vikram Singh's problems.

'File notings' of an outgoing babu

A babu who was unceremoniously moved out of the Chief Minister's Office recently is still the topic of discussion in the Secretariat.

Before moving out, he quietly pushed a file for regularising the services of a junior woman officer working on an ad hoc basis in the Department of Culture.

It is said that even after getting his transfer order, he stayed in his office and tried to have the confirmation order issued the same day, but the minister refused to sign the file. But why was the babu so desperate? There are as many stories as there are mouths.

Polluted: PCB's very own data

It seems that officials of the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board do not trust their own data. A board report says that Khurja is one of the most polluted cities in the country.

It has the highest level of suspended particulate matter (SPM) and respiratory suspended particulate matter (RSPM) in the state.

The officials, however, say the figures cannot be completely trusted. "Khurja is a small place. Who knows where they have put up the instruments to measure the SPM and RSPM? The machines must have been set up in a dusty area," said an officer.

LDA sweetens the housing issue

The Lucknow Development Authority has started offering sugar candy with a glass of water to persons visiting its office for registration of their properties during the Saturday camp. "The allottees come from far-off places. They are our customers and it is our responsibility to serve them some sweet and water, as we do with guests at home," said Vice-Chairman Mukesh Kumar Meshram. Courtesy is always welcome. But it will be a lot sweeter if Meshram could do something to improve the efficiency of the agency. Incidently, the LDA isn't the first to start the practice. In Bareilly, police stations have been asked to offer jaggery, roasted gram and water to complainants.

On cue, a new role for Ishmit

The IBSF World Billiards Championship, held at Bangalore recently, proved lucky for a veteran cueist of the state. UP Billiards and Snooker Association Secretary Ishtmit Singh Malik was voted the best referee by European Confederation of Billiards Sport officials. The man, who once donned the vest coat, was specially commended for his excellent handling of the exciting match between world champion Pankaj Advani and Sourav Kothari — the "young Bengal tiger of billiards".

Heading: Caught in debt trap, man kills family & self - Indian Express
Content:
The forest department has set up mobile checkposts in the district after the chinkara poaching case involving state minister Dharmaraobaba Atram.

Deputy conservator of forests (Pune) Ashok Khadse said two mobile teams are maintaining strict vigil on the forests. These have been started with the help of villagers, who will keep an eye open for poachers seeking to hunt endangered species in Indapur, Mulshi, Daund and Pune talukas.

Atram was charged with killing a chinkara, an endangered species, at Chaudharwadi in Pune district on June 14. The minister absconded for a few days, was arrested later and then granted bail.

Forest officers said the case could be cracked because of the vigilance of local villagers. "It is because of the villagers and forest officers that the chinkara poaching case came to light. Now with the mobile checkposts in place, it will help step up security," Khadse said.

The forest department has also taken up a green drive and beautification of Sinhagad and Purandar forts before the Commonwealth Youth Games take off. "Work is progressing fast and we have already got Rs 2 crore for beautifciation of Sinhagad fort," Khadse said. Before the Youth Games begin, the forest department plans to a green drive on patches of Panchgaon Parvati and Vetal tekdi.

Heading: At depots at least, bus utility set to break even - Indian Express
Content:
Labour contractor had taken a loan on behalf of another man, who vanished without repayment

Burdened with debt, a man murdered his wife and two children and then killed himself in their flat in Pimpri this morning. Vijay Poojari (50) strangled his wife Sudha (40), daughter Prerna (18) and son Pratik (10) before hanging himself, the police said.

Vijay was a labour contractor and Sudha a teacher at Jaihind Primary School in Pimpri. Prerna was a first year student at Manghanmal Udharam College of Commerce and Pratik a fifth-grade student at Jaihind School.

"Vijay first stabbed his daughter and then strangled her, as the wounds indicate. Then he strangled his wife and son with a nylon rope. Techincally, we have registered a case of murder against Vijay," said Assistant Commissioner of Police Prabhakar Patil.

The debt for which Vijay killed himself, it appeared, was not for himself but for another man. Patil said, "We found a suicide note in the house. Vijay wrote that he was committing suicide because he was in debt. He had taken Rs 23 lakh from a friend in February and given it to another man, Deepak Kashyap. Kashyap did not return the money by May 1 as promised. On June 30 and July 1, Kashyap issued two cheques that bounced. Humiliated and unable to repay the loan, Vijay said he had no option but to suicide. We are registering a case of abetment against Kashyap who is untraceable."

Sudha's mother stays in the same building at Victory Co operative Housing Society near Deluxe Theatre chowk. Neighbour Satish Ghoderao said, "Sudha's mother repeatedly knocked on the door this morning. When no one responded, she informed us. From outside we could hear the TV playing, but nobody was opening the door. So we got in touch with advocate Deepak Palande, who informed the police," he added. The police broken open the door and found the bodies.

Sudha had worked with Jaihind Primary School for 26 years, said principal Jyotika Malkani. "She was very hardworking teacher. Initially with the pre-primary section, she was promoted because of her good track record," said a shocked Malkani, adding: "Sudha had attended school on Saturday and interacted with parents as usual. When I mentioned a weak child, Sudha told me not to worry and she would take care of the child from Monday. She was so cheerful. Colleagues told her that her saree was shining and she was all smiles," the principal said.

Heading: Petrol pumps get extra diesel, put strike on hold - Indian Express
Content:
By the end of the month, all ten depots of the Pune Mahanagar Parivahan Mahamandal Limited (PMPML) would break even, said the bus utility's outgoing chief, S B Patil, who listed this as his topmost achievement in his short tenure that ended on Saturday.

"Three depots (Kothrud, Pune station and Katraj) have already broken even. The rest of the depots will be there by the month-end. At least at the depots, we have been able to balance our expenses and revenue," he said.

He credited the achievement to meticulous management and sticking to rational route structures.

The company has not been able to reduce its accumulated losses but Patil said a lot of other financial wrangles had been sorted out. "We were able to dispose of pending arrears of over Rs 8 crore in terms of DA and pension. These dues had been pending since 1995," he said.

The company had also for the first time paid Rs 50 lakh from its own coffers towards procurement of buses, Patil added. "Generally, the corporations pay for the new buses," he said.

Patil said that there had been a 25 per cent increase in the number of passengers travelling in PMPML buses in his tenure. "The average number of passengers per day had stagnated at around 7 lakh per day. Now it is over 8.25 lakh, because of which income has also increased," he said.

Patil joined the Pune Municipal Transport in June 2007 and will now be heading to Konkan as divisional commissioner. "After the merger in October 2007, a lot of employee related issues cropped up, which took a lot of our time. I know that we have not been able to improve the comfort of the passengers. However, we have been working on it; by the month-end, 162 new buses will arrive and frequency will go up. The PCMC has also given us Rs 8 crore for bus purchase, which will again help increase frequency. But for four to five months more, I would have been able to increase passenger comfort substantially. One year was not enough," he said.

Heading: Mixed luck for city shuttlers - Indian Express
Content:
Petrol pump dealers have put on hold their proposed strike after oil companies increased their diesel supply marginally in the last week. "They have been supplying about 15-25 per cent additional diesel. This has eased the shortage slightly," said Baba Dhumal, president of the District Petrol Pump Dealers' Association.

Last week, Dhumal had said pumps were running losses because oil companies were not supplying enough diesel. On Monday, pump dealers and oil companies will meet to discuss further ways to bridge the demand-supply gap.

A number of factors, such as preparations for the Commonwealth Youth Games, have spiked he demand. "Also, load shedding was responsible for additional demand in the last few months. IT and other companies were buying a lot of diesel to keep their generators running. This has reduced in the past few weeks," he said.

Heading: Institutes fail to turn up for seminar on ethics in Education - Indian Express
Content:
Neha Pandit won the women's category while Nihar Tilekar lost in the final of the badminton open championships organised by the Haveli Taluka Badminton Association held at the PYC Gymkhana Badmnton courtson Sunday.

Ishan Naqvi carried the confidence he got after beating top seed Nigel D'Sa and went on to beat Tilekar 22-20 and 21-11 in the final. " I feel great after this victory. The first game was hard fought and my opponent pushed me to the edge. The second game was much easier and I managed to win it easily." Said an excited Naqvi. When Tilekar was asked about the reasons for his loss he said, " I was not happy withthe length of my strokes. My left hand services were too short and I could not face my opponents deep smashes."

Neha Pandit comprehensively beat her opponent Sayali Rane in straight sets to lift the women's category of the open championships. Shebreezed past her opponent 21-17 and 21-17.

In the men's doubles section the duo of Varun Khanvilkar and Sameer Bhagwat made the city proud as they beat Aditya Pandya and Rohit Sadani 21-10, 16-21 and 21-12 in the final to lift the trophy.

"It feels great to win this tournament especially after we lost out in the district championships," said Khanvilkar.

Heading: Anti Narcotics Cell arrests two, seizes brown sugar worth over Rs 11 lakh - Indian Express
Content:
The organisers of the seminar 'Ethics in Education' were taken aback when only four institutes turned up for the event on Saturday. They drew a conclusion that if the education institutions did not turn up, that means they had issues sticking to ethics.

The seminar, organised by Public Concern for Governance Trust (PCGT) and Arya Samaj Pune, discussed issues like capitation fees and donations during admission processes. It was also attended by officers from the Income Tax department. B G Deshmukh, former cabinet secretary and chairman of PCGT, presided the event.

While all reputed educational institutes in the city were invited, none except representatives of four institutes — Synergy Institute of Management, St Meera's, Arya Vidya Mandir and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth - had turned up.

"We had also invited All India Council for Technical Education but no one turned up," said S C Nagpal, managing trustee of Arya Samaj and member of PCGT. S K Sharma, former chief commissioner of Income Tax department, Pune said that education has become a money-making business. Nagpal pressed for stringent action against corruption in education.

Heading: Power shortage due to high growth, says Patil - Indian Express
Content:
The Anti Narcotics Cell of city police have arrested two persons, including an "affluent" woman from Thane, for allegedly distributing brown sugar here. The police have seized 1.3 kg brown sugar worth Rs 11.43 lakh from the accused. One of the accused has been remanded to the police custody till September 24.

The accused have been identified as Annapurna Ramji Gaikwad (40), resident of Ambarnath in Thane and Dutta Suresh Bagal (20) of Bharatnagar in Pimpri.

Acting on a tip-off, a police team, including inspector Ganpat Nikam, sub inspector Bajirao Patil, constables Laxman Thorat, Sushil Kakade, Eknath Khule, Pradip Shinde, Deepak Mate, Mukund Salunke, Ashok Pernekar, Ashok Gate, Deepak Savant and Pratibha Shinde, nabbed Bagal near Pimpri railway station on Thursday. Bagal possessed about eight grams brown sugar.

After interrogating Bagal, the police raided Gaikwad's house in Thane on Friday and found a packet of brown sugar weighing 1.127 kg. Gaikwad, a widow, was arrested and produced before the city court on Saturday.

As many as 182 persons have been arrested from Pune Cantonment, Swargate, Pimpri, Khadki and other parts of the city in connection with the drug trade in the city in 2007 - 08.

Investigations revealed that several college students from affluent families are addicted to brown sugar. Additional Commission of Police (crime) Rajender Singh has directed the Anti Narcotics Cell to track the main source of brown sugar in the city. The breakthrough came in with the arrest of Bagal. "Our team has left for Mumbai and we are likely to unearth a big drug trafficking racket," said inspector Nikam.

"Though the Thane police said that Gaikwad does not have any past crime record, we are verifying if she has developed the property using the money made through drug trade," Nikam said. "We suspect that Gaikwad was associated to a big drug trafficking racket rooted in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan," Nikam added.

Heading: Small Talk - Indian Express
Content:
Some years back, Maharashtra was supplying electricity to four states, but now the condition is such that the state has to buy electricity from six states to meet its demand," said Deputy Chief Minister RR Patil, speaking at the golden jubilee celebrations of the Mechanical wing of Irrigation Department held in Dapodi.

Explaining the reasons for power shortage situation in the state, Patil said, "Analysts had some years ago predicted a certain quantum of electricity that the state would be consuming in the year 2020. But that amount had already been used by it in the year 2007. While the electricity generation in the whole country is 2.5 per cent last year and the growth 9.2 per cent, Maharashtra marked a growth rate of 9.5 per cent. This high growth has led to a gap in the electricity generation and consumption in the state."

Patil said that private companies poaching staff from the state government is a worrying issue. "In order to curb this problem, growth opportunities should be provided to deserving employees.

So, the mechanical wing of the irrigation department should not function like a 'government department' if the organisation has to flourish, he added.

Speaking on the occasion, Pune's guardian minister Ajit Pawar told the workers of the irrigation department that they will get the benefits of the Sixth Pay Commission. Many machines used here are very old and outdated. So, I would try to get money sanctioned from the state government, he added.

Heading: Tuning into right channels - Indian Express
Content:
Vikas Swarup on Slumdog Millionaire, the adaptation of his debut novel Q & A and winning the People's Choice Award at the Toronto International Film Festival

Slumdog Millionaire, British filmmaker Danny Boyle's movie based on Indian diplomat Vikas Swarup's debut novel Q & A, has won the People's Choice Award at the just concluded Toronto International Film Festival. And in Pretoria, Swarup has a million-dollar smile — his picaresque through urban India has not only wowed the audience in Canada but is also set to close the forthcoming London Film Festival. "I guess everybody loves a good fable. In fact, Simon Beaufoy (who adapted the novel) told me that it was the element of Dickensian drama that drew him to the book in the first place," says Swarup, now India's deputy high commissioner to South Africa, over the telephone.

The film, which revolves around the tale of a poor Dharavi waiter who wins the Indian version of Who Wants to be a Millionaire and who has to explain how he knew the answer to each question, is set to make its debut in India in November. It has a largely Indian cast — NRI Dev Patel playing the protagonist Jamal, Anil Kapoor as the quizmaster, and model Frieda Pinto and actor Irrfan Khan in other important roles. Even though Swarup has yet to see Boyle's adaptation of his novel, he is convinced that the director of Trainspotting and 28 Days Later would have done justice to it. "I have watched all his movies and I was certain that his own unique style will bring a completion to the craft. It was him and Simon's mastery over the script that made me sign the contract in the first place. I am sure it deserves every bit of the adulation it is getting," he says.

In fact, it was the involvement of Boyle and Beaufoy, who had earlier written The Full Monty, that made it easy for Swarup to accept the creative changes. "In any such adaptation, you can either accept the change or reject it. I knew they had retained the framework of the novel and I saw both the first and second drafts of the script since I had the creative rights. It would have been cinematically boring to have retained all the 12 questions and answers. I trusted their creative vision and now, I am waiting to see the DVD which Danny has promised he will send," he says.

Heading: Through the lens - Indian Express
Content:
Apart from lending finishing touches to her debut music album, VJ Anusha will fly to Germany this October to host the sequel of much talked about Shahrukh Khan tour-Temptations Reloaded

She dances, acts, hosts shows,and sets ablaze the stage as a performer.But this is not only what Anusha Dandekar is all about. The multifaceted artiste is busy channelising yet another creative streak in her to the right straits. Born and brought up in Australia when the loot gaye girl made her debut alongside Bollywood Badshah Amitabh Bachhan, speculations regarding her sticking to the industry for long did the rounds.

But soon after the film she slipped back to her comfort zone where she can be herself, the VJ den, occasionally making an appearance or two is some of the Bollywood flicks. "Being a VJ is not secondary to me. For me it is much more important and what I like to do is to experiment. That is why you can always spot me venturing into different aspects of acting, Vjying and now I want to do a bit of singing too," says an ecstatic MTV style check host.

In the city for the auditions of Brylcreem MTV Dhoni's Style11, a hair styling contest the MTV VJ shares what other than VJying keeps her busy.

The VJ turned actor toddles towards the world of music. With her two sisters she is all set to explore the other dimension of an artiste's persona with her soon-to-release music album. Attributing the traits of a singer in her to her mom Anusha says, "My mom used to sing very well but she never entered the public domain and from her, I guess, all three of us have picked up this flair." Anusha, who with her elder and her younger sister is featuring in the album, will also be doing some dance numbers for it. "Our band will also be the first ever Maharashtrian girl rock band. We have got R&B, fusion of pop and Hindi and Punjabi numbers. We will also like to add the Marathi touch to the album since this is the place from where we belong and we are working on that," says Anusha.

Apart from the album she is busy working with the Shahrukh's Troupe for King Khan's tour'-TemptationsReloaded. "I will be accompanying Shahrukh, Arjun Rampal, Katrina Kaif, Kareena Kapoor and Ganesh Hedge for the tour. I will be hosting it and will perform as well," says she.

With the grapevine suggesting her getting hitched with Roadies host Rannvijay, Anusha has just one sentence to sum it up. " We are friends nothing more than that." However the lady does not forget to add, " Right now he is in London shooting for a film," she blushes before signing off with the sentence "We like good friends, keep in touch."

Heading: Leaving the limelight - Indian Express
Content:
Atul Kasbekar, the man behind the much admired Kingfisher Calendar feels trust is the factor that keeps fashion industry going

Quite a hot shot

A graduate of Brooks Institute, Santa Barbara, USA, Atul Kasbekar has been actively shooting in India since 1991. He has been the face of professional division of Canon in the country for last two years.

His editorial work appears in editions of Cosmopolitan, Elle, L'officiel, and Vogue regularly. His advertising clients include Airtel, Canon, Pepsi, Rado, Tag heuer, and many more. He conceived the kingfisher calendar for UB group, which has turned out to be a cult phenomenon. The calendar has also acted as a launch pad for best-known faces in fashion and Bollywood circuit today.

"I like mad people, they make the world more exciting," feels Atul Kasbekar, renowned fashion photographer and honorary chairman of Photographer's Guild of India (PGI).

Kasbekar was in town to inspire the budding photographers and share some of his special work with a selected audience.

The event witnessed some of the finest works of Kasbekar and the story behind the scenes in most the interesting way. While he introduced the audience to the nitty-gritty of the art, he also shared some hard facts and risks that come as a part and parcel of the profession.

"Trust is the foundation stone of our profession. A successful use of photography to portray the best shade of any emotion is possible only when there is trust involved. The company shows trust in my ideas and allows me to use the lens as I please. In return I keep a balance between their requirement and experimentation. I do keep in mind the content of the editorial or the message that is to be given by the campaign and not make it my own trip," he explains, adding, "Another trust is between the photographer and the model. Talking, for example, about the winning idea of Kingfisher Calendar, we need a lot of trust to make people comfortable so that we get the expression right, which is not possible if one becomes conscious of their outfits. A high level of professionalism is needed for this."

A Mumbaikar at heart, Kasbekar has also adapted himself to the work style of West, where he gets to shoot most of his work.

Introducing an all-together new aspect of himself, the photographer says, "I believe in being like a sponge, who imbibes energies and qualities from anybody with whom he interacts. At times it may even be negative energy that I get inflicted with as well."

Consumed with light and its beauty, he says that he would prefer to burn himself in sun and watch the beauty of light rather than live in shade. "I am nuts when it comes to playing with light. I like doing all kinds of experiments with light in my photography. For example, I love to shoot with a controlled sunlight on my face than having it on my back which makes the picture look flat."

An ardent nature lover, Kasbekar feels that we should work with and in coordination with nature and not against it as it offers much more beauty than what we can create.

When asked about how he decides on locales, Kasbekar confesses that budget plays a vital role in deciding the location for the shoot. But creativity is bigger than that and helps him to create beauty out of nothing.

Heading: Father figure - Indian Express
Content:
There is a luminous connection between Bhansali's Devdas, Santoshi's Legend of Bhagat Singh and the Ganpati processions in the city. All of them have been using the 100-year-old petromaxes for illumination. Rahul Ware claims to be the sole owner of these petromaxes in the state, which are more than a century old.

"My grandfather had bought them second hand around 50 years ago and since then they have been hired for numerous purposes. Basically a product of Germany the petromaxes were available in a large number some years ago, however only 70 of them are left with me," adds Ware.

From Raj Kapoor's Barsaat and Awara to the Marathi's glorified Maaherchi Saree or the hilarious Hulchul the lamps have lit the glamour in many movies. "The petromaxes have been mostly used in films to depict historical occurrences or traditional setups. For instance they have been utilised to light Paro's Mahal in Devdas. However in the city people have been renting them for the jatras or baarats or even by the students from the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII). I had recently rented them out for the visarjan procession for the Mandai's Ganpati," shares Ware.

There is a secret and a skill that lights the darkness through this petromaxes. Describing the method, Ware says, "Fuel and air pressure in appropriate proportion is what it takes to light the lamps. We have been doing this since the last three generations and I alone light them hence have to be present on each location, wherever the lamps are being used."

Giving details about the upkeep of the petromaxes he elaboretes,

"Once a year during the rainy season the lamps are fixed and restored for one whole month. We work on the burner, filament and amend several parts to ensure their durability. The amount of light exuded is 250-candle power and unlike the usual petromaxes the bulb here is at the bottom below the kerosene tank. The silkwood or the mantle burns and can give out light for 12 hours if fuelled with two litres of kerosene. I charge rupees 150 to 300 for three hours."

Yet time refines even the finest and what is left is the symbolic amount of these petromaxes since they are neither manufactured anymore nor claim sufficient demand. "There is already a dearth of labour to carry them and we have been sustaining them with the spare parts, which had been bought decades ago. The dearth of manpower is so concerning that at times I have to refrain from taking orders," he adds.

Heading: Truly chivalrous - Indian Express
Content:
Completing 75 years on October 3, the 'singing' Bishop of Pune, father Valerian D'Souza feels that religious problems can be solved by tapping souls and faith

If a balanced outlook and political correctness are the qualities of a leader, then father Valerian D'Souza perfectly fits the bill. Completing 75 years on October 3, the Bishop of Pune has been beyond successful in living up to his image of a spiritual guru.

Father D'Souza, was ordained as the Bishop of Pune on September 25, 1977 and commenting on his journey for the past 31 years, he says, "It has been a wonderful journey. Like every journey, this one also had its ups and down but I am happy that today, right from maintaining peace to administration we have been successfully reaching out to people be it about education, charity or spirituality."

Father D'Souza is recognized worldwide as the Singing Bishop. Commenting on his identity as the only singing Bishop in the world, Father D'Souza laughs saying, "I must say this is an exaggeration. I think it is more like the saying- The rich man's joke is always humourous. But yes I do play guitar but am not a performer. The only time I get back to my identity of a singing bishop is during prayers, hymns and choirs."

On the day he got ordained, father D'Souza had declared that he would build his identity as a spiritual leader. And as a responsible spiritual leader who is unhappy about the current political situation in the country, father D'Souza feels, "Following one's religion should not at all be a problem for anyone. What is and has been a concern are religious followers imposing their own religious values on the believers of other religions. The sad part of the story is that this kind of violence or imposition is done under the name of god. I personally feel that religion is the means to reach god and everyone has their own right to choose that path. No one can be forcefully made to follow another religion." He further adds, "What happened in the churches in the country is a sad story because extremists of these sorts do not realize that the victims of such attacks are innocent people, sometimes belonging to their own religion as well! For instance, the victims of one of the attacks were nuns. Now these extremists do not understand that these nuns do not even step out of the churches most of the times."

Pune region which initially had 11 territories was initially divided into five for the ease of administration. Today however, there are two main regions and with over 60000 students getting education, existing orphanages, old age homes and the projects in the pipeline one of which is the centre for alcohol and drug addicts, Pune region is an epitome of effective as well as efficient administration. And the credit without saying goes to the realistic and practical leadership of father D'Souza. "But I have a lot of expectations from Pune. The entire world is shaken by religious forces acting in various parts of the world. And despite the diversity and cosmopolitan population of Pune, the city has managed to live up to its identity as a responsible place. The religious forces in Pune are quite balanced," says he as he further adds, "In fact Pune has the potential to be the example in front of the world. And I feel that this is the right time to take action. It is important that the spiritual leaders from all the religions in this city come together and unite under one flag. Religious entities can coexist.Religion is on a spiritual level and the problems that have been created due to religious extremism can be solved not by bloodshed but by tapping the faith and souls."

Heading: Car-free day today - Indian Express
Content:
Yuva Maitri seeks to fight violence against women by affecting a tectonic changes in the mentality of men

"By fighting against violence on women, I am, by no means, pitching against men, but helping them. My idea is to work on positive masculinity," advocates Harish Sadani, founder member of Men Against Violence and Abuse (MAVA).

With an objective of helping young boys become good and unbiased men, Sadani has started a project named Yuva Maitri (friendship among youth). The project aims to enable young men to adopt positive models of masculinity that promote gender sensitivity and help prevent violence and abuse of women.

"When the problem is violence against women by men, then the solution lies in changing both and not one. There have been efforts to tell women to be more aware of their rights but there is no one to tell men that what and why they should not be doing," says Sadani, adding, "The best thing is to change men so that such things could be avoided."

Starting with his project, Yuva Maitri, Sadani identified five rural colleges and one city-based college of Pune district and engaged first year students in his project. Elaborating about engaging only first year students in the project Sadani says that at this age, students are more attracted to the opposite sex and their mind tend to think about every thing that is 'forbidden' in society. They tend to make up wrong impression of things and indulge into wrong deeds like eve teasing, watching porn, or even looking down at girls.

After a successful attempt in Mumbai, Sadani chose Pune for his noble project. He selected 33 students from six colleges and arranged for sessions where boys came up with questions that haunted their minds.

"The questions that were put up by the boys ranged from issue of reservation for women to eve-teasing and rape. We complied these questions and then we started wall newspapers for colleges. We started placing a bulletin on the college's notice board wherein we would not only inform the students about gender bias issues but also ask for their response. Initially this was not well received but later it turned out to be a big hit. And then we went ahead with street plays, awareness songs and many contests," elaborates Sadani.

The effort seems successful when, while giving his feed back on his experinece, Ganesh Phule, a trained maitri of the project, comes up with his own example and does not goes on to speak big on social issues. "The best positive and most practical solution was to change ourselves. After being a part of Yuva Maitri, I realised that on what all spheres a girl is still denied freedom. The first example came from my home where I nearly had to launch a battle in order to convince my parents to let my sister choose her life partner. Equal participation of men in fight against denial of rights to women is better solution, " he feels.

Another changed-and-happy member of the project is Sunil Chachar, student, who took up to household work thereby annoying his relatives and society members. "After joining Yuva Maitri I realised that my mother should also have time for herself so I started doing household work. My relatives stopped talking to me for this," says Chachar.

Another experience, which Chachar feels is one of his greatest achievements, was of changing four utterly notorious boys of a local college. "The college management had already decided to expel those boys given their bad behaviour towards girls. After taking permission from the principal, I had a talk with these boys who confessed that they wanted to befriend girls but every girl hated them. So they started torturing girls by passing rude remarks on them. We explained to those boys that they have to win the confidence of a girl before befriending her. And to my surprise those boys were not only much accepted students of that college. But one of them also won the Ideal Students award," says Chachar.

Another 23-year-old member of the project, Amol Kale, who still feels that he has along way to go before he starts teaching others. He says, "I am in learning stage. I was one who used to get angry if I saw any male friend of my sister. But now I understand that it takes a pure and clean mind to be good and feel good. Thanks to Yuva Maitri project, which helped me improve. I now think what affect my action would have on others.

Heading: Tata Motors appoints new dealer for city - Indian Express
Content:
Various civic groups in association with the Pune Municipal Corporation will be conducting a car free day on Monday by organising a bicycle rally in order to give due recognition to non-motorised transport on the crowded city roads.

The World Car Free day is celebrated in many cities throughout the world and it would be started as a symbolic gesture in the city on Monday. The PMC has extended its support to the civic organisations in celebrating the World Car Free day. Social activist Sujit Patwardhan said they are not expecting disapperance of cars on the streets on the day, but hoping a beginning of discussion on giving due respect to non-motorised transport in the city while constructing infrastructure for the purpose. The bicycle rally will begin at 7.30 am from four different locations of Ozone in Aundh, near GPO in Camp, Karve statue in Kothrud and Shaniwarwada. All the four groups of cyclists will converge at Sambhaji Park on Jangli Maharaj Road at 9.30 am.

The campaign for promoting non-motorised transport has picked up with the civic administration making required provisions of footpaths and cycle tracks in the road development work under JNNURM. The PMC is to construct around 117-km long cycle track and Municipal Commissioner Praveensinh Pardeshi, an avid cyclist, have been promoting it by declaring every Tuesday as the cycle day at the civic headquarters. However, the initiative has died down with not many following the diktat. The PMC, along with various social organisations, is also planning a "hire and ride" cycle programme for Pune on the lines of that in Paris.

Heading: Orbittal opens office in Ranjangaon - Indian Express
Content:
Pratham Automobiles Pvt Ltd has been appointed as the Tata Motors Passenger Car third dealer in the city. S M Krishnan, vice president (commercial ), Tata Motors, said the company was extremely pleased with start of its third dealership in Pune. "The new Dealership will help in greater market penetration and will surely increase Tatas numbers on its home turf. With Tata having a large numbers of vehicles and models lined up for launches in the coming year like the recently launched Indica Vista, New Indigo and the much awaited Nano, and a new SUV is slated to be launched in this financial year," he said.

The new showroom of Pratham Automobiles was inaugurated by District Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar and Krishnan. Sanjeev Tiwari, regional manager, Tata Motors along with Rajiv Bhale, chairman of Pratham Automobiles and Kumar Tamhane, managing director of Pratham Automobiles were present on the occasion.

Speaking on the occasion, Kumar Tamhane and Raju Bhale said that the 94 Workshop Repair Bays — one of the largest single location workshops in the country — will come as a boon to large number of customers as Pune has a large waiting period for servicing of Tata Motors cars .

The new dealership would also offer pick up and drop facility for customers, apart from a modern workshop with all the latest equipment and specialized painting facility and expertise in insurance accidental claim settlement. A completely new concept of a accessories lounge with the entire range of accessories available will also be on display.

Located on the Mumbai-Bangalore bypass at Balewadi, Pratham Automobiles is one of the largest 3S facility in India, where sales, service and spares can be carried out at one location.

It has a 94 bay workshop which is one of the biggest in the country. Large showroom space, ultra modern paint shop facility, trained staff, open 365 days a year, stated a press note.

Heading: With India as focus, Walter Tools to set up manufacturing plant in city - Indian Express
Content:
Orbittal Electromech Engineering Projects Pvt Ltd, the electrical engineering firm, has inaugurated the divisional office at Ranjangaon.

The office was opened by Suresh Valekar, superintending engineer, Mahavitaran. Assistant engineer S J Kalrao, deputy engineer Priya Nitin Gokhale, Pravin Biche, managing director, Orbittal Electromech) and other directors-Sagar Bavdhankar, Nikhil Tambe and Prakash Biche-were also present on the occasion.

Orbittal is an electrical engineering firm focussing on turnkey electrical project execution for clients by offering them inventive, cost efficient services and solutions. On the occasion, Pravin Biche, managing director Orbittal Electromech) said, "Orbittal has a technical tie up with Elkon for their entire range of products and we get total design support from them together with critical component whenever required. We are involved in the designing and manufacturing of all types of HT / LT Electrical and Instrumentation Control panels. Our products are widely used for various applications and utilities in industrial and commercial sector. We have completed 40% project in Ranjangaon industrial estate." The turnover figure crossed 14 cr in FY 2007 - 08.

Heading: ‘Clean river’ campaign rolls on - Indian Express
Content:
Walter AG of Germany, the competence machining tools company, has unveiled its new global brand identity in India. The new brand image of Walter AG reflecting the synergies of the competence brands Walter, Walter Titex and Walter Prototyp will contribute significantly to walter tools turning into a 1 billion Eruo company by 2010, the company claimed.

Walter AG has an office Dapodi -- which is the only one in India. At a press conference at Hotel Le Meridien, Pawel Duzniak, Vice- President, Walter AG said: "India is fast developing into a major global economic power. At Walter, we see India as a key focus area in our growth plans. The growth here in auto, aerospace, power and engineering industries in particular will trigger an increasing demand for the metal processing tools industry. In such a scenario, Walter aims to emerge as a market leader by leveraging the distinct strengths of the new brand identity where we go beyond offering just hi-tech machining tools." He said the Indian arm of the company will definitively also take a central role in the Walter operation in South East Asia.

He said Walter AG also has a plan to set up a manufacturing unit in Pune in the near future. Vivek Bhonsle, managing director, Walter Tools India Pvt Ltd, said, "A prerequisite for this success is, however, an extensive product portfolio and staff with comprehensive specialist knowledge. And this is exactly what Walter can provide with the competence brands Walter, Walter Titex and Walter Prototype."

Heading: Rubber factory ready to bail out antibiotics public sector unit - Indian Express
Content:
Ganesh immersion is over, it is time now to clean the rivers. And taking initiative on this front is not the politicians, but corporates who have already embarked on the "Clean river" campaign from September 17. CII, Cummins India Ltd (CIL) and Subros Auto have launched the campaign during which volunteers will clean the river with the help of fishermen and other professionals, for a period of 10 days, till September 26.

The tentative areas shortlisted are Bundgarden, RTO Bridge, Z Bridge (Tilak Road), Kalyani Nagar, Harris bridge, Holkar bridge, Aundh bridge. A survey will be conducted and after consulting the PMC, the river cleaning process will begin in the area that requires most cleaning. The cleaning process would be carried out by hiring local fishermen and other professionals who have carried out such activities before. The waste material collected from the rivers will be disposed of, after consulting the Pune Municipal Corporation, stated a press release.

A campaign was flagged off by Suresh Jagtap, deputy commissioner, PMC and Dr Sanjeev Wavare, ward medical officer, PMC in the presence of PMC officials at the Z bridge on J M Road, which leads to Laxmi Road. The campaign has been launched in association with the Pune Municipal Corporation and other organisations.

Heading: Flooded again: nightmare will last till rehab project is complete - Indian Express
Content:
Proposes to reconstruction board: Will buy 20 acres of vacant land for Rs 120 cr and set up industrial complex

Hindustan Antibiotics Ltd, Pimpri, an ailing public sector unit, has a chance of staying afloat yet. Though it failed to raise money through the sale of a prime piece of vacant land, a prospective buyer has finally shown interest. A Bhosari-based industrial firm, Bhor Rubber Factory, is ready to pay Rs 120 crore for the 20-acre plot between Ajmera and Nehrunagar.

Sopan Bhor, managing director of the Bhor Rubber Factory, said they have already sent a proposal to the Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR), which is looking after Hindustan Antibiotics. "An acre of commercial land in the MIDC area costs Rs 6 crore. That means that plot should be on sale for Rs 120 crore. If BIFR gives its okay, we will pay the amount in barely one month," said Bhor.

The antibiotics firm, however, is looking at a higher price. "We are looking at around Rs 150 crore," company secretary A S Vaidya said. "But Bhor Rubber Factory is welcome to negotiate. If they really have such a proposal, they should come forward and discuss it. Only after discussions can things be worked out."

Bhor Rubber Factory prefers to negotiate directly with BIFR. It plans an industrial and commercial complex on the 20-acre plot. "The project would be a joint venture and this is an ideal location. The industrial and commercial complex will suit both the industry and domestic consumers," said Bhor, who is also the president of the Lagu Udyog Bharati.

Bhor said four-five financiers have evinced interest in buying the land and setting up an industrial and commercial complex. Since the company has now recalled the tenders, he suggested it should not go for another retendering. "The BIFR should hold direct negotiations with us. Also, it is imperative that the company should get clearance from the state government and the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation," he said.

But Vaidya said since Hindustan Antibiotics was a Central Government unit, re-tendering was inevitable.

On September 18, when tenders were opened, only two bids were found for the land. One party quoted Rs 34 crore and the other Rs 75 crore — both amounts much below the company's expectations.

Vaidya said the amount they are seeking to raise through the sale is part of the rehabilitation package announced by BIFR.

The company was declared sick in 1997 and was referred to BIFR. Last year, it had a turnover of Rs 120 crore. "This year we expect Rs 150 crore. All units of the company are working," Vaidya said.

Heading: City girl lights up the life of Kashmiri kids - Indian Express
Content:
A day after floodwaters swept into hutments in Pimpri and Sangvi, irrigation officials ruled out rehabilitation support to the dwellers as the slums were encroaching the riverbed. On Saturday, it was the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation that had to evacuate people from the flooded hutments in Sangvi and Pimpri.

Once the corporation completes work on a rehabilitation project, slums along the riverbed in Pimpri and Sangvi will disappear. With no support from the irrigation department, dwellers will see their huts flooded year after year, till the project is complete.

"The hutments were on the riverbed, within the blue line. They cannot be given any rehabilitation support because they were encroaching the river bed," said Avinash Surve, superintendenting engineer, Pune Irrigation Circle.

Four years ago, Pimpri-Chinchwad had witnessed its worst-ever floods with over 40,000 residents living along the Pavana river badly hit. District Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar had then directed the PCMC to take adequate steps to avoid a repeat of the situation.

When contacted, Municipal Commissioner Asheesh Sharma said those who had encroached the riverbed would be shifted to Sector 22 in Pradhikaran under the Slum Rehabilitation Project. "There are no new encroachments in the river. The ones affected yesterday are the old ones. All these will be shifted after the slum rehabilitation project is completed," Sharma said.

For the record, the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation is constructing 18,500 flats each measuring 350 square feet across the town under the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM). The project was launched last year at five places by the then municipal commissioner Dilip Band, who had vowed to make Pimpri-Chinchwad a slum-free city.

The slum rehabilitation project got cracking in March and has a deadline of 18 months. "By 2010 end, all the flats should be ready," Sharma said.

On Saturday, there was heavy rainfall in catchments areas as well, up to 112 mm in Sangvi and Pimpri. "The maximum discharge possible from Pavana is over 40,000 cusecs. But we released only 14,000 cusecs from Pavana dam. The flooding happened because the encroachments were on the bed of the Pawana River. But it did not last more than 2 hours," said Vijay Ghogare, executive engineer, Pune Irrigation Circle.

There was no flooding in Pimpri or Sanghvi or any other part of the city on Sunday and the discharge levels from the dam had been reduced. No water was released from Pawana and Mulshi. Vir dam was releasing 15,000 cusecs and Ujjani in Solapur district was releasing 90,000 cusecs.

"At Bundgarden the water level was only about 15,000 cusec, down from 75,000 cusec on Saturday. But the maximum water level can go up to 1.5 lakh cusecs," said Ghogare.

The meteorological department has predicted a "few spells of rain and thundershowers" in the next 48 hours. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to hover at 29°C and 22°C respectively.

Heading: Introduce health insurance at grassroots level - Indian Express
Content:
When youngsters prefer to do lucrative jobs, city-based girl Supriya Kalra has voluntarily opted to tread a different path. She works with a non-governmental organisation with 'Borderless World Foundation', which works for the welfare of orphan girls in the Kashmir valley. The NGO is credited with the launch of an exclusive girls' orphanage "Basera-e-Tabassum" (BeT) in Kupwara.

A postgraduate in social work with special work on medical and psychiatry from the Tata Institute of Social Science in Mumbai, Supriya joined the NGO this July as Project Development Manager.

Supriya said, "Though my days in BeT were numbered but every day spent there has been an experience of a lifetime. What more does one need than 50 warm hugs of innocent children when one returns to the orphanage after the day's work? The walls of this home are made of care, coated with the paint of love and affection. Amid the captivating beauty of Kupwara, I realised that there is so much pain, suffering beneath this cold soil of Kashmir. Each child's life is a pathetic tale to tell. They are so grief stricken that they have become immune to atrocities."

There are 59 orphans and all come from broken homes. Some lost their fathers and mothers remarried while others lost their complete families in the turmoil.

She said, "What more pain can a child go through than to live the life of an orphan. There are bunkers outside their homes and close to their schools. The playground often lies next to a graveyard. And life comes to a halt after sunset, except within the four walls of the house."

The NGO is running two BeTs, one at Sulkoote village in Kupwara district and other at Beerwah in Budgam district. These are being run from rented accommodations.

Supriya said, "Recently our NGO has got the approval of a third orphanage at Baramula where the infrastructure has been prepared by the Army on the orders of the state government. I will now look after this new orphanage."

She said, "These children are sent to good private schools for education. They require help to deal with problems such as recurring nightmares, difficulty in maintaining concentration, depression and a sense of hopelessness about the future. Most of all, they need help and someone to understand them."

Heading: Only 20% cast their votes - Indian Express
Content:
Dr Balbir Singh Shah is a member of the Punjab Medical Council (PMC) and is currently the chairman of the CME (Continuing Medical Education) Credit Accreditation Committee. Dr Shah, who is a professor of pathology at Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, talks to Sameer Kumar Sharma, about the pros and cons of being a doctor in the current scenario.

Ques: Why it is believed that the number of PCMS doctors violating the rule as regards private practice has increased over the years?

It is true that today number of government doctors who are believed to be working privately is more as compared to the trend a decade ago. And there are various reasons for that. Lure of money is one of the main factors, and there is another side to the problem.

But the government doctors should not violate the terms and conditions of their profession as they are already paid non-practising allowance by the government. And if they are not happy with the amount being paid to them, they should report it through a proper channel.

Ques: What is the other possible side that you just mentioned as a reason?

If there are no proper facilities or infrastructure, a doctor cannot do much. And for want of proper infrastructure and facilities, there is less of job satisfaction. Our health system is presently not living up to the expected level and therefore some doctors may not have the job satisfaction.

Ques: Are you hinting at the shortage of doctors in government colleges because of more prospects in the private sector?

This is true. Three major government colleges in the state have already been served noticed by the Medical Council of India as they were not able to recruit the required number of faculty members. This shows that there is a great need to pay more importance to the healthcare. So, instead of issuing a nominal budget for the sector, the government is required to release more funds.

Ques: Where do you think we lag behind in the public healthcare sector?

It is the infrastructure that we urgently need in the government colleges and hospitals. There are 38,000 registered medical practitioners with the PMC and our doctors in the state are very competent but they are not getting the right kind of environment to work. So they are settling abroad. As per an estimate, every seventh doctor in the US in some years is going to be an Indian. That speaks volumes about our expertise.

Ques: What is the first step that the government should take to provide better healthcare to all?

I think health insurance should be introduced at every level. With this, the rural and poor people can also avail themselves of better treatment at private hospitals.

Ques: PMC has introduced 50 compulsory credit hours for the doctors in the state. How will it benefit the doctors?

CMEs are important in order that the doctors are updated about the advancements in medicine. The doctors will now have to attend the CMEs seriously in order to earn 50 credit hours in five years. This will make them eligible for re-registration which will be done every five years now.

Heading: Missing trader: Cops say he is dead - Indian Express
Content:
PU SENATE POLLS: Bogus voting reported from two centres, results to be declared tomorrow

Barring the incident of bogus votes at Guru Nanak Khalsa College for Women and alleged booth capturing at the polling centre at Sargoda Khalsa Senior Secondary School, the polling for the Panjab University Senate elections passed off peacefully in the city today.

The poll observers said a comparatively low turnout was recorded at the 18 polling booths in the city as compared to the last year. In all, the total turnout was around 20 per cent.

In an attempt to cast fake votes at the centre at Sargoda School, some persons were caught resorting to using unfair means while polling was going on. A police officer said that some persons tried to use unfair means to allow bogus votes in the elections but the situation was immediately controlled after the police intervened.

The fake voting was allegedly being done in the name of Praveen Sharma, who is a candidate for Graduates Constituency from Arya College in the city. Sharma said that he was not aware of this until his wife, who had gone there to cast her vote, came to know about it. "I immediately talked to the presiding officer and asked him why it was being allowed when there was police force at the booth," he said, adding that he was not aware of who was doing this to tarnish his image.

Prof Mukesh Arora, a candidate in the lecturer constituency from the city, demanded repolling at the booth saying that in the wake of the incident at the polling at the Sargoda School centre, the polling should be redone.

Another case of fake voting has been reported from Guru Nanak Khalsa College for Women, where some persons were caught casting fake votes.

Polling percentage in the Graduates constituency, which is the largest constituency having over 4 lakh voters was recorded at somewhere close to 20 per cent. On the other hand, polling in the Lecturer constituency was reported to be around 90 per cent while 100 per cent polling took place in Principals' Constituency.

Some voters also complained about having to travel to farther polling booths to cast their vote instead of the booths that were close to their homes. "This should not happen to the voters. Since there is a booth right near my house in BRS Nagar, why should I travel all the way to Civil Lines to cast my vote?" a voter complained.

The polling took place at about 18 polling booths in the city from 9 am to 5 pm, with a break of one hour between 1 pm and 2 pm.

While the results of the Lecturers' and Principals' constituency are going to be announced on Tuesday, September 23, the results for Graduates Constituency are expected to be declared by September 24.

Heading: Rape of classmate: Two boys sent to juvenile jail for 14 days - Indian Express
Content:
The police investigations have revealed that a local industrialist, who went missing on August 12, has been murdered. According to SSP R K Jaiswal, the police have found some vital clues to substantiate the case.

Vinod Adya (55), owner of Sunshine Knitwear factory in the Industrial Area 'A', left his house for his factory on August 12. Neither did he reach his factory nor did he return home. When the family failed to locate him for a month, they lodged a missing report with the Division Number 6 police station.

Later, the police registered an FIR against unidentified persons. However, the family did not receive any ransom call, the police sources said.

Sources said that in past too, Adya had left his house without telling anyone and the police were hopeful that he will come back soon.

SSP Jaiswal, meanwhile, has confirmed that the investigations reveal that Adya has been murdered. "We have got some vital leads in this case which substantiate that Adya has been murdered and his body has been disposed of. We have identified the accused who have killed Adya."

Jaiswal further said that in this connection, a police party had been sent to Faridkot for further investigations. He, however, denied that any person has been arrested so far in the case.

Heading: RSP to contest LS elections independently - Indian Express
Content:
After arresting both the minors accused for allegedly raping their classmate yesterday, the police produced them before the special juvenile court.

The court has sent them to the Borstal children jail for 14 days.

The Division number 5 SHO Shavinder Singh Dhillon told Newsline that while one accused had been arrested yesterday afternoon itself, the second boy was arrested late in the evening. "Both these boys are below 18 years of age. The victim is also under 18," SHO Dhillon said.

The girl was reportedly raped in the playground of the Government College for Boys yesterday afternoon. A medical examination at the Civil Hospital had confirmed rape.

Heading: Panchayat members support doctor - Indian Express
Content:
The Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP) has decided to contest all the 13 Lok Sabha seats in Punjab on it's own and the party has announced it's candidates from Ludhiana and Fatehgarh Sahib Lok Sabha constituencies.

At a press conference here on Saturday, RSP state secretary Avtar Singh Janjua said the party has decided to field Amrik Singh Sekhon from Ludhiana and Bhupinder Singh Libra from Fatehgarh (reserve) Lok Sabha constituencies. Janjua said soon the party will announce it's candidates from the other constituencies.

Janjua said that as all the political parties had failed to take up the issues concerning the poor people, their party had decided to contest the next LS elections on it's own.

Heading: FIR registered against eunuchs - Indian Express
Content:
Some members of gram panchayat in Mansura village have come out in support of Dr Mandeep Kaur, an eye specialist, who was caught by a team of health department, practising in a private clinic.

A statement issued by the members of the panchayat and block samiti said the allegations against Dr Mandeep Kaur and another doctor have been fabricated .

The members said in the statement they are happy with the services of the doctor and have also written to the health minister to look into the case.

Heading: Onam celebrated by Kerala Kalavedi - Indian Express
Content:
The division number 8 police have registered an FIR against some eunuchs in connection with the castration of an 18-year-old Nikhil Sharma. However, no arrest have been made so far in this case.

According to the division number 8 SHO Ravinder Singh FIR has been registered against Radha Mahant, Renu, Parveen and Manga. These persons have been booked for injuring Nikhil Sharma. The FIR has been registered on the complaint of the victim. The SHO said that efforts were on to arrest the accused persons.

The victim is a migrant from Haridwar and was living in Threeke village. He had told mediapersons yesterday that he had started going with some eunuchs to earn his livelihood. He used to play musical instruments with the eunuchs. He alleged that after giving him a sedative mixed with tea, some eunuchs had castrated him.

Heading: Darbar-e-Khalsa Dal demand CBI inquiry into Ishmeet’s death - Indian Express
Content:
Kerala Kalavedi, an association of Keralites, celebrated Onam festival at Veer Palace, Chandigarh road. The function started with a colourful procession from Kalavedi office to Veer Palace. It included chendamelam, thalappoli, pulikali, decorated colourful umbrella, along with elephants. The procession was inaugurated by V A Hari, president of Kerala Kalavedi.

Women dressed in traditional clothes made colourful 'rangoli', called 'Athapookkalam', with different flowers, at Veer Palace. The athapookkalam jyot was lighted to welcome the raja mahabali. Onam feast that was served on banana leaves included more than 21 items including "pradhaman" (kheer). After the Onam feast, a cultural meeting was organised which included traditional Onam folk dance.

The winners of sports and participants of the cultural programmes were honoured. The programme was attended by Hakkam Singh Gyaspura, Mayor of Ludhiana, Sharanjit Singh Dhillon, Member of Parliament, Sunita Aggarwal, Deputy Mayor, Simranjit Singh Bains, Municipal Councillor among others.

The cultural meeting was followed by a show with performances by Cochin Harishree, a famous troupe of TV artistes from Kerala. A large number of people from in and around Ludhiana attended the programme.

Heading: PCMS association resents increase in retirement age - Indian Express
Content:
Darbar-e-Khalsa Dal, a Sikh organisation, has asked the Government of India to initiate a CBI inquiry into the death of Ishmeet Singh, winner of Star voice of India.

Addressing a gathering at the meeting of the organisation held at local gurdwara Gau Ghat, Jasdeep Singh Kaonke, president of the organisation, said its strange that Prime Minister of India Dr Manmohan Singh is not accepting the demand of a CBI enquiry. Ishmeet Singh had brought laurels for the whole Sikh community."

Kaonke said Ishmeet's death was a part of a pre planned deep-rooted conspiracy to stop the rising star from attaining a high position in the musical world of the country. He said the the criminals behind the alleged murder could be brought before the people only through CBI enquiry.

He said they would be forced to agitate against the government if their demand is not met. He also appealed all the social, religious and the political organisations of the state to come together and urge the government to accept their demand.

Heading: An uneasy calm prevails after LSE Chairman resigns - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab Civil Medical Services (PCMS) association has opposed the proposal of the Punjab government to increase the retirement age of medical teachers to 65 years.

Dr Hardeep Singh, president of PCMS Association said increasing the age of retirement is not the solution for shortage of medical teachers and threat of de-recognition of state medical colleges.

He said the proposal will lead to frustration in medical education as well as PCMS cadre. He alleged that rather than to solving the problem of shortage of teachers, it will lead to exodus of PCMS doctors as well as medical teachers whose promotions will be blocked by the increase in the retirement age.

He said it would trigger a chain reaction of demolishment of medical education cadre. Due to increase in retirement age the promotions of associate professors will be blocked for five more years.

Consequently, it also will delay the promotion of MD/MS doctors as assistant professors who are serving in PCMS cadre. He said it was ironic that on one hand MD/MS doctors are waiting to be posted and promoted and on the other hand the colleges are facing the threat of being derecognised.

"These doctors will be left with no alternative but to seek premature retirement and join private medical colleges. The problem of shortage of medical teachers in government medical colleges will be further aggravated," he added.

He said the situation of unemployment in medical specialists can be assessed by the fact that in the recent Punjab Public Service Commission selection of assistant professor for one post each in the department of eye and ENT more than 25 postgraduate doctors had applied.

Newly-elected members honoured

Dr Tarlok Bandhu, Professor of psychology, and Dr Ravinder Kaur, principal of Malwa Central College of Education, Ludhiana, were honoured at Malwa Khalsa Senior Secondary School for Boys, Model Gram. Khagesh Sharma, principal of the school, said, "They were honoured for being elected as senate members of Panjab University for the category of B.Ed colleges." Daljinder Singh, Advocate Manager of Malwa Khalsa School, honoured them with shawl and momento. Both the members thanked the school principal and Khalsa Dewan.

Educative programme held

Cherry Lane Play School organised a colourful educational programme in the school campus. To make students aware about different colours, four rooms were decorated. Children were made to learn colours in a playful way. Parents came to view the show.

Heading: Christians protest against atrocities - Indian Express
Content:
An uneasy calm prevails in Ludhiana Stock Exchange (LSE) after the sudden resignation of LSE Chairman S.P. Sharma. Sharma said he had to resign because of the unfriendly atmosphere among the board of directors. He said he was feeling suffocated in the exchange. There is lack of transparency and he had no choice but to submit his resignation before the board of directors of LSE.

Meanwhile, the scene is hotting up in the exchange for the elections of directors of LSE securities, LSE commodities and LSE. For the first two, the elections will be held on September 27 and elections of two shareholder directors and a broker holder director of LSE would be held on September 30.

Three posts of directors are vacant in LSE securities and 4 posts in LSE commodities and the last date of withdrawing nominations is September 22. According to sources, once the elections of directors are through, few candidates will also try for the vacant post of chairman.

It needs to be mentioned that though Sharma has resigned, the allegations and counter allegations between a group of directors are still going on.

Heading: Eyes on Commonwealth Games 2010: Oscar - Indian Express
Content: Raising their voice against atrocities on the Christians in Orissa and Karnataka, the Christian community today blocked traffic near Christian Medical College and Hospital for about two hours. The protest was led by Varis Masih, paster committee and women and youth fellowship of Kalvery church. The christian leaders said the government should take necessary steps to curb this injustice. They appealed to the christians of Punjab to unite.

Heading: 67-year-old carpenter murdered - Indian Express
Content:
After having walked away with the Player of the Tournament by winning four titles in the 19th Yonex Chandigarh State Open Badminton Championship, international shuttler Oscar Bansal hopes to repeat his performance this year also. "I am in good form now and hopefully, I will be able to repeat last year's performance in the championship," says the student of Bachelor of Engineering in Electronics and Communication in Panjab University. "But right now I am concentrating on the North Zone Championship to be held at Amritsar," adds Bansal.

After a roller-coaster ride during the past year, Oscar has come a long way. Having blossomed into a fine shuttler, he has graduated to the senior circuit from the junior level. "The transition of a player from junior to senior is quite hard to adjust. There is hardly any competition at the junior level but in the senior circuit you have to be a versatile player and know the game and playing style of your opponent," says the 19-year-old shuttler who has represented India in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand and Czech Republic.

The 36 days coaching camp from June 14 to July 20 at Bangalore has worked wonders for him. "It was an enriching experience. All the top ranked Indian shuttlers of the likes of Anup Aridhar and Anand Bhatt were present there. I played few games against them and managed to surpsise them with my game. Even the coach present there praised my game. My fitness level has improved a lot from the camp since a lot of emphasis was being given on physical training at the camp apart from coaching," says the bespectacled Oscar who started playing the game when he was 11 years old.

Oscar is currently looking forward to the Commonwealth Games 2010.

"Our coach Gopichand will hold camps for about 20-25 days and after that he will select the players. I have attended the camps in Hyderabad for two-three times. Hopefully I will play in the Commonwealth Games but my ultimate goal is to play for the Olympics. I have kept that goal in mind and I am working hard to improve my game," says the shuttler who recently participated in the Panjab University Badminton Inter-college tournament.

Heading: 13 men, 10 bombs and days of careful planning — the result was 9/13: police - Indian Express
Content:
A 67-year-old carpenter Prem Singh, was murdered at Samrala road near Railway over bridge at Khanna on Sunday. He was allegedly attacked with a musli (an iron striker used to grind the pickles) on the head and face. The musli was recovered from the site. Police is suspecting it as a case of enmity. Prem Singh, who was also a leader of Shiromani Akali Dal (A), is survived by three sons, all carpenters.

The incident took place at about 2 pm in the basement of the house-cum-saw mill of Prem Singh. His son Amritpal Singh told the Newsline, "My father has leased out the saw mill. He used to go to the basement for prayers in the morning and evening."

"At about 1.30 pm he had tea at a nearby tea shop with one Jassa Singh of Lalherri road and went to the basement with him," he added.

His other son Kamaljit Singh said, "I was having my lunch and my daughter went to call my father for lunch but came back crying. When we reached the room my father was lying in a pool of blood." Labourers working outside the room said they did not hear any voice. Jassa Singh is still absconding.

A police party led by SSP Arun Pal Singh, SP(D) Gurmit Singh and DSP(D) Balwinder Singh reached the spot and started the investigation. Finger print experts and dog squad were called on for investigating. SSP Arun Pal Singh said, "The cause of murder could be the enmity between victim and accused."

"The labourers present near the incident site are also being interrogated," he added. "Investigation is on and we are verifying all the facts." A case was registered on the complaint of Amritpal Singh.

Heading: The men in the police net - Indian Express
Content:
The serial bomb blasts that rocked the Capital on September 13 was a result of careful planning and analysis by the 13-member terror module, led by Atif Ameen, police said on Sunday. Joint Commissioner of Police, Special Cell, Karnal Singh claimed that the entire planning and dispatching manpower to the scheduled places was done by Atif, the suspected leader of the Indian Mujahideen group in Delhi.

On September 19, the police said, all those responsible for planting the bombs assembled at Atif's L-18 flat in the morning and left for their chosen destinations around 4 pm. DCP (South) H G S Dhaliwal said Atif had planned the explosions for evening to ensure "maximum injuries".

Officers said it was Atif and Junaid who had planted the bombs in GK-I market, where two explosions occurred after 6 pm. They had wrapped the bomb in two polythene bags and stuffed them with banana peels, before throwing it in dustbins. Mohammed Shakeel, who was arrested on Sunday from Jamia Nagar, had planted the bomb in an auto-rickshaw that exploded in front of the Gaffar Market. The officers said he had hired an auto from Batla House to Nizamuddin.

"He (Shakeel) wanted the bomb to explode in the evening and the auto driver was driving fast. He kept coaxing the driver to drive slow. On the way, he even asked him to stop the auto so that he could have an ice-cream.
