After waiting for about 15 minutes, when the auto driver said he could not wait any longer, Shakeel got in and asked him to head for Gaffar Market," said Dhaliwal.

Mohammed Sajid, who was killed in Friday's encounter, had planted the bomb that went off on Barakhamba Road, the police said. He too had taken an auto-rickshaw to the blast site and threw the brown polythene

bag containing the bomb in a dustbin.

The bomb that went off in the Park was allegedly planted by Zeeshan, arrested by the police from Jhandewalan late on

Friday.

The officers said it was Zeeshan who had planted the other bomb too in Central Park, which was defused later. The police defused another bomb in front of Regal Cinema, which was allegedly planted by Saif, who is in police custody at present. The third bomb to be defused was found at the Children's Park, which had been planted by Sada Bhai alias Malik, the police said.

According to the police, one of the bombs developed technical glitches at the last moment and could not be used. Saqib Nisar, arrested on Sunday night, was to plant it in Karol Bagh, they added. The tenth bomb is yet to be recovered.

After planting the bombs, the accused were instructed to get at least 30 metres away from the sites, as that was their radius, the police said. After the explosions, they assembled at Atif's L-18 flat and "celebrated the successful operation", claimed DCP Dhaliwal.

Heading: Had they told us, we could have been of big help to cops: Jamia Nagar residents - Indian Express
Content:
Till a few days ago, they were regular faces in the Jamia Nagar. After the Friday encounter and the arrests, they are the 'faces of terror'. According to police, it took the suspected terrorists days of planning to give shape to 9/13. SAHIM SALIM profiles the accused

Saqib Nisar, 23

Arrested on his birthday, "good looking" Saqib Nisar has excellent manners and is very polished, according to the police. His main job was to give "a good image" to the group. According to the police, he has many girlfriends and he could be seen chatting on the Internet most of the time. Nisar is pursuing his final year MBA through correspondence from Sikkim Manipal University. Prior to this, he worked as a recruiting officer with a private group in Nehru Place. He has won a medal in economics in Jamia School, claims his family. He had appeared for IAS in 2006 and is a former NCC cadet, say officers, adding that he has been living in F-68/1, Abu Fazal. His family has been living there for the last 35 years. The family is from Azamgarh.

Mohammed Shakeel, 24

According to investigating officers, he was the second in command to Atif in the Indian Mujahideen's Delhi chapter. In Atif's absence, he kept a close watch on the group and planned its affairs. His main job, say the officers, was "indoctrination". He distributed "jihadi literature" among the members of the group and motivated them. He is reportedly a final year student of MA (Economics) at Jamia Millia Islamia university. Shakeel met Atif many years ago through his cousin, Shahdab, Atif's childhood friend. Atif trusted him a lot and he was the only one in the group who was allowed to go back to his hometown after the blasts, according to the police. He basically belongs to Azamgarh, but his family is now settled in Bhulandshehar. His father reportedly owns a printing press.

Zia-ur-Rehman, 22

He was in charge of logistics in the group, say the police. Zia was the one who arranged for the L-18 house through his father, who was the caretaker of the building. In collaboration with Atif, the police claim, he had selected the spots where the bombs were to be planted. He is a final year BA student at Jamia, say the police. He has an O-level diploma in computer science. He is from Azamgarh too.

The reactions

* "There is no way my elder brother could be linked to any terror activity. TV channels are reporting that he planted bombs in Ahmedabad. He has not gone outside the city in many years."

— Sharique Nisar, Saqib's brother

* "Saqib had taken the Indian Administrative Services examination in 2006 because he wanted to root out corruption from the country."

— Shakir, another brother

* "People in the locality always looked up to him as an achiever. I don't believe he had any terror links."

— M K Kamal, neighbour

* "Officers had come over several times on Saturday, asking for but he was not at home. Around 3 pm, Abba jaan took him to the police station. Since then, he has not returned."

— Zia-ur-Rehman's brother, who did not want to be named

* "The owner of the flat had asked Abba jaan to rent it out. He asked around in Jamia campus if anybody needed any flat. That is how he came in touch with Atif."

— Zia's another brother

* "There should be a high-level, impartial investigation into the Batla House encounter. This will expose the reality of those involved in terror activities."

— Nusrat Ali, Jamat-e-Islami Hind Secretary General

(With inputs from Mandakini Gahlot and Sweta Dutta)

Heading: L-18 owner suspended for ‘irregularities’ - Indian Express
Content:
Two days after the encounter at Batla House left Inspector Mohan Chand Sharma and two suspected terrorists dead, the mood in Jamia Nagar is that of anger, suspicion and mistrust.

According to residents of the area, Sharma's life could have been saved had the police taken them into confidence and sought their help.

Irfanullah Khan, convener of the Jamia Nagar Coordination Committee and member of the Samata Party, said: "We have held meetings with Central ministers and even the Home Minister (Shivraj Patil) about the problems we face. Had the police told us about the presence of terrorists here, we could have been of big help to them."

"Sharma was known as a brave man here too," Khan said about the slain inspector.

Khan has been living in the area for the last at least 20 years. His house is located just around 100 metres away from L-18, where the encounter took place.

Abdur Rehman Abid, secretary of the committee, said: "People listen to the members of the committee. We could have helped force the boys (who were killed) to surrender peacefully."

Shadab Khan, 20, a student of MBA in Jamia Millia Islamia university, said: "We never get to know the real picture. Even the faces of the terrorists who were killed were not shown to us."

Shadab and his friends from the university had claimed it to be a fake encounter when Newsline spoke to them on Friday. Five boys, who were neighbours of the suspected terrorists, had been picked up after the encounter and released later.

"It is the holy month of Ramzan and people get too sensitive at such a time. We are suspicious too, leave alone the youth," said Irfanullah Khan.

The area had witnessed riots and tension in the month of Ramzan last year. A police chowki had been burnt down after a policeman allegedly insulted an aged Mufti and threw his Quran Sharif in a drain.

Subsequently, a police station was set up in the area to ensure a larger khaki presence and a better policing network.

As anticipated, the situation got tense after the encounter too, but Khan and some professors from the university helped calm the protestors outside L-18, barely a few metres from the Khaliullah Masjid.

Fayyaz Ahmed Khan, a lecturer in the engineering department of the university, was near the spot where the encounter took place. He had said on Friday: "The failure of the system is apparent, but we need to stick to the judgment of our brave policemen."

Heading: Private Unlimited - Indian Express
Content:
The owner of L-18, Batla House, where the Delhi Police shot down two suspected terrorists, Atif and Sajid, has been suspended by the Uttar Pradesh government. Mohsin Nisar works as an executive engineer with the public works department in Ghaziabad.

Government officials, however, did not link his suspension to the encounter. They claimed to have detected irregularities in the work he supervised as executive engineer with the National Highway division.

According to official sources, the letter of suspension was dispatched on September 19, the same day the encounter took place in his house in Jamia Nagar.

According to Ghaziabad District Magistrate Deepak Aggarwal, an inquiry was constituted six months ago to check whether allegations of irregularities in the NH project were true. "The executive engineer was charged for the irregularities and his letter of suspension was dispatched on September 19. We are yet to receive the letter, but I have the confirmation of his suspension," Aggarwal said.

While Nissar could not be contacted, the UP Police said he had been detained by the Delhi Police. Deputy Commissioner of Police (South District) H G S Dhaliwal, however, said Nissar was not in their custody. "Nisar filed a complaint against Rehman, the caretaker of L-18, for cheating him. He said he did not know that his tenants were not verified as per law," he said.

Abdul Rehman, the caretaker and father of Zia-ur-Rehman, who was among the three persons arrested on Sunday, has been arrested on charges of forgery and cheating.

Abdul Rehman was Nisar's stenographer, sources said.

Heading: Who let the Dogs in? - Indian Express
Content:
If you want to host a rocking party, there's no better venue than the city's hippest restaurants.

Swish brunch dos with wine-guzzling fashionistas, Med-nights with air-kissing P3Ps and liquor promotions with finger-licking food are the done events at Delhi's popular restaurants. A crop of new restaurants in the city are making sure that they're busy on lean nights as well, by renting out their premises for birthday bashes, baby showers or even bachelor nights, without hassling regular guests at their venue.

At Retro Sushi, the new Japanese lounge bar at Jaypee Vasant Continental, the mood is upbeat and the venue works well for a swanky party, with its dark interiors and open space that doubles up as a dance floor. "We can no longer rely on advertisements and walk-in guests. Private parties help us bring in guests through word-of-mouth publicity," says Rishi Levi, director of Retro Fly Pvt. Ltd that promotes Retro Sushi. Often for these private events, the lounge bar brings out beautiful velvet ropes to cordon off the party area and the party space is usually kept close to kitchen for easy access.

Apart from getting publicity and possibly more footfall to the restaurant, private parties add substantially to overall revenue, says Varun Tuli who runs The Yum Yum Tree in New Friends Colony. "Private dos contribute about 10 to 15 percent to the revenue and it's the easiest way to advertise," says Tuli. Check out the diner's almost hidden bar lounge or its outdoor seating which is perfect for sun bathing; there is a space for every mood. "It was a conscious call to keep separate dining areas. They add character to the space and help in hosting parties without disturbing regular diners," he adds.

"It is difficult to entertain 100 guests at home without ruining the interiors. Also, restaurants not only offer professional services, the package takes care of everything a party needs," says Kashif Farooq of Urban Pind. The lounge added a smart terrace space called Urban Café and is a hit with expats who love to party outdoors. "We easily accommodate around 150 people on the terrace. With live grill counters and good music the mood is perfectly set". At Urban Pind, private parties contribute about 15 to 20 percent to the revenue and Farooq also offers VIP access cards to his important patrons.

At Tabula Rasa in Saket that hosts 10 private parties every month, owner Sohrab Sitaram has plans of adding smart facilities for his banqueting guests. "In future we plan to introduce sound proof arrangements, separate rest rooms and entry doors for party guests," offers Sitaram. The reason he states, is that it can be suicidal to mix regular guests with a partying group. "More and more people prefer to host parties in restaurants since the staff is better trained and food is freshly prepared as per their choice. Also, organizing a party at a trendy restaurant works as a snob value for the host," he adds. For Tabula Rasa, private parties contribute over 40 percent to the total turnover.

"Hosting parties are very important for any restaurateur these days," acknowledges Ramola Bachchan. At her restaurant Manre, the space is seamlessly divided into fine-dining, lounge and open terraces. "It is crucial for a restaurant to have an independent party space," she says. Manre has Mezze and Maza floors with a Turkish setup and canopies that set the party mood and acoustics are well-maintained. The space can accommodate 200 people. "Floral décor is usually a part of the package unless the requirement is elaborate," says Bachchan. The F Bar and Kitchen in Gurgaon boasts a separate luxe space for private parties. Called F Prive, the space can accommodate 150 people and has some flattering services on offer including a separate entry door, butler service, pick ups and drops and a concierge service. "Gurgaon brings us lots of corporate parties. At F Prive we offer a 7-star service with a private bar and console," says Sachin Kohli, co-owner of F Bar & Kitchen, Gurgaon. The space, however, is usually booked a week in advance and orders are selected based on the guests' profile. A new designer outfit, could be a reason good enough to celebrate. And restaurants in the city will surely not complain.

Heading: Maple Sonata - Indian Express
Content:
A Delhi-based adoption site paves the way for animals and animal lovers

Two weeks ago, Penelope Spencer was saddled with seven puppies that her pet Honey had given birth to. The significant increase in dog population in her apartment led her landlady to serve her with an eviction notice. "If I wanted to keep them, I'd have clear out of my apartment as well," says Spencer who frantically looked all over the city for people to adopt the pups. It was only when Malleka Gupta (pictured below) and www.dogadoption.in stepped in, all seven puppies found a home.

Gupta, 25, has been running her site for a few months now and it is the Capital's only functioning adoption site for dogs. An avid dog lover, Gupta adopted an Indian/Street pup during her college years but it wasn't till later, when a female dog near her house, gave birth to eight beautiful Indian pups that she began to use the net for dog adoptions. "I placed ads on various social networking sites and over a period of time, found homes for all of them. One important requirement to get them adopted, was to bring them inside the house and get their vaccinations and begin their house training," says Gupta who has fostered over 18 pups. The site is becoming increasingly popular with animal lovers and is a god-send for people who want to adopt, report missing pets or put an advertisement up for adoption. Gupta doesn't charge for the services and the site is divided into different sub-pages informing one of the sterilization and pet care techniques, missing pets and lastly, one section called My Pet. "It's important to encourage people to write in about their adopted pets. That way, other interested parties feel more confident about going ahead with the adoption," says Gupta.

It's not been all hunky-dory for Gupta. From previous unpleasant experiences, she has learnt to conduct a verification process to ensure the safety and security of all the adopted pups. "I make the adopting family sign an adoption form containing all the important details about the family. I check on the pet regularly and inform them that they will have to cooperate. Only when the family agrees to these terms and conditions is the adoption procedure is complete," says Gupta. But even then, some families manage to fake information and give away the animals they've adopted or let them loose on the streets again. But Gupta doesn't let the bad experiences deter her. Apart from adoption, Gupta is constantly trying to educate people about pet care and how to deal with street dogs. "One needs to treat an animal just like a human being and give them love. In turn, not only are they the most loyal of all animals, they also become family," says Gupta. Paws up for this site.

For more information log on to www.dogadoption.in or email dogadoption.in@gmail.com

Heading: Taking Stock - Indian Express
Content:
This Canadian pianist concentrates on creating drama, onstage

The air around the piano, insists 31-year-old Canadian pianist Mathieu Gaudet, currently on a seven-city tour of India, must sparkle with gold dust. "Otherwise it's not worth anything. Nobody wants to listen to notes," insists Gaudet before a show at the IIC on Friday evening.

As far as Gaudet is concerned, piano playing begins with the heart not the fingers. His personal style is flamboyant and what makes him appealingly different is his instinct for the piano, and the sheer passion with which he plays it. It's earned him a long list of prestigious awards, a major CD deal and stints with the best pianists in Canada and the US, from Julian Martin to Paul Stewart.

The "purity of conviction" that famous French pianist Jean-Phillipe Goddard once spotted in Gaudet's rendition of Schumann's Fantasy had led the musician into other avenues. After a doctorate on Sergei Rachmaninov, he is now pursuing a medical degree from the University of Montreal. "I grew up in the smallest village in Canada that has just 2,000 people and two piano teachers," smiles Gaudet.

In India he travels by train because "planes are the greatest cause of global warming." He hates air-conditioners and prefers sleeper-class, where his co-passengers are unguarded like the urban elite. "Even in Canada, I don't own a car and cycle everywhere," says the pianist who's been a doctor-in-training in Kenya as well as among the Inuit people.

As in life, so in music Gaudet is an actor juggling roles. While playing Robert Schumann's Dances for the Fellowship of David in Delhi, for instance, he effortlessly takes on the role of the two central characters the composer was writing about: the flamboyant Florestan in the first half and the more restrained Eusebius in the second. "It's a pain," he grins. "But, a musician must expose his raw spots. He must be vulnerable. Only then, with the air around his piano sparklewith gold."

Heading: Five-year-old run over by car, brother critical - Indian Express
Content:
"Bahut ho gaya, chaddo tussi. Thankfully I am no longer playing the character of a Punjabi woman. I think it's time I started exploring other roles," chuckles actor Kirron Kher, 53, who plays a Bengali character in her latest movie, the delightfully titled Saas Bahu Aur Sensex. Kher along with co-star Masumeh Makhija and director Shona Urvashi (of Chup Ke Se fame in 2003) dropped by at Spice World on Thursday for the premiere of their film. The plot is based on middle class aspirations juxtaposed against the regular fluctuations in the Stock market. The star cast may not be too impressive, but there is consolation since it is the first Hindi film Warner Brothers is representing in India.

Kher plays a middle class woman, Binita Sen, from Kolkata who lives in a Mumbai neighbourhood with her daughter played by Tanushree Dutta. She wants to start life afresh but she lives in a flat with saas bahu serials obsessed women. So is she a fan of the Kyunkis? "No way. There is already so much drama in real life," smiles Kher. The stock market angle is provided by veteran actor Farooque Shaikh, who is a broker in the film and educates Kher on the stock market. "I am clueless about the stock market. I keep away from such things. Working with Farooque was a pleasure since he is a complete ladies man," says Kher. Will it work? It just might, considering Bollywood can be as unpredictable as the Sensex.

Heading: No place to call home - Indian Express
Content:
Five-year-old Monu and his brother Sahil, 7, were hit by a speeding Skoda car on Sunday morning. Monu died on the spot, while Sahil is battling for life at the Sunder Lal Jain Hospital. The siblings from a J J Colony in Wazirpur were playing behind a stationery Blueline bus when the car, coming at high speed from the opposite direction, rammed into them. Their father runs a small shop nearby.

Eyewitness accounts say the illegal bus stop near the colony, where the Blueline bus of route number 142 was parked, is partly to blame. They said the children, who were playing on a parked scooter just behind the bus, suddenly jumped on the road and came in the way of the recklessly-driven car.

Locals beat up the car's driver and damaged the car. When alerted about the accident, a police party rushed to the spot. They have arrested the driver and impounded the offending vehicle.

The Ashok Vihar police have registered a case of rash and negligent driving against the driver.

Heading: In Lajpat Nagar, police turn to ragpickers for help - Indian Express
Content:
2 lakh The number of homeless people in the Capital

A report by the National Legal Services Authority, prepared with research assistance from the Jawaharlal Nehru University and submitted recently before the Delhi High Court, documents the status of destitute women in Delhi. The report initiates a probe by the High Court on steps needed to combat homelessness

Homeless women in Delhi

The 1991 census reported total houseless in Delhi to be around 29,000. The rough estimate as per a joint study by the Shahdara Mental Hospital and a Delhi-based NGO shows at least a lakh homeless in the year 2000. The estimate in the year 2007 is about 2 lakh. Of this total population only 4 per cent were women.

Socio-demographic profile

* A report filed in the Delhi High Court on September 10 shows that out of a sample study of 4,192 homeless women on the Capital's streets, 79.6 per cent were in the productive age group of 16 to 45. 77.3 per cent were married. 22.7 per cent were single women. In the group of single women 8.9 per cent were unmarried, 10.3 per cent divorced and 2.9 per cent widowed.

* 79.4 per cent of the homeless women in Delhi were living with their families. 11.5 per cent women were living with their children and the rest 8.9 per cent were living alone.

* Nearly all the women (92.3 per cent) were illiterate. 63.2 per cent women had been in Delhi for a period ranging from five years to more than 20 years. 2.8 per cent were born and brought up on the streets of Delhi.

Sleeping place

* 65. 9 per cent sleep on the roadside. 10 per cent in parks and 8.1 per cent in religious places. Only 6.1 per cent women use facilities like shelters and government homes.

* 57 per cent women are located in south and central Delhi. 30 per cent in West Delhi and only 13 per cent in East Delhi.

Reasons for homelessness

* 69.9 per cent cite absence of any source of income. 18.5 per cent loss of their jhuggies.

* 2.9 per cent women report personal and domestic problems. 0.7 per cent report mental illness, while 1.6 per cent cite desertion by husbands.

Source of livelihood

52.2 per cent sell small items on footpaths. 18.4 per cent do odd jobs.

8.1 per cent have no source of income. 18.5 per cent resort to begging.

Discrimination and harassment

* 96.7 per cent women report harassment of some sort or the other.

* 26.7 per cent report emotional harassment alone, while 28.5 per cent add physical or financial harassment to it.

* 76.9 women report maximum harassment from law enforcers, while 1.6 per cent blame local anti-social elements.

Heading: 9/13 remembrance: Pooja Nadipat, 17 - Indian Express
Content:
Not 'scared' of the men in khaki any more, they share information with police in lieu of protection

The heart of Delhi, Connaught Place, is just a distant corner in her world that is limited between Khadar village, where she lives, and the bustling Lajpat Nagar market, where she works. But, Lailee knows how a 10 year-old ragpicker like her had fished out a bomb and informed the police about it minutes after the twin blasts rocked CP on September 13.

"That boy was rewarded because he helped the police. We will be rewarded too if we find a bomb," says the 10-year-old. The ragpicker in Lajpat Nagar's Central Market heard about the incident from Shafir (9), another ragpicker, while rummaging through the waste for paper and plastic.

Lailee is among the 5,000 ragpickers who are part of a programme initiated by Chetna, an organisation working with street children in Lajpat Nagar and its adjoining areas.

"We aim to create an interface between the police and the ragpickers working in the area," explains Sanjay Gupta, who heads the programme.

"We have helped the police find things," says eight-year-old Zaida, recalling how a boy had found a laptop wrapped in a plastic bag and given it the "police guard". The laptop was apparently stolen and hidden in one of the dustbins.

Under the programme that started three years ago, a group of ragpickers led by one of them, visits the local police station once a month and interacts with officers. "These children often get into trouble with the police because of street fights and thefts, and are scared of the men in khaki. The programme helps create friendly ties between them. While these kids help the police, giving them clues on the whereabouts of miscreants, in return they get protection from the police," adds Gupta, recalling how a group of street children and ragpickers had helped the police trace two missing boys after the blasts in Sarojini Nagar in 2005.

Most of the ragpickers in Lajpat Nagar are part of the programme and are residents of Khadar village near Mathura Road.

While the Delhi Police has initiated the "eyes and ears" scheme, aiming to develop a local intelligence network of street vendors and ragpickers, Shayantani Das of Chintan, which works with ragpickers in the New Delhi area, believes the recent blasts have given some recognition to the huge population of ragpickers in the city.

"It is essential to organise them in groups. Most of them are children and are vulnerable to street violence and drug abuse. We need help from the police through such initiatives," says Das.

While Chintan has been sending about 250-odd ragpickers to the New Delhi Municipal Council for its door-to-door garbage collection initiative since last year, it is only now that the civic agency has decided to issue smart cards and uniforms to the rag pickers working in the area. "Whether we like it or not, it is the ragpicker who lifts things that we don't like to touch. Even if they were made to lift bombs, at least the episode made the authorities acknowledge their potential and decide to give them uniforms and gloves," she says.

"We have a good network of ragpickers and safai karamcharis who carry out our door-to-door collection plans in the area. We have now asked our circle officers to keep in touch with them to keep a vigil on suspicious activities and miscreants," said Medical Officer of Health (NDMC) Dr P K Sharma. He said all supervisors in the area had been officially instructed to check the dustbins every morning and evening, besides keeping a regular vigil and submit reports regularly to him.

Heading: Yamuna just 23 cm short of danger mark - Indian Express
Content:
"She was a religious girl, a blessing from the goddess Durga herself and hence we had named her Pooja, why did the goddess let her die then?" asks an inconsolable Rama Nadipat, who is himself recuperating in the Orthopaedics ward at Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital.

A week after the blast in Gaffar Market, he lies at RML with a fractured left arm and chest injuries. Rama's relatives have just informed him that his youngest daughter Pooja is dead. Pierced by splinters, Pooja, 17, was declared dead on arrival at the Lady Hardinge Medical College last Saturday.

"For the last few days, Pooja had been insisting that we shift to Ravi Nagar," says Rama.

"'Baba let us all shift to some better place,' she would say. Perhaps she had an inkling that something sinister was about to happen, but I just brushed away her words."

Originally from Rajasthan, Rama and his family has been living in Gali no. 42 in Karol Bagh for years now. It was, however, a matter of a few minutes before his world came crashing. While the blast claimed Pooja's life, Rama's elder daughter Santosh, 22, is battling for life in the neuro-surgery ward at RML and his wife Krishna lies in the post-operative theatre on the second floor of the hospital, oblivious of her younger daughter's death.

"Pooja was the most pampered one and the most beautiful," Rama says.

"She was the most gentle soul, very cultured and kind." The family had been looking for a suitable match for her and she was to be married soon.

"'Have you had food baba? And what about your medicines,' she would ask, making sure always that I had no troubles," he adds, wiping his eyes with his green hospital gown.

"I do not know why this happened to her, she never harmed anyone. She was the blessed one and the rest of us were probably saved because of her grace, for we were all at the same spot at the time of the blast," Rama says, trying to compose himself.

For now, he will have to break the death to his wife.

"The goddess has called my Pooja back, but I know she is watching us. My daughter will never leave us," he says.

Heading: Teachers on contract to tide over severe crisis in government schools - Indian Express
Content:
The water level in the Yamuna in the Capital touched 204.6 m on Sunday, just 23 cm short of the danger mark, after Haryana released nearly four lakh cusecs of water into the river.

Officials, who have had to take precautionary measures to tackle the "alarming situation", also fear the water level may surpass its five-year record by tomorrow. "The danger mark may be breached tomorrow morning," Delhi government sources said.

It is for the first time in the last ten years that such a huge quantity of water has been released from the Tajewala barrage by Haryana, which is witnessing heavy rainfall."We have alerted all people living in the Yamuna's catchment areas. We have taken all precautionary measures," a senior official with the Delhi Flood and Irrigation Department said.

People living adjacent to the Yamuna banks have been warned and directed to evacuate to safer places.

All officials have been alerted and logistics have been arranged to meet any eventualities. "Control rooms have been set up at various strategic places to keep a round-the-clock check on water flow, which has been steadily increasing due to constant rains in the northern states," the official said. After touching the danger mark of 204.88 m on August 7, the water level shot up on August 17 to reach 205.55 m, much above the danger mark, for the first time in the last five years.

Heading: Delhi underground - Indian Express
Content:
With government schools facing a major faculty crunch, the Delhi Directorate of Education (DoE) has proposed a plan to allow school principals to appoint teachers on contract as a short-term measure. The proposal is likely to come up before the Delhi cabinet in the next few days.

The Indian Express had reported in June that close to 7, 000 Trained Graduate Teacher (TGT) posts and more than 1,200 assistant teacher posts in Delhi government schools were vacant. Official sources have said that more than 8000 vacancies still exist in various categories of schoolteachers, the maximum being in the primary education sector.

The proposal, if passed by the Delhi Cabinet, will allow principals to employ qualified teachers on short-term contract basis.

Sources say that the number of students in government schools has gone up from 8 lakh to 12 lakh in the last four years, but the number of teachers has not increased accordingly. The proposal, if passed, will enable principals to appoint teachers from the local pool of qualified people.

There is a set procedure for such an appointment with a committee constituted to select the candidates. "Even the Kendriya Vidyalayas allow principals to hire teachers on contract in a crunch situation," said a source.

These appointments will not be regularised since it is the responsibility of the Delhi State Subordinate Services Board (DSSSB) to recruit teachers. "It is taking too long for the DSSSB to recruit teachers. We expect exam results soon. So hopefully, some vacancies will be filled by regular teachers," said an official source.

"We hope a number of women who might not have applied earlier due to various commitments will apply to local schools now," said an official source.

Heading: Delhi Metro ties up with Easy Cabs for better mobility from stations - Indian Express
Content:
Eyeing compensation

A curious outcome of the last weekend's serial blasts was the flow of "victims" that started trickling into hospitals a day or two later. According to the chief medical officer (CMO) of a leading government hospital, a few people with minor and superficial injuries showed up at the hospital two days after the blasts, eying the hefty compensation package. In the absence of any firm evidence about the cause of their injuries, the CMO promptly guided them to the SHO of the police station at the blast sites, after administration of first aid.

Out of bounds

Jalvayu Vihar seems to have become a no-entry zone for senior Noida policemen, ever since the infamous Arushi-Hemraj murder case. Being the local law enforcement authority the Noida police have to provide personnel to the CBI, which has been investigating the case, for peripheral security, but senior officers have been maintaining a safe distance from the crime spot ever since the investigation was taken away from them. When it was pointed out by someone that the recently appointed SSP of Noida, R K Chaturvedi, hadn't even visited the high-profile crime spot, he reportedly said he didn't even sleep facing that direction, leave alone visiting the site.

A piece of the pie

Everyone wants a piece of the action when it comes to the Delhi Assembly, including politicians who are no longer elected to the House. Ajay Maken, a former Speaker of the Assembly, who is now a Lok Sabha MP from New Delhi and Minister of State for Urban Development, was seen at the recently concluded session. Sources in the party said the senior Congress leader was desperate to be seen at the session, as he too wanted to take credit for the much-hyped provisional regularisation scheme for unauthorised colonies in the city, announced recently by the Delhi government. Moreover, several party leaders said that though the Congress doesn't have a chance in the forthcoming Assembly polls, Maken was busy positioning himself for the polls after five years.

What's in a name

For repeated non-appearance in court, a lawyer argued at length before a magistrate to have accused Manjit Singh declared a "proclaimed offender". Interestingly, the lawyer knew nothing about the whereabouts or the address of Singh but kept pressing for action. Accepting his demand would have meant declaring any and all "Manjit Singhs" proclaimed offenders and open to arrest. Judicious enough, the magistrate told the lawyer that he could not put in jeopardy the liberty of all the persons with that name and turned his plea down, asking him to furnish detailed particulars of the accused.

In the times of terror

How is a South Delhi school taken over by the Delhi Government from a "corrupt" trust connected to the Delhi blasts that rocked the Capital on September 13? Well, the sole link is a remark from a Delhi High Court judge — one of two judges hearing the case of the hapless institution — a couple of days after the attacks. "We have to be careful on who is running schools, especially when there is a global warning against terror," the judge said. The connection is still hazy though.

All is quiet

After a long time, the BJP-led Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) managed to have a peaceful House meeting last week. Usually, House meetings end up in scenes of utter chaos with both the ruling party and the Opposition hurling accusations at each other. In almost every meeting in the last few months, the agenda has invariably been left unattended due to skirmishes that took off right during the first hour. The September 8 meeting was, however, a welcome change and a member of the Opposition remarked right in the face of the Mayor that the recent foreign study tour seemed to have smoothened rough edges between the leaders of the two parties. The leaders of the Opposition, who usually devised ways to disrupt proceedings by getting megaphones, sat through the meeting trying to shush other members who out of habit were getting into brawls with Opposition members. In a long time, all the items on the agenda were discussed and that too within the stipulated two hours.

Gain without pain

The Delhi University Teachers Association has been crying hoarse demanding the immediate submission of the Pay Review Committee report but if a department is missing in all the action, it is the Law Faculty. On Wednesday, when the entire teaching staff of DU was out on the roads, protesting, teachers of the Law Faculty were busy taking classes. S N Singh, Dean of Law Faculty, who is always first to protest any sort of unlawful activities in DU, took note of the situation and said in good humour: "So what if we have not taken part in the protest, we will reap the benefits in any case (if the Pay Review Committee report is submitted)."

Heading: Chatter box - Indian Express
Content:
Aiming to provide easy mobility from its stations, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has tied up with a radio taxi service.

The service is scheduled to begin after a month, according to a statement issued by the DMRC. The cab agency, Easy Cabs, will set up kiosks at 25 Metro stations, including Rithala, Pitampura, Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Central Secretariat, Pragati Maidan and Dwarka among others. In order to avail the cab services, commuters can contact the personnel manning the kiosks, who in turn will arrange for a taxi to the specified destination.

As for the financial details, the DMRC has said Easy Cabs will pay a rent to the corporation for the space they will use at the stations. The DMRC will also receive a portion of the revenue generated, as per a fixed formula worked out with the agency. The deal will be valid for three years to start with. DMRC sources say a need for the service was felt as certain parts of Delhi, such as South Delhi, are yet to come under the Metro umbrella.

"These taxis will help commuters reach South Delhi, Noida, Gurgaon, the airport and other areas immediately, once this service becomes operational, since the Metro will be reaching these destinations only in the next two years," a DMRC official said.

DMRC already has 120 feeder buses running on 17 routes, ferrying over 60,000 commuters every day. It is also providing a cycle renting service at the Vishwavidyalaya Metro Station, which now has 30 cycles available for hire.

Heading: Talking point with Munish makhija - Indian Express
Content:
Nagging pain

DON'T lie about your knee pain, or you'll get an earful from Aroona Irani, as Jasveer Kaur did on Sahara One's Saas vs Bahu. Kaur had to stop her performance midway due to a knee sprain, but she got quite a dressing down from judge Irani later when she delivered a power packed re-performance. The reason? Irani thought she had faked her knee pain. Irani also lost her cool with Soumya Tandon, who intervened on Kaur's behalf. "What do you know?" the senior actress reportedly yelled at her. But Soumya believes in letting the past go. So let's hope there's no more of this drama on one more reality show.

Two for the money

NACH Baliye chugs into its fourth season and who better to host it than last season's winners Aamir Ali and Sanjeeda Sheikh. But Ali is neither confirming nor denying this rumour. He says, "It's not a necessary legacy for the previous winners to host the new season every time. The main question is if the audience wants to see the couple on the show again." If the rumours are indeed true, this will be the second show that Ali and Sheikh will be working together in, after Kya Dil Mein Hai. If ever there was a karma connection, this is it.

Toon time

SKATOONY is back with its second season on Pogo. The world's first animated/live action quiz show, Skatoony, will begin airing on September 21. It is the only show in the world which has kids competing with cartoon characters for real prizes like the Sony Playstation 3. The show promises to be smarter, funnier and wackier, this time. We just can't wait, can we?of this year.

Dancing Queen

MORE news from Saas vs Bahu. Marathi mulgi Amita Chandekar was kicked out of the show in spite of being the highest individual scorer. The lady was referred to as the 'Sachin Tendulkar' of her team and outscored the other Bahus like Shilpa Saklani and Chhavi Mittal, as well as the Saas' like Jayati Bhatia, Priya Arya and Komolika Guha. Even hard-to-please judge Aroona Irani appreciated her performance. But the lady is optimistic. She says, "I am hoping that even if my team loses, by virtue of being the top individual scorer, I get a wild card to re-enter the fray as per the show's format." We'll keep our fingers crossed, Amita.

Heading: Masala fare - Indian Express
Content:
The maverick VJ-actor talks about his latest show, Cash Cab

Ques: What is the concept behind Cash Cab?

The show is primarily a quiz show. There is a guy who drives a cab and the people who get in are subjected to a quiz. If you answer correctly, you stand to win as much as Rs 20,000. This show is basically for the common people, the kind who get into cabs.

Ques: Tell us about your character on the show.

My character is called Munna, which is a name that lots of people know me by even in my real life. Munna's a Jat taxi driver and he has his opinions set in life. His speech is cut-throat and he catches people unawares and basically makes it very awkward for them by saying whatever he wants. That's part of the funny element on the show.

Ques: How is Munna different from Uddham Singh, a character that you made famous before?

Uddham Singh is basically Munna. They're both Jat and are highly opinionated.

Ques: What attracted you to this show?

There are quite a few things, actually. One is that the show is constantly on the move; it's not shot in a studio. I also get to weave a common thread with the common people, something that does not happen on other shows. Also playing the part of a cab driver is fun. And then there is the money. There are shows which offer a lot more money, but if you ask the average person on the streets, he'll be very happy with even Rs 20,000.

Ques: What was it like working with Bindass, after having worked with Channel [V]?

Not very different, since half the people I worked with there, are here now. But there are quite a few new people as well, so it's been great. As I like to say, it's been quite an education working here and it's a lesson in Shakespeare's Comedy of Errors.

Ques: First Uddham Singh, now Munna. Do you think you're changing perceptions about TV-show hosts?

With this show, a lot of the usual ideas that people have about TV-show hosts, will change. If Uddham Singh was in Class IV, then Munna would be in Class VIII.
